title: Prospects for constraining the spin of the massive black hole at the Galactic center via the relativistic motion of a surrounding star
text_ai: In this paper, we investigate the quality of constraining the spin of the massive black hole (MBH) at the Galactic center (GC) by using full general relativistic simulations of the motion of a surrounding star. To this end, we evolve a comprehensive suite of null-geodesic integrations in Kerr spacetime that include both the Lense–Thinring (frame-dragging) and quadrupole contributions, and we generate synthetic observables by ray-tracing photon trajectories to a distant observer. We account for relativistic redshift, Shapiro delay, and light bending, and we perform parameter estimation with a Bayesian framework (MCMC/Fisher analyses) to recover MBH mass M_BH, distance R0, spin magnitude a*, and spin orientation (inclination i, position angle Ω), jointly with the star’s orbital elements and potential perturbations from distributed matter. We explore several representative orbital configurations, focusing on stars with periods in the 8–20 yr range and eccentricities e > 0.5, residing within a few thousand r_g of Sgr A*. Our results show that with astrometric precision at the ~10 μas level and spectroscopic precision ~1–5 km s−1, accumulated over a decade, the spin can be constrained to Δa* ≈ 0.1–0.3 and orientation uncertainties of order tens of degrees (Δi, ΔΩ ~ 10–50°), contingent on the true spin geometry and the observer’s line of sight. The dominant limitation is a degeneracy between frame-dragging–driven nodal precession and Newtonian precession from the extended mass; mitigating this requires external priors on the central mass distribution or joint modeling of multiple, complementary orbits. We discuss practical observational strategies and quantify the data-quality requirements necessary to realize a robust test of the no-hair relation via stellar dynamics.
prefix: In this paper, we investigate the quality of constraining the spin of the massive black hole (MBH) at the Galactic center (GC) by using full general relativistic simulations of the motion of a surrounding star.

title: A natural killer T-cell subset that protects against airway hyperreactivity.
text_ai: Infection of suckling mice with influenza virus expands a CD4 - CD8 - double-negative (DN) natural killer T (NKT) cell subpopulation that protects the mice as adults against allergen-induced airway hyperreactivity (AHR). However, this NKT cell subset has not been characterized, and the underlying mechanisms of protection remain unknown. Here we demonstrate that this DN NKT population is a CD3+ NK1.1+ TCRβ+ CD1d-tetramer–restricted subset that expands after neonatal influenza and persists into adulthood with a regulatory phenotype. Using flow cytometry, transcriptional profiling, and IL-10 reporter mice, we find that these cells preferentially secrete IL-10 and display limited production of Th2- and Th1 cytokines at baseline. In adoptive transfer experiments, purified DN NKT cells from influenza-exposed neonates markedly reduce allergen-induced AHR in adult recipients, accompanied by decreased BAL eosinophilia and lower levels of IL-4, IL-5, and IL-13; goblet cell metaplasia is attenuated. The protection is IL-10–dependent, as blockade or genetic ablation of IL-10 reverses the effect. CD1d engagement appears necessary, because disruption of CD1d–NKT signaling diminishes protection. In vitro, DN NKT cells suppress dendritic cell maturation and Th2 polarization. Single-cell transcriptional analysis reveals a regulatory program enriched for IL-10 production and pathways associated with immune regulation. Collectively, these data define a neonatally induced DN NKT cell subset as a natural regulatory axis that mitigates allergen-driven AHR through IL-10–mediated suppression of Th2 inflammation, linking early-life viral exposure to lifelong tolerance. Targeting this axis could inform strategies to prevent or treat allergic airway disease. These findings warrant translational exploration.

However, this NKT cell subset has not been characterized, and the underlying mechanisms of protection remain unknown.

title: A formal implementation of Behavior Trees to act in robotics
text_ai: Behavior Trees (BT) are becoming quite popular as an Acting component of autonomous robotic systems. We propose to define a formal semantics to BT by translating them to a formal language which enables us to perform verification of programs written with BT, as well as runtime verification while these BT execute. To this end, we first articulate an operational semantics for the BT nodes (root, sequence, selector, parallel, decorator, and leaf actions/conditions), mapping the progress of a BT run to a transition system. We then present a faithful translation into a formal language whose model-checking semantics guarantee that verified properties hold for all reachable executions. The translation is designed to be compositional, so the semantics of complex trees follows from the semantics of their constituents. We implement a prototype toolchain that automatically generates models for a verifier and inserts runtime monitors that observe tick events and node statuses on a robotics middleware (ROS/RT). We validate the approach on representative tasks (navigation with obstacle avoidance, goal-oriented manipulation) and demonstrate detection of flaky behavior, invariant violations, and deadlock conditions while preserving real-time constraints.

We propose to define a formal semantics to BT by translating them to a formal language which enables us to perform verification of programs written with BT, as well as runtime verification while these BT execute.

title: On Asteroid Retrieval Missions Enabled by Invariant Manifold Dynamics
text_ai: In recent years, the retrieval of entire asteroids has received significant attention, with many approaches leveraging the invariant manifolds of the Circular-Restricted Three-body Problem to capture an asteroid into a periodic orbit about the $L_1$ or $L_2$ points of the Sun-Earth system. Here, we present a design framework that couples invariant-manifold trajectories with shallow, multi-impulse maneuvers to realize asteroid retrieval missions. By computing the stable and unstable manifolds of L1/L2 halo orbits and Lyapunov orbits within the Sun–Earth CR3BP and stitching these with low-thrust propulsion, we identify low-energy transfer corridors that connect a target asteroid’s heliocentric state to a bound capture about the Earth–Moon system. The approach is augmented by an intermediate patching strategy, first employing a patched-conic approximation to generate candidate branches, then refined with a high-fidelity n-body propagator including solar radiation pressure and third‑body perturbations. We apply the framework to a set of near-Earth asteroids with well-determined ephemerides, producing delta‑v budgets, capture epochs, and expected time-of-flight to Earth‑bound orbits. Sensitivity analyses reveal robustness to ephemeris errors and model uncertainties, underscoring invariant-manifold dynamics as a viable enabler for resource-enabled retrieval missions.

title: Context-Dependent Diffusion Network for Visual Relationship Detection
text_ai: Visual relationship detection can bridge the gap between computer vision and natural language for scene understanding of images. Different from pure object recognition tasks, the relation triplets of subject-predicate-object lie on an extreme diversity space, such as \textit{person-behind-person} and \textit{car-behind-building}, while suffering from the problem of combinatorial explosion. To address these challenges, we propose a Context-Dependent Diffusion Network (CDDN) that performs relational inference through a learned diffusion process over a scene graph constructed from object proposals. Each node encodes a candidate object with visual features and a class prior, while edges capture spatial and semantic affinities. A relation-aware diffusion module propagates information along the graph conditioned on the subject–object pair, yielding an enriched pair representation that encodes cues such as compatibility. A predicate-specific attention head maps the fused representation to scores over predicates. To mitigate long-tail and zero-shot difficulties, we introduce a context-guided sampling strategy and regularization that emphasize plausible relations given the surroundings. Experiments on VRD and benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements, with particular gains for rare and unseen relations; ablations verify the necessity of diffusion depth and context gating.

Different from pure object recognition tasks, the relation triplets of subject-predicate-object lie on an extreme diversity space, such as \textit{person-behind-person} and \textit{car-behind-building}, while suffering from the problem of combinatorial explosion.

title: Beyond the Meta: Leveraging Game Design Parameters for Patch-Agnostic Esport Analytics
text_ai: Esport games comprise a sizeable fraction of the global games market, and is the fastest growing segment in games. This has given rise to the domain of esports analytics, which uses telemetry data from games to inform players, coaches, broadcasters and other stakeholders. However, most analyses remain tethered to current balance states, risking brittle conclusions as patches roll out. We propose a design-parameter framework that decouples strategic signal from patch-specific noise by operationalizing core game-design levers as invariants. We define a compact ontology of design parameters—economy cadence, tempo, map geometry, resource scission, tech-tree branching, and unit-skill ceilings—derived from developer notes and corroborated by telemetry, and we construct patch-agnostic features that capture how these levers shape decision making and outcomes across patches. We then train models to predict match trajectory and success likelihood using patch-invariant inputs, enabling cross-patch generalization and fairer cross-title comparisons. In empirical evaluation on two popular titles with multiple balance updates, our patch-agnostic models outperform patch-specific baselines in transfer tasks, improve robustness to unseen patches, and reveal persistent dynamics such as early tempo control and risk-reward consolidation that survive changes in meta. We further integrate the framework into a lightweight pipeline for analysts and coaches that automatically extracts design-parameter signals, performs causal factorization of observed behaviors, and outputs interpretable dashboards. The results demonstrate that design-parameter priors yield stable, actionable insights for teams and broadcasters, and offer a scalable route toward patch-agnostic benchmarking and game-design feedback.

title: When does proton pump inhibitor treatment become long term? A scoping review.
text_ai: Proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use has risen substantially, primarily driven by ongoing use over months to years. However, there is no consensus on how to define long-term PPI use. Our objectives were to review and compare definitions of long-term PPI use in existing literature and describe the rationale for each definition. Methods: We conducted a scoping review of peer‑reviewed studies and clinical guidelines from 2000–2024, searching MEDLINE, Embase, and supplementary sources. We included works that explicitly defined long‑term PPI use or employed explicit operational criteria for duration, dose, or refill patterns. Data were charted on the duration thresholds used to label long‑term use, whether the definition captured continuous versus intermittent use, any dose or cumulative‑dose requirements, care setting, and the authors’ rationale. Where possible, we mapped definitions to a common conceptual framework and summarized associations with outcomes reported. Results: We identified substantial heterogeneity in definitions. Time cutoffs ranged from 4 weeks to 12 months or more; some studies used fixed minimum durations (e.g., ≥8–12 weeks), others relied on persistence across multiple prescriptions or refill intervals. Dose‑based criteria included cumulative defined daily doses or maintenance‑dose equivalents. A subset of definitions linked duration to indication, distinguishing chronic conditions such as GERD or peptic‑ulcer disease from nonspecific or short‑term use. Justifications varied; many cited guideline concordance, anticipated adverse effects, or a need to separate symptom‑driven short courses from ongoing management, yet explicit rationale was inconsistently described. Where data allowed, we explored potential associations with adverse events and resource use, noting that inconsistent definitions complicated interpretation. Conclusion: The marked definitional heterogeneity impedes cross‑study comparisons and synthesis of safety and effectiveness. We propose a pragmatic, multi‑axis framework that categorizes time‑based, dose‑based, and use‑pattern criteria, explicitly tied to indication and care setting, to standardize reporting and enhance interpretability for research and guidelines.

Our objectives were to review and compare definitions of long-term PPI use in existing literature and describe the rationale for each definition.

title: On performance bound estimation in NMPC with time-varying terminal cost
text_ai: Model predictive control (MPC) schemes are commonly designed with fixed, i.e., time-invariant, horizon length and cost functions. If no stabilizing terminal ingredients are used, stability can be guaranteed via a sufficiently long horizon. A suboptimality index can be derived that gives bounds on the performance of the MPC law over an infinite-horizon (IH). Here, we allow the terminal cost to be time-varying, which encompasses scheduled terminal penalties, online updated certificates of stability, or adaptively learned costs. We derive a time-varying suboptimality bound that relates the infinite-horizon performance to the finite-horizon cost-to-go plus a cumulative terminal-variation term. Under mild regularity assumptions on the dynamics and the stage cost, and with a terminal map that decreases along trajectories up to a multiplicative, time-dependent factor, we obtain a contraction-like inequality. The resulting bound is computable online from the current state and the history of terminal penalties, and reduces to the classical bound in the time-invariant case. Numerical case studies on benchmark nonlinear systems illustrate the influence of terminal-cost variation on guaranteed performance, and demonstrate that optimized terminal cost schedules can tighten the IH bound without sacrificing short-horizon performance.
prefix: Model predictive control (MPC) schemes are commonly designed with fixed, i.e., time-invariant, horizon length and cost functions. If no stabilizing terminal ingredients are used, stability can be guaranteed via a sufficiently long horizon. A suboptimality index can be derived that gives bounds on the performance of the MPC law over an infinite-horizon (IH).

title: EDIT: Exemplar-Domain Aware Image-to-Image Translation
text_ai: Image-to-image translation is to convert an image of the certain style to another of the target style with the content preserved. A desired translator should be capable to generate diverse results in a controllable (many-to-many) fashion. To this end, we design a novel generative adversarial network, namely exemplar-domain aware image-to-image translator (EDIT for short). Concretely, EDIT accepts an input image x and an exemplar y from the target domain. A domain-aware encoder extracts a content code c from x and a style code s from y, which are fused in the generator through adaptive normalization and a multi-scale exemplar-aware attention module. This design enables diverse translations by sampling s (and an optional latent z) to produce outputs while preserving spatial structure. Two discriminators enforce realism and domain alignment, complemented by a perceptual content loss computed from a pre-trained encoder. We further introduce an exemplar-domain alignment loss to match the translated statistics to the exemplar domain and suppress content distortion. Training optimizes adversarial, cycle-consistency, style-reconstruction, perceptual, and diversity objectives. Empirical results on multiple datasets show state-of-the-art fidelity and richer, exemplar-guided diversity compared with baselines.

title: Time-dependent electron transport through a strongly correlated quantum dot: multiple-probe open boundary conditions approach
text_ai: We present a time-dependent study of electron transport through a strongly correlated quantum dot. The time-dependent current is obtained with the multiple-probe battery method, while adiabatic lattice density functional theory in the Bethe ansatz local-density approximation to the Hubbard model describes the dot electronic structure. Steady-state currents and transient responses are analyzed as a function of bias, interaction strength, and dot-lead coupling. The dot spectrum is embedded in a self-consistent mean field updated on the same time scale as the MBP propagation, yielding dynamics that capture correlation-induced blockade and screening. We quantify accuracy by comparing the time-averaged current and occupation with benchmark results in limiting regimes and demonstrate that the multiple-probe boundary conditions correct spurious reflections and enable stable propagation. Our calculations reveal pronounced Coulomb blockade stairs in the current–voltage characteristics, with transient oscillations that decay on a timescale set by lead bandwidth and U. For strong coupling, we observe a nontrivial interplay between coherence and interaction, leading to delayed switching and hysteresis in parameter windows. The framework provides a versatile platform for exploring transient correlation phenomena in nanoscale devices.
prefix: We present a time-dependent study of electron transport through a strongly correlated quantum dot. The time-dependent current is obtained with the multiple-probe battery method, while adiabatic lattice density functional theory in the Bethe ansatz local-density approximation to the Hubbard model describes the dot electronic structure.

title: Bordetella biofilms: a lifestyle leading to persistent infections.
text_ai: Bordetella bronchiseptica and B. pertussis are Gram-negative bacteria that cause respiratory diseases in animals and humans. The current incidence of whooping cough or pertussis caused by B. pertussis has reached levels not observed since the 1950s. Although pertussis is traditionally known as an acute childhood disease, it has recently resurged in vaccinated adolescents and adults. Here, the capacity of Bordetella to adopt a biofilm lifestyle is framed as a major driver of persistence, relapse, and transmission. In the airway, B. bronchiseptica and B. pertussis form surface-attached communities that resist mucociliary clearance, embed within a self-produced matrix, and display phenotypic heterogeneity that buffers populations against antimicrobial pressures. Biofilm residency arises from coordinated regulation by the BvgAS two-component system and ancillary regulators that sense temperature, osmolarity, and nutrient limitation, triggering transitions between planktonic and sessile states. Matrix constituents, including exopolysaccharide and adhesins such as fimbriae, contribute to structural integrity and epithelial adhesion. In vivo models reveal localized biofilms on respiratory mucosa; clinical samples indicate persistent colonization despite vaccination. Therapeutic strategies that disrupt biofilms or promote clearance could reduce disease burden and transmission.
prefix: Bordetella bronchiseptica and B. pertussis are Gram-negative bacteria that cause respiratory diseases in animals and humans. title: The ileal FGF15/19 to hepatic FGFR4 axis regulates liver regeneration after partial hepatectomy in mice.
text_ai: Fibroblast growth factor (FGF) has been considered to modulate liver regeneration (LR) after partial hepatectomy (PH) at the tissue level. Previous studies have demonstrated that FGF15 and FGF19 induce the activation of its receptor, FGF receptor 4 (FGFR4), which can promote hepatocellular carcinoma progression and regulate liver lipid metabolism. To delineate the causal role of the ileal FGF15/19–FGFR4 axis in LR, we used mice with ileal FGF15 deficiency (Fgf15fl/fl; Villin-Cre) and hepatocyte FGFR4 deletion (Fgfr4fl/fl; Alb-Cre), together with pharmacologic FGFR4 blockade (BLU9931). Partial hepatectomy was performed, and regeneration was monitored by liver-to-body weight ratio, hepatocyte proliferation (Ki-67, PCNA), and cell-cycle regulators (Ccnd1, Ccne1, Birc5). Serum FGF15/19 and hepatic FGFR4 signaling readouts (p-ERK1/2, p-JNK) were quantified, and transcriptomics (RNA-seq) characterized proliferative and metabolic gene programs. Results showed that PH induced a surge of ileal FGF15 and circulating FGF15, which correlated with hepatic FGFR4 activation and a proliferative response. Loss of ileal FGF15 blunted FGFR4 signaling, reduced cyclin expression, and impaired LR, as evidenced by diminished liver mass restoration and lower Ki-67 labeling. FGFR4 blockade reproduced these deficits in control mice, whereas mice with intact FGFR4 signaling demonstrated efficient LR. Mechanistically, the axis promoted entry into S phase via ERK1/2-driven transcriptional programs and coordinated metabolic remodeling, including lipid-handling gene expression, without substantially increasing apoptosis. Conclusion: The ileal FGF15/19 to hepatic FGFR4 axis is necessary for optimal LR after PH in mice, revealing a gut-derived signal that couples intestinal nutrition with hepatic regeneration and identifying FGFR4 as a potential therapeutic target to enhance postoperative liver growth.

Previous studies have demonstrated that FGF15 and FGF19 induce the activation of its receptor, FGF receptor 4 (FGFR4), which can promote hepatocellular carcinoma progression and regulate liver lipid metabolism.

title: Impact of macronutrient supplements for children born preterm or small for gestational age on developmental and metabolic outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
text_ai: Nutritional supplements may improve development of infants born small (preterm or small for gestational age [SGA]) but may increase the risk of later metabolic disease. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the effects of macronutrient supplements for infants born small on later development and metabolism. We identified 21 randomized or quasi-randomized trials (n ≈ 1,813 infants) that compared macronutrient supplements with standard nutrition in those born preterm or SGA. Supplements included protein- enriched feeds, energy-dense formulations, and lipid- enriched regimens initiated in the neonatal period and continued for varying durations up to several months. Primary outcomes encompassed neurodevelopmental performance assessed at ≥18 months corrected age with standardized instruments (e.g., Bayley scales, WPPSI) and metabolic markers measured in early childhood (up to 5 years), including BMI or adiposity indices, fasting glucose and insulin, Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance (HOMA-IR), and lipid profiles. Secondary outcomes included growth parameters during infancy and adverse events. Risk of bias was evaluated with the RoB 2 tool; certainty of evidence was appraised using GRADE criteria. In meta-analysis, random-effects models were used to accommodate between-trial heterogeneity. Sensitivity analyses explored imputations for missing data, study design, and supplement type. Pre-specified subgroup analyses examined gestational category (<32 weeks vs 32–<37 weeks), SGA status, type of macronutrient augmentation (protein-enriched vs energy- dense vs lipid-enriched), and duration of supplementation. Results indicate that macronutrient supplementation modestly accelerated in-hospital weight gain, with a small improvement in weight-for-age z-scores at discharge (MD +0.28 z-score, 95% CI 0.12 to 0.44; I2 ≈ 56%). The effects on longer-term growth were variable, with several trials reporting higher BMI z-scores or adiposity indices at 2–5 years in supplemented children (pooled MD +0.15 z-score, 95% CI 0.03 to 0.27; I2 ≈ 42%). Neurodevelopmental outcomes showed no consistent, clinically meaningful advantage. Pooled analyses of cognitive development at 18–24 months corrected age yielded a standardized mean difference (SMD) near zero (SMD 0.09, 95% CI −0.02 to 0.20; I2 ≈ 40%), and motor and language domains displayed small, non-significant trends (SMDs ~0.10; 95% CIs crossing null). Taken together, evidence for durable neurodevelopmental benefit is limited. Metabolic outcomes in later childhood were heterogeneous. Fasting glucose differences were small and non-significant (MD 0.03 mmol/L, 95% CI −0.02 to 0.08), whereas fasting insulin (MD +2.7 mU/L, 95% CI 0.5 to 5.0) and HOMA-IR (MD +0.8 units, 95% CI 0.1 to 1.5) suggested a potential rise in insulin resistance risk in some analyses. Lipid profiles showed inconsistent patterns, with no uniform direction of effect. Across trials, adverse events did not differ significantly between groups (risk ratios for NEC, sepsis, or mortality generally null). Overall certainty of evidence ranged from low to moderate due to methodological limitations, heterogeneity in supplement formulations and durations, and imprecision in long-term outcomes. Our findings imply that macronutrient supplements in infancy can enhance early weight gain but yield uncertain and modest effects on subsequent neurodevelopment, while potentially altering later metabolic risk markers. Clinical decisions should balance the short-term growth advantages against uncertain long-term metabolic implications, until higher-quality, standardized trials with long-term follow-up clarify these relationships.

We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the effects of macronutrient supplements for infants born small on later development and metabolism.

title: Basal and stimulated calcitonin levels in patients with type 2 diabetes did not change during 1 year of Liraglutide treatment.
text_ai: The administration of Liraglutide, a long-acting GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonist, is associated with C-cell adenomas and carcinomas in rats. In humans, GLP-1R is highly expressed in C-cells hyperplasia (CCH) and in medullary thyroid cancer (MTC), though no changes in basal serum calcitonin (bCT) levels were recorded in type 2 diabetic (T2DM) patients treated with Liraglutide. Methods: In this prospective, single-center study, 68 adults with type 2 diabetes initiating liraglutide (0.6–1.8 mg/d) were followed for 12 months. Exclusion criteria included thyroid disease or prior C-cell pathology. Basal calcitonin (bCT) and stimulated calcitonin (sCT) after a standard calcium stimulation test (20 mL of 10% calcium gluconate IV) were measured at baseline, 6 and 12 months. Thyroid ultrasound was performed at baseline and 12 months. Linear mixed models adjusted for age, sex, BMI, eGFR, and smoking history assessed change over time. Results: Baseline mean age 59.1±8.5 years, 52% male, BMI 31.8±4.6 kg/m2. bCT was 6.0 (IQR 4.5–7.4) pg/mL at baseline, 6.1 (4.6–7.5) at 6 months, and 6.0 (4.7–7.3) at 12 months (p=0.74 for time). sCT peak after stimulation was 65–80 pg/mL across visits with no significant change (p=0.66). Neither ultrasound-defined C-cell lesions nor medullary thyroid cancer were detected. Results were consistent across subgroups stratified by sex, age (<60 vs ≥60) and renal function. Conclusion: One year of liraglutide therapy in adults with T2DM did not alter basal or calcium-stimulated calcitonin, suggesting no detectable liraglutide-induced C-cell activation in this timeframe. These findings support thyroid safety but longer follow-up and larger, diverse cohorts are required to fully exclude rare events.

title: Improving Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer via Progressive Code-Switching
text_ai: Code-switching is a data augmentation scheme mixing words from multiple languages into source lingual text. It has achieved considerable generalization performance of cross-lingual transfer tasks by aligning cross-lingual contextual word representations. However, uncontrolled and over-replaced code-switching would augment dirty samples to model training. To address this, we propose Progressive Code-Switching (PCS), a curriculum-guided augmentation that modulates the rate and granularity of language mixing across training steps. PCS starts from coherent monolingual inputs and incrementally substitutes tokens with translations from target language according to a learned schedule. The replacement probability is conditioned on word-level difficulty, lexical frequency, and alignment confidence, thereby reducing early-stage noise while promoting cross-lingual context exploration later. To preserve task-relevant semantics, we incorporate a lightweight consistency objective between original and code-switched outputs and constrain replacements to preserve key predicate structures. We validate PCS on zero-shot cross-lingual transfer across sentiment analysis, question answering, and named-entity recognition in language pairs. Our results show consistent gains over baselines and standard random augmentation, with larger margins for distant language pairs and low-resource settings. Ablation confirms the necessity of progressive scheduling and alignment-guided replacements.
prefix: Code-switching is a data augmentation scheme mixing words from multiple languages into source lingual text. It has achieved considerable generalization performance of cross-lingual transfer tasks by aligning cross-lingual contextual word representations. title: Searching for exotic object companions in the dense core of NGC 362: a multi-wavelength and multi-epoch photometric analysis
text_ai: The dense cores of globular clusters (GCs) are efficient environments for the production of exotic stellar populations, including millisecond pulsars (MSPs), low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs) and cataclysmic variables (CVs). Most of these objects likely form through two- and three-body interactions and are useful tracers of the cluster's dynamical evolution. By combining Chandra X-ray detections with multi-epoch HST optical/UV imaging and contemporaneous ground-based time-domain photometry, we identify plausible counterparts to X-ray sources and probe the full range of exotic-object companions in the core. Our astrometric tie and proper-motion cleaning yield cluster membership down to M_V ≈ 8, while PSF photometry delivers robust colors in the crowded center. We apply color–magnitude and color–color diagnostics, together with Hα narrowband excess, to separate CVs, quiescent LMXBs and MSP companions from the dense field. Variability analysis across six epochs over a decade reveals CV-like flickering and dwarf-nova–type outbursts, as well as ellipsoidal modulations and eclipses consistent with interacting binaries. For sources with both X-ray and optical/UV evidence, we compute X-ray–to–optical flux ratios and build spectral-energy distributions to guide classification. The resulting census shows a centrally concentrated population of interacting binaries, including several robust CV candidates and a handful of plausible MSP-companion systems. The spatial and dynamical properties align with formation through close encounters and exchange interactions in the dense core, in agreement with dynamical-model expectations for NGC 362. We provide a vetted catalog of counterparts and membership probabilities to enable spectroscopic confirmation and population synthesis in this cluster.
prefix: The dense cores of globular clusters (GCs) are efficient environments for the production of exotic stellar populations, including millisecond pulsars (MSPs), low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs) and cataclysmic variables (CVs). title: Exocomets in the Proxima Centauri system and their importance for water transport
text_ai: The scenario and efficiency of water transport by icy asteroids and comets are still amongst the most important unresolved questions of planetary systems. A better understanding of cometary dynamics in extrasolar systems shall provide information about cometary reservoirs and give an insight into water transport especially to planets in the habitable zone. To this end, we perform a parameter study with N-body integrations of a Proxima Centauri–like star hosting the inner planet Proxima b and an outer belt of icy planetesimals with varying radial extents (0.5–5 AU) and ice fractions. Particles are treated as massless test bodies and the simulations include stellar radiation pressure and Poynting–Robertson drag where appropriate, as well as general-relativistic precession for the inner zone. We quantify transport channels and define water delivery efficiency as the fraction of belt mass reaching perihelion within the habitable-zone boundary (≈0.05 AU). Our results show that, in configurations with a moderately massive belt (~0.01–0.05 Earth masses) and Proxima b alone, secular diffusion and weak resonances can inject a subset of bodies onto highly eccentric orbits, delivering material to the inner system on 10^7–10^8 yr timescales. The presence of additional outer planets amplifies the influx by stirring sources and creating resonant pathways, potentially increasing delivery efficiency by up to an order of magnitude in favorable alignments. Water transport remains stochastic, dominated by rare injections rather than steady flux, but can replenish surface volatiles during early system evolution. These findings support exocomet-driven water delivery to Proxima b. Further work should explore potential observables of exocomet activity in Proxima.
prefix: The scenario and efficiency of water transport by icy asteroids and comets are still amongst the most important unresolved questions of planetary systems. title: Device-Independent Bit Commitment based on the CHSH Inequality
text_ai: Bit commitment and coin flipping occupy a unique place in the device-independent landscape, as the only device-independent protocols thus far suggested for these tasks are reliant on tripartite GHZ correlations. Indeed, we know of no other bipartite tasks, which admit a device-independent formulation, but which are not known to be implementable using only bipartite nonlocality. Here we construct a device-independent bit-commitment protocol replacing tripartite GHZ resources by a bipartite nonlocal game, implemented with untrusted devices that interact locally with the committing party and the receiving party. The protocol comprises CHSH rounds to test nonlocality and generate a certifiable correlation that safeguards concealment, while the encoding of the committed bit is embedded in the choice of measurement settings and the subsequent reveal phase. We provide a composable security analysis under standard non-signalling and quantum-side-information assumptions, yielding explicit bounds on the cheating probabilities as a function of the observed CHSH violation and the round count. The binding condition is enforced by monogamy of nonlocal correlations, which constrains the adversary's simultaneous control over both channels. Our finite-statistics treatment yields practical parameter regimes for near-term realization.
prefix: Bit commitment and coin flipping occupy a unique place in the device-independent landscape, as the only device-independent protocols thus far suggested for these tasks are reliant on tripartite GHZ correlations. Indeed, we know of no other bipartite tasks, which admit a device-independent formulation, but which are not known to be implementable using only bipartite nonlocality.

title: Next generation testing strategy for assessment of genomic damage: A conceptual framework and considerations.
text_ai: For several decades, regulatory testing schemes for genetic damage have been standardized where the tests being utilized examined mutations and structural and numerical chromosomal damage. This has served the genetic toxicity community well when most of the substances being tested were amenable to such assays. Over the past decades, the genetic toxicity landscape has evolved with the emergence of high-content, high-resolution assays and systems biology approaches that enable interrogation of damage induction, persistence, and repair across molecular, cellular, and tissue contexts. These advances reveal that genomic insult is not a monolithic event but a cascade of mechanistically linked processes that may diverge in time, dose, and tissue. Classical assays—while foundational—rarely capture the full spectrum of damage, its kinetics, or its downstream biological significance, particularly for low-dose exposures, cumulative regimens, or agents requiring metabolic activation. In parallel, the recognition that genomic injury intersects with replication stress, chromatin dynamics, epigenetic remodeling, and genome instability across the life course argues for a reexamination of how we define, detect, and interpret genotoxic risk. The proposed framework therefore seeks to harmonize mechanistic insight with practical, decision-relevant information to inform risk assessment more robustly and ethically. We propose a next-generation testing strategy that is tiered, modular, and mechanism-informed, anchored in adverse outcome pathway concepts and supported by a flexible data integration platform. This strategy emphasizes three interdependent components: (i) a mechanistic map of genomic damage and repair processes that links molecular initiating events to intermediate biomarkers and to adverse outcomes; (ii) a suite of complementary readouts spanning in silico predictions, in vitro and ex vivo assays, and, where appropriate, in vivo or organotypic models; and (iii) an evidence integration and decision framework that explicitly characterizes uncertainty, variability, and context of use, including exposure scenarios and metabolic capacity. The framework is designed to accommodate the heterogeneity of substances encountered in regulatory contexts—from substances with straightforward metabolic activation profiles to complex mixtures and xenobiotics with multiple modes of action. In the mechanistic map, we place DNA damage induction, replication stress, and chromatin misregulation as central nodes, with downstream consequences such as mutational spectra, chromosomal rearrangements, numerical and structural chromosomal abnormalities, and genome instability. Reparation pathways (base excision repair, homologous recombination, non-homologous end joining, and their regulation by cell cycle and chromatin state) become essential interpretive anchors, as do damage-response signaling programs (e.g., ATM/ATR, p53, and downstream transcriptional networks). By integrating these processes with tissue- and cell-type–specific susceptibilities, the framework accommodates context-dependent risk and supports extrapolation across exposure routes and species to the extent justified by evidence. The testing architecture comprises multiple tiers designed for fit-for-purpose application. Tier 0 emphasizes in silico screening, including structure-activity relationships and mechanistic plausibility assessments, to prioritize chemicals and identify potential red flags. Tier 1 comprises high-throughput in vitro assays that interrogate core events such as DNA strand breaks, replication fork dynamics, and early damage signaling, leveraging miniaturized and multiplexed readouts. Tier 2 expands to more mechanistic in vitro and ex vivo systems that capture metabolic activation, chromatin context, and cell-type–specific responses, including high-content imaging, single-cell analyses, and targeted omics readouts. Tier 3 integrates organoid, tissue-on-a-chip, or in vivo systems where necessary to address physiological complexity, pharmacokinetics, and long-term consequences; the selection of Tier 3 approaches would be guided by the weight of evidence, feasibility, and ethical considerations aligned with 3Rs principles. Tier 4 remains the post-market or post-licensing surveillance layer, wherein ongoing real-world data, pharmacoepidemiology, and computational surveillance support continuous risk refinement. A core feature of the framework is the deployment of mechanistically informative endpoints beyond traditional mutation frequency and chromosomal aberration counts. These include (but are not limited to) markers of replication stress (e.g., replication fork progression, RPA foci dynamics), double-strand break repair activity (γH2AX, 53BP1 foci, RAD51 engagement), and chromatin and epigenetic alterations (histone modification patterns, chromatin accessibility changes, and DNA methylation/epigenomic signatures). In parallel, non-targeted and targeted omics readouts—transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and epigenomics—provide integrative fingerprints of cellular state and repair pathway engagement. Single-cell resolution adds a further layer, capturing heterogeneity in responses and enabling the identification of subpopulations at greater risk of persistent damage or misrepair. Data integration is implemented through a formal, quantitative decision framework that blends bioinformatic pipelines, mechanistic modelling, and quantitative risk assessment. A structured evidence appraisal guides the weighting, combination, and interpretation of endpoints across tiers, with explicit treatment of uncertainties arising from assay limitations, model assumptions, and inter-individual variability. Dose–response characterizations employ flexible modelling approaches—such as benchmark dose concepts and Bayesian hierarchical models—to accommodate diverse data streams and to facilitate extrapolation within and across species, tissues, and exposure modalities. The framework also anticipates mixtures and sequential exposures by incorporating interaction effects and time-dependent dynamics, thereby improving extrapolation to real-world scenarios. Regulatory acceptance and practical implementation require explicit alignment with validation, standardization, and governance principles. We advocate a fit-for-purpose validation strategy that emphasizes mechanistic relevance, consistency across laboratories, robust QA/QC, and clear criteria for decision-making at each tier. Standardization of endpoints, data formats, and reporting conventions will enable comparability and reanalysis, supporting meta-analyses and cross-study synthesis. The framework also embraces transparency and data-sharing, encouraging open repositories for multi-omics and imaging data, along with ontologies that harmonize endpoint definitions and interpretations across jurisdictions. Ethical, logistical, and economic considerations are integrated from the outset. By reducing reliance on traditional whole-animal testing while maintaining or enhancing predictive accuracy for human risk, the strategy aligns with the 3Rs and accelerates the availability of safer substances. The modular design permits incremental adoption by regulators and industry, enabling continuity with existing regulatory expectations while offering a clear pathway toward enhanced information content and mechanistic understanding. Together, the proposed next-generation framework provides a coherent, scalable, and scientifically grounded approach to assessing genomic damage that reflects contemporary knowledge of DNA repair, chromatin biology, and systems-level biology. It offers a practical road map for integrating novel endpoints with established readouts, balancing ambition with feasibility, and delivering decision-ready evidence that is transparent, reproducible, and relevant to diverse regulatory contexts. By foregrounding mechanistic interpretation, contextual exposure assessment, and rigorous uncertainty characterizations, this framework aspires to advance genomic damage assessment to a level commensurate with modern toxicology and public health needs.

title: On T-Duality and Integrability for Strings on AdS Backgrounds
text_ai: We discuss an interplay between T-duality and integrability for certain classical non-linear sigma models. In particular, we consider strings on the AdS_5 x S^5 background and perform T-duality along the four isometry directions of AdS_5 in the Poincare patch. The T-dual of the AdS_5 sigma model is again a sigma model on an AdS_5 space. We show that the T-dual model preserves classical integrability: a Lax connection with the same zero-curvature equation exists after the Buscher-like transformation along the AdS5 isometries. The duality acts as a canonical transformation on the phase space and induces a map between the conserved nonlocal charges, with monodromy matrices related by a gauge transformation. In the bosonic truncation the dual coordinates describe AdS5 again and the Z4-graded current algebra is carried over to the dual frame. We present the dual action in coset form and verify the persistence of the flatness condition for the full classical dynamics. These results extend to the full AdS5 x S5 supercoset with appropriate fermionic T-duality, suggesting a broader network of dual descriptions for string dynamics on AdS backgrounds.

The T-dual of the AdS_5 sigma model is again a sigma model on an AdS_5 space.

title: Evaluating QoS Parameters for IPTV Distribution in Heterogeneous Networks
text_ai: The present work presents an architecture developed to evaluate the QoS parameters for the IPTV heterogeneous network. At its very basic level lie two software technologies: Video LAN and Windows Media Services with two operating systems: Windows and Linux. An architecture consisting of modular components enables controlled experimentation across heterogeneous networks, including local multicast domains, campus LAN/WAN links, and wireless access segments. The evaluation framework integrates Video LAN and Windows Media Services on Windows and Linux to ensure cross‑platform interoperability. A measurement layer combines passive monitoring with active traffic generation; emulation tools impose configurable delay, jitter, and loss, while DiffServ-based QoS policies simulate priority handling. IPTV streams are captured at edge and host points, recording end‑to‑end latency, startup delay, playout buffer underruns, and channel-switch times. Video quality is evaluated with objective measures (PSNR/SSIM) supplemented by a MOS proxy. Results demonstrate the framework’s ability to expose QoS–quality tradeoffs under varying load and terminal conditions, informing scheduling, buffering, and transcoding strategies and providing a reproducible basis for cross‑platform IPTV QoS assessment. The approach supports comparative studies and scalable evaluations.

title: Twin-width and types
text_ai: We study problems connected to first-order logic in graphs of bounded twin-width. Inspired by the approach of Bonnet et al. [FOCS 2020], we introduce a robust methodology of local types and describe their behavior in contraction sequences -- the decomposition notion underlying twin-width. We develop a unified, type-centric view of the contraction process. For each step along a given d-width contraction sequence, we assign to every vertex a bounded-size local type that records all FO-equivalences visible across the cut induced by the already processed part. The r-local type (for a fixed quantifier rank r) captures the full information that any FO formula of rank at most r could distinguish about the vertex’s neighborhood relative to the past, while remaining oblivious to details that are FO-indistinguishable. We prove that, for fixed d and r, the set of possible r-local types is finite and depends only on d and r, not on the size of the graph. Moreover, after each contraction, only the two merged vertices and their incident relations may affect a bounded number of local types; all other vertices retain their previously assigned types. This yields a robust, compositional semantics: the global FO-type of the graph can be assembled from the multiset of local types along the traversal of the sequence. From this, we derive an automaton-based model of FO evaluation. There exists a finite-state transducer, depending only on d and the formula φ (more precisely on its quantifier rank), that processes the contraction sequence from bottom to top and outputs the truth value of φ on the final graph. Consequently, FO model checking on graphs of bounded twin-width, when a d-width contraction sequence is provided, is fixed-parameter tractable with respect to the formula size; in particular, linear-time in the graph size for fixed d and φ. We further show that the method extends to counting quantifiers and to a broad class of FO-definable transductions, enabling uniform meta-algorithmic conclusions for dense and sparse variants within bounded twin-width. This local-type framework thus yields a canonical, decomposition-based explanation of FO definability in twin-width and furnishes practical, implementable model-checking routines.

title: A brain proteomic investigation of rapamycin effects in the Tsc1+/- mouse model.
text_ai: Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) is a rare monogenic disorder characterized by benign tumors in multiple organs as well as a high prevalence of epilepsy, intellectual disability and autism. TSC is caused by inactivating mutations in the TSC1 or TSC2 genes. Rapamycin-dependent normalization of mTOR signaling was accompanied by widespread but heterogeneous shifts in the brain proteome, revealing both convergent and region-specific mechanisms that underlie the therapeutic effects in Tsc1 haploinsufficiency. We conducted quantitative, label-free proteomics on cortical, hippocampal, and cerebellar tissue from wild-type and Tsc1+/− mice, with and without rapamycin exposure during a defined developmental window. Differential expression analyses identified a core set of proteins dysregulated by Tsc1 haploinsufficiency across regions, enriched for components of translational control, synaptic architecture, cytoskeletal dynamics, and energy metabolism. Notably, ribosomal proteins, translation initiation factors, and regulators of protein turnover were upregulated in the Tsc1+/− brain, consistent with heightened mTOR-driven anabolic activity, while markers of autophagy and lysosomal function were diminished, aligning with impaired catabolic flux. Region-specific effects were evident, with the hippocampus exhibiting the most pronounced perturbations in synaptic protein networks, whereas the cortex showed greater dysregulation of mitochondrial and metabolic pathways. Rapamycin treatment produced a robust, but incomplete, reversion of these proteomic alterations. Across regions, we observed significant downregulation of ribosomal machinery and translation regulators toward wild-type levels, accompanied by increased abundance of autophagy-lysosome–associated proteins, including lysosomal hydrolases and autophagy adaptors. These changes correlated with reduced phosphorylation of canonical mTOR targets and a partial restoration of proteostasis. However, a subset of Tsc1+/−–altered proteins remained resistant to rapamycin, delineating a persistent proteomic residue that may underlie residual behavioral or synaptic phenotypes. The rapamycin-responsive module encompassed proteins implicated in synaptic vesicle cycling, cytoskeletal remodeling, and energy supply, suggesting coordinated normalization of neuronal signaling and structural integrity. Conversely, rapamycin-insensitive modules highlighted sustained alterations in cytoskeletal regulators and mitochondria-associated proteins, implying divergent regulation of biogenesis and organellar quality control independent of acute mTOR suppression. Integrative network analyses revealed that rapamycin effectively reconnected disrupted protein–protein interaction communities centered on translation control, autophagy, and synaptic function, reinforcing the mechanistic link between mTOR suppression and proteome stabilization. Pathway enrichment highlighted attenuated ribosome biogenesis, restored lysosomal degradation, and moderated actin- and microtubule-based motility as key axes of rescue. Collectively, our brain-wide proteomic atlas demonstrates that rapamycin exerts regionally nuanced corrections of Tsc1+/−–driven dysproteostasis, identifies candidate biomarkers of response, and clarifies molecular pathways warranting consideration in dose optimization and combinatorial strategies for TSC-related neurodevelopmental phenotypes.

title: The role of T-helper/T-suppressor ratio in the adaptive immune response: a dynamical model
text_ai: Recent experimental studies have suggested the ratio between T-helper and T-suppressor lymphocytes as an index of immunosuppression in HIV, cancer, immunosenescence and inflammatory and auto-immune diseases. However, a quantitative understanding of the impact of this ratio on the immune response has lagged behind data and its validity as a tool for prognostic monitoring or therapeutic target remains an open question. Here, we formalize a minimal yet mechanistically grounded dynamical model in which helper (Th) and suppressor (Ts) lymphocytes regulate clonal expansion and effector differentiation of antigen-specific T cells. The model couples Th and Ts populations through activation, proliferation, and regulatory feedback mediated by cytokines and immune checkpoints. We show that the Th/Ts ratio acts as a control parameter shaping the amplitude, duration, and breadth of the adaptive response, with regime shifts producing either robust clearance or chronic activation. Through analytic and numerical bifurcation analysis, we identify thresholds for switch-like transitions in effector output and for the onset of immunosuppression. Parameter sweeps reveal non-monotonic dependence on initial ratio and total T-cell pool, consistent with clinical heterogeneity across diseases.

title: Performance evaluation of a new route optimization technique for mobile IP
text_ai: Mobile ip (mip) is an internet protocol that allows mobile nodes to have continuous network connectivity to the internet without changing their ip addresses while moving to other networks. The packets sent from correspondent node (cn) to a mobile node (mn) go first through the mobile node's home agent (ha), then the ha tunnels them to the mn's foreign network. This paper proposes a novel route optimization technique that allows the correspondent node to route traffic directly to the mobile node when feasible, by updating a lightweight binding cache at CN. The approach extends conventional MIP by introducing hop-by-hop validation, selective tunneling, and on-demand binding updates to reduce triangular routing while preserving the binding security. When a valid binding exists and the CN can reach MN via a path, subsequent packets bypass the HA tunnel and follow the direct path via MN’s care-of address, with the HA acting mainly as registrar and security proxy. An adaptive policy governs activation to prevent instability during topology changes. The design remains compatible with standard MIPv6 and HMIPv6 as a drop-in extension. We evaluated the technique using discrete-event simulations in ns-3 under realistic mobility traces and traffic loads, comparing against baseline MIP route optimization. Metrics include end-to-end latency, path length, handover interruption time, signaling overhead, and MN energy consumption. Results show significant latency and tunnel-overhead reductions, with modest binding-update increases; improvements are more pronounced at moderate mobility and in networks with lower path diversity. This demonstrates robustness.

title: Amorphous SiO2 nanoparticles promote cardiac dysfunction via the opening of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore in rat heart and human cardiomyocytes.
text_ai: Silica nanoparticles (nanoSiO 2 ) are promising systems that can deliver biologically active compounds to tissues such as the heart in a controllable manner. However, cardiac toxicity induced by nanoSiO 2 has been recently related to abnormal calcium handling and energetic failure in cardiomyocytes. Moreover, the precise mechanisms underlying this energetic debacle remain unclear. Here, we evaluated whether nanoSiO2 drive energetic collapse via opening the mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) in the intact heart and human cardiomyocytes. In vivo–like experiments were conducted in isolated rat hearts (Langendorff perfusion) exposed to escalating nanoscale silica suspensions, and complementary studies were performed in human cardiomyocytes derived from induced pluripotent stem cells. Across models, nanoSiO2 promoted a rapid disruption of mitochondrial homeostasis, as evidenced by a decrease in mitochondrial membrane potential (Δψm), enhanced calcium overload, and accelerated mitochondrial swelling. These mitochondrial derangements preceded, and paralleled, a burst of reactive oxygen species production and a marked fall in cellular and mitochondrial ATP content, consistent with energetic collapse. Calcium retention capacity assays and pharmacological interrogation indicated that the observed mitochondrial dysfunction was mediated by mPTP opening, with substantial sensitization to calcium and oxidant stress. The involvement of cyclophilin D was supported by protection with cyclosporin A and sanglifehrin A, which markedly attenuated Δψm dissipation, cytochrome c release, and ATP depletion, and restored mitochondrial respiration and contractile performance. In the Langendorff heart preparations, nanoSiO2 exposure reduced developed force, lowered heart rate–corrected contractility, and diminished rate-pressure product, effects that were substantially reversed by mPTP blockade. In hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes, nanoSiO2 caused irregular beat patterns, reduced contraction amplitude, and shortened calcium transient decay times, all of which were mitigated by mPTP inhibitors. Mechanistic analyses revealed that nanoSiO2–induced mPTP opening was preceded by mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake and oxidative challenge, with subsequent release of pro-apoptotic factors and impaired oxidative phosphorylation. Notably, these effects were dose- and time-dependent and were more pronounced in conditions where basal antioxidant defenses were compromised. Importantly, CsA pre-treatment not only preserved Δψm and ATP production but also maintained contractile function and spontaneous calcium handling in both models, confirming the causal role of mPTP opening in nanoSiO2-induced cardiotoxicity. These data identify amorphous SiO2 nanoparticles as potent activators of the mPTP-driven pathway of mitochondrial energetic failure, linking nanoparticle exposure to cardiac dysfunction in rat heart and human cardiomyocytes, and position the mPTP as a therapeutic target to mitigate nanoparticle-associated cardiotoxicity.

title: Treatment of pediatric vesicoureteral reflux using endoscopic injection of hyaluronic acid/dextranomer gel: intermediate-term experience by a single surgeon
text_ai: OBJECTIVES: Endoscopic injection of non-animal-stabilized hyaluronic acid/dextranomer gel is an increasingly recognized treatment option for vesicoureteral reflux. The procedure is minor compared with open surgery and, when successful, avoids the need for long-term antibiotic prophylaxis. We present data from 3 years of using non-animal-stabilized hyaluronic acid/dextranomer gel to treat children with vesicoureteral reflux. METHODS: A retrospective review was performed of all pediatric patients treated for vesicoureteral reflux with non-animal-stabilized hyaluronic acid/dextranomer gel (Deflux) by a single surgeon from 2006 through 2009. Indications included vesicoureteral reflux grades II–IV with febrile urinary tract infections or breakthrough infections despite prophylaxis. Preoperative evaluation comprised renal/bladder ultrasonography, voiding cystourethrogram (VCUG), and selective DMSA scanning. Injections were delivered transurethrally using the STING technique, with up to three injections per ureter as needed. Follow-up included clinical assessment and repeat VCUG at 3–12 months; outcomes were assessed for radiographic resolution or downgrading of reflux, need for additional injections or ureteral reimplantation, and procedure-related complications. RESULTS: A cohort of 34 children (52 ureters) with mean age in early school years and female predominance underwent Deflux injections. Median follow-up extended to 24 months. Durable resolution or downgrade to grade I–II reflux was achieved in the majority of treated ureters after the initial injection. Approximately one third of ureters required a second injection for persistent reflux, and a small subset ultimately underwent open ureteral reimplantation for ongoing high-grade reflux or recurrent febrile UTIs. Antimicrobial prophylaxis was discontinued in patients with durable radiographic improvement. Perioperative complications were uncommon and limited to transient dysuria, low-grade fever, and self-limited hematuria; no serious adverse events, ureteral obstruction, or decline in renal function were observed during follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: Endoscopic injection of hyaluronic acid/dextranomer gel provides a safe, effective intermediate-term approach for pediatric vesicoureteral reflux when performed by an experienced surgeon, with high rates of reflux resolution/downgrading and a favorable safety profile, reducing reliance on long-term antibiotic prophylaxis. Further multicenter, long-term studies are needed to define durability and identify predictors of success.

We present data from 3 years of using non-animal-stabilized hyaluronic acid/dextranomer gel to treat children with vesicoureteral reflux.

title: An invariant joint alternative, by frames, to Einstein and Schroedinger equations
text_ai: The Hodge-de Rham Laplacean is an extension to forms of the wave equation. A frame is a quartuple of 1-forms. The Hodge-de Rham Laplacean is modified to model it on the frame itself (not on the standard frame $dx$). This modified Laplacean is invariant. An invariant joint system is constructed by promoting the metric to a frame field e = (e^0,e^1,e^2,e^3) and formulating dynamics with a frame-covariant Hodge–de Rham Laplacian Δ_e built from e and its connection. The resulting field equations couple Δ_e acting on frame-valued 1-forms to a matter sector carried by a covariantly constant spinor ψ, yielding a nonlinear, diffeomorphism-invariant pair that generalizes both Einstein gravity and a Schrödinger-type dynamics. A frame-invariant action is offered, from which a conserved, frame-covariant stress-energy current follows. In the weak-field, slow-velocity limit, the leading order reproduces Einstein’s equations with a source given by ψψ†, while a Born-like Schrödinger equation emerges for ψ in regimes where geometric effects are subdominant. The construction provides an invariant, frame-based alternative to standard formulations, with well-posedness discussed for representative backgrounds. Numerical demonstrations on backgrounds illustrate consistency.

title: Long-segment posterior cervical decompression and fusion: does caudal level affect revision rate?
text_ai: Posterior cervical decompression and fusion (PCDF) is a commonly performed procedure to address cervical myelopathy. A significant number of these patients require revision surgery for adjacent-segment disease (ASD) or pseudarthrosis. Currently, there is no consensus among spine surgeons on the inclusion of proximal thoracic spine instrumentation. We performed a multicenter retrospective review of consecutive adults undergoing long-segment PCDF (≥4 levels) from 2005–2023, with caudal instrumentation ending at either the cervicothoracic junction (CTJ; typically C7–T1) or the upper thoracic spine (T2–T3). Exclusion criteria included acute trauma, infection, tumor, prior fusion spanning the study levels. Primary outcome was revision surgery for adjacent-segment disease (ASD) or pseudarthrosis. Secondary outcomes included radiographic fusion, segmental and global sagittal balance, and perioperative complications. Data on demographics, smoking, osteoporosis, number of levels fused, and use of supplemental posterior fixation were collected. Fusion was defined radiographically by continuity of present bridging trabeculae across the intended construct at follow-up ≥12 months. Survival analysis with revision-free curves was performed; multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, comorbidity index, smoking, osteoporosis, and levels fused. Results: Among 312 cases, 159 terminated at the CTJ and 153 extended to the upper thoracic spine. ASD/pseudarthrosis revisions occurred in 21/159 (13.2%) vs 9/153 (5.9%), respectively (P=0.02). Four-year revision-free survival was 76% for CTJ and 88% for upper thoracic constructs (log-rank P=0.01). On multivariable analysis, CTJ ending remained associated with higher revision hazard (HR 1.95, 95% CI 1.12–3.41, P=0.02). Fusion rates favored the upper thoracic group (92% vs 82%, P=0.04). Complication rates did not differ significantly. These data suggest that extending caudal instrumentation to the upper thoracic spine in long-segment PCDF lowers revision risk for ASD/pseudarthrosis, with acceptable perioperative risk.

title: Reflection on young adult transitional care in the boston children's hospital perioperative care coordination clinic.
text_ai: The complexity of pediatric healthcare has increased due to advancement in research and identification of new treatment modalities. With these advancements, life expectancy has increased creating a greater need for young adult transition into adult medical settings and specialty care (Marani et al., 2020). Building on a growing body of transition research, this reflection analyzes the perioperative care coordination clinic as a nexus where pediatric and adult care imaginaries converge. Methods included a thematic synthesis of clinician narratives, patient and family journey maps, and audit of preoperative workflows over 12 months. Findings reveal core tensions: preserving family-centered support while promoting patient agency, ensuring accurate medication reconciliation across age-related formularies, and harmonizing perioperative risk assessment with evolving care plans as patients mature. Clinicians described variable readiness for self-management, gaps in health literacy, and friction between pediatric safety nets and adult-system expectations. In response, the clinic implemented structured transition events, including joint preoperative consultations, standardized transfer communications, and a shared electronic handoff template. Education for patients and families emphasized autonomy in consent, postoperative expectations, and resource navigation. Early indicators point to improved completion of preoperative instructions, fewer medication discrepancies, and greater satisfaction with the coordination of care, though causal inferences remain limited. The reflection concludes that deliberate, developmentally appropriate transition strategies within perioperative settings are essential to mitigate fragmentation and adverse events. Recommendations include scalable handoff protocols, alignment of insurance and specialty access, and further mixed-methods inquiry into long-term outcomes and equity across diverse populations.

title: Return to Play After Multiligament Knee Injuries in National Football League Athletes.
text_ai: Return to play (RTP) of National Football League (NFL) athletes after isolated anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tears has been reported. However, no studies have reported on RTP of NFL athletes after multiligament knee injuries. NFL athletes with multiligament knee injuries have lower RTP rates and longer recoveries than athletes with isolated ACL tears. Methods: Retrospective cohort of NFL players sustaining multiligament knee injuries requiring operative reconstruction from 2005–2023, identified through publicly available injury reports, team announcements, and NFL data sources. Multiligament knee injury (MKI) was defined as disruption of at least two major knee ligaments (eg, ACL with PCL, LCL, or MCL) with documented surgical treatment. Excluded were isolated meniscal injuries, chondral injuries without ligament disruption, and nonoperative management. Primary outcome: return to NFL competition (RTP). Secondary outcomes included time to RTP (months), return to preinjury level (games started/played relative to baseline), post‑RTP durability (career length after RTP), and performance metrics (games, starts, approximate value). A contemporaneous control cohort consisted of NFL players with isolated ACL injuries identified in the same period. Controls were matched in a 2:1 ratio on age, position, and era. Analyses included Kaplan–Meier estimation of time to RTP, log‑rank tests for comparison, and Cox proportional hazards models to identify predictors of RTP. Secondary analyses compared postinjury performance with matched ACL controls, using appropriate regression techniques and sensitivity analyses to account for era and position effects. Significance was set at p<0.05. Results: Thirty‑two MKI cases were identified; 15 players (47%) returned to NFL play. Median time to RTP among returnees was 13.8 months (IQR 11.0–16.5). Among returnees, post‑RTP workload in the first season represented 42% of preinjury level (games started and played). Recurrent knee injuries occurred in 3 returnees (20%). The ACL‑only control cohort (n=64) demonstrated higher RTP (83%) and shorter time to RTP (median 9.2 months). After adjustment for position, era, and baseline performance, MKI status independently predicted lower probability of RTP (HR 0.38; 95% CI 0.22–0.67; p=0.001) and longer time to RTP by ~4 months (p=0.003). Among those returning, postinjury performance did not differ significantly from matched ACL controls. Durability analyses showed a shorter post‑RTP career length for the MKI group compared with controls, driven primarily by reduced early workload and increased susceptibility to reinjury. Conclusions: Multiligament knee injuries in NFL athletes substantially diminish RTP rates and prolong recovery relative to isolated ACL injuries, with lower odds of returning to preinjury level play and reduced early post‑RTP workload. When return occurs, performance trajectory may approximate that of ACL‑injured peers, underscoring the importance of individualized rehabilitation and cautious RTP decision‑making. These findings highlight the need for ongoing advances in surgical techniques, graft selection, and rehabilitation protocols to optimize outcomes in this high‑demand population.

NFL athletes with multiligament knee injuries have lower RTP rates and longer recoveries than athletes with isolated ACL tears.

title: Duration of antibody response following vaccination against feline immunodeficiency virus.
text_ai: Objectives Recently, two point-of-care (PoC) feline immunodeficiency virus (FIV) antibody test kits (Witness and Anigen Rapid) were reported as being able to differentiate FIV-vaccinated from FIV-infected cats at a single time point, irrespective of the gap between testing and last vaccination (0-7 years). Methods A multicenter, cross-sectional study was conducted to quantify the duration of vaccine-induced FIV antibodies and to assess the ability of two PoC antibody tests to differentiate vaccination from infection over a 0–7-year interval after vaccination. Cats with documented FIV vaccination history (n = 120) and cats with laboratory-confirmed FIV infection (n = 80) were recruited from 12 veterinary clinics. Vaccinated cats were stratified by time since last vaccination: 0–1 year (n = 40), 1–3 years (n = 30), 3–5 years (n = 25), and 5–7 years (n = 25). All animals underwent testing with Witness FIV Antibody Test and Anigen Rapid FIV Antibody Test, performed according to manufacturers’ protocols by blinded operators. FIV infection status was independently determined by directed PCR for FIV proviral DNA (pol region) on whole blood, serving as the reference standard. A conventional anti-FIV p24 ELISA was used to quantify antibody titres as a secondary reference, enabling comparison of quantitative antibody levels with qualitative PoC results. Data were analyzed to determine sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values of each PoC test for identifying vaccination status versus infection, stratified by time since vaccination; receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and area under the curve (AUC) were computed to assess discrimination. Logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, and breed were used to evaluate whether combining PoC results with ELISA titres improved discrimination. A subset of vaccinated cats (n = 40) with serial samples over time was analyzed to describe antibody trajectory. Results The proportion of vaccinated cats with a positive PoC result declined with time since vaccination. Witness yielded positive results in 38/40 (95%) of 0–1 year, 22/30 (73%) of 1–3 years, 12/25 (48%) of 3–5 years, and 7/25 (28%) of 5–7 years post-vaccination. Anigen Rapid yielded positive results in 37/40 (93%) 0–1 year, 21/30 (70%) 1–3 years, 11/25 (44%) 3–5 years, and 6/25 (24%) 5–7 years post-vaccination. Among PCR-confirmed infected cats, PoC test positivity remained high across intervals (Witness 34/40, 85%; Anigen Rapid 36/40, 90% in acute and chronic subgroups), with no consistent, time-dependent decline evident. Specificity for distinguishing vaccination from infection using either PoC test alone remained poor across intervals (AUCs: Witness 0.59; Anigen Rapid 0.60). The combination of test results did not meaningfully improve discrimination (AUC ≈ 0.61). Quantitative anti-FIV antibody titres by ELISA were significantly higher in infected cats than in vaccinated cats across all intervals (P < 0.01) and exhibited a gradual decline in vaccinated cats with increasing time since vaccination, consistent with waning vaccine-induced antibodies. In the serial-sampling subset, vaccine-induced titres waned over approximately 4–5 years, with some rebound following reported booster vaccination, but remained detectable in a minority beyond 5 years. Conclusions The evaluated PoC antibody tests do not reliably differentiate FIV-vaccinated from FIV-infected cats across the full 0–7-year window after vaccination. Although ELISA titres were consistently higher in infected cats and waned over time after vaccination, the overlap in PoC results between groups limits clinical utility for DIVA purposes. These findings underscore the continued need for DIVA-capable diagnostics or alternative strategies (e.g., vaccination records, molecular testing) to distinguish infection from vaccination in feline patients.
