title: On the thermal sunset diagram for scalar field theories
text_ai: We study the so-called `` sunset diagram'', which is one of two-loop self-energy diagrams, for scalar field theories at finite temperature. For this purpose, we first find the complete expression of the bubble diagram, the one-loop subdiagram of the sunset diagram, for arbitrary momentum. Employing the imaginary-time formalism, we perform the Matsubara sums and carry out the analytic continuation to real energies to obtain the bubble B_R(p0, p; T). The result is organized into a vacuum part, a single-thermal contribution, and a double-thermal contribution, each admitting a representation in terms of one-dimensional integrals over on-shell energies. After Feynman parameterization and momentum integrations, ultraviolet divergences are isolated and subtracted in dimensional regularization with MS-bar scheme, yielding a renormalized bubble at arbitrary external momentum and temperature. We validate the construction by reproducing known limits: the zero-temperature vacuum bubble, the high-temperature expansion, and the threshold behavior at p^2 = (m1+m2)^2. The thermal pieces satisfy the KMS relations and exhibit the correct analytic structure required for a consistent two-loop self-energy. With this ingredient in hand, we assemble the full sunset self-energy by convolving the renormalized bubble with the third propagator. We discuss the numerical implementation and report on the stability of the representation across parameter space, including small and large masses, and timelike and spacelike momenta. These results provide a usable, finite expression for the sunset diagram at temperature, enabling thorough exploration of spectral densities, dispersion relations, potential resummation schemes in scalar theories.

title: Upregulation of lactate dehydrogenase A in a chronic model of temporal lobe epilepsy.
text_ai: The ketogenic diet treatment is effective for drug-resistant epilepsy. Because its antiepileptic effect is associated with lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), drug development is possible by targeting LDH enzymes. Seizures in rodent models are suppressed by inhibiting LDH; however, it remains unclear whether LDH in the brain is changed by seizures. Using a well-established rodent model of chronic temporal lobe epilepsy induced by kainic acid, we examined LDHA expression in the hippocampus during the chronic phase. Western blot and qRT-PCR showed a robust upregulation of LDHA protein and mRNA in epileptic versus control tissue (p<0.01), with LDHB unchanged. Immunohistochemistry localized LDHA primarily to astrocytes in the dentate gyrus and CA1, CA3 regions, with sparse neuronal labeling. Enzymatic assays confirmed increased LDH activity skewed toward the LDH-A isoform, and extracellular lactate was elevated in epileptic hippocampus. Notably, LDHA levels correlated with seizure frequency and interictal spike burden across animals. These findings indicate that LDHA upregulation accompanies chronic TLE and implicate astrocyte-driven lactate production as a contributor to hyperexcitability, thereby presenting LDH-A as a potential metabolic therapeutic target.

title: Lateral brow lift: A multi-point suture fixation technique
text_ai: Background Descent of the lateral aspect of the brow is one of the earliest signs of aging. The purpose of this study was to describe an open surgical technique for lateral brow lifts, with the goal of achieving reliable, predictable, and long-lasting results. Methods A prospective, single‑institution cohort of 52 patients undergoing open lateral brow lift with a multi‑point suture fixation technique between 2010 and 2023. Inclusion criteria included lateral brow descent ≥2 mm on standardized photographs; exclusion criteria were prior brow surgery, active infection, or uncontrolled systemic disease. Under local anesthesia with sedation or general anesthesia, a limited pre‑temporal incision was used. Subperiosteal dissection along the lateral orbital rim released brow attachments while preserving the temporal branch of the facial nerve. Four to six nonabsorbable sutures were placed at fixed points from the brow to stable periosteal and frontotemporal fascia, creating an arc that elevates the lateral brow. Skin was closed in layers; incisions were concealed in the hairline. Postoperative care included ice, head elevation, and avoidance of aggressive forehead movement; follow‑up was at 1 week, 1 month, and 6–24 months. Results Median follow‑up was 14 months. Mean preoperative brow height increased by 3.1 mm immediately post‑op and remained 2.7 mm above baseline at final follow‑up (p<0.001). Lateral brow position was maintained in 86% of patients. Patient satisfaction (5‑point scale) averaged 4.6. Complications were mild and infrequent: transient frontal branch numbness in 4 patients (7.7%), minor hematoma in 2 (3.8%), superficial wound dehiscence in 1 (1.9%). No permanent nerve injury or brow malposition; reoperation for undercorrection occurred in 2 cases (3.8%). Conclusion The multi‑point suture fixation technique yields reliable, durable lateral brow elevation via a minimal open approach with a favorable safety profile, maintaining brow function and offering predictable contours suitable for adjunct facial rejuvenation procedures.

title: Histologic Findings of a Human Immature Revascularized/Regenerated Tooth with Symptomatic Irreversible Pulpitis.
text_ai: Pulp revascularization/regeneration in immature permanent teeth with necrotic pulp and/or apical periodontitis is an effective approach for inducing root maturation. Previous histologic studies showed cementoid/osteoid tissue and/or periodontal ligament-like tissue formed within the root canals. This case report describes the histologic findings of a human symptomatic irreversible pulpitis immature permanent tooth with most of the pulp removed after a revascularization/regeneration procedure. Histologic examination of the extracted tooth demonstrated a canal lumen filled with heterogeneous tissue rather than organized pulp. The predominant component was a fibrous connective tissue interspersed with abundant capillaries and sparse inflammatory cells. Along the dentin walls, a layer of odontoblast-like cells with irregular predentin-like matrix was evident, whereas islands of mineralized tissue with a cementoid/osteoid appearance extended toward the apex, forming partial barriers within the canal. No classic pulp tissue with a defined vasculature or innervation was observed. Immunohistochemical staining supported a mixed phenotype comprising dentinogenesis-associated markers within a mineralized matrix and markers compatible with periodontal ligament–like tissue in pericanalicular regions. The periapical tissues exhibited chronic inflammatory infiltrates without acute suppuration and showed only minimal resorption. These histologic features align with reported patterns of revascularization/regeneration but also reveal substantial deviation from normal pulp architecture, particularly in a case presenting symptomatic irreversible pulpitis. The regenerated tissue appeared to consist of cementoid/osteoid and periodontal ligament–like elements with limited evidence of true multipotent pulp tissue and odontoblastic organization. Collectively, the findings underscore the heterogeneity of regenerated tissues in immature teeth and have implications for interpreting vitality status, long-term root maturation, and the goals of regenerative endodontic procedures in the context of pulpal inflammation.

title: Primarily Undergraduate Institutions and the Astronomy Community
text_ai: This White Paper highlights the role Primarily Undergraduate Institutions (PUIs) play within the astronomy profession, addressing issues related to employment, resources and support, research opportunities and productivity, and educational and societal impacts, among others. To illuminate these dimensions, the paper surveys the distribution of faculty appointments, postdoctoral and staff roles, and the research output generated within PUIs, comparing trajectories with larger research universities. It examines access to telescope time, data archives, computational infrastructure, and the extent to which teaching duties are integrated with inquiry-led scholarship. It highlights institutional practices that foster undergraduate discovery, sustained mentoring, and cross-institutional collaborations that convert student participation into publishable results and graduate-school preparation. The analysis identifies persistent barriers—unequal grant support, limited instrumentation, high teaching loads, and administrative demands—that impede research productivity and career progression for PUI researchers. The paper proposes scalable solutions: shared facilities and grant mechanisms, formal collaboration frameworks, professional development for mentors, and policy changes that recognize teaching-integrated research in evaluation metrics. Finally, it articulates educational and societal impacts, including enhanced science literacy, workforce diversification, and broader engagement with local communities through astronomy at PUIs.

title: Higher-order conservation laws for the non-linear Poisson equation via the characteristic cohomology
text_ai: We study higher-order conservation laws of the non-linearizable elliptic Poisson equation $ \frac{{\partial}^2 u}{\partial z \partial \bar{z}} = -f(u) $ as elements of the characteristic cohomology of the associated exterior differential system. The theory of characteristic cohomology determines a normal form for differentiated conservation laws by realizing them as elements of the kernel of a linear differential operator. From the standpoint of the variational bicomplex, differentiated conservation laws are represented by horizontal forms on the infinite prolongation modulo the contact ideal, and the characteristic cohomology prescribes a normal form by characterizing those classes in the kernel of a linear differential operator. We derive an explicit description of this operator in terms of f and its derivatives and show that every differentiated conservation law is equivalent, modulo trivial laws, to a universal linear combination of a finite set of normal forms whose coefficients are functions of u and its jets along solutions. In particular, the cohomology is generated by a finite basis in each order, and the higher-order densities can be computed recursively from the base data (f, f', …). Examples for polynomial and exponential nonlinearities illustrate the construction and highlight the dependence on nonlinearity.

title: Third-order analysis of pseudopotential lattice Boltzmann model for multiphase flow
text_ai: In this work, a third-order Chapman-Enskog analysis of the multiple-relaxation-time (MRT) pseudopotential lattice Boltzmann (LB) model for multiphase flow is performed for the first time. The leading terms on the interaction force, consisting of an anisotropic and an isotropic term, are successfully identified in the third-order macroscopic equation recovered by the lattice Boltzmann equation (LBE), and then new mathematical insights into the pseudopotential LB model are provided. Building on the second-order foundations, the present third-order Chapman–Enskog analysis reveals that the MRT pseudopotential LB model comprises two distinct force contributions in the recovered momentum equation: an anisotropic term encoding directional bias and an isotropic correction that renormalizes capillarity and the equation of state. The anisotropic component persists under standard discretizations of the forcing operator and stems from the tensorial projection inherent to MRT; the isotropic part contributes a symmetric gradient term that modifies surface tension and pressure balance in a thermodynamically consistent manner. Numerical validation on planar and curved interfaces shows reduced spurious currents and improved Laplace-Young consistency when the third-order corrections are included; constitutive parameters can be tuned to suppress anisotropy without sacrificing stability. Guided by these findings, we propose practical remedies: select MRT relaxation times to equalize higher-order tensor contractions, employ more isotropic gradient operators for the forcing, or add explicit third-order corrections if necessary. The framework also clarifies how third-order terms map to effective adjustments of surface tension and EOS, enabling more accurate multiphase simulations across wide density contrasts.

title: Ten-Year Evaluation of the TOYOTA Prehospital Stroke Scale for Tissue Plasminogen Activator Intravenous Therapy in the Real World.
text_ai: Emergency medical services are an important part of acute stroke management. We devised a prehospital stroke scale, the TOYOTA prehospital stroke scale for tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) intravenous therapy (TOPSPIN) for triaging patients with ischemic stroke and especial indications for intravenous t-PA therapy in December 2006; this scale comprises 5 items including consciousness, atrial fibrillation, language disorder, disturbance of the upper extremities, and disturbance of the lower extremities. Methods: This was a retrospective, multicenter observational study within the TOYOTA Stroke Network (TSN), linking prehospital TOPSPIN records with hospital stroke registries and imaging results from December 2006 through December 2016. We included all EMS encounters in which TOPSPIN was completed for suspected ischemic stroke and had subsequent hospital adjudication. Exclusion criteria comprised hemorrhagic strokes, stroke mimics without imaging confirmation, and missing outcome data. Primary outcomes were the diagnostic performance of TOPSPIN for identifying patients eligible for intravenous t-PA under contemporary guidelines, defined by hospital administration of t-PA within 4.5 hours of symptom onset. Secondary outcomes included prehospital-to-treatment metrics (on-scene time, transport time, door-to-needle time), rates of t-PA administration among eligible patients, symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH), and functional outcome at 90 days (modified Rankin Scale 0–2). We evaluated a range of TOPSPIN thresholds (score ≥2 vs ≥3) using sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, comorbidities, distance to stroke center, and year of presentation to assess temporal trends. All analyses accounted for clustering by EMS agency and period effects related to guideline updates. Results: Among 29,800 suspected stroke transports with TOPSPIN data, 7,250 (24.3%) had imaging-confirmed ischemic stroke. At a threshold of TOPSPIN ≥2, sensitivity was 0.71 (95% CI 0.69–0.73) and specificity 0.58 (0.56–0.60), with PPV 0.32 (0.30–0.34) and NPV 0.87 (0.86–0.89); AUC 0.66. t-PA administration among ischemic cases rose from 40% in 2006–2010 to 62% in 2011–2016 (p<0.001). Median door-to-needle time decreased from 52 to 38 minutes (p<0.001). sICH occurred in 1.6% of treated patients. Good functional outcome (mRS 0–2) at 90 days increased from 39% to 54% over the decade (p<0.001). Subgroup analyses showed greater gains in rural/remote EMS networks and during hours with established stroke centers. Conclusions: Over ten years, TOPSPIN facilitated greater identification of IV t-PA-eligible ischemic stroke patients and contributed to substantial reductions in treatment times without compromising safety, translating into improved short‑term functional outcomes. Ongoing refinements, standardized training, and integration with regional stroke hubs remain essential to sustain gains in diverse prehospital settings.

title: Patient Insurance Status Is Associated With Care Received After Transfer Among Pediatric Patients in the Emergency Department.
text_ai: To determine whether frequency of interfacility transfer varied by insurance status among pediatric emergency department (ED) patients. Secondarily, we tested for an association between insurance status and odds of transfer with discharge from the second ED without observation or admission. We used the 2016 New York State ED and Inpatient Databases to identify all patients <18 years. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of all pediatric ED encounters (<18 years) in the 2016 New York State ED and Inpatient Databases. Insurance status was categorized as private, public (Medicaid), or uninsured/other. The primary outcomes were (1) occurrence of any interfacility transfer during the index ED visit and (2) among those transferred, disposition at the receiving ED, specifically discharge from the second ED without observation or admission. We used multivariable logistic regression to estimate adjusted odds ratios (AORs) for transfer by insurance category, controlling for age, sex, race/ethnicity, primary diagnosis (injury vs medical), chronic conditions, mode and time of arrival, and hospital characteristics (teaching status, bed size, ownership), as well as urban versus rural location. A second model restricted to transferred patients to assess the odds of discharge from the second ED without observation/admission. We accounted for clustering by hospital and applied sampling weights to produce state-representative estimates. Secondary analyses examined potential interactions between insurance status and urbanicity and were stratified by diagnostic category. Results: Transfer frequency varied by insurance status, with publicly insured and uninsured patients more (or less) likely to be transferred than privately insured patients after adjustment. In the transferred cohort, public and uninsured status were associated with higher odds of discharge from the receiving ED without observation or admission compared with private insurance. Findings were consistent across urban/rural settings and across hospital characteristics in sensitivity analyses. Conclusions: Insurance status is associated with post-transfer care trajectories among pediatric ED patients in New York, suggesting persistent disparities in access to definitive care after interfacility transfer. Strategies to standardize transfer criteria and to ensure equitable downstream care are warranted to reduce inequities and optimize ED efficiency.

title: A Review on the Applications of Transformer-based language models for Nucleotide Sequence Analysis
text_ai: In recent times, Transformer-based language models are making quite an impact in the field of natural language processing. As relevant parallels can be drawn between biological sequences and natural languages, the models used in NLP can be easily extended and adapted for various applications in bioinformatics. Across nucleotide sequences, pretrained transformers have demonstrated capacity to capture syntax and long-range dependencies beyond conventional k-mer methods. This review surveys architectures, pretraining objectives, tokenization strategies (k-mer, byte-pair, and nucleotide-level), and fine-tuning paradigms applied to DNA, RNA, and translated protein sequences. We summarize representative tasks including promoter and enhancer annotation, splice-site and variant effect prediction, gene expression inference, and regulatory network elucidation, as well as structure-aware and interaction-centric benchmarks. We discuss data resources, evaluation practices, and reproducibility challenges, with attention to interpretability through attention attribution and feature-attribution techniques. We highlight methodological gaps, such as limited long-range context handling, data bias, and the need for multimodal integration with epigenomic and 3D genome data. We conclude with directions toward scalable, interpretable, and transferable models for comprehensive nucleotide sequence analysis.

title: The Association between Reasons for a Rapid Response Team Alert and Immediate Patient Management in Total Hip Arthroplasty Patients.
text_ai: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the value and efficacy of rapid response teams (RRTs) for different triggering events in total hip arthroplasty (THA) patients. A retrospective review of all RRT events at a single, tertiary referral center from 2014 to 2016 was performed. We conducted a retrospective chart review of all rapid response team (RRT) activations for adult total hip arthroplasty (THA) inpatients at a single tertiary center between January 2014 and December 2016. Trigger reasons were categorized a priori into six groups: respiratory distress or hypoxemia; hemodynamic instability or cardiovascular concerns; acute neurologic change; pain, agitation, or delirium; device-related alarms or malfunctions; and other/uncategorized causes. Data extracted included patient demographics, ASA score, comorbidities (e.g., COPD, CHF, diabetes), time since surgery, first-line interventions by the RRT, subsequent imaging or laboratory workups, and downstream disposition (ICU transfer, floor observation, or discharge). Primary outcomes were immediate management decisions and escalation patterns. Secondary outcomes included time to escalation, length of stay, ICU-free days, and in-hospital mortality. Descriptive statistics described cohort characteristics. Categorical variables were compared with chi-square or Fisher exact tests; continuous variables with t-tests or Mann-Whitney U tests as appropriate. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent associations between trigger category and ICU transfer or need for operative intervention, adjusting for age, sex, BMI, ASA class, and comorbidity burden. A two-tailed alpha of 0.05 defined significance. A total of 214 RRT activations in THA patients were identified during the study period. Trigger distribution: respiratory distress or hypoxemia (approximately 28%), cardiovascular instability (approximately 26%), neurologic changes (approximately 15%), pain/agitation (approximately 20%), device-related alarms (approximately 6%), and other causes (approximately 5%). Immediate management included airway support or oxygen therapy (majority), vasopressor use (most of those with instability), blood transfusion in a minority, analgesia/sedation adjustments, and targeted imaging. ICU transfer occurred in a substantial subset (approximately 40%). On multivariable analysis, triggers of respiratory distress (OR 2.7; 95% CI 1.8–4.0) and cardiovascular instability (OR 2.1; 95% CI 1.3–3.3) were independently associated with ICU transfer. No trigger category independently predicted mortality; overall in-hospital deaths were rare and not directly attributable to RRT events. The association between RRT trigger and immediate management in THA patients demonstrates that certain physiologic derangements prompt rapid escalation and aggressive intervention, whereas others permit conservative management. These findings justify tailored RRT activation criteria and postoperative surveillance strategies to optimize resource utilization and patient safety in THA care pathways.
prefix: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the value and efficacy of rapid response teams (RRTs) for different triggering events in total hip arthroplasty (THA) patients. A retrospective review of all RRT events at a single, tertiary referral center from 2014 to 2016 was performed.

title: MOSEv2: A More Challenging Dataset for Video Object Segmentation in Complex Scenes
text_ai: Video object segmentation (VOS) aims to segment specified target objects throughout a video. Although state-of-the-art methods have achieved impressive performance (e.g., 90+% J&F) on existing benchmarks such as DAVIS and YouTube-VOS, these datasets primarily contain salient, dominant, and isolated objects, limiting their generalization to real-world scenarios. MOSEv2 introduces a large-scale collection of video sequences captured in unconstrained environments, featuring densely populated scenes, frequent occlusions, abrupt lighting shifts, motion blur, camera jitter, and dramatic viewpoint changes. Each sequence is densely annotated at pixel level for the target object, with additional metadata for occlusion state, re-identification cues, and inter-object relationships to facilitate richer analyses. To emulate realistic deployment, we include single-object and multi-object episodes, with distractors of varying similarity and nonrigid motion patterns that confound appearance-based tracking. We extend evaluation beyond traditional J&F and IoU by incorporating measures of temporal stability, boundary adherence under clutter, and long-term persistence after occlusion, as well as re-identification performance across discontinuities. A cross-dataset protocol assesses generalization by training on one distribution and testing on distinct scene types, mirroring practical transfer needs. Baseline experiments with contemporary VOS architectures reveal pronounced robustness gaps under severe occlusion, rapid motion, and background clutter, underscoring the limits of current priors and memory modules. MOSEv2 also provides standardized baselines and ablation studies that dissect the contributions of appearance models, temporal consistency modules, and refinement strategies under challenging conditions. We anticipate that MOSEv2 will spur development of models with persistent memory, explicit occlusion handling, and smarter distractor suppression, ultimately closing the gap between laboratory benchmarks and real-world deployment.

title: A 52 hours VLT/FORS2 spectrum of a bright z~7 HUDF galaxy: no Ly-alpha emission
text_ai: We aim to determine the redshift of GDS-1408, the most solid z~7 galaxy candidate lying in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field. We have used all the VLT spectra of GDS-1408 collected by us and two other groups with FORS2 at VLT in the last five years, for a total integration time of 52hr. The co-added spectrum yields no statistically significant Lyα line near the expected 0.97 μm region for z ≈ 7. We derive a robust 5σ upper limit on the Lyα line flux of F(Lyα) < 1.5 × 10^−18 erg s^−1 cm^−2 for line widths in the 100–300 km s^−1 range, translating to rest-frame equivalent width upper limits EW0 ≲ 8–9 Å depending on the assumed continuum level. The continuum redward of the break is detected in the merged spectrum with a signal-to-noise sufficient to constrain the UV spectral slope and to tighten the photometric redshift prior, yielding a redshift interval tightly overlapping with z ≈ 6.8–7.2. Taken together, the spectroscopic non-detection of Lyα and the full broad-band photometry favor a redshift consistent with the HUDF-based estimate z ≈ 7.0 ± 0.2–0.3. The ultraviolet luminosity of GDS-1408 corresponds to a star-formation rate of order tens of solar masses per year, in line with its bright rest-frame UV continuum. The absence of Lyα, given this SFR, implies either a low Lyα escape fraction fesc(Lyα) or substantial damping by the intergalactic medium, or a combination thereof. When placed in the context of z ≈ 7 galaxy samples, the non-detection adds to the growing evidence for strong Lyα attenuation at the tail of reionization and supports models invoking a significant neutral fraction of the IGM at z ≳ 7, or site- and ISM-dependent Lyα suppression mechanisms. Our results provide the tightest spectroscopic constraint to date for GDS-1408 and illustrate the continued challenge of securing redshifts for bright z ≳ 7 galaxies with current facility capabilities; they also highlight the pivotal role of forthcoming near-infrared spectroscopy (and JWST) for definitive confirmation.

title: Discovering momentum-dependent magnon spin texture in insulating antiferromagnets: Role of the Kitaev interaction
text_ai: We theoretically show that the Kitaev interaction generates a novel class of spin texture in the excitation spectrum of the antiferromagnetic insulator found in the Kitaev-Heisenberg-$\Gamma$ model. In conducting electronic systems, there is a series of vortex type of spin texture along the Fermi surface induced by Rashba and Dresselhaus spin-orbit coupling. Using a Holstein-Primakoff expansion around the Néel state on the honeycomb lattice, we diagonalize the bosonic Bogoliubov–de Gennes Hamiltonian to obtain the magnon eigenmodes and their spin polarization vectors across the Brillouin zone. The Kitaev interaction acts as an intrinsic momentum-dependent spin-orbit field in the magnon problem, yielding a noncollinear, momentum-resolved spin texture in the eigenmodes that is absent when only Heisenberg exchange is present. The texture manifests as vortex-like patterns with winding numbers dictated by the bond-dependent anisotropy and lattice symmetry; the Gamma term further modulates the texture by tilting and shifting the cores, providing a tunable handle on the spin orientation of magnons without external fields. We quantify the texture by the momentum-resolved spin expectation S(k) of each magnon branch and relate it to the Berry curvature and, in regimes where time-reversal symmetry is broken, to topological invariants of the magnon bands. The resulting topology gives rise to finite thermal Hall responses and, under open boundaries, chiral edge modes that accompany the bulk texture. Experimentally, polarization-resolved inelastic neutron scattering and spin-resolved Raman scattering can map S(k), while magnon spin currents driven by thermal gradients offer transport signatures of the texture. Our work thus reveals a robust mechanism for momentum-selective magnon spin control in insulating antiferromagnets with Kitaev interactions.

In conducting electronic systems, there is a series of vortex type of spin texture along the Fermi surface induced by Rashba and Dresselhaus spin-orbit coupling.

title: Spatiotemporal model of a key step in endocytosis: SNX9 recruitment via phosphoinositides
text_ai: Clathrin mediated endocytosis (CME) is an ubiquitous cellular pathway that regulates central aspects of cell physiology such as nutrient uptake, modulation of signal transduction, synaptic transmission and membrane turn-over. Endocytic vesicle formation depends on the timed production of specific phosphoinositides and their interactions with various endocytic proteins. Here we present a coarse-grained, reaction–diffusion model that couples phosphoinositide metabolism to the recruitment dynamics of SNX9, a PX-BAR protein implicated in early membrane curvature generation during CME. The model tracks cytosolic and membrane-bound pools of PI(4,5)P2, PI(3,4)P2 and PI4P, together with SNX9 monomers and oligomers, and a simplified clathrin–pit scaffold. Binding of SNX9 to the membrane proceeds via two lipid interfaces with distinct affinities, incorporating competitive binding to PI lipids and cooperative self‑association driven by BAR‑domain–mediated curvature. PI kinases and phosphatases generate spatiotemporal lipid gradients that seed SNX9 recruitment, while membrane deformation from SNX9 oligomers feeds back to concentrate lipids and promote further binding. The system is simulated on a two‑dimensional patch with realistic diffusion constants, reaction rates and pit lifetimes; parameter sweeps identify regimes in which SNX9 rapidly concentrates at sites of active PI turnover, preceding or co‑occurring with clathrin assembly. Results reproduce qualitative features of endocytic timings and predict a robust, curvature‑facilitated switch: modest changes in PI(4,5)P2 or PI(3,4)P2 levels yield large shifts in SNX9 dwell time and pit progression. Perturbations removing PI binding or symmetry‑breaking curvature abrogate recruitment, consistent with SNX9 acting as a lipid–shape integrator essential for efficient vesicle budding.

title: Dimensions of Higher Order Factor Analysis Models
text_ai: The factor analysis model is a statistical model where a certain number of hidden random variables, called factors, affect linearly the behaviour of another set of observed random variables, with additional random noise. The main assumption of the model is that the factors and the noise are Gaussian random variables. Within this framework, we specify a hierarchy in which the observed p variables are linked to q first-order factors, which in turn are driven by r higher-order factors, possibly with residual uniqueness. We derive the dimension of the model in terms of p, q, r and the structure of the loading matrices, and we analyze identifiability conditions under weak rotation constraints. The paper characterizes the implied covariance structure, showing how the second- and higher-order factor loadings determine the noncentral moments and the factor correlation matrix, and we discuss equivalence classes induced by orthogonal rotations. We develop criteria for determining the plausible dimensionality in practice, propose an information-criterion based approach and a bootstrap-based procedure to assess stability, and illustrate performance with simulations and an empirical dataset.

The main assumption of the model is that the factors and the noise are Gaussian random variables.

title: Negative-Tension Branes and Tensionless 1/2 Brane in Boundary Conformal Field Theory
text_ai: In the framework of boundary conformal field theory we consider a flat unstable D$p$-brane in the presence of a large constant electromagnetic field. Within this framework we derive the exact boundary state for fluctuations around the unstable Dp-brane in the presence of a constant electromagnetic field. We show that a class of tachyon profiles defines exactly marginal boundary deformations, so that the boundary conformal structure is preserved along the condensation process. In the regime of a large electric field the open string metric becomes effectively degenerate in directions aligned with the field, giving rise to a noncommutative worldvolume geometry. Tachyon condensation along these directions drives the system to two infrared fixed points: a negative-tension brane and a tensionless 1/2 brane. We compute disk partition functions and couplings to dilaton and RR–form fields, demonstrating that the negative tension manifests as a sign flip of the boundary energy density, whereas the 1/2 brane exhibits vanishing tension with a residual half-brane charge. Boundary-state overlaps with gravitons and RR fields corroborate the solitonic interpretation and are consistent with K-theory predictions for fractional defect branes in boundary conformal field theory. The results illuminate how strong-field limits realize nonperturbative, lower-dimensional objects within a robust BCFT framework.

title: Modelling Population-Level Hes1 Dynamics: Insights from a Multi-Framework Approach
text_ai: Mathematical models of living cells have been successively refined with advancements in experimental techniques. A main concern is striking a balance between modelling power and the tractability of the associated mathematical analysis. In this work we model the dynamics for the transcription factor Hairy and enhancer of split-1 (Hes1), whose expression oscillates during neural development, and which critically enables stable fate decision in the embryonic brain. To this end, we implement and compare three complementary modelling strands: (i) a canonical delay-differential equation model of the Hes1 negative feedback loop with transcriptional delay; (ii) a stochastic, single-cell gene-expression model that captures bursts in transcription and translation; and (iii) a population model obtained by coupling cells through Notch-Delta–mediated interactions and deriving mean-field or pairwise-coupled ODEs. Across frameworks we quantify oscillation period, amplitude, and coherence, and describe how intercellular coupling and noise alter phase relationships and escape from delays. Our results reveal regimes in which population-level waves stabilise fate decisions, and identify signatures enabling inference of coupling strength from population data. These insights inform experimental design and data interpretation.

title: Nature of excitons bound to inversion domain boundaries: Origin of the 3.45-eV luminescence lines in spontaneously formed GaN nanowires on Si(111)
text_ai: We investigate the 3.45-eV luminescence band of spontaneously formed GaN nanowires on Si(111) by photoluminescence and cathodoluminescence spectroscopy. This band is found to be particularly prominent for samples synthesized at comparatively low temperatures. At the same time, these samples exhibit a peculiar morphology, namely, isolated long nanowires are interspersed within a dense matrix of short ones. Here we assign the band to excitons bound to inversion domain boundaries (IDBs) that form at polarity interfaces within the spontaneously grown GaN nanowires on Si(111). Spatially resolved cathodoluminescence maps reveal elongated emission features parallel to the nanowire arms, matching the projected IDB network inferred from the observed coalescence morphology. Photoluminescence spectra collected at 5–60 K show a pronounced line at about 3.45 eV, with a narrow FWHM at the lowest temperature and a small Stokes shift relative to the free A-exciton. The line quenches with increasing temperature following an Arrhenius-type behaviour with an activation energy of tens of meV, consistent with recombination of a localized exciton bound to an IDB. Spectral decomposition indicates a dominant IDB-bound exciton component at low temperature, accompanied by a weaker high-energy shoulder near the free-exciton edge, attributable to less strongly localized or quasi-bound states at IDBs or to surface-related transitions. The intensity of the 3.45-eV emission scales with the density of long nanowires embedded in a matrix of shorter ones, establishing a direct link between growth-induced polarity fragmentation and IDB formation. Our results provide a robust assignment of the 3.45-eV luminescence to IDB-bound excitons and offer a spectroscopic handle to probe polarity fluctuations in spontaneously formed GaN nanowires on Si(111).

title: Interacting Q-balls
text_ai: We study non-topological solitons, so called Q-balls, which carry a non-vanishing Noether charge and arise as lump solutions of self-interacting complex scalar field models. Explicit examples of new axially symmetric non-spinning Q-ball solutions that have not been studied so far are constructed numerically. Our time-dependent simulations study collisions of these axially symmetric, non-spinning Q-balls in 3+1 dimensional Minkowski space, solving the nonlinear Klein–Gordon equation for a self-interacting complex scalar with a global U(1) symmetry. We examine head-on and off-axis encounters with fixed total charge but differing relative phase and individual charges. The dynamics depend sensitively on phase, velocity, and impact parameter, yielding a rich phenomenology: quasi-elastic scattering, fusion into a larger Q-ball, partial charge transfer with radiation, and, in some cases, fission into daughter Q-balls with dispersive waves. We map the dynamical phase diagram for representative potentials and identify long-lived bound states near merger as well as transient oscillon-like remnants. The results emphasize the crucial role of relative phase in nonlinear superposition of non-topological solitons and provide constraints for cosmological or particle-theory models in which Q-balls arise from global U(1) sectors.

title: Terminal Brain Damage: Exposing the Graceless Degradation in Deep Neural Networks Under Hardware Fault Attacks
text_ai: Deep neural networks (DNNs) have been shown to tolerate "brain damage": cumulative changes to the network's parameters (e.g., pruning, numerical perturbations) typically result in a graceful degradation of classification accuracy. However, the limits of this natural resilience are not well understood in the presence of small adversarial changes to the DNN parameters' underlying memory representation, such as bit-flips that may be induced by hardware fault attacks. In this work, we reveal a contrasting regime in which minimal, adversarial bit-flips in parameter storage precipitate abrupt, terminal performance collapse, a phenomenon we term terminal brain damage. We evaluate quantized models (8-bit and 4-bit weights) across standard backbones (ResNet-18, MobileNet) and a vision transformer, using realistic fault models (random, burst, and correlated bit flips) injected at the memory level. Across datasets and mappings (CIFAR-10, ImageNet subsets; SRAM/weight-banks on FPGA-like hardware), we observe a sharp threshold where accuracy collapses far beyond what graceful degradation would predict. Early-layer flips propagate nonlinearly, reconfiguring decision boundaries and yielding systematic misclassifications rather than diffuse noise. We develop a diagnostic framework to quantify terminal vulnerability: per-layer flip-rate thresholds, interaction effects, and a metric forecasting the onset of terminal damage. Our results challenge the assumption of natural fault tolerance in deployed DNNs and motivate memory-layout protections and training-time defenses to avert catastrophic failures. We also quantify the potential for adversarially staged faults to bypass safety nets and degrade confidence calibration, and erode trust in automated decisions.

title: Testing Sparsity Assumptions in Bayesian Networks
text_ai: Bayesian network (BN) structure discovery algorithms typically either make assumptions about the sparsity of the true underlying network, or are limited by computational constraints to networks with a small number of variables. While these sparsity assumptions can take various forms, frequently the assumptions focus on an upper bound for the maximum in-degree of the underlying graph $\nabla_G$. To address this, we introduce a formal testing procedure for sparsity that treats an upper bound on the maximum in-degree as a hypothesis about the data-generating BN. We develop statistics that aggregate local dependence into a global sparsity diagnostic, while remaining agnostic to the parameterization of conditional distributions. Under a Bayesian framework, we compare marginal likelihoods or Bayes factors for DAGs constrained to ∇_G ≤ k versus unconstrained alternatives, using efficient trans-dimensional proposals to explore model space. We also propose a resampling-based calibration to obtain finite-sample p-values for the sparsity tests. Empirical studies on synthetic networks and real datasets show that the tests reliably detect sparsity violations and guide practitioners toward robust structure discovery, balancing fit and complexity.

title: Current laboratory performance of starlight suppression systems, and potential pathways to desired Habitable Worlds Observatory exoplanet science capabilities
text_ai: We summarize the current best polychromatic (10 to 20 % bandwidth) contrast performance demonstrated in the laboratory by different starlight suppression approaches and systems designed to directly characterize exoplanets around nearby stars. We present results obtained by internal coronagraph and external starshade experimental testbeds using entrance apertures equivalent to off-axis or on-axis telescopes, either monolithic or segmented. Across internal coronagraphs and external starshade analogs, laboratory demonstrations have approached the stringent broadband contrasts required for direct-imaging of nearby habitable-zone planets, albeit with limiting assumptions on stability and model-based calibration. In polychromatic tests spanning 10–20% bandwidth, the best performance has been reported in the 10^−9 range for off-axis, unobscured or lightly obscured pupils, and in the 10^−8 to several×10^−9 range for on-axis apertures with central obstructions. Internal coronagraph testbeds employing high-order DMs, robust low-order wavefront sensing, and optimized apodization or pupil-remapping schemes have demonstrated contrast floors compatible with initial Habitable Worlds Observatory requirements when subjected to controlled environmental disturbances. External-starshade-like experiments emphasize petal alignment tolerances, edge diffraction control, and coherence between the occulting structure and telescope aperture, achieving comparable broadband suppression within narrow inner-working-angle regimes, and revealing critical sensitivities to jitter, polarization, and bandwidth. We synthesize these results to map pathways toward HWO capabilities, highlighting the essential roles of (i) scalable, ultra-stable wavefront control, (ii) broadband, low-cost manufacturable masks and occulters, and (iii) integrated calibration and post-processing. A staged, cross-platform development plan is outlined to close remaining performance gaps.

title: Optimizing Geometric Multigrid Methods with Evolutionary Computation
text_ai: For many linear and nonlinear systems that arise from the discretization of partial differential equations the construction of an efficient multigrid solver is a challenging task. Here we present a novel approach for the optimization of geometric multigrid methods that is based on evolutionary computation, a generic program optimization technique inspired by the principle of natural evolution. Key to the approach is the automatic encoding of multigrid components as a compact genotype, together with a fitness function that balances rate of convergence and computational cost on representative discretizations. We employ a steady-state evolutionary strategy with mutation, recombination, and survival selection to explore the design space of relaxations (smoothers, damping factors), grid-transfer operators (restriction/prolongation), cycle strategies, and coarse-level solvers. To keep evaluations tractable, we deploy surrogate-based pruning and parallel execution on multicore architectures; fitness is measured on a suite of linear and nonlinear PDE discretizations, with noise-tolerant estimates of spectral radius and practical error reduction. The resulting configurations demonstrate superior convergence factors and reduced runtime relative to classical geometric multigrid across test problems, with enhanced robustness to anisotropy and grid irregularities.

title: A DNN Based Post-Filter to Enhance the Quality of Coded Speech in MDCT Domain
text_ai: Frequency domain processing, and in particular the use of Modified Discrete Cosine Transform (MDCT), is the most widespread approach to audio coding. However, at low bitrates, audio quality, especially for speech, degrades drastically due to the lack of available bits to directly code the transform coefficients. To mitigate this degradation, we propose a deep neural network (DNN) based post-filter operating directly in the MDCT domain. The network is trained to estimate a multiplicative mask modulating the decoded MDCT coefficients, suppressing residual energy while preserving speech components. The filter processes each frame with a receptive field and exploits inter-frame context to capture temporal dynamics. It is designed for real-time deployment with low parameter count. Training relies on an informed objective combining a spectral mean-squared error in the MDCT domain with a perceptual loss correlated to PESQ and STOI. The approach is evaluated on corpora across codecs and bitrates, focusing on low-bitrate conditions. Results demonstrate improvements over a traditional MDCT post-filter, with PESQ gains of 0.25–0.45 and improved intelligibility at modest cost and scalable deployment.

title: WhisperFuzz: White-Box Fuzzing for Detecting and Locating Timing Vulnerabilities in Processors
text_ai: Timing vulnerabilities in processors have emerged as a potent threat. As processors are the foundation of any computing system, identifying these flaws is imperative. Recently fuzzing techniques, traditionally used for detecting software vulnerabilities, have shown promising results for uncovering vulnerabilities in large-scale hardware designs, such as processors. WhisperFuzz is a white-box fuzzing framework that instruments a microarchitectural model to expose timing variability along energy and timing constraints. It combines timing-coverage guided input generation with precise microarchitectural awareness, treating caches, branch predictors, memory buses, and speculative pipelines as first-class visibility surfaces. A timing oracle measures latency distributions, jitter, and leakage metrics under controlled perturbations, while a gradient-free search steers inputs toward regions with maximal timing sensitivity. The fuzzer employs RTL/HDL-aware instrumentation to attribute observed timing differences to candidate resources and stateful paths, enabling localization of leakage through a differential, coverage-driven analysis. Our contributions include (i) a formalization of timing vulnerability surface and a leakage score that couples absolute delay with variance across microarchitectural states; (ii) an efficient white-box fuzzer that uses timing-variance feedback to achieve high coverage of timing-sensitive paths; (iii) a localization engine that maps observed leakage to RTL/HDL components for targeted mitigation; and (iv) an empirical evaluation on open-source core implementations and cycle-accurate simulators, demonstrating discovery of previously unreported timing channels, including cache-access, speculative-execution, and memory-ordering paths. WhisperFuzz outperforms state-of-the-art software fuzzers adapted to hardware by achieving higher timing-variance coverage per seed and enabling precise hotspot localization, thus integrating smoothly into hardware design verification and pre-silicon mitigation workflows.

title: Addressing UX Practitioners' Challenges in Designing ML Applications: an Interactive Machine Learning Approach
text_ai: UX practitioners face novel challenges when designing user interfaces for machine learning (ML)-enabled applications. Interactive ML paradigms, like AutoML and interactive machine teaching, lower the barrier for non-expert end users to create, understand, and use ML models, but their application to UX practice is largely unstudied. Despite promise, practitioners confront ambiguities around goal alignment, transparency, and evaluability of ML components within UX workflows. We propose an integrative design approach that couples problem framing in UX with interactive ML tooling, enabling designers to explore model behavior without deep ML expertise. Our study develops a task-based methodology and a lightweight toolkit that includes model-teleology dashboards, feature-importance proxies, and adjustable constraint settings to steer AutoML outputs toward user-centred objectives. We validate the approach through a multi-session design study with 12 UX professionals across two domains, comparing traditional ML-assisted design to the interactive ML workflow. Quantitative measures (System Usability Scale, trust in automation, task completion time) and qualitative interviews reveal improved comprehension of model limitations, more principled tradeoffs, and fewer deployment-origin errors. We discuss design implications, practical guidelines, and directions for future research.

Interactive ML paradigms, like AutoML and interactive machine teaching, lower the barrier for non-expert end users to create, understand, and use ML models, but their application to UX practice is largely unstudied.

title: Galactic Stellar and Substellar Initial Mass Function
text_ai: We review recent determinations of the present day and initial mass functions in various components of the Galaxy, disk, spheroid, young and globular clusters. As a general feature, the IMF is well described by a power-law form for $m\ga 1 \msol$ and a lognormal form below. Across the Galaxy, the IMF inferred from resolved populations remains broadly robust, yet several systematic deviations are evident. In the disk, the high‑mass slope is close to Salpeter, with α≃2.3 for m≳0.5–1 M⊙, while the low‑mass end is well described by a lognormal or a multi‑part power law that peaks near 0.2–0.3 M⊙ and declines toward the substellar boundary near ≃0.075 M⊙. In the bulge and thick disk, some studies prefer a somewhat different high‑mass behaviour or a higher characteristic mass, though results depend sensitively on crowding, extinction, and selection. Globular clusters exhibit pronounced depletion of the lowest‑mass stars in their outer regions due to evaporation and tidal stripping, complicating recovery of the primordial IMF. The substellar regime, including brown dwarfs, extends the IMF toward the planetary‑mass domain with a shallow rise and possible turnover; the exact form and the binary fraction in this regime remain debated. We discuss strategies for disentangling true IMF variations from dynamical processing, using Gaia astrometry and kinematics, deep infrared surveys, and microlensing. Unresolved multiplicity, metallicity‑dependent mass–luminosity relations, and dynamical effects are principal systematics. The IMF governs the stellar mass budget, integrated light, and chemical yields of galaxies, and the paper highlights prospects for constraining its universality with forthcoming data. We also consider how IMF constraints delimit theories of fragmentation, turbulence, and early feedback in star‑forming regions.

title: The EXP pair-potential system. I. Fluid phase isotherms, isochores, and quasiuniversality
text_ai: The exponentially repulsive EXP pair potential defines a system of particles in terms of which simple liquids' quasiuniversality may be explained [A. K. Bacher et al., Nat. Commun. 5, 5424 (2014); J. C. Dyre, J. Phys. Condens. Matter 28, 323001 (2016)]. This paper and its companion present a detailed simulation study of the EXP system. This paper and its companion report a comprehensive simulation study of the EXP fluid over a wide range of densities and temperatures. We characterize the equation of state by isotherms and isochores in reduced units, and quantify the degree of quasiuniversality through data collapse on isomorphs—curves along which structure and dynamics are invariant in reduced coordinates. Confirming the hidden scale-invariance paradigm, the radial distribution function, static structure factor, and diffusion constants collapse when expressed in reduced units and plotted against ρ^{1/3} r. We show that both the average potential energy and the virial obey simple (approximately linear) scaling with density, yielding a near-constant density-scaling exponent γ. The high virial–potential-energy correlation coefficient (R>0.9) persists across the explored state space, underlining the robustness of the EXP quasiuniversality.

title: RIDCP: Revitalizing Real Image Dehazing via High-Quality Codebook Priors
text_ai: Existing dehazing approaches struggle to process real-world hazy images owing to the lack of paired real data and robust priors. In this work, we present a new paradigm for real image dehazing from the perspectives of synthesizing more realistic hazy data and introducing more robust priors into the network. To achieve this, we introduce RIDCP, a framework coupling haze synthesis with a discrete latent prior from clean imagery. First, we curate a codebook of clean image patches by applying a vector-quantized autoencoder to a diverse set of scenes, emphasizing texture, color fidelity, and structural details. The codebook constrains the reconstructed image to lie within the manifold of natural textures. Second, during dehazing, we project intermediate estimates onto the codebook prior via a lightweight coder–decoder module, which enforces patchwise consistency and suppresses spurious haze. This projection is complemented by a physics-informed restoration module that estimates transmission and atmospheric light under a principled constraint, while leveraging the discrete prior to refine edges and textures. We synthesize hazy training pairs with enhanced realism by combining physically grounded airlight models, depth-informed scattering, and domain randomization, aligning synthetic distributions with real-world statistics. Additionally, we exploit unpaired real hazy images to regularize the prior through a consistency loss and a progressive distillation strategy, enabling robust generalization to unseen scenes and lighting. Empirical results demonstrate that RIDCP surpasses state-of-the-art dehazing methods on multiple benchmarks, delivering sharper textures, more accurate colors, and reduced halo artifacts, with improved perceptual quality.

title: Kinks scattering in deformed $\varphi^6$ model
text_ai: The deformed model $\tilde{\varphi}^{(6)}$ is introduced based on the $\varphi^4$ model using a deformation functional $F[\varphi]$ including a free parameter $a$. The kink solutions in different sectors and their internal modes are obtained as functions of the deformation parameter and their characteristics are evaluated as well. Small-fluctuation spectra around the kink backgrounds are computed from the stability operator, revealing a deformation-dependent spectrum of discrete modes. The internal (shape) mode, when present, shifts in frequency with a and governs energy exchange between translational and vibrational degrees of freedom. Kink–antikink collisions are simulated for several sectors and incident velocities across the deformation range, showing elastic reflection, inelastic capture, and multi-bounce windows whose location and width depend on a. A two-mode collective-coordinate model captures the resonance mechanism by mapping energy transfer between translational and the primary internal mode. The deformation also modifies the asymptotic vacua and the effective potential, interpolating between φ^4-like and φ^6-like scattering with a tunable critical velocity and window structure. Thus, the deformation parameter a acts as a control knob for non-integrable kink dynamics in the deformed φ^6 landscape.

title: One for the Future: measuring the mass transfer rate in the ULX M82 X-2 by using orbital period changes will take millenia
text_ai: Bachetti et al. (2021) have recently claimed to measure the mass transfer rate in the pulsing ULX system M82 X-2 by following the change of its orbital period over 7 yr. Here, we assess the feasibility of constraining the mass transfer rate in M82 X-2 by tracking orbital-period evolution over decades. Using standard binary-evolution formalisms and accretion-torque theory, the expected Pdot scales with donor response and angular-momentum losses; for a high-rate ULX at a distance of 3.6 Mpc the effect remains minute. Our modelling shows that the anticipated orbital-period derivative yields projected phase shifts that accumulate at the level of microseconds to milliseconds over decades to centuries, far below X-ray timing precision. Even under assumptions—conservative mass loss, efficient angular-momentum extraction, and maximal Roche-lobe overflow—the cumulative signal would require delays of several millennia to reach a significant detection. We therefore conclude that model-independent measurement of Mdot from Pdot is untenable within human timescales, and that constraints must rely on joint fitting of timing, spectral, and luminosity data with priors on donor structure.

title: Fully On-board Low-Power Localization with Multizone Time-of-Flight Sensors on Nano-UAVs
text_ai: Nano-size unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) hold enormous potential to perform autonomous operations in complex environments, such as inspection, monitoring or data collection. Moreover, their small size allows safe operation close to humans and agile flight. An important part of autonomous flight is localization, which is a computationally intensive task especially on a nano-UAV that usually has strong constraints in sensing, processing and memory. This paper presents a fully onboard, low-power localization framework that exploits a compact multizone Time-of-Flight sensor head integrated with the vehicle’s inertial measurements. The core idea is to convert depth cues into pose-consistent constraints for real-time estimation on resource-constrained hardware. A two-tier processing chain is implemented: (i) a lightweight, event-driven preprocessor that suppresses multipath and spurious returns using zonal consistency checks, and (ii) a lean probabilistic SLAM engine that fuses IMU data with the zone measurements to estimate 6-DoF pose and to maintain a sparse map of the proximate environment. The SLAM back-end relies on an EKF-like formulation with a compact state and a motion-compensated observation model, enabling observability under aggressive maneuvers and partial occlusions. Validation comprises simulations and flights on a nano-UAV platform, with comparisons to vision-based baselines. The approach demonstrates robust localization in GPS-denied settings, tolerating low update rates and low compute, while maintaining stable flight through cluttered indoor trials. Energy profiling confirms a duty-cycled operation that preserves flight time, achieving centimeter- to decimeter-level accuracy over indoor ranges.

title: Intra-abdominal hypertension and the abdominal compartment syndrome
text_ai: The pressure within the abdominal cavity is normally little more than atmospheric pressure. However, even small increases in intra-abdominal pressure can have adverse effects on renal function, cardiac output, hepatic blood flow, respiratory mechanics, splanchnic perfusion and intracranial pressure. IAH is defined as sustained or recurrent intra-abdominal pressure ≥12 mm Hg, graded I–IV by the World Society of the Abdominal Compartment Syndrome (WSACS). Acute abdominal compartment syndrome (ACS) is diagnosed when IAP >20 mm Hg with new organ dysfunction or failure. Incidence varies with illness and therapy; IAH/ACS follow major trauma or surgery, pancreatitis, sepsis and heavy resuscitation. Elevated IAP impairs abdominal perfusion pressure (APP = mean arterial pressure − IAP) and compromises splanchnic, renal, hepatic and cardiorespiratory function through reduced venous return, diaphragmatic restriction and systemic inflammatory activation. Diagnosis hinges on accurate measurement of IAP, typically by bladder pressure via a Foley catheter, with measurements at end expiration and in a standardized fashion. Serial monitoring is essential in high-risk cohorts. Management begins with resuscitation optimization and measures to decrease IAP without compromising perfusion: judicious fluid administration, diuresis when appropriate, sedation and analgesia with avoidance of excessive abdominal wall tone, gastric decompression, and optimization of ventilation. If IAP remains elevated or ACS develops despite these strategies, decompressive laparotomy with temporary abdominal closure is indicated to restore organ perfusion and prevent multi-organ failure. Timely intervention improves organ function and survival, though mortality remains high in severe disease. This review synthesizes definitions, mechanisms, diagnostics and therapies to guide practice.

title: Topological Cycle Graph Attention Network for Brain Functional Connectivity
text_ai: This study, we introduce a novel Topological Cycle Graph Attention Network (CycGAT), designed to delineate a functional backbone within brain functional graph--key pathways essential for signal transmissio--from non-essential, redundant connections that form cycles around this core structure. We first introduce a cycle incidence matrix that establishes an independent cycle basis within a graph, mapping its relationship with edges. By integrating cycle-aware pruning with attention, CycGAT routes information along cycle-free paths while preserving meaningful motifs. The cycle incidence module constrains edge-wise attention by penalizing reliance on co-cyclic edges and promoting backbone links that minimally complete the independent cycle basis. We implement a heterogeneous message passing scheme that fuses local node features with global cycle coordinates, producing edge representations that reflect proximity and topology. Evaluations on resting-state fMRI datasets from multiple subjects use subject-specific graphs constructed with a common parcellation. CycGAT outperforms standard GCN/GAT baselines in predicting task-relevant connections, yields sparser, more interpretable backbones, and aligns with canonical networks. Ablation analyses confirm the critical role of cycle constraints and cycle-incidence regularization.

title: Windows over a New Low Energy Axion
text_ai: We outline some general features of possible extensions of the Standard Model that include anomalous U(1) gauge symmetries, a certain number of axions and their mixings with the CP-odd Higgs sector. As previously shown, after the mixing one of the axions becomes a physical pseudoscalar (the axi-Higgs) that can take the role of a modified QCD axion. In this framework the axi-Higgs acquires mass and couplings through its mixing with the CP-odd Higgs sector, while the remaining axions populate a light spectrum with suppressed Standard Model interactions. The low-energy effective theory features a single physical pseudoscalar whose mass is set by nonperturbative dynamics and whose couplings to photons and gluons are controlled by a small number of anomaly coefficients and mixing angles. We perform a complete diagonalization of the CP-odd sector and derive the resulting couplings to gauge bosons, fermions and the Higgs, allowing us to translate ultraviolet input into phenomenological observables. We identify several experimentally accessible windows: rare meson decays and flavor-changing processes that can reveal anomalous U(1) remnants, beam-dump and fixed-target experiments sensitive to light ALPs, and astrophysical and cosmological probes that constrain the axion-photon and axion-electron couplings. In particular, the axi-Higgs can behave as a QCD-axion–like particle with modified relic abundance and distinct isocurvature signatures, while allowing for an enhanced two-photon decay rate within the reach of upcoming helioscope and haloscope programs. Our results delimit viable regions and guide experimental strategies for uncovering a low-energy axion sector.

title: The Density-Potential Mapping in Quantum Dynamics
text_ai: This work studies in detail the possibility of defining a one-to-one mapping from charge densities as obtained by the time-dependent Schr\"odinger equation to external potentials. Such a mapping is provided by the Runge-Gross theorem and lies at the very core of time-dependent density functional theory. Building on the foundational results, we scrutinize the precise hypotheses under which the density-to-potential map is bijective and identify the breakdowns that can occur in practice. We review the conditions of v-representability, emphasizing the necessity of a given initial many-body state, sufficiently regular (analytic in time) external potentials, and appropriate boundary conditions. The analysis clarifies the functional-analytic structure of the mapping, its dependence on the initial wavefunction, and the way in which the continuity equation constrains the pair (density, current). We discuss extensions to nonadiabatic and interacting regimes, linear-response formulations, and the implications for approximate exchange-correlation functionals. The work also addresses gauge freedom, possible nonuniqueness, and the implications for inverse problems and numerical reconstruction, including stability, discretization effects, and error bounds in TDDFT simulations, and beyond.

title: Electric generation and ratcheted transport of contact-charged drops.
text_ai: We describe a simple microfluidic system that enables the steady generation and efficient transport of aqueous drops using only a constant voltage input. Drop generation is achieved through an electrohydrodynamic dripping mechanism by which conductive drops grow and detach from a grounded nozzle in response to an electric field. By exploiting the interplay of electrostatic stresses and interfacial tension, the device yields a repeatable train of drops propagating along a ratcheted channel geometry. Each drop acquires charge during formation and exchanges limited charge with subsequent wall contacts, producing an electrokinetic push that, combined with asymmetric confinement, yields stepwise transport without external actuation. Operation persists under a constant dc voltage, with no moving parts and minimal Joule heating for common conductivities. We report generation frequencies spanning tens of hertz and droplets with diameters tunable by nozzle radius and liquid conductivity. Transport velocity scales with voltage and channel asymmetry, yielding high rectification efficiency and reduced coalescence. The scheme provides a scalable route to on-chip generation, routing, and analysis of droplets in lab-on-a-chip platforms.

title: Optimized quantum implementation of elliptic curve arithmetic over binary fields
text_ai: Shor's quantum algorithm for discrete logarithms applied to elliptic curve groups forms the basis of a "quantum attack" of elliptic curve cryptosystems. To implement this algorithm on a quantum computer requires the efficient implementation of the elliptic curve group operation. Such an implementation requires we be able to compute inverses in the underlying field. Here, we present a reversible quantum realization of elliptic-curve arithmetic over GF(2^m) optimized for fault-tolerant platforms. The design rests on core ingredients. First, a compact binary-field multiplier and a fast squaring module whose depth scales linearly with m, implemented with reversible carry-save techniques to minimize T-count. Second, an Itoh–Tsujii inversion pipeline tailored to the quantum setting, enabling a single inversion after a polynomial number of multiplications and squarings; all ancillary qubits are uncomputed to reclaim space. Third, a projective-coordinate representation deployed with a Montgomery ladder to suppress inversions during scalar multiplication and to expose a single inversion at the end for point-conversion. The circuit uses data-independent control and depth-parallelism to yield uniform costs for point operations. We provide resource estimates (qubits, T gates, depth) as a function of m and evaluate them for representative binary-curve sizes. Our results show substantial reductions in T-depth and qubit count relative to naïve inversions, while preserving numerical stability and compatibility with fault-tolerant schemes. These improvements sharpen the quantum cost of ECC cryptanalysis on binary-field curves and inform countermeasures. This informs assessment and defenses.

title: Vegetarianism and veganism compared with mental health and cognitive outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
text_ai: Vegetarian and vegan diets are increasing in popularity. Although they provide beneficial health effects, they may also lead to nutritional deficiencies. Cognitive impairment and mental health disorders have a high economic burden. A meta-analysis was conducted to examine the relationship between vegan or vegetarian diets and cognitive and mental health. A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, PsycINFO, and Scopus was conducted through 2024 to identify observational studies and randomized trials reporting cognitive or mental health outcomes for vegan or vegetarian diets. Eligibility required clearly defined exposure and validated assessments of depression, anxiety, or cognitive function. Data were extracted in duplicate and synthesized with random-effects models. Primary outcomes included incident depression and anxiety, global cognitive performance, and standardized test scores; secondary outcomes encompassed quality of life and dementia incidence. Risk of bias was assessed with the Newcastle‑Ottawa Scale and Cochrane tools, and heterogeneity explored by subgroup analyses and meta-regression. From 8,900+ records, 68 studies (n>1.3 million participants) met criteria. For depression, vegetarian diets were not associated with risk (OR 1.05, 95% CI 0.96–1.14; I2 46%). Vegan diets showed a modest association with depressive symptoms (OR 1.18, 95% CI 1.02–1.36; I2 58%). Anxiety outcomes showed no consistent association for vegetarians (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.88–1.12) and a non-significant trend for vegans (OR 1.12, 95% CI 0.98–1.28). Global cognition yielded a trivial deficit (SMD −0.04, 95% CI −0.09 to 0.01; I2 63%), with larger effects in subgroups with micronutrient deficiency. Dementia incidence was rare and heterogeneous across studies. Overall certainty ranged from low to moderate because of confounding, measurement error, and dietary misclassification. These data do not indicate large adverse cognitive or mental health effects of vegetarian or vegan diets in general populations. However, vegan patterns lacking adequate B12, iron, or omega‑3 intake may relate to modestly higher depressive symptoms and poorer cognitive test performance in susceptible groups; ensuring nutritional adequacy and appropriate supplementation is advisable when adopting strict plant‑based diets.

title: Extracting black-hole rotational energy: The generalized Penrose process
text_ai: In the case involving particles the necessary and sufficient condition for the Penrose process to extract energy from a rotating black hole is absorption of particles with negative energies and angular momenta. No torque at the black-hole horizon occurs. Extending the construction to arbitrary classical fields, one replaces the particle’s negative-energy condition by the existence of negative conserved energy with respect to the horizon-generating Killing field χ^a = ξ^a + Ω_H ψ^a. The relevant currents are built from the stress–energy T_{ab} and the Killing vectors, yielding energy and angular-momentum fluxes across the horizon and at infinity. A mode or localized field configuration possesses negative χ-energy in the ergoregion if ω < mΩ_H in the standard Boyer–Lindquist decomposition, or, more generally, if the conserved charge −χ^a T_{ab} χ^b is negative. When such negative χ-energy is absorbed by the hole, the exterior field loses energy and angular momentum while the hole’s rotational energy decreases. In stationary scattering, this appears as superradiant amplification: the reflected or outgoing field carries away more energy than was incident, at the expense of the hole’s spin. The process is governed by the balance laws T^r_t and T^r_φ evaluated on the horizon, and the net extraction rate is set by the horizon’s angular velocity Ω_H. Thus the generalized Penrose process furnishes a unified framework for energy extraction by particles, electromagnetic waves, and other fields, including magnetohydrodynamic outflows, with the condition set by negative χ-energy relative to the horizon generator.

title: Seismic hazard assessment in Menton, France: Topographical site effect zoning considering a semi-empirical approach and a Machine Learning scheme
text_ai: The presence of topography influences the seismic ground motion and may result in strong amplifications, generally at the top of hills and reliefs. The increasing urbanization of hills requires an accurate estimation of these effects even in areas of moderate seismicity. To address this, we implement a hybrid workflow that combines a semi-empirical topographic amplification model with a machine-learning (ML) classifier to delineate topographic site-effect zones for Menton. A high-resolution DEM (10 m) and geology-geomorphology maps yield descriptors such as local slope, slope gradient, plan and profile curvature, and roughness. The semi-empirical component provides an amplification factor A_top as a function of slope and relief, calibrated against regional strong-motion data and corrected for distance to abrupt topographic features. The ML module (gradient boosting) learns the residual, nonlinear dependence of observed amplification on the same descriptors and spectral period (0.05–2 s). Cross-validation yields a three-class zoning (low, moderate, high) with accuracies exceeding 0.75 and robust uncertainty estimates. The resulting map supports seismic hazard assessment, urban planning, and retrofit prioritization for hillside districts, and offers a transferable framework for Mediterranean coastlines with moderate seismicity.

title: A Generic Framework for Clustering Vehicle Motion Trajectories
text_ai: The development of autonomous vehicles requires having access to a large amount of data in the concerning driving scenarios. However, manual annotation of such driving scenarios is costly and subject to the errors in the rule-based trajectory labeling systems. To address this, we introduce a generic, data-driven framework for unsupervised clustering of vehicle motion trajectories that is agnostic to sensor modality and sampling characteristics. The pipeline comprises (i) robust pre-processing including temporal alignment, gap filling, and ego-vehicle motion compensation; (ii) flexible trajectory representation that merges kinematic features with learned embeddings to capture curvature, interactions, and lane-changing behavior; (iii) a modular clustering backbone supporting distance-based, density-based, and model-based approaches, with emphasis on dynamic time warping and derivative-based similarity to accommodate heterogeneous sampling; (iv) cluster validation and labeling strategies, including silhouette-based criteria and interpretability through prototypes and transition graphs; and (v) an interactive refinement layer enabling human-in-the-loop corrections. Evaluation on several public driving datasets demonstrates improved labeling efficiency, richer scenario coverage, and preserved physical plausibility at scale, promoting reproducible benchmarking across platforms.

title: Two-year follow-up of mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists for chronic central serous chorioretinopathy.
text_ai: To evaluate the long-term oral mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRa) treatment in chronic central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC). Patients with chronic non-resolving CSC (defined as foveal subretinal fluid (SRF) lasting >4 months with retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) alterations) treated with MRa only (eplerenone or spironolactone) for at least 6 months were retrospectively included. Methods: This retrospective, single-center study included consecutive eyes with chronic non-resolving CSC treated with MRa (eplerenone or spironolactone) for ≥6 months and with ≥24 months of follow-up. Primary outcome: complete SRF resolution on OCT at 6, 12, and 24 months. Secondary outcomes: changes in BCVA, central subfield thickness (CST), and evolution of RPE alterations. Safety was monitored via serial serum potassium and creatinine measurements. Results: Thirty-eight eyes from 29 patients were analyzed (mean age 55.2 ± 8.7 years; male 26/29). Baseline BCVA was 68.2 ± 7.5 letters; CST 342 ± 55 μm. SRF resolved in 15/38 eyes (40%) at 6 months, 24/38 (63%) at 12 months, and 22/38 (58%) at 24 months. Mean BCVA improved by 6.8 ± 4.2 letters at 24 months (p<0.001). CST decreased by 60 ± 30 μm at 24 months (p<0.01). RPE alterations stabilized or improved in 60% of eyes. Hyperkalemia occurred in 5 eyes (13%), necessitating dose adjustment; two required discontinuation. No acute kidney injury. After 24 months, 3 eyes with persistent SRF underwent adjunctive photodynamic therapy, achieving SRF resolution. Conclusions: Long-term MRa therapy may yield durable SRF reduction and functional gains in chronic CSC, with acceptable safety in carefully monitored patients. Larger prospective trials are warranted to define optimal agent, dose, and duration.
