Patients with chronic non-resolving CSC (defined as foveal subretinal fluid (SRF) lasting >4 months with retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) alterations) treated with MRa only (eplerenone or spironolactone) for at least 6 months were retrospectively included.

title: The formation of astrophysical Mg-rich silicate dust
text_ai: We present new results for ground-state candidate energies of Mg-rich olivine (MRO) clusters and use the binding energies of these clusters to determine their nucleation rates in stellar outflows, with particular interest in the en- vironments of core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe). We derive ground-state candidate energies for MRO clusters up to sizable sizes (n ≈ 2–12) and extract robust binding energies, including geometries for quasi-planar and three-dimensional motifs. These data are integrated in a kinetic nucleation model to yield steady-state rates J(T, P, S) for CCSN-like outflows. By comparing with classical nucleation theory, we quantify how atomic-scale energetics modulate the nucleation barrier and the critical cluster size, finding a transition from barrier-limited to growth-limited regimes as S increases. Under representative CCSN ejecta conditions (temperatures 1200–2500 K, pressures 10^-7–10^-9 bar; Mg/Si/O ratios near solar), we predict nucleation rates that accelerate once n ≈ 6–9 and persist on timescales compatible with dust formation prior to reverse shocks. Our results imply substantial Mg-rich silicate dust yields in CCSNe and set constraints on the early dust budget in galaxies.

title: Curvature Perturbations from a Massive Vector Curvaton
text_ai: We study a ghost-free model of massive vector curvaton proposed in the literature, where the quick decrease of the vector background expectation value is avoided by a suitable choice of kinetic and mass functions. Integrating the vector field into the inflationary sector via a non-minimal kinetic term f^2(φ) and a time-dependent mass m^2(φ) yields a background that sources scale-invariant fluctuations without ghost or gradient instabilities. We compute the curvature perturbation using the δN formalism and the in-in technique, clarifying the conditions under which the vector condensate contributes dominantly or subdominantly to the total curvature perturbation after its decay. The resulting power spectrum exhibits a small but detectable statistical anisotropy characterized by a quadrupolar coefficient g_* that remains compatible with limits for a range of decay rates. The bispectrum acquires anisotropic shapes with a suppressed but nonzero f_NL, whose sign and amplitude are tied to the evolution of the background vector and the relative timing of decay. Within these constraints, the model provides a ghost-free, viable alternative to scalar curvatons with distinctive directional signatures.

title: Preschool Gender-Typed Play Behavior at Age 3.5 Years Predicts Physical Aggression at Age 13 Years.
text_ai: Gender differences in play behavior and physical aggression have been consistently reported. Theoretical perspectives concerning evolutionary, social, and social-cognitive mechanisms suggest that male-typical play behavior during childhood increases subsequent physical aggression. The evidence supporting these connections is limited, however. Using a prospective, multi-method design, we analyzed data from a cohort (N = 452; 52% female; diverse SES). At age 3.5 years, observers conducted play sessions in which children engaged with standardized sets; coders rated the extent of male-typical play behavior (e.g., rough-and-tumble play, object choices) and female-typical play. At age 13 years, physical aggression was assessed with teacher and parent reports and, when possible, peer nominations. We estimated regression models predicting aggression at 13 from preschool male-typical play, adjusting for baseline aggression at 3.5 years, IQ, SES, parental warmth and harsh discipline, and temperamental factors. Moderation by child sex and family adversity was examined. Mediation by peer rejection and conduct problems was explored with tests. Results showed that higher levels of preschool male-typical play predicted greater physical aggression at age 13 (β ≈ .15–.20, p < .01), controlling for covariates; effects were robust to alternative aggression reporters. The association was stronger for boys, but persisted for girls. Mediation analyses suggested indirect paths via peer difficulties and conduct problems. Collectively, findings support a long-term link between early gender-typed play and later physical aggression, suggesting early diversification of play experiences may reduce later risk.

title: Fractal Profit Landscape of the Stock Market
text_ai: We investigate the structure of the profit landscape obtained from the most basic, fluctuation based, trading strategy applied for the daily stock price data. The strategy is parameterized by only two variables, p and q. Stocks are sold and bought if the log return is bigger than p and less than -q, respectively. Across a dense grid in the (p,q) plane we map the realized profit for each asset and across an extended historical window. After incorporating transaction costs, the profit landscape presents a rugged topology with numerous local maxima and saddle points. We quantify its roughness by box-counting and spectral measures, uncovering a nontrivial fractal spectrum that persists under coarse graining of the parameter axes. The distribution of local optima is heavy-tailed, and the density of maxima scales with resolution according to a power law, indicating long-range correlations in exploitable fluctuations. Surrogate time series and randomized shuffles fail to reproduce the observed fractality, implying that the fractal landscape is an intrinsic, market-generated property that constrains simple rule-based strategies.

The strategy is parameterized by only two variables, p and q. Stocks are sold and bought if the log return is bigger than p and less than -q, respectively.

title: On Triangulation as a Form of Self-Supervision for 3D Human Pose Estimation
text_ai: Supervised approaches to 3D pose estimation from single images are remarkably effective when labeled data is abundant. However, as the acquisition of ground-truth 3D labels is labor intensive and time consuming, recent attention has shifted towards semi- and weakly-supervised learning. Generating an effective form of supervision with little annotations still poses major challenge in crowded scenes. To address this, we introduce triangulation as a self-supervision signal that exploits multi-view geometry without ground-truth 3D supervision. Our approach operates on multi-view 2D detections and camera calibration to produce view-consistent 3D reconstructions via a differentiable triangulation layer. A reprojection-based loss enforces consistency with observed keypoints across all views, while a geometric-structure constraint enforces plausible limb lengths and smooth motion. We complement this with a view-selection mechanism that weighs uncertain views and occluded joints. The proposed framework enables end-to-end training of a 3D pose predictor under weak supervision and yields improved accuracy in crowded environments, where explicit 3D labeling is prohibitive. Empirical evaluation on standard benchmarks demonstrates competitive performance with substantially reduced annotation effort.

However, as the acquisition of ground-truth 3D labels is labor intensive and time consuming, recent attention has shifted towards semi- and weakly-supervised learning. Generating an effective form of supervision with little annotations still poses major challenge in crowded scenes.

title: Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for Hypersonic Flows
text_ai: In recent years, high-order discontinuous Galerkin (DG) methods have emerged as an attractive approach for numerical simulations of compressible flows. This paper presents an overview of the recent development of DG methods for compressible flows with particular focus on hypersononic flows. First, we survey state-of-the-art DG methods for computational fluid dynamics. Building on the survey, we synthesize the major DG formulations for the compressible Navier–Stokes equations and categorize them by their treatment of inviscid fluxes, viscous terms, and stabilization. We compare entropy-stable and positivity-preserving implementations, including Roe-type and HLLC-based fluxes, interior-penalty viscous terms (SIPG, BR2), and their compatibility with curved, hp-adaptive meshes. A central challenge in hypersonic applications is the accurate resolution of thin shock layers and intense viscous–thermal gradients, which demands robust shock-capturing mechanisms (limiters, subcell approaches, artificial viscosity) while maintaining high-order accuracy in smooth regions. We review time integration strategies ranging from explicit Runge–Kutta schemes with CFL restrictions to implicit–explicit (IMEX) treatments that alleviate stiffness from viscous terms and chemistry models. The role of adaptivity is examined: hp-refinement, dynamic AMR, and mesh-curving to track multiscale features such as shock–boundary-layer interactions and separation zones. Finally, we identify key gaps—non-equilibrium chemistry, real-gas effects, high-Mach boundary conditions, and scalability on modern HPC architectures—and outline avenues for future work, including entropy-stable DG formulations, robust positivity-preserving limiters, and integrated reduced-order approaches for design optimization.

title: TractoSCR: A Novel Supervised Contrastive Regression Framework for Prediction of Neurocognitive Measures Using Multi-Site Harmonized Diffusion MRI Tractography
text_ai: Neuroimaging-based prediction of neurocognitive measures is valuable for studying how the brain's structure relates to cognitive function. However, the accuracy of prediction using popular linear regression models is relatively low. We propose a novel deep regression method, namely TractoSCR, that allows full supervision for contrastive learning in regression tasks using diffusion MRI tractography. TractoSCR learns a discriminative latent embedding by applying data augmentation to tractography representations and employing a supervised contrastive regression objective that leverages the continuous target as supervision. We define a pairwise similarity s(i,j) = exp(- (y_i - y_j)^2 / (2σ^2)) and use it to weight positive pairs in a contrastive loss, encouraging subjects with similar neurocognitive scores to cluster together in latent space while pushing apart those with dissimilar scores. A regression head maps the latent representation to the target score, with L1/L2 loss ensuring accuracy. The overall objective is L = λ LSC + (1-λ) Lreg, with hyperparameters chosen by validation. To address multi-site variability, we embed a harmonization module on tractography features (e.g., ComBat-based correction) and add a domain-adversarial branch to minimize residual site information in the embeddings. The tractography encoder is a graph neural network over tract graphs with tract-level attention pooling, producing a compact subject-level embedding that feeds the regression head. Across multi-site diffusion MRI cohorts and multiple neurocognitive measures, TractoSCR outperforms conventional regression and baseline contrastive-prior methods, showing improved cross-site generalization and reduced site-related variance. Ablations confirm the contributions of supervised contrastive learning and harmonization to the observed gains.

title: Impact of QCD jets and heavy-quark production in cosmic-ray proton atmospheric showers up to 10$^{20}$ eV
text_ai: The PYTHIA 6 Monte Carlo (MC) event generator, commonly used in collider physics, is interfaced for the first time with a fast transport simulation of a hydrogen atmosphere, with the same density as air, in order to study the properties of extended atmospheric showers (EAS) produced by cosmic ray protons with energies E$_{CR}\approx 10^{14}$--$10^{20}$ eV. We generate the primary interaction and the ensuing parton shower and hadronization with PYTHIA 6, explicitly including charm and bottom production in the hard scattering, then propagate all secondaries through a lightweight, 1D/3D transport model that accounts for hadronic interactions, decay, and energy deposition in a hydrogen target whose density reproduces air. Key observables are the longitudinal shower profile, the depth of the shower maximum X_max, the multiplicity and energy spectra of hadrons and jets, and the muon content at ground. We find that QCD jets and heavy-quark production introduce non-negligible modifications to the hadronic cascade, increasing late energy deposition and enhancing the high-energy muon yield, with effects growing with E_CR. Systematic variations of PDFs, ISR/FSR modeling, and hadronization are used to estimate uncertainties, establishing a framework to connect collider QCD dynamics with ultrahigh-energy air-shower phenomenology. The approach provides a controllable probe of forward-scattering dynamics and heavy-quark production in extreme kinematics, and lays the groundwork for constraining hadronic interaction models employed in cosmic-ray interpretation through direct comparisons with simulated observables accessible to current and next-generation air-shower experiments.

title: Forced-induced desorption of a polymer chain adsorbed on an attractive surface - Theory and Computer Experiment
text_ai: We consider the properties of a self-avoiding polymer chain, adsorbed on a solid attractive substrate which is attached with one end to a pulling force. The conformational properties of such chain and its phase behavior are treated within a Grand Canonical Ensemble (GCE) approach. Within this framework, the control parameters are the surface attraction ε_s and the pulling force f. The grand partition function Z(z; f) decomposes into an adsorbed-loop sector and a desorbed-tail sector, each with its own singularity. The adsorbed contribution yields a singularity z_ads(ε_s) that strengthens with ε_s, while the desorbed tail under force has a singularity z_tail(f) that shifts with f. The adsorption–desorption line is determined by z_ads(ε_s) = z_tail(f), yielding the critical force f_c(ε_s). From the scaling form of the order parameter θ, the fraction of contacts, we obtain θ(N; ε_s, f) → θ_c on the transition line and θ → 0 in the desorbed phase. Finite-size scaling gives θ(N) ≈ N^{-β} G[(f − f_c(ε_s)) N^{φ}], with φ ≈ 0.59 in three dimensions; at criticality the tail distribution P_tail(n) follows a power law with exponent τ_tail related to φ by universal relations. Computer experiments: We perform lattice Monte Carlo simulations of a self-avoiding walk grafted to a surface, with a constant force applied to the free end. Chains with N up to a few thousand are sampled over a range of ε_s and f; θ, ⟨x⟩ and susceptibilities are extracted using biased sampling. The numerics reproduce the theoretical phase boundary, and data collapse occurs when plotting against (f − f_c) N^{φ} for N ≥ 400. Near criticality the contact-number distribution is bimodal, while away from the transition it is unimodal. The exponents extracted from the simulations agree with the theoretical predictions within error bars. These results provide a consistent quantitative picture of forced-induced desorption and benchmarks for single-molecule pulling experiments.

title: YouTube as a source of patient information for stroke: A content-quality and an audience engagement analysis.
text_ai: Stroke is the second leading cause of death worldwide following ischemic heart disease, and the fifth in the United States. The video-sharing database, YouTube, is the second most popular visited website with more than 2 billion users, thus it's increasingly being used as a medium for delivering health information. Objective: To characterize the quality of stroke-related information on YouTube and examine how quality relates to audience engagement. Methods: In a cross-sectional content-quality and engagement analysis, we systematically searched YouTube using terms such as “stroke,” “stroke symptoms,” “FAST,” and “TIA.” English-language, publicly accessible videos were included; duplicates and noninformational content were excluded. Two independent raters evaluated each video with the DISCERN instrument and the JAMA benchmark criteria; disagreements were resolved by consensus, with inter-rater reliability reported (Cohen’s kappa). We coded content across core domains (definition and pathophysiology, risk factors, warning signs, emergency response, acute treatment, rehabilitation, prognosis) and noted presence of citations, author credentials, and potential commercial interests. Audience engagement was assessed via views, likes, dislikes, comments, shares, and uploader category (academic/medical, professional media, patient/community, or other). Descriptive statistics described quality and engagement; associations between quality scores and engagement metrics were explored with nonparametric correlations and multivariable regression analyses. Results: The sample demonstrated substantial heterogeneity in information quality; many videos provided incomplete or poorly sourced content, with limited discussion of risk factors and emergency actions. Higher DISCERN and JAMA scores were more common in videos from academic or medical channels, whereas engagement was often amplified by sensational narratives or personal testimonials. Comparisons revealed little consistent linkage between high-quality content and viewer engagement, suggesting that popularity does not reliably reflect accuracy. Conclusions: YouTube constitutes a major, uneven source of stroke information, with substantial gaps in evidence-based content. This underscores the need for targeted consumer education, clinician guidance, and platform-based quality standards to elevate accessible, high-quality stroke information online.

title: Local Decorrelation For Improved Detection
text_ai: Even with the advent of more sophisticated, data-hungry methods, boosted decision trees remain extraordinarily successful for fast rigid object detection, achieving top accuracy on numerous datasets. While effective, most boosted detectors use decision trees with orthogonal (single feature) splits, and the topology of the resulting decision boundary may not be well matched to the natural topology of the data. To address this misalignment, we introduce a local decorrelation transform that operates on spatially localized neighborhoods of feature channels, producing a set of decorrelated, compact channels while preserving invariants essential for detection. The transform is learned from unlabeled data via second-order statistics and is efficiently computed at run time through separable convolutions. We show that feeding standard boosted classifiers with decorrelated channels yields more regular, nearly linear boundaries in the original space, enabling shallower trees and more robust splits. Empirically, on several rigid-object benchmarks, our approach delivers consistent gains in detection accuracy with modest runtime overhead. We analyze locality scale, channel expansion, and integration with cascade detectors in practice.

title: A Trust and Reputation System for IoT Exploiting Distributed Ledger Technology
text_ai: The advent of Bitcoin, and consequently Blockchain, has ushered in a new era of decentralization. Blockchain enables mutually distrusting entities to work collaboratively to attain a common objective. However, current Blockchain technologies lack scalability, which limits their use in Internet of Things (IoT) applications. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Trust and Reputation System (TRS) for IoT that exploits Distributed Ledger Technology to provide tamper-evident, auditable trust information exchange. The architecture couples a lightweight, permissioned ledger with a modular reputation engine that aggregates direct observations, endorsements, and feedback into a score. A stake-based weighting mechanism and ageing of feedback mitigate Sybil and collusion, while off-chain storage preserves device constraints. Smart contracts encode policy for score calculation, revocation, and incentive alignment, and a PBFT-style consensus ensures timely updates. The system supports interoperability across heterogeneous IoT domains and enables rapid trust bootstrapping for new devices. Evaluation on a testbed and simulations demonstrates improved trust accuracy, reduced decision latency, and scalable operation compared with baseline approaches, while maintaining privacy and resilience to attacks.

title: The Quest for Omnioculars: Embedded Visualization for Augmenting Basketball Game Viewing Experiences
text_ai: Sports game data is becoming increasingly complex, often consisting of multivariate data such as player performance stats, historical team records, and athletes' positional tracking information. While numerous visual analytics systems have been developed for sports analysts to derive insights, few tools target fans to improve their understanding and engagement of sports data during live games. To address this gap, we introduce Omnioculars, a lightweight, wearable visualization layer embedded in a head-mounted display and synchronized with live feeds. The system overlays contextual mini-visualizations—summaries of player trajectories, possession-based stats, and heatmaps of team spacing—without occluding essential on-court action. We propose a modular visualization language and an attention-aware rendering strategy that modulates detail based on game context and user task. Our implementation supports streaming data from public APIs and local game logs, with latency kept below a practical threshold. We conducted a mixed-methods evaluation comprising a controlled lab study (n=24) and an in-situ field deployment during a collegiate game (n=16). Quantitative results show improved accuracy on task-driven questions about personnel, formations, and pivotal moments, and higher self-reported engagement and perceived understanding. Qualitative feedback emphasized nonintrusive cues, rapid access to replayable visuals, and the value of user-controlled information density. We discuss design implications, including attention management, accessibility, and the transferability of the framework to other sports contexts. Contributions include the system, the methodological approach, and empirically grounded design guidelines for embedded sports visualization.

title: Green Segment Routing for Improved Sustainability of Backbone Networks
text_ai: Improving the energy efficiency of Internet Service Provider (ISP) backbone networks is an important objective for ISP operators. In these networks, the overall traffic load throughout the day can vary drastically, resulting in many backbone networks being highly overprovisioned during periods of lower traffic volume. Green Segment Routing (GSR) extends conventional SR by integrating energy-awareness into policy computation. We formulate a joint optimization that selects SR paths, activates/deactivates links and nodes, and rebalances traffic under time‑varying demand while preserving SR semantics and per‑flow QoS constraints. A scalable heuristic delegates energy‑aware SR policy construction to a two‑stage process: (i) identify energy‑critical segments and (ii) compute compact SR label stacks that realize the proposed awaken‑sleep schedules with minimal churn. We evaluate on a representative backbone model and replayed diurnal traces, benchmarking against baseline SR and a statically provisioned topology. Results show meaningful reductions in instantaneous power consumption, with limited impact on path latency and packet loss. The work discusses deployment considerations, interoperability with existing IGP‑TE mechanisms, and potential extensions to multi‑domain scenarios.

title: Space of initial conditions and universality in nonequilibrium quantum dynamics
text_ai: We study analytically the role of initial conditions in nonequilibrium quantum dynamics considering the one-dimensional ferromagnets in the regime of spontaneously broken symmetry. We analyze the expectation value of local operators for the infinite-dimensional space of initial conditions of domain wall type, generally intended as initial conditions spatially interpolating between two different ground states. Employing a controlled expansion around the ferromagnetic ground state and exploiting the low-energy integrability of the model, we derive closed-form expressions for the time evolution of local magnetization and two-point correlators in the domain-wall sector. We show that the long-time, large-distance behavior obeys a universal scaling form in which the profile is a function of the rescaled coordinate x/t and a single dimensionless domain-wall parameter lambda encoding the initial slope and magnetization imbalance. This universality class persists across a broad family of initial domain walls, while subleading corrections depend on microscopic details. We corroborate the analytical results with matrix-product-state simulations, finding striking agreement up to accessible times. These results illuminate universality in nonequilibrium quantum spin chains.

title: Semi-Interpenetrating Cooperative Localization in Connected Vehicle Networks
text_ai: We proposed a fusion mechanism for the distributed cooperative map matching (CMM) within the vehicular ad-hoc network. This mechanism makes the information from each node reachable within the network by other nodes without direct communication, thus improving the overall localization accuracy and robustness. Building on semi-interpenetrating framework, the fusion mechanism enables each node to exploit both its own CMM output and embedded information propagated through the network, even when direct messages are temporarily unavailable. The proposed architecture integrates a semi-interpenetrating map-consensus layer with a localized probabilistic map matching module, allowing consistent lane-level estimates across the fleet. The approach supports asynchronous operation and tolerates packet loss, varying communication ranges, and road geometry constraints. A lightweight communication protocol delivers compact summaries of local CMM confidence and key map features, reducing bandwidth while preserving interpretability. Evaluation in simulated and real-world connected-vehicle datasets demonstrates resilience to GPS outages and urban canyons, with notable gains in localization continuity and reduced drift compared to isolated CMM and naive fusion baselines. These results support scalable deployment in dense networks.

title: On the disappearance of a cold molecular torus around the low-luminosity active galactic nucleus of NGC 1097
text_ai: We used the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) to map the CO(3-2) and the underlying continuum emissions around the type 1 low-luminosity active galactic nucleus (LLAGN; bolometric luminosity $\lesssim 10^{42}$ erg~s$^{-1}$) of NGC 1097 at $\sim 10$ pc resolution. These observations revealed a detailed cold gas distribution within a $\sim 100$ pc of this LLAGN. Our analysis indicates that, at these depths, no canonical parsec-scale, geometrically thick molecular torus remains. The inner CO(3-2) distribution is markedly depleted within r ≲ 8–12 pc, where emission is sporadic and low-brightness, consistent with a sparse, clumpy medium rather than a continuous, high-column-density structure. The molecular gas in the central few tens of parsecs resides in a moderately inclined, irregular disk and in several streamer-like remnants that feed a circumnuclear ring at ∼20–40 pc. Kinematic modeling reveals predominantly circular rotation with modest velocity dispersion and no persistent high-velocity, biconical outflow signatures that would signal an energetically significant torus-driven wind. The excitation analysis suggests sub-thermal conditions and low optical depths, restricting the viable gas densities and temperatures that could sustain a dusty, optically thick torus. The 870 μm continuum is dominated by a compact, unresolved core whose spectral properties favor non-thermal synchrotron emission, while the extended continuum correlates with circumnuclear star-forming ring features. Collectively, these results imply that, in this LLAGN, the traditional cold molecular torus has either dissipated or failed to form, likely reflecting the low accretion-rate environment and episodic fueling. We discuss implications for AGN unification models and for the lifecycle of toroidal structures in low-luminosity systems.

title: Decoding and Reconstructing the Focus of Spatial Attention from the Topography of Alpha-band Oscillations.
text_ai: Many aspects of perception and cognition are supported by activity in neural populations that are tuned to different stimulus features (e.g., orientation, spatial location, color). Goal-directed behavior, such as sustained attention, requires a mechanism for the selective prioritization of contextually appropriate representations. Here, we exploit the spatially distributed patterns of alpha-band power to infer the locus of attention on a trial-by-trial basis. Participants maintained attention to a cued location while responding to a target, with electroencephalography recorded from a sensor array. Alpha power (8–12 Hz) was estimated topographically across scalp regions, and we implemented a forward encoding model that maps retinotopic position to a pattern of alpha-topography. By fitting the model in a cross-validated framework, we reconstructed, for each trial, a probabilistic attention map over angular and eccentric coordinate space. We derive both discrete decoding accuracy for a set of labeled locations and a continuous reconstruction metric (e.g., expected location, peak-probability rank, or correlation with true focus). Across participants, decoding remained above chance during the cue–target interval, and reconstruction accuracy scaled with the magnitude of attention bias and behavioral performance. Control analyses ruled out ocular/muscle artifacts, and generalized across sessions and tasks, indicating a robust, modality-independent code. The approach provides a noninvasive readout of the focus of spatial attention from alpha topography, with implications for brain–computer interfaces and theories of rhythmic biasing in perception.

title: Successful intra-class switching among IL-17 antagonists: a multicentre, multinational, retrospective study.
text_ai: IL-17 blockers are among the newer anti-psoriatic treatment options and little is known about the interclass switching. We have thus initiated a multi-center, multi-national, retrospective study to assess the treatment response of patients who were switched from one IL-17 blocker to another. Multicenter, multinational, retrospective study of adults with plaque psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis switching between IL-17 inhibitors (secukinumab, ixekizumab, brodalumab). Data were collected from 12 centers in 7 countries (2015–2023). Primary endpoint: PASI75 at 12 weeks post-switch; secondary endpoints: PASI90/100, DLQI, and safety. A total of 312 patients were analyzed. Switch sequences included secukinumab→ixekizumab (149), ixekizumab→brodalumab (72), secukinumab→brodalumab (31), and other sequences (60). At 12 weeks, PASI75 occurred in 63% (196/312); PASI90 in 37% (115/312); PASI100 in 15% (47/312). DLQI declined from 14 to 6 (p<0.001). The switch was driven by suboptimal efficacy in 77% (n=240) and adverse events in 23% (n=72). Serious adverse events occurred in 0.6% (n=2); any adverse event occurred in 22%. By 24 weeks, 9% had discontinued; durability among initial PASI75 responders was 58% at 24 weeks. No unexpected safety signals were observed. Conclusion: Intra-class switching yields meaningful responses with acceptable safety; the 24-week durability among initial responders was favorable, and switching for inefficacy predicted better subsequent response than switching for intolerance.

title: Being a real nurse: A secondary qualitative analysis of how public health nurses rework their work identities.
text_ai: Many Western nations are emphasizing the importance of population health across health care delivery organizations and education systems. Despite significant momentum to integrate population health into nursing practice, a parallel effort to examine how these efforts impact practicing nurses' views of their professional role and work identity has not occurred. Using a secondary qualitative analysis of interview and field notes from studies with public health nurses, we reframe narratives of professional legitimacy. We apply an interpretive, identity-based thematic approach to examine how nurses articulate being 'a real nurse' amid population-level mandates, preventive-care targets. Findings reveal three core processes: (a) renegotiation of nursing authority through alignment with public health objectives, (b) boundary-work differentiating clinical skill from public health competencies, and (c) dissonance between rapid service delivery and longitudinal community care. These dynamics yield identity work marked by moral contiguity, ambiguity, and tactical compliance, while enabling outreach and advocacy. Implications for education, leadership, and policy stress recognizing identity work as legitimate professional labor and supporting sustainable role development within population health imperatives.

title: When Prompt Engineering Meets Software Engineering: CNL-P as Natural and Robust "APIs'' for Human-AI Interaction
text_ai: With the growing capabilities of large language models (LLMs), they are increasingly applied in areas like intelligent customer service, code generation, and knowledge management. Natural language (NL) prompts act as the ``APIs'' for human-LLM interaction. To improve prompt quality, best practices for prompt engineering (PE) have been developed, including writing guidelines and templates. However, NL prompts remain brittle across model families and even minor rewordings can yield divergent behavior, undermining reproducibility in human-AI workflows. This motivates CNL-P as a natural and robust API: a constrained natural language prompt that preserves user intent while enforcing machine-checkable rules on scope, format, and safety. We formalize CNL-P around a lightweight grammar with domain annotations and verifiable constraints (task boundary, output type, invocation style, length bounds, and safety guards). A prompt compiler translates CNL-P into back-end prompts for diverse LLMs, aiming to preserve semantics while bounding variance. Our contributions are fourfold: (i) a design space for CNL-P templates, including disambiguation and error-handling mechanisms; (ii) tooling for static analysis and versioned prompt libraries integrated with software engineering pipelines (linting, testing, CI); (iii) an evaluation protocol across code, reasoning, and knowledge tasks showing reduced cross-model variance and higher instruction adherence with fewer hallucinations; (iv) two human-in-the-loop case studies illustrating improved task outcomes and user trust. We discuss limitations and future directions, notably constraint scalability and domain adaptation. Explainability and governance remain open challenges.

title: Can Large Language Models Match Tutoring System Adaptivity? A Benchmarking Study
text_ai: Large Language Models (LLMs) hold promise as dynamic instructional aids. Yet, it remains unclear whether LLMs can replicate the adaptivity of intelligent tutoring systems (ITS)--where student knowledge and pedagogical strategies are explicitly modeled. We propose a prompt variation framework to assess LLM-generated instructional moves' adaptivity and pedagogical soundness across 75 real-world tutoring scenarios from an ITS. To operationalize adaptivity, we introduce a taxonomy of 12 instructional moves drawn from ITS practice (scaffolding, hint ladders, corrective feedback, and metacognitive prompts) and instantiate a prompt variation space that conditions on an inferred student knowledge state, a specified learning objective, and interaction style (hint-first, prompt-first, or mixed). Across 75 real-world ITS scenarios spanning algebra, physics, and language arts, we generate LLM responses under each prompt setting and recruit domain experts to rate outputs on adaptivity fidelity, pedagogical soundness, and cognitive-load risk. We quantify an Adaptivity Fidelity Score (AFS) that fuses alignment with the ITS’s next-best pedagogical move and contextual appropriateness, a Pedagogical Soundness Score (PSS) measuring accuracy and clarity of feedback, and a Student-Model Alignment (SMA) index capturing alignment with simulated mastery trajectories. Results show moderate adaptivity overall (AFS ≈ 0.56–0.74) with substantial sensitivity to prompt design: rationale/chain-of-thought prompts and explicit scaffolds improve alignment, whereas direct answer provision often undercuts adaptivity. Hybrid configurations that integrate retrieval of worked exemplars and explicit state tracking materially close the gap to ITS baselines.

title: Multiple single-photon generations in three-level atoms coupled to cavity with non-Markovian effects
text_ai: In this paper, we show how to generate the multiple single-photon wavepackets of arbitrary temporal shape from an optical cavity coupled with $N$ three-level atoms driven by a driving field in the non-Markovian regime. We formulate a microscopic Hamiltonian for N ladder-type atoms coupled to a single cavity mode and driven by an external field, while the cavity leaks into a structured reservoir that induces non-Markovian dynamics. We derive a non-Markovian master equation using a time-convolutionless projection operator approach and a pseudo-mode representation of the environment, yielding integro-differential equations for the cavity field and collective atomic amplitudes. The output field is obtained from a generalized input–output relation that retains memory effects. We show that for any target envelope ε(t) with unit norm and a prescribed total excitation, there exists driving protocols Ω(t) that map the initial state to a train of M single-photon wave packets emitted into the external channel, with fidelity limited by non-Markov backaction and detector inefficiencies. Numerical simulations for representative envelopes demonstrate faithful reproduction of the target profiles and controllable photon spacing. The collective enhancement of the atom–cavity coupling grows with N, enabling generation of multiple photons at rate, while non-Markov memory can be harnessed by optimal control to suppress unwanted emission and preserve high single-photon purity. The scheme is compatible with on-chip implementations and remains robust under realistic loss channels. These results lay the groundwork for scalable quantum-light sources in photonic networks.

title: DIViS: Domain Invariant Visual Servoing for Collision-Free Goal Reaching
text_ai: Robots should understand both semantics and physics to be functional in the real world. While robot platforms provide means for interacting with the physical world they cannot autonomously acquire object-level semantics without needing human. In this paper, we investigate how to minimize human effort and intervention to teach robots perform real world tasks that incorporate semantics. To address this, we propose DIViS, a two-stage framework that learns a domain-invariant visuomotor policy for goal-directed navigation with collision avoidance. We train a visual encoder to extract semantic and geometric features through self-supervised losses and cross-domain consistency, aligning representations across simulation, lab, and real world. A differentiable collision checker informs a visual servoing controller that minimizes distance to the goal while respecting obstacles. The planner uses a learned affordance map predicting safe actions and a geometric cue for obstacle-free progress. Importantly, annotation is minimized by weakly supervised demonstrations and synthetic-to-real adaptation with domain randomization. We evaluate on cluttered tabletop and indoor navigation tasks with unseen objects and backgrounds. DIViS achieves robust, collision-free goal reaching under domain shifts, surpassing baselines in success rate and trajectory efficiency, while remaining stable in real time. Ablations confirm the impact of domain-invariant encoding, collision-aware control, and reduced supervision. Our results indicate that domain invariance is key to reducing human input while guaranteeing safe, goal-directed behavior. We release accompanying data and code.
prefix: Robots should understand both semantics and physics to be functional in the real world. While robot platforms provide means for interacting with the physical world they cannot autonomously acquire object-level semantics without needing human. In this paper, we investigate how to minimize human effort and intervention to teach robots perform real world tasks that incorporate semantics.

title: Current Predictive Indices and Nomograms To Enable Personalization of Radiation Therapy for Patients With Secondary Malignant Neoplasms of the Central Nervous System: A Review.
text_ai: The proper treatment of brain metastases continues to be a challenge for oncologists given the variability of individual patients' prognoses and the variety of treatment options available to address brain metasteses. There have been efforts since the 1990s to develop prognostic indices and nomograms to help clinicians determine the best approach for individuals with secondary malignant neoplasms of the central nervous system. These tools have been validated primarily in retrospective cohorts and are robust for common primaries (lung, breast, melanoma). The adopted indices, RPA and GPA/DS-GPA, provide prognostic subgroups but show limited discrimination in the era of targeted therapies and immune checkpoint inhibitors. Contemporary nomograms and calculators have attempted to refine estimates by incorporating tumor histology, number and size of metastases, extracranial disease, performance status, and treatment variables (WBRT, SRS, or surgery) as well as evolving systemic therapy. Despite improvements, validation remains variable, and applicability to patients with rare primaries or post-treatment changes is uncertain. The review highlights gaps and suggests a framework for integrating prognostic tools into personalized RT decision-making.

There have been efforts since the 1990s to develop prognostic indices and nomograms to help clinicians determine the best approach for individuals with secondary malignant neoplasms of the central nervous system.

title: Tackling solvent effect by coupling electronic and molecular Density Functional Theory
text_ai: Solvation effect might have a tremendous influence on chemical reactions. However, precise quantum chemistry calculations are most often done either in vacuum neglecting the role of the solvent or using continuum solvent model ignoring its molecular nature. Here we present a two-way coupling between Kohn–Sham electronic density functional theory for the solute and a molecular density functional theory description of solvent. The solvation free energy is obtained from a variational functional that couples the quantum electron density to the solvent’s orientation-density distribution through electrostatic, steric, and dispersion interactions, together with solvent reorganization. Unlike continuum models, the solvent is treated explicitly at the molecular level, enabling hydrogen bonding, specific solvation motifs, and correlations in the solvent structure. The framework retains the ab initio character of electronic DFT while leveraging an MDFT representation of solvent that scales favorably with system size. We validate the method on solutes in polar and nonpolar media, evaluating solvation energies, structural signatures (solvent radial and angular distributions), and shifts in electronic and vibrational spectra. The results show a marked improvement over vacuum and continuum approaches for reaction energetics and barrier heights, capturing solvent reorganization and specific solute–solvent interactions with comparable accuracy to explicit solvent simulations but at a fraction of the cost. We discuss limitations, potential extensions to excited states and photochemical processes, and integration into standard quantum-chemistry workflows.

title: FedNST: Federated Noisy Student Training for Automatic Speech Recognition
text_ai: Federated Learning (FL) enables training state-of-the-art Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models on user devices (clients) in distributed systems, hence preventing transmission of raw user data to a central server. A key challenge facing practical adoption of FL for ASR is obtaining ground-truth labels on the clients. FedNST introduces a federated semi-supervised regime that marries Noisy Student Training with standard FL optimization to exploit unlabeled client data without exchanging raw audio. In each round, a global teacher, instantiated as an exponential moving average of the clients’ last-models, emits pseudo-labels for the clients’ unlabeled audio. Local students are trained with a joint objective: supervised loss on labeled utterances and a pseudo-label loss on unlabeled samples, using strong data augmentation (SpecAugment, noise injection) and NST-style noise to improve generalization. After local optimization, updates are uploaded and aggregated (FedAvg/FedProx) to refresh the global model, while the teacher is updated by federated EMA. Confidence-based pseudo-label filtering and weighting address non-IID data. Results on LibriSpeech and multilingual benchmarks show WER gains with fewer labels.

title: Significant core shift variability in parsec-scale jets of active galactic nuclei
text_ai: The apparent position of jet base (core) in radio-loud active galactic nuclei changes with frequency because of synchrotron self-absorption. Studying this `core shift` effect enables us to reconstruct properties of the jet regions close to the central engine. To quantify temporal changes, we analyze a uniform, multi-epoch, multi-frequency VLBI dataset for a sample of bright, radio-loud AGN. Core positions are measured relative to stationary, optically thin jet features using precise alignment across 4.6–43 GHz. The frequency dependence of the core offset is fit with the synchrotron-self-absorption framework, yielding the core-position offset Ω_r and the index k_r that trace the inner-jet stratification. Assuming conical geometry and approximate equipartition, Ω_r is translated into the magnetic-field strength B1 at 1 pc and the electron-density normalization N1. We detect significant core-shift variability in a substantial fraction of sources, with Δr_core between frequency pairs fluctuating on timescales of months to years. In several objects, shifts imply magnetic-field and density changes at sub-parsec distances by factors of order unity to a few. Variability often accompanies compact flares and evolving jet component speeds, consistent with shocks and changing Doppler boosting that modulate the core's optical depth. Our results show that core shifts are dynamic tracers of conditions near the jet base and must be accounted for when inferring launching scales, magnetic-energy transport, and jet collimation in parsec-scale AGN.

title: REPOSE: Distributed Top-k Trajectory Similarity Search with Local Reference Point Tries
text_ai: Trajectory similarity computation is a fundamental component in a variety of real-world applications, such as ridesharing, road planning, and transportation optimization. Recent advances in mobile devices have enabled an unprecedented increase in the amount of available trajectory data such that efficient query processing can no longer be supported by a single machine. REPOSE orchestrates distributed indexing and search by partitioning trajectory data across workers and constructing Local Reference Point Tries at each node to compactly encode reference trajectories and support top-k pruning decisions. The LRPT enables reuse of reference prefixes across queries and supports incremental updates without rebuilding the index. We introduce a bound-driven pruning strategy that computes lower bounds on the distance to any trajectory via local references, together with upper bounds to cull candidates early. The query plan proceeds in phases: pruning at workers, followed by an aggregator for ranking, thereby reducing inter-node communication. We provide correctness guarantees, analyze communication and time complexity, and validate REPOSE on real-world datasets, achieving near-linear scalability and speedups over distributed approaches.

Recent advances in mobile devices have enabled an unprecedented increase in the amount of available trajectory data such that efficient query processing can no longer be supported by a single machine.

title: Economic Rationality under Specialization: Evidence of Decision Bias in AI Agents
text_ai: In the study by Chen et al. (2023) [01], the large language model GPT demonstrated economic rationality comparable to or exceeding the average human level in tasks such as budget allocation and risk preference. We design a suite of decision problems spanning budget allocation, portfolio choice, and risk-taking, deploying domain-specialized agents and LLMs. Rigorously comparing expected utility maximization with prospect-theoretic predictions, we quantify deviations associated with loss aversion, probability weighting, and framing effects. Across application domains—finance, supply chain operations, healthcare, and public policy—we observe that specialization improves alignment with relevant rationality yet induces systematic biases when contexts demand transfer or novel constraints. In particular, agents trained with reward shaping toward efficiency exhibit risk-neutral or risk-seeking propensities that diverge from normative benchmarks, suggesting bias emergent from optimization pressure and constraint leakage. These results challenge claims of AI economic rationality and imply that rationality is contingent on training objectives, prompt structure, and environmental structure. They offer guidance for designing governance frameworks and economic models that accommodate artificial agents' decision biases.

title: Measurement of the Higgs boson mass with $H \rightarrow \gamma\gamma$ decays in 140 fb$^{-1}$ of $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV $pp$ collisions with the ATLAS detector
text_ai: The mass of the Higgs boson is measured in the $H\to\gamma\gamma$ decay channel, exploiting the high resolution of the invariant mass of photon pairs reconstructed from the decays of Higgs bosons produced in proton-proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV. The mass is extracted from a maximum-likelihood fit to the diphoton invariant-mass spectrum, using a per-event mass-resolution categorization that ranks events by expected resolution. A data-driven background description is combined with simulation-based signal shapes, with calibration and validation performed in sidebands and in dedicated control samples. Photons are calibrated with a multistep scheme anchored to Z→ee decays, conversions, and in situ corrections, and per-event resolution is incorporated into the fit. The analysis uses the full 140 fb−1 data sample from LHC Run 2 at √s = 13 TeV with ATLAS. The measured mass, combining all categories, has a total uncertainty with the dominant contribution from the photon-energy scale and calibration. The result is compatible with the Standard Model expectation and with previous ATLAS measurements within uncertainties.

title: Decoupled two-dimensional superconductivity and continuous melting transitions in layered superconductors immersed in a parallel magnetic field
text_ai: Possible phases and the B-T phase diagram of interlayer Josephson vortices induced by a magnetic field parallel to the superconducting layers are investigated by Monte Carlo simulations based on the anisotropic, frustrated XY model. Three phases are identified: a three-dimensionally ordered Josephson vortex lattice with interlayer coherence at low temperature, a decoupled regime in which superconductivity remains quasi-long-range within each layer but interlayer phase coherence vanishes, and a normal vortex liquid at high temperature where all coherent features are lost. The B–T phase diagram exhibits a continuous decoupling line T_d(B) separating the 3D lattice from the 2D-like superconducting regime, followed by a melting line T_m(B) in which the intra-layer Josephson vortex lattice loses positional order. Finite-size scaling of the in-layer helicity modulus and of vortex-correlation functions supports KT-like (or 2D XY-type) critical behavior at T_m, with a universal jump of the in-plane stiffness and algebraic decay of intra-layer correlations in the decoupled phase. The interlayer stiffness diminishes continuously along T_d, signaling a crossover from 3D coherence to effectively decoupled 2D sheets governed by fluctuating interlayer phase differences. The interlayer structure factor shows sharp Bragg peaks in the 3D lattice, which broaden and eventually vanish as the system enters the decoupled and melted regimes, while in-plane correlations retain their distinctive quasi-long-range character in the decoupled state. The results persist across a broad range of anisotropy and system sizes, underscoring a robust mechanism for continuous melting and a decoupled two-dimensional superconducting phase in layered superconductors under a parallel magnetic field.

title: Language Embedded 3D Gaussians for Open-Vocabulary Scene Understanding
text_ai: Open-vocabulary querying in 3D space is challenging but essential for scene understanding tasks such as object localization and segmentation. Language-embedded scene representations have made progress by incorporating language features into 3D spaces. However, their efficacy heavily depends on neural networks that are resource-intensive in training and rendering. To address this, we introduce Language Embedded 3D Gaussians (LE3DG), a compact, differentiable scene representation that pairs a finite mixture of 3D Gaussians with language-conditioned priors. Each Gaussian encodes a localized affinity in 3D space via learnable mean and covariance, plus a light appearance embedding accessible through a shared language encoder. Given a text query, a small projection predicts per-Gaussian scores from the query embedding, enabling open-vocabulary grounding without full-field neural radiance fields. Rendering and reasoning proceed through tractable volumetric compositing, producing differentiable score maps for object localization and voxel-level segmentation. LE3DG delivers competitive open-vocabulary performance while reducing training time and memory relative to encoder–decoder scene networks, and generalizes to unseen phrases via frozen language representations.

Language-embedded scene representations have made progress by incorporating language features into 3D spaces. However, their efficacy heavily depends on neural networks that are resource-intensive in training and rendering.

title: Learning Deep Representations of Fine-grained Visual Descriptions
text_ai: State-of-the-art methods for zero-shot visual recognition formulate learning as a joint embedding problem of images and side information. In these formulations the current best complement to visual features are attributes: manually encoded vectors describing shared characteristics among categories. Despite good performance, attributes have limitations: (1) finer-grained recognition requires commensurately more attributes, and (2) attributes do not provide a natural language interface. We propose to learn deep representations that jointly model images and fine-grained textual descriptions collected from open-domain corpora. Our approach encodes images with a CNN, encodes descriptions with a bidirectional LSTM, and projects both into a shared embedding. A cross-modal attention module aligns descriptive phrases with visual regions, producing discriminative region-level descriptors. Training uses a margin-based ranking loss over seen categories, supplemented by a description reconstruction objective to preserve semantic fidelity. At test time, unseen categories are recognized by matching their natural-language descriptions to image embeddings, enabling zero-shot inference without hand-crafted attributes and providing a natural language interface for querying. Empirical results demonstrate robust gains for unseen classes.

title: Hyper Strategy Logic
text_ai: Strategy logic (SL) is a powerful temporal logic that enables strategic reasoning in multi-agent systems. SL supports explicit (first-order) quantification over strategies and provides a logical framework to express many important properties such as Nash equilibria, dominant strategies, etc. While in SL the same strategy can be used in multiple strategy profiles, each such profile is evaluated w.r.t. the same history, yielding a concrete outcome that may depend on the choices of all agents. Hyper Strategy Logic (HSL) extends SL by permitting hyper-quantification over strategies across branches and agents, enabling cross-profile reasoning. We present a formal syntax and trace-based semantics for hyper-quantified strategies over admissible plays. The framework supports binding, guarded quantification, and composition operators on families of strategies. We establish decidability results under bounded horizons and provide automata-based model-checking techniques. Illustrative examples from coalition formation, resilience under perturbation, and information-flow constraints highlight its expressiveness. Compared to SL, HSL specifications when hyper-quantification ranges over single profiles, remaining compatible with standard model-checkers via reductions to nested automata.

title: Saliency-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Visual Explanations
text_ai: Explainable AI (XAI) has gained significant attention for providing insights into the decision-making processes of deep learning models, particularly for image classification tasks through visual explanations visualized by saliency maps. Despite their success, challenges remain due to the lack of annotated datasets and standardized evaluation pipelines. Saliency-Bench is a unified benchmark that integrates (i) a curated collection of datasets with high-quality, human-annotated saliency maps aligned to model explanations, (ii) a standardized suite of evaluation metrics and protocols spanning faithfulness, localization accuracy, and robustness—including AUC variants, NSS, CC, KL divergence, and perceptual similarity—and (iii) an end-to-end evaluation toolkit with ready-to-run baselines, reproducible experiment scripts, and a public leaderboard. It also provides domain-aware splits to assess generalization across scenes, object scales, and textures, as well as support for both automatic proxies and human judgments. Through comprehensive experiments across architectures and explanation methods, Saliency-Bench reveals substantial metric- and dataset-dependent discrepancies in method rankings, emphasizes the influence of annotation quality, and offers a principled platform to drive the development of more faithful, stable, and actionable visual explanations.

title: Less or More: Towards Glanceable Explanations for LLM Recommendations Using Ultra-Small Devices
text_ai: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown remarkable potential in recommending everyday actions as personal AI assistants, while Explainable AI (XAI) techniques are being increasingly utilized to help users understand why a recommendation is given. Personal AI assistants today are often located on ultra-small devices such as smartwatches, which have limited screen space. To address this, we investigate the design space of glanceable explanations that preserve causal rationales while remaining legible within a glance. We operationalize glanceability as a triad of brevity, salience, and actionability, restricted to compact typography and iconography suitable for 1–2 line display on ultra-small screens. We compare two explanation modalities for LLM-driven recommendations: (i) minimalist one-sentence rationales and (ii) layered on-demand disclosures that can be expanded via taps or haptics. A modular rendering pipeline is implemented on smartwatch platforms and evaluated across health and productivity tasks. We evaluate with a mixed-methods protocol: subjective measures of perceived understandability, trust, cognitive load, and satisfaction. Objective measures include time-to-interpretation, accuracy of action prediction, and interruption rate. We also study the influence of interaction modality (tap, crown rotate, or glance) on uptake and fatigue. Results show concise glanceable rationales enable faster decisions while preserving baseline trust. Whereas layered disclosures improve detailed comprehension without overwhelming brief glances. The paper closes with design guidelines and an evaluation framework for glanceable XAI on ultra-small devices.

title: Insights into the effects of sleep disordered breathing on the brain in infants and children: Imaging and cerebral oxygenation measurements.
text_ai: Sleep disordered breathing (SDB) is a common condition in infants and children. SDB encompasses a spectrum of respiratory disorders, which are defined as either obstructive or central in nature. Obstructive SDB ranges in severity from primary snoring (PS), to obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). Here we combine imaging markers with cerebral oxygenation measurements to characterize its impact on the developing brain. Methods: a cross-sectional cohort of infants and children across PS, OSA, and controls was recruited. Overnight polysomnography quantified sleep fragmentation and desaturation; near-infrared spectroscopy tracked cerebral oxygenation. Structural MRI included voxel-based morphometry and diffusion tensor imaging to assess gray and white matter integrity, complemented by resting-state fMRI. Results: compared with controls, children with OSA showed reduced gray matter volume in prefrontal and temporal regions and decreased fractional anisotropy in major tracts, notably the corpus callosum and superior longitudinal fasciculus. Resting-state analyses revealed altered connectivity within the default mode and executive networks. Across groups, greater desaturation burden correlated with lower brain volumes and poorer cognitive scores, especially in attention and working memory. In infants, SDB related to slower cortical maturation and myelination. Interventions (adenotonsillectomy or CPAP) yielded improved nocturnal oxygenation and partial normalization of imaging measures at short-term follow-up, suggesting reversibility, though some alterations persisted. These findings underscore brain-level consequences of pediatric SDB and the value of integrated imaging–oxygenation phenotyping for risk stratification.

title: General convergence analysis of stochastic first order methods for composite optimization
text_ai: In this paper we consider stochastic composite convex optimization problems with the objective function satisfying a stochastic bounded gradient condition, with or without a quadratic functional growth property. These models include the most well-known classes of objective functions analyzed in the literature: non-smooth Lipschitz functions and composition of a (potentially) non-smooth function and a smooth function, with or without strong convexity. Building on a unifying Lyapunov framework, we derive a generic descent inequality that bounds the expected distance to the optimal set by a contraction term plus a controlled stochastic error, with constants determined solely by the gradient bound and the step size. This yields a single, coherent analysis that covers SGD with proximal steps, stochastic mirror-descent, and their accelerated or variance-reduced variants, without requiring smoothness of all components or strong convexity a priori. We establish that, under convexity, the expected objective residual decays at a sublinear rate that matches the standard stochastic optimization bounds when appropriate steps are chosen, while the presence of a quadratic functional growth modulus guarantees linear convergence in expectation for the same class of methods. For non-smooth terms, the proximal operator can be computed inexactly with summable error without loss of the rate, and minibatch or block-coordinate implementations fit naturally into the framework. The theory thereby unifies and extends known results, clarifying how SBG bounds and QFG govern convergence across composite stochastic problems.

title: Unraveling the Complexity of Imported Malaria Infections by Amplicon Deep Sequencing.
text_ai: Imported malaria and recurrent infections are becoming an emerging issue in many malaria non-endemic countries. This study aimed to determine the molecular patterns of the imported malaria infections and recurrence. Blood samples were collected from patients with imported malaria infections during 2016-2018 in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China. DNA was extracted from whole blood and subjected to amplicon deep sequencing of a panel of polymorphic loci tailored to the dominant species in the region (P. falciparum: msp1 block 2, msp2, glurp; P. vivax: msp1P and msp3α). Libraries were prepared and sequenced on an Illumina MiSeq platform. Reads were processed with a validated haplotype-calling pipeline to deconvolute mixed infections and correct for artefacts; haplotypes with a relative abundance ≥1% were retained. Complexity of infection (MOI) was inferred from the maximum number of distinct haplotypes per specimen, and within-host diversity was summarized by the Fws index. For paired baseline–recurrence samples, haplotype overlap across loci classified episodes as relapse/recrudescence or reinfection. Results showed extensive multiclonality, with multiclonal infections in a notable fraction of samples. Among 22 paired recurrence episodes, 12 retained concordant haplotypes across all loci, indicating relapse/recrudescence, while 10 displayed non-overlapping haplotypes, consistent with reinfection. This approach enhances attribution of recurrence etiology and supports refined surveillance and control of imported malaria. These findings inform management of imported malaria and border screening.

title: MedHallu: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Detecting Medical Hallucinations in Large Language Models
text_ai: Advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) and their increasing use in medical question-answering necessitate rigorous evaluation of their reliability. A critical challenge lies in hallucination, where models generate plausible yet factually incorrect outputs. In the medical domain, this poses serious risks to patient safety and clinical decision-making. MedHallu comprises clinical vignettes spanning common medical specialties, derived from textbooks, guidelines, and clinician-validated sources to serve as gold standards for factual correctness, evidence provenance, and safety-critical conclusions. Each item is annotated for (i) the presence and type of hallucination (e.g., fact substitution, misinterpretation, missing contraindication), and (ii) the required evidence trail. Detection is operationalized through three paradigms: output-level plausibility calibrated to gold facts; knowledge-grounded verification against curated medical knowledge bases; and inference-trace analysis to assess reliability. We benchmark several leading LLMs under zero-, one-, and few-shot settings, revealing substantial ungrounded claims and domain-specific variability. MedHallu offers open datasets, standardized metrics, and evaluation protocols to support reproducible, safety-oriented medical AI research. The benchmark also enables trackable benchmarking against evolving clinical standards globally.

title: Parallelized Wireless Sensing System for Continuous Monitoring of Microtissue Spheroids.
text_ai: Currently, the use of electrical readout methods for the investigation of microtissue spheroids in combination with lab automation tools is hindered by the cable connections that are required to interrogate the on-chip-integrated electrodes. To overcome this limitation, we developed a wireless sensor scheme, which can detect the size variation of microtissues during long-term culturing and drug exposure assays. The system comprises a parallel array of miniaturized sensing nodes integrated with standard microtiter-plate formats and interrogated by a single wireless reader. Each node uses paired microfabricated electrodes to form a noninvasive impedance sensor, allowing estimation of spheroid size from dielectric contrast and scattering phenomena without optical access. The nodes are passively powered by inductive coupling and communicate measurements through a time-multiplexed protocol to a central controller, minimizing heat and electromagnetic exposure. Soft-packaging and biocompatible encapsulation ensure autoclave compatibility and long-term stability in culture. Calibration against optical diameter measurements yields a sub-5% error in the 200–600 µm range. In a 48-well parallel assay, the system tracks growth curves and drug-induced size changes with subhourly sampling, enabling real-time kinetic analysis. Embedded signal processing extracts radius estimates from impedance magnitude and phase, with drift compensation and temperature correction. The platform integrates with lab automation workflows, reduces cabling, and increases screening throughput for microtissue-based assays. The modular architecture supports future expansion to multiplexed sensing modalities.

title: Annama H chondrite - mineralogy, physical properties, cosmic ray exposure, and parent body history
text_ai: The fall of the Annama meteorite occurred early morning (local time) on April 19, 2014 on the Kola Peninsula (Russia). Based on mineralogy and physical properties, Annama is a typical H chondrite. It has a high Ar-Ar age of 4.4 Ga. Petrography shows a predominantly equilibrated H-chondrite texture with abundant chondrules embedded in a fine-grained silicate matrix. Olivine (Fa around 16–18) and orthopyroxene (Fs around 14–16) dominate, with minor troilite and kamacite–taenite blebs. Glass-bearing mesostasis and rare shock veins attest to moderate impact processing (S4). The bulk composition and modal abundances are typical for H chondrites, with limited sulfide inclusions. Measured physical properties yield a bulk density near 3.2 g cm−3 and low porosity (<2%), consistent with a compact, brecciated specimen. Noble gas cosmogenic data indicate a single, relatively short CRE history (a few million years), compatible with ejection from an H-chondrite parent body after shallow burial and rapid disruption. Integrated chronometry (Ar-Ar 4.4 Ga) and cooling indicators constrain rapid cooling and subsequent exposure in a small-body regolith.

title: Closure of Secundum Atrial Septal Defects by Using the Occlutech Occluder Devices in More Than 1300 Patients: The IRFACODE Project: A Retrospective Case Series.
text_ai: The Occlutech Figulla ASD device series (OFSO) shows an improved device design for interventional ASD closure, larger follow-up series are missing. We retrospectively reviewed the feasibility, safety, implantation properties, results, and follow-up of ASD closure using Occlutech devices over a 5 year period by establishing a multi-institutional collaborative result registry with 16 contributing centers from 11 countries (IRFACODE). Methods: a retrospective multicenter registry of consecutive patients undergoing transcatheter closure of secundum ASD with Occlutech OFSO devices at 16 centers from 11 countries during 2015–2020. Data collected included demographics, defect anatomy, rim adequacy, device type and size, access route, procedural success, fluoroscopy time, hospital stay, and imaging. Endpoints: acute procedural success defined as device deployment without intraprocedural rupture or embolization; device-related adverse events; residual shunt at discharge and during follow-up. Follow-up visits occurred at 1, 6, and 12 months and annually thereafter. Results: 1,320 patients were included. Overall procedural success was 99.2% with immediate closure 99.5% after final device release. Major adverse events occurred in 0.6% (device embolization 0.2%); erosion, tamponade, and death were not observed. Minor residual shunt at discharge 3.8% decreased to 0.9% at last follow-up. Median hospital stay 1 day; median fluoroscopy time 16 minutes. Conclusions: In a large, real-world cohort, OFSO devices enabled safe and effective ASD closure with low complication rates, durable closure, and favorable mid-term functional outcomes.

title: The influence of dysbiosis on kidney stones that risk up renal cell carcinoma (RCC).
text_ai: Kidney stone is a common urological condition, the prevalence and incidence of which has escalated in the last few years due to dietary habits and other related medical conditions such as obesity and diabetes mellitus. It is a chronic disease which leads to loss of kidney function(s) and nephrectomy. Emerging data indicate that dysbiosis, with reduced oxalate-degrading taxa and a pro-inflammatory microbiota, contributes to stone pathogenesis by increasing intestinal oxalate absorption and urinary supersaturation. Conversely, certain microbial shifts may modulate lithogenic risk through short-chain fatty acid production, bile acid signaling, and ammonia generation, thereby affecting renal epithelial injury and crystal retention. Moreover, chronic lithiasis establishes a persistent inflammatory milieu that can facilitate oncogenic pathways and genomic instability, potentially elevating the risk of renal cell carcinoma (RCC) in susceptible individuals. This study synthesizes evidence on how intestinal microbiota perturbations intersect stone disease with RCC risk, and evaluates microbiome-targeted strategies for prevention. Our findings underscore the need for profiling in stone formers to clarify causal links.

It is a chronic disease which leads to loss of kidney function(s) and nephrectomy.

title: Strong versus Weak Coupling Confinement in N=2 Supersymmetric QCD
text_ai: We consider N=2 supersymmetric QCD with the gauge group SU(N_c)=SU(N+1) and N_f number of quark matter multiplets, being perturbed by a small mass term for the adjoint matter, so that its Coulomb branch shrinks to a number of isolated vacua. We map each vacuum to a Seiberg–Witten curve factorization and identify the mutually local BPS states that condense in the infrared. In the weakly coupled region, monopole or dyon condensation triggers confinement of electric charges, producing flux tubes whose tensions scale with the magnetic charge and N-ality of the representation. By contrast, at strong coupling a magnetic dual description remains reliable in a subset of vacua and confinement proceeds through a different pattern of condensates, including non-Abelian components that leave a residual gauge symmetry unconfined. We quantify these mechanisms by computing order parameters, such as monopole or dyon condensates, Wilson loop behavior, and the resulting string tensions, comparing semiclassical estimates to exact Seiberg–Witten data. Across the r-vacua, confinement phenomenology exhibits a continuous interpolation between the two regimes, consistent with dual descriptions.

title: Combining cues to judge distance and direction in an immersive virtual reality environment.
text_ai: When we move, the visual direction of objects in the environment can change substantially. Compared with our understanding of depth perception, the problem the visual system faces in computing this change is relatively poorly understood. Here, we tested the extent to which participants' judgments of visual direction could be predicted by standard cue combination rules. Across a range of self-motion trajectories, including lateral translation and forward motion, observers judged the direction to a flashed target after movement onset. We manipulated cue availability by degrading or removing sources of directional information: optic flow, perspective and texture cues, and proprioceptive/motor signals simulated with latency or jitter. These manipulations yielded conditions with differing cue reliabilities. Predictions used a Bayesian cue–integration model weighting cues by reliability and adapting to scene and motion context. Across conditions, responses were predicted by the model. When texture or optic flow is degraded, reliance shifts toward perspective and motor cues, maintaining accurate direction judgments; conversely, rich motion cues reduce susceptibility to perspective distortions. The model captured trial-by-trial variance and biases, such as under- or over-rotations at large angles, arising from nonlinear mappings between world- and head-centered updates. Overall, findings indicate updating visual direction during ego-motion in immersive VR follows near-optimal cue integration, extending cue-combination theory to dynamic, multisensory contexts. These results extend cue integration theory to active, immersive viewing.

title: Clustering, order conditions, and languages of interval exchanges
text_ai: For any interval exchange transformation $T$ (standard or generalized), if we define a morphism $\phi$ from the set of letters to the set of the return words of a word in the natural coding, respecting the lexicographical order, the word $\phi v$ clusters (for the Burrows-Wheeler transform) for the permutation of $T$ if and only if the word $v$ clusters for the permutation of the induced map of $T$ on the cylinder $[w]$. Using this criterion, we prove that clustering is invariant under the canonical projection associated with any induced map on a cylinder, provided the morphism respects the natural order of return words. We derive necessary and sufficient order conditions on the induced permutation that ensure equivalence of clustering between T and its first-return map to [w]. Consequently, the Burrows–Wheeler transform applied to the natural coding of an IET or its generalized counterpart yields the same collection of clusterings as that obtained from the language of return words. This establishes a structural link between interval exchanges, their languages, and BWT-based statistics.
