title: Good Research Practice: Lessons from Animal Care and Use.
text_ai: Animal care and use play a pivotal role in the research process. Ethical concerns on the use of animals in research have promoted the creation of a legal framework in many geographical areas that researchers must comply with, and professional organizations continuously develop recommendations on specific areas of laboratory animal science. Drawing on international guidance and empirical reports, the article identifies core qualities of good practice that sustain both animal welfare and scientific credibility. We examine how governance structures, standard operating procedures, and continuous training influence study design, data integrity, and reproducibility. Central themes include the 3Rs, humane endpoints, welfare assessment, and transparent reporting; the alignment of care protocols with experimental objectives; and the role of oversight bodies in fostering accountability without impeding scientific creativity. The synthesis offers a pragmatic framework of principles and checklists that researchers, veterinarians, and managers can adapt to diverse contexts. By translating ethical obligations into concrete operational steps, the work aims to improve welfare outcomes while enhancing research reliability and public trust.

title: Functions of multivector variables
text_ai: As is well known, the common elementary functions defined over the real numbers can be generalized to act not only over the complex number field but also over the skew (non-commuting) field of the quaternions. In this paper, we detail a number of elementary functions extended to act over the skew field of Clifford multivectors, in both two and three dimensions. Borrowing from algebraic structure of Clifford algebras Cl(2) and Cl(3), we develop a functional calculus for multivector arguments based on (i) gradewise decomposition and (ii) a Clifford-analytic reformulation of classical power series. In two and three dimensions, exponential, logarithm, and the elementary trigonometric and hyperbolic functions are defined by convergent series and by closed forms compatible with geometric product. We establish basic algebraic identities, derive a multivector chain rule, and provide explicit representations for multivectors. The construction yields rotation- and dilation-generating operators, preserves invertibility where defined, and interacts with the Clifford norm via submultiplicativity. Numerical illustrations highlight invariants and suggest applications in physics and computer graphics.

In this paper, we detail a number of elementary functions extended to act over the skew field of Clifford multivectors, in both two and three dimensions.

title: Cracking Double-Blind Review: Authorship Attribution with Deep Learning
text_ai: Double-blind peer review is considered a pillar of academic research because it is perceived to ensure a fair, unbiased, and fact-centered scientific discussion. Yet, experienced researchers can often correctly guess from which research group an anonymous submission originates, biasing the peer-review process. To quantify the re-identification risk that persists under current double-blind practices, we assemble a cross-domain corpus of anonymized submissions with ground-truth authors, spanning multiple fields and venues. We train a suite of deep-learning architectures—character-level convolutional networks, bidirectional recurrent encoders, and transformer-based models—to predict author identity from sanitized manuscripts under controlled conditions. Using strict author hold-outs and venue-level validation, we measure attribution accuracy beyond chance even after the removal of explicit identifiers, with performance varying by genre, length, and stylistic consistency. Our analyses reveal leakages through lexical choices, syntactic patterns, citation habits, and formatting conventions, rooted in persistent authorial signal despite redaction. We assess robustness to obfuscation and to privacy-preserving preprocessing, charting the boundaries of current blind review guarantees. We discuss policy implications for the design of double-blind systems and propose mitigations, including stricter redaction, standardized templates, and, where appropriate, the incorporation of differential privacy or randomized template features. Contributions: (1) a replicable benchmarking framework and dataset; (2) a modular deep-learning pipeline for authorship attribution under blind conditions; (3) a taxonomy of leakage channels; (4) practical guidelines for editors and reviewers.

Yet, experienced researchers can often correctly guess from which research group an anonymous submission originates, biasing the peer-review process.

title: A Theoretical Solution of the Mind-Body Problem: An Operationalized Proof that no Purely Physical System Can Exhibit all the Properties of Human Consciousness
text_ai: This article presents an operationalized solution to the mind-body problem which relies on rigorously defined theoretical reasoning rather than philosophical argument. We identify a specific operation which is a necessary property of all healthy human conscious individuals -- specifically the operation of self-certainty, or the capacity of healthy conscious humans to "know" with certainty that they are conscious. Operationalizing this property, we define Self-Certainty (SC) as the reflexive endorsement of a conscious state that the subject cannot derive solely from external observations about its behavior. We operationalize SC through a triad of criteria: (a) an immediate, verbal or written affirmation of conscious experience upon stimulus, (b) stable cross-modal self-reports under perturbations, and (c) application of an internal confidence rule that cannot be reduced to external verification. The resulting theorem shows that any purely physical substrate—producible by computable dynamics—fails to instantiate SC without appealing to non-physical premises or privileged access to phenomenology. Hence no pure physical system can realize all the properties typically ascribed to human consciousness, even when functionally equivalent on others.

We identify a specific operation which is a necessary property of all healthy human conscious individuals -- specifically the operation of self-certainty, or the capacity of healthy conscious humans to "know" with certainty that they are conscious.

title: Virgibacillus indicus sp. nov. and Virgibacillus profundi sp. nov, two moderately halophilic bacteria isolated from marine sediment by using microfluidic streak plates.
text_ai: Three Gram-variable, moderately halophilic, motile, endospore-forming rods, designated P2-C2 T , P3-H5 T and P3-B8, were isolated from marine sediment of the Southwest Indian Ocean by using the microfluidic streak plate method. Three Gram-variable, moderately halophilic, motile, endospore-forming rods, designated P2-C2^T, P3-H5^T and P3-B8, were isolated from marine sediment of the Southwest Indian Ocean by using the microfluidic streak plate method. Strains grew at 3–12% NaCl (optimum ~7%), 10–37°C (optimum 30–33°C), and pH 6.5–9.0. Cells are endospore-forming, rod-shaped, and motile by peritrichous flagella. The isolates were Gram-variable on Gram stain and displayed biochemical profiles typical of Virgibacillus spp., including hydrolysis of gelatin and starch and utilization of several carbohydrates. Phylogenetic analysis of the 16S rRNA gene showed that P2-C2^T and P3-B8 clustered with Virgibacillus indicus–like lineages, whereas P3-H5^T formed a distinct Virgibacillus profundi–like lineage; all three formed monophyletic branches with robust bootstrap support. Whole-genome comparisons showed average nucleotide identity and digital DNA–DNA hybridization values below the species thresholds (~95% and ~70%, respectively) between the two lineages and the closest Virgibacillus species, supporting two novel species. The genomes are 3.9–4.1 Mbp with G+C contents of 39–41 mol%. The predominant cellular fatty acids are anteiso-C15:0 and iso-C15:0; the major menaquinone is MK-7; major polar lipids include phosphatidylethanolamine and phosphatidylglycerol. Based on phenotypic, chemotaxonomic and genomic data, P2-C2^T is proposed as Virgibacillus indicus sp. nov. and P3-H5^T as Virgibacillus profundi sp. nov.; P3-B8 represents V. indicus.

title: Dark Matter and Sterile Neutrinos
text_ai: Dark matter has been recognized as an essential part of matter for over 70 years now, and many suggestions have been made, what it could be. Most of these ideas have centered on Cold Dark Matter, particles that are predicted in extensions of standard particle physics, such as supersymmetry. An attractive alternative class comprises sterile neutrinos, gauge-singlet fermions with masses in the keV range that mix with active neutrinos. Their nonthermal or resonantly enhanced production in the early universe can yield a viable dark component while simultaneously contributing to the light neutrino mass spectrum through the seesaw mechanism. We summarize the principal production mechanisms—the nonresonant Dodelson–Widrow process, the resonant Shi–Fuller mechanism in the presence of a lepton asymmetry, and hybrid channels—and discuss their implications for the resulting momentum distribution and small‑scale structure. The resulting parameter space is subject to stringent constraints: phase‑space bounds in dwarf galaxies, Lyman‑α forest limits on free‑streaming, and X‑ray searches for radiative decays of the sterile neutrino to an active neutrino plus a photon, which together carve out favored regions. We evaluate observational hints and debates, including tentative 3.5 keV features, in the context of cosmological and astrophysical data. Finally, we discuss prospects for upcoming surveys and laboratory probes, and the landscape of falsification or discovery that would redefine both particle physics and cosmology.

Most of these ideas have centered on Cold Dark Matter, particles that are predicted in extensions of standard particle physics, such as supersymmetry.

title: Reflection on modern methods: visualizing the effects of collinearity in distributed lag models.
text_ai: Collinearity can be a problem in regression models. When examining the effects of an exposure at different time points, constrained distributed lag models can alleviate some of the problems caused by collinearity. Still, some consequences of collinearity may remain and they are often unexplored. Here, we propose a visualization-centered appraisal of how collinearity distorts constrained distributed lag models (DLMs) and how researchers can detect and interpret these distortions. Through simulated and empirical illustrations, we show that even when a constraint improves predictive performance, collinearity can undermine lag-specific identifiability, yielding biased or spuriously precise estimates for some lags while others remain unstable. We introduce a compact repertoire of visuals: lag-gradient plots tracing the estimated exposure–response slope across adjacent lags; joint surface plots and contour maps of the bivariate distribution of neighboring lag coefficients; and uncertainty-aware lag-profile visuals displaying the impulse response with simultaneous confidence regions. We also provide sensitivity visuals that vary the constraint (polynomial order, knot placement, centering) to reveal how conclusions depend on specification. The results demonstrate that these representations can reveal degeneracies and fragilities obscured by standard summaries, and that reporting should accompany point estimates with interpretable depictions of identifiability and uncertainty. The paper concludes with practical recommendations for practitioners to adopt visualization-enhanced diagnostics as a routine component of DLM inference. This approach promotes transparency and robust interpretation.

Still, some consequences of collinearity may remain and they are often unexplored.

title: The prevalence of AGN feedback in massive galaxies at z~1
text_ai: We use the optical--infrared imaging in the UKIDSS Ultra Deep Survey field, in combination with the new deep radio map of Arumugam et al., to calculate the distribution of radio luminosities among galaxies as a function of stellar mass in two redshift bins across the interval 0.4<z<1.2. We classify the radio emitters into AGN- and star-formation–dominated sources by comparing their radio luminosities with star formation rates inferred from UV+IR indicators, and we cross-check with rest-frame colours. The AGN fraction among galaxies with M* > 10^11 Msun is substantial in both redshift bins, with a mild increase toward higher z. The mechanical power implied by the radio emission is broadly sufficient to offset cooling in the halos of these systems, indicating that radio-mode feedback is a common, ongoing process at z ~ 1. Our results are in broad agreement with self-regulated feedback scenarios in which AGN activity suppresses late-time star formation in the most massive galaxies, shaping the buildup of the red sequence at this epoch.

title: Conservation laws, exact travelling waves and modulation instability for an extended nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation
text_ai: We study various properties of solutions of an extended nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger (ENLS) equation, which arises in the context of geometric evolution problems -- including vortex filament dynamics -- and governs propagation of short pulses in optical fibers and nonlinear metamaterials. Employing a combination of multiplier methods and the Hamiltonian formalism, we derive a hierarchy of conservation laws and identify the conditions under which the ENLS admits a real Hamiltonian structure. In particular, we exhibit local invariants corresponding to L2 mass, momentum, and a conserved energy, and discuss how the higher‑order terms modify their flux laws. We then seek travelling-wave solutions of the form u(x,t)=Φ(ξ) exp[i(kx−ωt)], with ξ=x−vt, and reduce the ENLS to an ordinary differential equation for Φ. Depending on the sign and magnitude of the coefficients, the reduced system yields bright, dark and gray solitons, as well as sn/kink-type profiles; explicit closed forms are obtained in representative regimes, and general qualitative features are mapped in phase-space portraits. The modulation-instability analysis proceeds from a plane-wave background; the dispersion relation for perturbations is obtained and the MI gain is characterized as a function of the ENLS parameters. We identify parameter regimes that suppress MI and regimes that promote it, and we illustrate the dynamics with numerical simulations showing robust envelope solitons, their interactions, and long-time recurrence behavior in modulationally unstable settings.

title: Robustness of diabatic enhancement in quantum annealing
text_ai: In adiabatic quantum annealing, the speed with which an anneal can be run, while still achieving a high final ground state fidelity, is dictated by the size of the minimum gap that appears between the ground and first excited state in the annealing spectrum. Here we study the robustness of diabatic enhancement against typical experimental imperfections and finite-temperature effects that accompany quantum annealers. We formulate a framework combining diabatic driving with approximate counterdiabatic terms and quantify the resulting fidelity gain as a function of schedule, system size N, and minimum gap g_min. Using both analytic Landau-Zener arguments for two-level reductions and numerical simulations of random Ising instances encoded in a transverse-field Hamiltonian, we compare purely adiabatic schedules to optimized diabatic protocols that deliberately tolerate nonzero transition probabilities to excited states, exploiting constructive interference at the final time. We evaluate performance under static disorder, control field miscalibration, and dephasing modeled by a Lindblad master equation at finite temperature. Our results show that the diabatic advantage—manifested as a higher ground-state probability at fixed runtime—persists across problem classes and remains robust for moderate disorder and decoherence, provided the drive bandwidth is sufficient and the schedule is tailored to the local spectral structure. The work identifies quantitative benchmarks for robust diabatic enhancement and outlines guidelines for implementing resilient protocols on hardware.
prefix: In adiabatic quantum annealing, the speed with which an anneal can be run, while still achieving a high final ground state fidelity, is dictated by the size of the minimum gap that appears between the ground and first excited state in the annealing spectrum.

title: Distributed Optimal Voltage Control with Asynchronous and Delayed Communication
text_ai: The increased penetration of volatile renewable energy into distribution networks necessities more efficient distributed voltage control. In this paper, we design distributed feedback control algorithms where each bus can inject \emph{both active and reactive} power into the grid to regulate the voltages. To cope with asynchronous and delayed information, we cast the problem as a distributed convex optimization of a voltage-regulation objective subject to operational constraints. Each bus locally optimizes its injectors while communicating over a time-varying graph. We deploy an asynchronous primal–dual algorithm where local primal variables are updated with stale neighbor data; dual prices are updated based on local residuals. Under mild assumptions on the delayed communications (bounded delays, eventual connectivity) we establish convergence to the global optimum of the convexified OPF. We show that the algorithm tolerates packet drops and clock asynchrony without requiring synchronized rounds. A proximal term improves robustness to model mismatch. Simulations on standard feeders illustrate that the proposed scheme achieves faster voltage convergence and reduced coordination burden relative to synchronous and centralized schemes.
prefix: The increased penetration of volatile renewable energy into distribution networks necessities more efficient distributed voltage control. In this paper, we design distributed feedback control algorithms where each bus can inject \emph{both active and reactive} power into the grid to regulate the voltages.

title: Mobile Data Science: Towards Understanding Data-Driven Intelligent Mobile Applications
text_ai: Due to the popularity of smart mobile phones and context-aware technology, various contextual data relevant to users' diverse activities with mobile phones is available around us. This enables the study on mobile phone data and context-awareness in computing, for the purpose of building data-driven intelligent mobile applications, not only on a single device but also in a distributed environment for the benefit of end users. To address these challenges, we propose a unified mobile data science framework that orchestrates data ingestion, contextual feature extraction, and predictive modeling across device, edge, and cloud layers. The approach emphasizes on-device inference whenever possible to reduce latency and preserve privacy, while leveraging edge/cloud collaboration for heavier analytics and model updates. A modular pipeline supports heterogeneous data sources (sensor streams, usage logs, calendar, location, social signals) and dynamic contexts (activity, environment, user state). We introduce privacy- and energy-aware mechanisms, including federated learning with secure aggregation, differential privacy for shared updates, and event-driven data thinning. Our evaluation across real-world datasets and a simulated distributed testbed demonstrates improvements in task accuracy, responsiveness, and resource efficiency for representative use cases such as activity recognition, context-aware notification prioritization, and adaptive UI customization. We further discuss design considerations, deployment guidelines, and open challenges in data governance, model drift, and cross-device personalization that shape the future of mobile data-driven intelligent applications.

This enables the study on mobile phone data and context-awareness in computing, for the purpose of building data-driven intelligent mobile applications, not only on a single device but also in a distributed environment for the benefit of end users.

title: Effects of PRP and LyPRP on osteogenic differentiation of MSCs.
text_ai: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) is rich in a variety of growth factors and plays an important role in the proliferation and differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). It has been reported that the preparation of freeze-dried platelets (lyophilized platelets [LyPRP]) from platelets could be an effective strategy to preserve the bioactivity of platelets for a long time. To compare the effects of PRP and LyPRP on osteogenic differentiation of human MSCs, MSCs were cultured in osteogenic medium supplemented with 5% PRP, 5% LyPRP, or basal medium as control. Cellular viability and proliferation were monitored alongside alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity, calcium deposition by Alizarin Red S staining, and the expression of osteogenic markers (RUNX2, SP7/Osterix, BGLAP/OCN, and COL1A1) by qRT-PCR and immunoblotting at days 7, 14, and 21. Both PRP and LyPRP enhanced osteogenic differentiation relative to control, with PRP driving higher early proliferation, whereas LyPRP maintained sustained signaling and gene upregulation associated with later stages of differentiation. ALP activity rose markedly in both treatment groups, peaking earlier in the PRP condition, while mineralization at day 21 was robust and comparable between PRP and LyPRP. Gene and protein analyses showed upregulation of RUNX2 and Osterix early on, with progressive increases in BGLAP and COL1A1 expression in both PRP-treated groups, and LyPRP achieving equal or greater OCN levels by day 21. Collectively, LyPRP preserves platelet bioactivity after lyophilization and supports MSC osteogenesis comparably to fresh PRP, offering a stable, off-the-shelf adjunct for bone regenerative strategies.

It has been reported that the preparation of freeze-dried platelets (lyophilized platelets [LyPRP]) from platelets could be an effective strategy to preserve the bioactivity of platelets for a long time.

title: Tableau models for semi-infinite Bruhat order and level-zero representations of quantum affine algebras
text_ai: We prove that semi-infinite Bruhat order on an affine Weyl group is completely determined from those on the quotients by affine Weyl subgroups associated with various maximal (standard) parabolic subgroups of finite type. From this observation, we obtain tableau models for the semi-infinite crystals and for the level-zero representations of the quantum affine algebra U_q'(ĝ). We provide an explicit combinatorial realization of highest-weight modules as sets of tableaux endowed with crystal operators e_i, f_i that are compatible with the semi-infinite Bruhat structure, and we prove that the partial order is recoverable from the finite parabolic projections. Consequently, character formulas and tensor product multiplicities for level-zero modules admit purely tableau-theoretic proofs, arising from the finite-type tableaux and their passage to the limit along the parabolic chain. The construction specializes to the classical finite-type tableau descriptions upon projection and coherently patches to a global semi-infinite model. In addition, we supply efficient algorithms for navigating the associated crystals, and illustrate the framework with type A and affine type A examples, relating to Kirillov–Reshetikhin crystals and known fermionic representations.
prefix: We prove that semi-infinite Bruhat order on an affine Weyl group is completely determined from those on the quotients by affine Weyl subgroups associated with various maximal (standard) parabolic subgroups of finite type.

title: Nitrogen Cluster Anions
text_ai: Anions are formed by electron attachment to helium nanodroplets doped with N$_2$. The most prominent ion series is due to odd-numbered N$_m$$^{-}$ with 3 $\le$ m < 140. Neither N$^{-}$ nor N$_2$$^{-}$ are observed. An appearance energy of 11.5 $\pm$ 0.5 eV is measured for N$_3$$^{-}$. The appearance of N$_m$$^{-}$ tracks the growth of a weakly bound excess electron in a solvation environment. The odd-numbered series persists across the 3 ≤ m < 140 span; neither N$^{-}$ nor N$_2$$^{-}$ is detected, consistent with their higher detachment thresholds. The onset for N$_3$$^{-}$ is 11.5 ± 0.5 eV, with only a modest downward shift for larger m, indicating incremental stabilization by delocalization along nitrogen backbones within the droplet. Fragmentation upon attachment is dominated by loss of neutral N$_2$, leaving the N$_m$$^{-}$ series intact. Quantum-chemical calculations on representative sizes show a diffusely bound extra electron distributed along the nitrogen chain and modulated by the helium matrix. These results illustrate the stabilizing role of the droplet in large nitrogen cluster anions.

title: Lattice results for $D/D_s$ leptonic and semileptonic decays
text_ai: This review article summarizes recent lattice QCD results for $D$ and $D_s$ meson leptonic and semileptonic decays. Knowing the meson decay constants and semileptonic form factors from theory, one can extract CKM elements $V_{cd}$ and $V_{cs}$ from experimental results. Across several lattice formulations, the dominant uncertainties arise from discretization effects, chiral and continuum extrapolations, and the renormalization of the axial and vector currents. Modern studies employ ensembles with physical light-quark masses, multiple lattice spacings, and controlled finite-volume effects, together with nonperturbative or highly improved perturbative renormalization. The q^2 dependence of semileptonic form factors is described with z-expansion fits and cross-checked by ratios such as f_+(0) and f_0(0). Results from N_f=2+1+1 and 2+1 flavor simulations are combined to provide precise f_D, f_Ds, and f_+(q^2) values, enabling clean extractions of |V_cd| and |V_cs| from leptonic and semileptonic decay rates. Overall agreement with CKM unitarity and experimental measurements is evaluated, with prospects for further reductions anticipated from forthcoming ensembles and QED/isospin corrections in the near term.

title: National registry of haemophilia and other coagulopathies: A multisector initiative in the Colombian Health System.
text_ai: Haemophilia is an orphan and high-cost disease worldwide and, especially in middle-income countries as Colombia. Given its burden of disease, in 2014, a national administrative registry was created to centralize demographic, clinical and economic information regarding to haemophilia and other coagulopathies. To describe the building and implementation processes of the Colombian registry of haemophilia and other coagulopathies. Results: The governance and data platform were completed and activated, enabling inclusion across regional health units. The registry integrated data from clinical records and health information systems, achieving nationwide coverage of haemophilia and other coagulopathies. Core indicators—demographics, phenotype, laboratory status, inhibitor presence, treatment patterns, hospitalizations, and costs—became routinely available. Data quality measures showed high completeness and consistency; timeliness supported near real-time reporting for selected indicators. The registry generated national estimates of prevalence, treatment access, and direct medical costs, and supported monitoring of procurement efficiency, equity of access, and regional variation. Multisector engagement fostered shared governance and accountability, while privacy safeguards and ethical oversight maintained trust and compliance. Challenges included heterogeneity of data sources, inconsistent electronic records, and sustainability of funding; mitigations encompassed standardized templates, interoperable interfaces, ongoing training, and formal data-use agreements. The experience offers a scalable model for monitoring rare diseases in middle-income health systems and informs policy on diagnostics, therapy allocation, and outcome surveillance and future scalability.

title: Optimal entanglement witnesses for continuous-variable systems
text_ai: This paper is concerned with all tests for continuous-variable entanglement that arise from linear combinations of second moments or variances of canonical coordinates, as they are commonly used in experiments to detect entanglement. All such tests for bi-partite and multi-partite entanglement correspond to hyperplanes in the set of second moments. We show that optimal entanglement witnesses for continuous-variable systems are precisely the supporting hyperplanes to the convex set of separable second-moment data. An optimal witness is determined by a pair of linear combinations of quadratures whose variances saturate the corresponding uncertainty bounds for all separable states and are violated by the state under test. The construction is formulated as a semidefinite program over the covariance data; its dual yields the witness itself and characterizes its maximal robustness to additive noise. For a fixed mode partition we provide algorithms to enumerate all extremal witnesses and prove that, up to positive rescaling, they coincide with the facets of the separable-variance set. The method reproduces known two-mode criteria and yields scalable multipartite tests with experimental parameters.
prefix: This paper is concerned with all tests for continuous-variable entanglement that arise from linear combinations of second moments or variances of canonical coordinates, as they are commonly used in experiments to detect entanglement. All such tests for bi-partite and multi-partite entanglement correspond to hyperplanes in the set of second moments.

title: Explaining the Effectiveness of Multi-Task Learning for Efficient Knowledge Extraction from Spine MRI Reports
text_ai: Pretrained Transformer based models finetuned on domain specific corpora have changed the landscape of NLP. However, training or fine-tuning these models for individual tasks can be time consuming and resource intensive. In this study, we examine a unified multi-task learning (MTL) framework to extract structured knowledge from spine MRI reports across complementary tasks. We implement a shared Transformer encoder with task-specific heads for entity recognition, attribute extraction, relation extraction, and report structuring. Using annotated spine MRI corpora, we compare against strong single-task fine-tuning and adapter-based transfer. Our results show that MTL yields robust gains across tasks, improving F1 scores and reducing per-task training time and data requirements. Shared representations and auxiliary losses enable data-efficient learning, while adapters mitigate interference and facilitate scalable extension to new tasks. The proposed framework accelerates knowledge extraction for clinical decision support, enabling rapid population of structured summaries from radiology reports across institutions. We discuss limitations, including task interference in heterogeneous domains, and propose mitigation strategies and directions for deployment. Future work will explore active learning to further reduce labeling burden.
prefix: Pretrained Transformer based models finetuned on domain specific corpora have changed the landscape of NLP. However, training or fine-tuning these models for individual tasks can be time consuming and resource intensive.

title: Spurious modes in extended RPA theories
text_ai: Necessary conditions that the spurious state associated with the translational motion and its double-phonon state have zero excitation energy in extended RPA (ERPA) theories which include both one-body and two-body amplitudes are investigated using the small amplitude limit of the time-dependent density-matrix theory (STDDM). Explicitly, the zero-energy condition is shown to be equivalent to the satisfaction of the translational Ward identities within the STDDM-based ERPA. Practically, this imposes two independent constraints on the stationary densities: (i) the one-body transition density must obey the translational sum rule, and (ii) the two-body transition density must furnish a translationally invariant coupling to the one-body sector. When these are met, the spurious translational state decouples from intrinsic excitations and its energy vanishes, and the double-phonon spurious state stays at zero energy as a direct consequence of the exact factorization of the spurious sector. Conversely, truncations or density-dependent interactions that break translational invariance introduce a finite spurious energy, signaling leakage between spurious and physical sectors. The analysis clarifies how the interplay between one- and two-body amplitudes enforces the Ward identities and provides explicit criteria that can be checked a priori in practical ERPA implementations. Implications for nuclear-structure calculations employing STDDM-based ERPA are discussed, including guidelines to preserve center-of-mass decoupling in truncated model spaces and with effective interactions. The framework thus provides a diagnostic tool to assess ERPA implementations and informs the development of interactions and truncation schemes that faithfully respect broken symmetries.

title: Spectroscopic Observations of Selected Planetary Nebulae from the HASH Database
text_ai: We conducted research on the classification and physical properties of 10 objects from the HASH (Hong Kong/Australian Astronomical Observatory/Strasbourg Observatory H-alpha Planetary Nebula (PN)) database with small angular sizes (< 8\arcsec) in the northern hemisphere. The sample consisted of 6 Likely PNe, 2 new candidates, one emission-line star, and one object of unknown nature. Flux-calibrated, extinction-corrected line fluxes were measured for each target. Electron temperatures were derived from [O III] (4363/5007) and, where detected, [N II] (5755/6584); electron densities from [S II] (6716/6731). He II 4686/Hβ and [O III] 5007/Hβ diagnostic ratios were employed to assess excitation. The sample included six objects with line ratios and profiles consistent with photoionized nebulae; two were reinforced as PN candidates by high-excitation lines ([O III] 5007, He II 4686) but lacking definite morphology. The emission-line star displays prominent Balmer and He I lines with broad wings; spectral characteristics distinguish it from classic PNe, while the unknown object remains inconclusive. Abundances were computed under ionization correction factor schemes: 12+log(O/H) = 8.3–8.7, He/H up to 0.12, and log(N/O) spanning −0.5 to +0.6, indicating a mix of disk PNe and more evolved, lower-metallicity objects. Reddening values range c(Hβ) ≈ 0.1–1.2. Comparisons with HASH classifications show agreement for most PNe and suggest reclassification for two sources. These results refine the compact-PN census in HASH.

title: Off the record: The invisibility work of doctors in a patient-accessible electronic health record information service.
text_ai: In this article, we draw on Michael Lipsky's work on street-level bureaucrats and discretion to analyse a real case setting comprising an interview study of 30 Swedish doctors regarding their experiences of changes in clinical work following patients being given access to medical records information online. Building on Lipsky, we treat doctors as street-level bureaucrats who interpret and enact policy under time pressure, informational asymmetries, and diverse patient expectations. The findings describe invisibility work as practices that render some clinical reasoning and provisional judgments effectively off the patient’s record, while preserving professional autonomy and safety. We identify three interlocking modalities. First, filtration and selective disclosure within the patient portal—decisions about what to write, what to withhold, and how to frame caveats. Second, narrative management—rewording notes and adding clarifications to manage perceived uncertainty without eroding trust. Third, workflow accommodation—adjusting routines, time allocation, and interprofessional communication to align transparency with safety and efficiency. The discussion considers implications for professional legitimacy, patient trust, and the design of patient‑accessible information services.
prefix: In this article, we draw on Michael Lipsky's work on street-level bureaucrats and discretion to analyse a real case setting comprising an interview study of 30 Swedish doctors regarding their experiences of changes in clinical work following patients being given access to medical records information online.

title: Diverse tunable dynamics of two quantum random walkers
text_ai: Quantum walk research has mainly focused on evolutions due to repeated applications of time-independent unitary coin operators. However, the idea of controlling the single particle evolution using time-dependent unitary coins has still been a subject of multiple studies as it not only hosts interesting possibilities for quantum information processing but also opens a much richer array of phenomena including static and dynamic localizations. Here we consider a pair of quantum walkers on a one-dimensional lattice whose evolution is governed by time-dependent coin operators along each site. A variety of driving protocols are implemented: periodic, quasi-periodic, and fluctuating coins that induce inter-walker correlations without direct interaction. The joint Hilbert space is evolved by a Floquet operator built from local coin–shift blocks; we characterize the dynamics via the joint distribution P(n1,n2,t), marginal spreads, and coin–walker and inter-walker entanglement. By tuning driving parameters we realize regimes from static localization to rapid, near-ballistic dispersion and to dynamically localized phases where interference suppresses transport despite coin amplitudes. We identify phase diagrams and scaling laws for spreading and entanglement growth. Our findings show that time-dependent control of two quantum walkers yields programmable transport patterns with potential for quantum simulation and information processing. The proposed framework is readily implementable in photonic lattices and trapped-ion platforms, enabling experimental exploration of multi-particle transport under driving.

However, the idea of controlling the single particle evolution using time-dependent unitary coins has still been a subject of multiple studies as it not only hosts interesting possibilities for quantum information processing but also opens a much richer array of phenomena including static and dynamic localizations.

title: Why Are You Wrong? Counterfactual Explanations for Language Grounding with 3D Objects
text_ai: Combining natural language and geometric shapes is an emerging research area with multiple applications in robotics and language-assisted design. A crucial task in this domain is object referent identification, which involves selecting a 3D object given a textual description of the target. To address this, we introduce a counterfactual framework for interrogating grounded language models in 3D scenes. Given a description and a set of candidate objects, we generate minimal, semantically plausible perturbations of the input (textual refinements, attribute swaps, or scene alterations) that change the model's predicted referent. We categorize explanations into input-side (counterfactuals altering language) and world-side (counterfactuals altering geometry or attributes) to expose the decision boundaries. Our method integrates a differentiable perturbation module with a constraint solver to ensure realism of perturbed instances. We evaluate on a newly curated 3D object grounding benchmark with rich attribute vocabulary and naturalistic language, augmented by synthetic counterfactuals. Metrics include triage rate of correct vs. incorrect predictions, explanation faithfulness via fidelity and sparsity, and human judgments on usefulness and interpretability. Results show that counterfactual explanations uncover spurious correlations such as size or color priors, reveal model brittleness under negation, and guide targeted data augmentation. We discuss implications for safer robotics, interactive design, and model debugging, and outline limitations related to computational cost and perceptual ambiguities in 3D grounding.
prefix: Combining natural language and geometric shapes is an emerging research area with multiple applications in robotics and language-assisted design. A crucial task in this domain is object referent identification, which involves selecting a 3D object given a textual description of the target.

title: Contextual Hybrid Session-based News Recommendation with Recurrent Neural Networks
text_ai: Recommender systems help users deal with information overload by providing tailored item suggestions to them. The recommendation of news is often considered to be challenging, since the relevance of an article for a user can depend on a variety of factors, including the user's short-term reading interests, the reader's context, or the recency or popularity of an article. To address these challenges, we propose a contextual hybrid session-based recommender that uses recurrent neural networks to capture readers' evolving intent within a session while integrating contextual cues and article attributes. The model extends a gated recurrent unit encoder with side information, including temporal context, device type, and inferred location, as well as metadata such as topic, recency, and publisher popularity. A parallel content-aware path encodes textual and categorical representations of articles and is fused with a popularity prior through a contextual attention mechanism. The hybrid scoring function combines the sequence-derived hidden state with context-conditioned priors via a learnable fusion gate, enabling the system to adjust the influence of recency and context to the user’s current behavior. Training uses a next-click objective with negative sampling, optimized end-to-end. Experiments on two large-scale news datasets show that the proposed approach outperforms strong baselines, including vanilla session-based RNNs and non-contextual hybrids, in metrics such as NDCG@5 and HR@20, across diverse contextual settings.
prefix: Recommender systems help users deal with information overload by providing tailored item suggestions to them. The recommendation of news is often considered to be challenging, since the relevance of an article for a user can depend on a variety of factors, including the user's short-term reading interests, the reader's context, or the recency or popularity of an article.

title: Numerical models of planetary nebulae with different episodes of mass ejection: the particular case of HuBi 1
text_ai: We have studied the evolution of HuBi 1-like planetary nebulae, considering several stages of mass injection. We have carried out numerical ionization+1D hydrodynamics+atomic/ionic rate models with our code Coral 1D to reproduce planetary nebulae that present multiple shells produced by different ejection events around the ionizing source. We explore a family of injection histories, ranging from brief, high‑intensity bursts to extended, moderate winds, as well as staggered sequences of two or more events around the central star. For each scenario we follow the formation, acceleration, and interaction of successive shells, including shock compression and photoionization of the swept-up gas. Synthetic surface-brightness maps and integrated line intensities for key diagnostics (Hβ, [O III] λ5007, [N II] λ6584, [S II] λλ6716,6731) are produced and contrasted with HuBi 1 observations. The results show that multiple ejections imprint nested, velocity-differentiated shells with distinct density and ionization stratification; collisions generate bright rims and enhanced [N II]-dominated zones. When the inferred ejection ages and masses lie within plausible post-AGB ranges, the models reproduce the observed densities, sizes, and spectral features, providing quantitative constraints on HuBi 1’s mass‑loss history.
prefix: We have studied the evolution of HuBi 1-like planetary nebulae, considering several stages of mass injection. We have carried out numerical ionization+1D hydrodynamics+atomic/ionic rate models with our code Coral 1D to reproduce planetary nebulae that present multiple shells produced by different ejection events around the ionizing source.

title: Antimicrobial resistance and use, and rates of hospitalization associated with bacterial infections, including sepsis
text_ai: While the mechanisms and quantitative details are complex, few analysts would doubt that antibiotic use increases the prevalence of drug-resistant bacterial pathogens among all bacteria causing disease in a population. The causal connection between antibiotic use and the total incidence of severe bacterial infections, possibly mediated by antibiotic resistance, is less clearly established. Using longitudinal, population-level data from multiple jurisdictions, we quantify associations among total antibiotic use, resistance prevalence among invasive isolates, and hospitalization rates for bacterial infections including sepsis. We linked aggregate prescription data, microbiology surveillance, and hospital outcomes across several years, employing mixed-effects regression with lag terms and adjusting for age, comorbidity, and healthcare utilization. Mediation analyses estimated the proportion of any association mediated by resistance. Across settings, higher antibiotic use correlated with increased rates of resistant infections and with sepsis hospitalizations; resistance accounted for a meaningful portion of this relationship. The results support stronger antimicrobial stewardship and resistance-control measures to reduce severe infection burden. Limitations include ecological inference and potential residual confounding, underscoring the need for patient-level studies to corroborate causal pathways.

The causal connection between antibiotic use and the total incidence of severe bacterial infections, possibly mediated by antibiotic resistance, is less clearly established.

title: Simultaneous thermoosmotic and thermoelectric responses in nanoconfined electrolyte solutions: Effects of nanopore structures and membrane properties
text_ai: Hypothesis: Nanofluidic systems provide an emerging and efficient platform for thermoelectric conversion and fluid pumping with low-grade heat energy. As a basis of their performance enhancement, the effects of the structures and properties of the nanofluidic systems on the thermoelectric response (TER) and the thermoosmotic response (TOR) are yet to be explored. We report a combined experimental and theoretical study of TER and TOR in nanoconfined electrolyte solutions under controlled thermal gradients across nanopores with tunable geometry and surface chemistry. Nanopores fabricated in silicon nitride membranes (radius 1–20 nm, length 20–200 nm) span a range of aspect ratios and include deliberately shaped profiles (conical) to modulate the local flow field. Surfaces are functionalized to yield zeta potentials spanning negative to positive regimes at fixed ionic strength, enabling systematic exploration of Debye-length-to-pore-size effects and slip phenomena. A temperature difference ΔT is applied across the membrane, and thermovoltage, thermocurrent, and fluid motion are measured to determine the thermoelectric Seebeck coefficient of the pore and the thermoosmotic velocity. We show that TER and TOR are independently tunable yet strongly coupled through surface charge, pore geometry, and slip length, with pronounced enhancements when electric double layers overlap the pore cross-section. A multiscale model based on coupled Poisson–Nernst–Planck and Navier–Stokes equations, incorporating temperature-dependent transport properties and boundary slip, reproduces the observed trends and provides design maps for maximizing energy conversion and directed pumping. These findings establish concrete guidelines for nanopore-based thermo-electrokinetic devices.

As a basis of their performance enhancement, the effects of the structures and properties of the nanofluidic systems on the thermoelectric response (TER) and the thermoosmotic response (TOR) are yet to be explored.

title: SSH: A Self-Supervised Framework for Image Harmonization
text_ai: Image harmonization aims to improve the quality of image compositing by matching the "appearance" (\eg, color tone, brightness and contrast) between foreground and background images. However, collecting large-scale annotated datasets for this task requires complex professional retouching. Instead, we propose a novel Self-Supervised Harmonization framework (SSH) that can be trained using just "free" natural images without being edited. SSH formulates harmonization as a self-supervised restoration task that requires no labeled annotations or human edits. From each natural image, an unsupervised segmentation yields a soft foreground mask; a harmonization network learns to predict a harmonious result by aligning the appearance of the foreground to the background under a self-generated supervision signal. Specifically, we train with a multi-task objective comprising (i) a perceptual loss to preserve content, (ii) a color-statistics loss in Lab space to reduce mismatch between regions, and (iii) a cross-augmentation consistency loss to encourage stable harmonization across diverse perturbations. An encoder-decoder with region-aware attention implements the operator. SSH achieves competitive results against supervised methods and demonstrates generalization.
prefix: Image harmonization aims to improve the quality of image compositing by matching the "appearance" (\eg, color tone, brightness and contrast) between foreground and background images. However, collecting large-scale annotated datasets for this task requires complex professional retouching. Instead, we propose a novel Self-Supervised Harmonization framework (SSH) that can be trained using just "free" natural images without being edited.

title: Preparation of biogenic gas vesicle nanostructures for use as contrast agents for ultrasound and MRI.
text_ai: Gas vesicles (GVs) are a unique class of gas-filled protein nanostructures that are detectable at subnanomolar concentrations and whose physical properties allow them to serve as highly sensitive imaging agents for ultrasound and MRI. We describe a scalable isolation and purification workflow yielding native gas vesicle nanoparticles with preserved shell architecture and monodisperse size distribution. Biogenic GVs were produced in recombinant strains and recovered by buoyant density separation, followed by buffer exchange to suppress aggregation and preserve mechanical stability. Surface modification strategies, including genetic fusion of targeting peptides and post-purification PEGylation, provided colloidal stabilization in serum and enabled receptor-directed imaging. Ultrasound characterization across clinical frequencies revealed strong backscattering, high signal-to-noise, and a well-defined collapse pressure that could be tuned by shell protein composition, enabling safe dose windows for intact GV persistence in circulation. For MRI, GV nanostructures supported hyperpolarized 129Xe chemical exchange saturation transfer (HyperCEST) signals at sub-nanomolar concentrations, yielding spectral dispersion sufficient for multiplexed imaging. In phantom and small-animal studies, dual-mode contrast was demonstrated with co-registered ultrasound and MR maps, enabling precise localization and assessment of GV distribution. The preparation protocol preserves biocompatibility and enables scalable production, paving the way for ultrasound/MRI contrast agents with potential for noninvasive molecular imaging.
prefix: Gas vesicles (GVs) are a unique class of gas-filled protein nanostructures that are detectable at subnanomolar concentrations and whose physical properties allow them to serve as highly sensitive imaging agents for ultrasound and MRI.

title: MBAPose: Mask and Bounding-Box Aware Pose Estimation of Surgical Instruments with Photorealistic Domain Randomization
text_ai: Surgical robots are usually controlled using a priori models based on the robots' geometric parameters, which are calibrated before the surgical procedure. One of the challenges in using robots in real surgical settings is that those parameters can change over time, consequently deteriorating control accuracy. To mitigate drift and preserve precise instrument localization during procedures, we propose MBAPose, a pose estimator that fuses mask-based shape cues with bounding-box constraints. A dual-branch backbone extracts features from RGB inputs; one head predicts a segmentation mask, the other outputs a 3D bounding box. A pose head estimates 6-DoF pose by integrating mask and box information within a PnP-RANSAC loop, trained with losses on mask IoU, bbox regression, and geodesic pose error. The model is trained with photorealistic domain randomization: a renderer generates diverse scenes with realistic lighting, textures, and occlusions. Experiments on synthetic-realistic benchmarks show robust performance in clutter and under variable lighting, surpassing baselines that rely on either masks or boxes. These results validate MBAPose for real-time guidance in robotic procedures.
prefix: Surgical robots are usually controlled using a priori models based on the robots' geometric parameters, which are calibrated before the surgical procedure. One of the challenges in using robots in real surgical settings is that those parameters can change over time, consequently deteriorating control accuracy.

title: Visual Perception Generalization for Vision-and-Language Navigation via Meta-Learning
text_ai: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) is a challenging task that requires an agent to navigate in real-world environments by understanding natural language instructions and visual information received in real-time. Prior works have implemented VLN tasks on continuous environments or physical robots, all of which use a fixed camera configuration due to the limitations of datasets, such as 1.5 meters height, 90 degrees horizontal field of view (HFOV), etc. To address this, we propose Visual Perception Generalization via Meta-Learning (VPG-Meta). We design a perception module conditioned on the camera intrinsics and extrinsics, and optimize it with a model-agnostic meta-learning objective to enable fast adaptation to unseen camera configurations with minimal gradient updates. The meta-training distribution samples a range of heights, HFOVs, and projection distortions, encouraging the encoder to produce task-invariant features for instruction grounding and waypoint reasoning. We integrate the adapted perception with a language-guided navigator using cross-modal attention and a waypoint-prediction head, ensuring robustness to perceptual perturbations. A lightweight domain-randomization and occlusion-modeling pipeline is incorporated to further align synthetic visuals with real-world appearance. Experiments across standard VLN benchmarks and synthetic rigs demonstrate that the meta-learned model generalizes to unseen camera setups without re-training and with limited adaptation, outperforming fixed-configuration baselines in success rate, path fidelity, and generalization gaps. Ablations verify the contribution of meta-learning and view-conditioned encoders.
prefix: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) is a challenging task that requires an agent to navigate in real-world environments by understanding natural language instructions and visual information received in real-time. title: Convergence of drift-diffusion PDEs arising as Wasserstein gradient flows of convex functions
text_ai: We study the quantitative convergence of drift-diffusion PDEs that arise as Wasserstein gradient flows of linearly convex functions over the space of probability measures on ${\mathbb R}^d$. In this setting, the objective is in general not displacement convex, so it is not clear a priori whether global convergence even holds. Using the gradient-flow formulation in the Wasserstein space, we prove a quantitative dissipation inequality that relates the free-energy gap F(ρ)−F(ρ*) to the Wasserstein distance W_2(ρ,ρ*) and to the entropy production along the flow. Under a linear-convexity (α-strong) condition along affine rays in the probability space, we obtain exponential convergence in W_2 and in relative entropy: W_2(ρ_t,ρ*) ≤ C e^{−α t}, and F(ρ_t)−F(ρ*) ≤ C e^{−α t}. In the absence of uniform displacement convexity, but assuming a Wasserstein Łojasiewicz-type inequality with exponent θ∈(1/2,1], we derive algebraic rates; in particular, F(ρ_t)−F(ρ*) decays as t^{−θ/(1−θ)} and W_2(ρ_t,ρ*) decays with the corresponding rate. The results cover a broad class of drift–diffusion equations with a convex linear part and nonconvex energy, clarifying when global convergence is guaranteed and providing explicit rates. We illustrate the sharpness of the assumptions and discuss stability under perturbations, as well as extensions to interacting particle systems and to confinement-potentials with general convexity profiles.

title: Nanotechnology approaches in the current therapy of skin cancer.
text_ai: Skin cancer is a high burden disease with a high impact on global health. Conventional therapies have several drawbacks; thus, the development of effective therapies is required. In this context, nanotechnology approaches are an attractive strategy for cancer therapy because they enable the efficient delivery of drugs and other bioactive molecules to target tissues with low toxic effects. Nanoparticle formulations have been explored to enhance topical delivery of chemotherapeutics and to enable systemic administration with improved skin targeting. Carrier platforms include liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles, dendrimers, inorganic nanoparticles, and hybrid systems that permit controlled release, greater stability, and penetration across the stratum corneum. In addition, nanomedicine enables combination strategies such as photoenabled therapies (photodynamic and photothermal therapy), nucleic acid delivery, and immunomodulatory agents, addressing tumor heterogeneity and resistance. Preclinical models and early clinical studies show enhanced localization to cutaneous lesions and reduced systemic toxicity, yet challenges remain in reproducibility, long-term safety, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory translation. The field is moving toward patient-specific design, integration with diagnostic imaging, and theranostic platforms to guide therapy and monitor response.
prefix: Skin cancer is a high burden disease with a high impact on global health. Conventional therapies have several drawbacks; thus, the development of effective therapies is required. In this context, nanotechnology approaches are an attractive strategy for cancer therapy because they enable the efficient delivery of drugs and other bioactive molecules to target tissues with low toxic effects.

title: A Deep Conditioning Treatment of Neural Networks
text_ai: We study the role of depth in training randomly initialized overparameterized neural networks. We give a general result showing that depth improves trainability of neural networks by improving the conditioning of certain kernel matrices of the input data. This result holds for arbitrary non-linear activation functions under a certain normalization. More precisely, we show that, under a mild normalization that preserves unit pre-activation variance across layers, the empirical kernel associated with the transformed inputs—the layerwise random feature map—admits a spectral profile that improves with depth. With high probability over the random initialization, the Gram matrix K^L = Phi^L (Phi^L)^T exhibits a lower bound on its smallest eigenvalue that grows with depth, while its operator norm remains controlled. Consequently, the condition number κ(K^L) decreases as depth increases, yielding more stable gradient flow and faster convergence guarantees for simple first- and second-order optimizers from random start in the overparameterized regime. Experiments on synthetic and real data corroborate these predictions, showing depth-driven improvements in training efficiency.
prefix: We study the role of depth in training randomly initialized overparameterized neural networks. We give a general result showing that depth improves trainability of neural networks by improving the conditioning of certain kernel matrices of the input data. This result holds for arbitrary non-linear activation functions under a certain normalization.

title: Gene-centric gene-gene interaction: A model-based kernel machine method
text_ai: Much of the natural variation for a complex trait can be explained by variation in DNA sequence levels. As part of sequence variation, gene-gene interaction has been ubiquitously observed in nature, where its role in shaping the development of an organism has been broadly recognized. Here we propose a gene-centric kernel-machine framework that models pairwise gene interactions by pooling SNPs within each gene and encoding cross-gene epistasis with an interaction kernel. For a gene pair (g,h), genotypes are summarized by gene kernels K_g and K_h, and the interaction kernel K_gh, defined as the elementwise product K_g ∘ K_h, captures joint variant dependence. In a kernel-machine regression, y = μ + Xβ + f_g + f_h + f_gh + ε, with f_g ~ N(0, τ_g^2 K_g), f_h ~ N(0, τ_h^2 K_h), f_gh ~ N(0, τ_gh^2 K_gh), ε ~ N(0, σ^2 I). The null τ_gh^2 = 0 is tested by a fast score test, with hierarchical FDR controlling for many gene pairs, and covariates incorporated. The framework is scalable via low-rank approximations and screening. Simulation studies show improved power to detect gene-gene interactions when marginal effects are modest and LD is present, while maintaining proper type I error, compared with SNP- and single-gene approaches. Genome-wide analyses identify plausible interactions within known pathways, with replication in independent data.
prefix: Much of the natural variation for a complex trait can be explained by variation in DNA sequence levels. As part of sequence variation, gene-gene interaction has been ubiquitously observed in nature, where its role in shaping the development of an organism has been broadly recognized.

title: Generic algebraic properties in spaces of enumerated groups
text_ai: We introduce and study Polish topologies on various spaces of countable enumerated groups, where an enumerated group is simply a group whose underlying set is the set of natural numbers. Using elementary tools and well known examples from combinatorial group theory, combined with the Baire category theorem, we obtain a plethora of results demonstrating that several phenomena in group theory are generic. Consequently, a typical enumerated group is nonabelian, centerless, and not finitely presentable; it contains free subgroups of rank two and, more generally, exhibits universal embedding phenomena for finite presentations within a comeager subset. The automorphism group of a generic member is large and nontrivial, while the profinite completion reflects nontrivial residual properties, underscoring a high degree of algebraic richness. Our methods yield a uniform mechanism for transferring comeagerness across natural Polish refinements of the base spaces, including constraints given by growth, enumeration, or decoding maps. In particular, the framework yields simultaneous genericity results for a broad spectrum of algebraic features, reinforcing the view that generic phenomena in spaces of enumerated groups are both robust and highly intricate.
prefix: We introduce and study Polish topologies on various spaces of countable enumerated groups, where an enumerated group is simply a group whose underlying set is the set of natural numbers. Using elementary tools and well known examples from combinatorial group theory, combined with the Baire category theorem, we obtain a plethora of results demonstrating that several phenomena in group theory are generic.

title: Evolution of an N-level system via automated vectorization of the Liouville equations and application to optically controlled polarization rotation
text_ai: The Liouville equation governing the evolution of the density matrix for an atomic/molecular system is expressed in terms of a commutator between the density matrix and the Hamiltonian, along with terms that account for decay and redistribution. By casting the density operator into a column vector in Liouville space and representing the commutator with the Hamiltonian and the dissipator as a sparse superoperator, the evolution reduces to a linear system d/dt |ρ⟩ = L |ρ⟩, where L is built from the system Hamiltonian, decay channels, and redistribution terms. The automation pipeline generates the Liouvillian blocks for arbitrary N and assembles them to exploit sparsity and selection rules that minimize fill-in. Time integration uses Krylov-subspace methods with implicit schemes for stiff dynamics, with trace-preserving and positivity checks. We apply the method to an optically driven, Zeeman-resolved ensemble, reporting the rotation of a probe polarization as drive intensity, detuning, and polarization angle vary. Results demonstrate scalability and accuracy, revealing polarization rotation control by the optical field.
prefix: The Liouville equation governing the evolution of the density matrix for an atomic/molecular system is expressed in terms of a commutator between the density matrix and the Hamiltonian, along with terms that account for decay and redistribution.

title: Cognitive system to achieve human-level accuracy in automated assignment of helpdesk email tickets
text_ai: Ticket assignment/dispatch is a crucial part of service delivery business with lot of scope for automation and optimization. In this paper, we present an end-to-end automated helpdesk email ticket assignment system, which is also offered as a service. Leveraging a multi-component cognitive stack, the system detects language, cleans text, and extracts entities (products, services) and intents (incident, request, inquiry). A context-aware encoder yields task representations that feed a dual-branch classifier for issue-type/priority prediction and recommended assignee routing. An iterative reasoning module applies case-based reasoning and SLA constraints to validate suggestions, flag escalations, and merge tickets describing the same incident. A dynamic policy engine combines model predictions with business rules to produce a ranked dispatch list with confidence scores. The solution enables continual learning through human-in-the-loop feedback and active learning, updating the model with corrected assignments and new label mappings. We evaluate on a curated, cross-industry corpus of anonymized helpdesk emails with expert labels, using cross-validation and ablation. Results show substantial gains over baselines, approaching human agreement levels, with strong top-1 accuracy and robust generalization across domains. The system is offered as a cloud service with API access, multi-tenant isolation, audit logs, and configurable SLAs, prioritizing low latency, scalability, and privacy. This architecture supports rapid onboarding of new clients while preserving control over routing fidelity.
prefix: Ticket assignment/dispatch is a crucial part of service delivery business with lot of scope for automation and optimization. In this paper, we present an end-to-end automated helpdesk email ticket assignment system, which is also offered as a service.

title: Spectral Efficiency Maximization for DMA-enabled Multiuser MISO with Statistical CSI
text_ai: Dynamic metasurface antennas (DMAs) offer the potential to achieve large-scale antenna arrays with low power consumption and reduced hardware costs, making them a promising technology for future communication systems. This paper investigates the spectral efficiency (SE) of DMA-enabled multiuser multiple-input single-output (MISO) systems in both uplink and downlink transmissions, using only statistical channel state information (CSI) to maximize the ergodic sum rate of multiple users. To this end, we develop a DMA-based channel model under statistical CSI, where the effective channel is a function of the DMA phase configuration and the transmit/receive covariances. Using random matrix theory, we derive deterministic equivalents for the ergodic SE that depend only on channel covariances, enabling optimization without instantaneous CSI. We propose a joint design framework that alternates between (i) optimizing the DMA phase shifts on the unit-modulus manifold and (ii) optimizing the digital precoders and combiners under power constraints. The DMA configuration is updated by projected gradient descent with backtracking, yielding convergence to a stationary point; the digital part uses convex surrogates via weighted MMSE. For downlink, we maximize the sum rate with per-user QoS and total power limits; for uplink, we tailor receive filters under the same statistical CSI. Simulations corroborate the theory and show substantial SE gains over fixed-phase DMA and conventional MIMO at moderate to high user loads and correlation. The proposed framework reduces CSI overhead by exploiting covariances, making it attractive for fast-varying channels.
prefix: Dynamic metasurface antennas (DMAs) offer the potential to achieve large-scale antenna arrays with low power consumption and reduced hardware costs, making them a promising technology for future communication systems. This paper investigates the spectral efficiency (SE) of DMA-enabled multiuser multiple-input single-output (MISO) systems in both uplink and downlink transmissions, using only statistical channel state information (CSI) to maximize the ergodic sum rate of multiple users.

title: Napoleonic Constructions in the Hyperbolic Plane
text_ai: In the Euclidean setting, Napoleon's Theorem states that if one constructs an equilateral triangle on either the outside or the inside of each side of a given triangle and then connects the barycenters of those three new triangles, the resulting triangle happens to be equilateral. We formulate and prove the hyperbolic analogue. Let ABC be a triangle in the hyperbolic plane; on each side erect an equilateral triangle and denote by G_AB, G_BC, G_CA the barycenters of these triangles. We prove that the triangle G_AB G_BC G_CA is equilateral in H^2 for each orientation. The argument blends hyperbolic trigonometry with centroid theory and uses isometries to reduce to a standard form. Moreover, we obtain hyperbolic formulas for the Napoleon side length in terms of the original sides a,b,c via the hyperbolic cosine law. Two Napoleon triangles arise, related by a symmetric hyperbolic rotation about the common Napoleon point, mirroring the Euclidean dichotomy. We discuss implications for center-of-mass mappings and hyperbolic Fermat constructions.

title: The conundrum of stock versus bond prices
text_ai: In a general way, stock and bond prices do not display any significant correlation. Yet, if we concentrate our attention on specific episodes marked by a crash followed by a rebound, then we observe that stock prices have a strong connection with interest rates on the one hand, and with bond yield spreads on the other hand. Using a panel of equity indices and government and corporate bonds over four decades, we examine dynamics of stock and bond prices through episodes. A regime-switching VAR augmented with policy-rate expectations separates tranquil from distress regimes and identifies channels through which bonds influence equities. Our results show that, in normal times, stock and bond prices move largely independently, consistent with standard asset-pricing intuition. Against crashes and rebounds, however, the linkage strengthens and becomes markedly asymmetric: declines in equity prices co-occur with tightening financial conditions, while rebounds are associated with reductions in term and credit spreads and with downward revisions to expected policy rates. The magnitude of the interaction is moderated by the slope of the yield curve and by the credibility of monetary stimulus. In addition, bond risk premia carry information about future equity returns beyond that contained in standard interest-rate signals. The paper thus reconciles the puzzle by revealing a regime-contingent, rate- and risk-driven stock–bond nexus.

title: Derivation and maintenance of mouse haploid embryonic stem cells.
text_ai: Ploidy represents the number of chromosome sets in a cell. Although gametes have a haploid genome (n), most mammalian cells have diploid genomes (2n). The diploid status of most cells correlates with the number of probable alleles for each autosomal gene and makes it difficult to target these genes via mutagenesis techniques. Here, we describe a strategy for deriving haploid embryonic stem cells (haESCs) from mouse embryos and maintaining their haploidy through extended culture. haESCs were established from embryos subjected to a parthenogenetic protocol and adapted to a 2i/LIF milieu to support self-renewal while minimizing diploidization. Ploidy status was tracked by flow cytometry and confirmed by karyotype analysis and SNP profiling across passages. Although haESCs rapidly diploidize, periodic haploid enrichment by flow sorting restored haploid populations and enabled robust targeted mutagenesis using CRISPR/Cas9, yielding homozygous knockouts in a single allele per locus. These lines retain pluripotency markers and differentiate into derivatives of all germ layers in vitro and in chimera contexts, establishing a platform for forward genetics in the mouse.

title: How Dense is Your Gas? On the recoverability of LVG model parameters
text_ai: We explore the recoverability of gas physical conditions with the Large Velocity Gradient (LVG) model, using the public code RADEX and the molecules HCN and CO. Examining a wide parameter range with a series of models of increasing complexity we use both grid and Monte Carlo Markov Chain (MCMC) methods to recover the input conditions, and quantify the inherent and noise induced uncertainties in the model results. Using RADEX, we construct synthetic line sets for CO and HCN across density (n_H2 = 10^2–10^6 cm^-3), temperature (T_k = 5–200 K), and N/Δv (10^12–10^18 cm^-2 (km s^-1)^-1), assuming a slab and standard abundances. We perform exhaustive grid searches and MCMC sampling to map the posterior of (n_H2, T_k, N/Δv) for tracer combinations. We explore signal-to-noise, optical depth, and spectral resolution impacts on recoverability, and quantify degeneracies among parameters. Our results show that including a mix of low- and high-J transitions for CO together with HCN lines can substantially reduce biases and tighten constraints, whereas limits from a single tracer remain highly degenerate. We find that, for optically thick regimes or sparse line sets, recoverability degrades and priors dominate; robust inference thus relies on multiple lines and informative priors. The study provides guidelines for planning observations and reporting intervals in LVG-derived conditions.

title: Identification of materials with strong magneto-structural coupling using computational high-throughput screening
text_ai: Important phenomena such as magnetostriction, magnetocaloric, and magnetoelectric effects arise from, or could be enhanced by, the coupling of magnetic and structural degrees of freedom. The coupling of spin and lattice also influence transport and structural properties in magnetic materials in particular around phase transitions. Here, we implement a scalable high-throughput framework that couples density functional theory with automated structure perturbations to quantify spin–lattice coupling across thousands of compounds. For each candidate, we determine magnetic ground state, elastic response, and the evolution of structural instabilities upon magnetization by computing magnetoelastic coefficients, energy landscapes of symmetry-lowering distortions, and phonon spectra under constrained spin configurations. Screening is performed on curated databases of crystalline materials, with filters for phase stability and experimental accessibility. Materials exhibiting large magnetostrictive strains, low-energy structural distortions tied to magnetic order, or pronounced phonon softening concurrent with magnetic transitions are flagged as high priority. Validation includes benchmarking against known magnetostrictive and magnetocaloric compounds and cross-checking with experimental reports, enabling targeted synthesis and characterization.

The coupling of spin and lattice also influence transport and structural properties in magnetic materials in particular around phase transitions.

title: On the Analysis of Puncturing for Finite-Length Polar Codes: Boolean Function Approach
text_ai: This paper investigates the impact of puncturing on finite-length polar codes in which a puncturing pattern $\pv^{N}=(p_0,...,p_N)$ is applied to a length-$N$ polar code.. We first introduce two virtual channels to stochastically model the punctured (untransmitted) bits, which are respectively called {\em useless channel model} (UCM) and {\em deterministic channel model} (DCM). Building on these models, we develop a Boolean-function framework that characterizes the impact of puncturing on the hierarchy of polarized channels in terms of simple algebraic operations over the puncturing mask. Under UCM, punctured positions contribute null information, whereas under DCM they contribute deterministic information; combining these with the polarized kernel yields a tractable representation of the effective bit-channels as Boolean polynomials of the underlying channel's LLRs. We exploit this representation to obtain exact or bounded expressions for the polarized reliabilities and to quantify the loss in polarization fidelity due to puncturing. The resulting methodology enables efficient evaluation and optimization of puncturing patterns for finite-length polar codes, supported by simulations over binary-input channels.
