title: Are Bitcoins price predictable? Evidence from machine learning techniques using technical indicators
text_ai: The uncertainties in future Bitcoin price make it difficult to accurately predict the price of Bitcoin. Accurately predicting the price for Bitcoin is therefore important for decision-making process of investors and market players in the cryptocurrency market. Using daily closing prices of BTC-USD from 2015 to 2024, we construct a comprehensive feature set of technical indicators (SMA/EMA with 5–20 day windows; RSI(14); MACD; Bollinger Band width; ATR; OBV; CCI; stochastic %K/%D; rate of change). Additional features include lagged returns and interaction terms. The task is framed as both regression (predict next-day return or price) and classification (direction on the next day). A suite of models is trained: regularized linear models (Ridge, Lasso, Elastic Net), tree-based ensembles (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost), and a recurrent neural network (LSTM) that ingests the technical features. Evaluation uses walk-forward cross-validation and out-of-sample tests across subperiods to mimic real trading. Metrics include RMSE, MAE, MAPE for point forecasts, and directional accuracy together with an economic-value proxy under a simple, cost-aware trading rule. Results show that indicator-enhanced models outperform baselines across horizons up to a week, with gains varying by volatility regime. XGBoost delivers the strongest out-of-sample performance, while LSTM offers competitive results when combined with momentum features. MACD convergence, RSI thresholds, and volatility-adjusted indicators emerge as the most informative. The improvements translate into economically meaningful gains after accounting for transaction costs in a basic long-only strategy. The findings contribute to the literature on crypto-price predictability by highlighting regime-dependent, albeit conditional, predictability achievable through machine learning applied to technical indicators.

title: Automated Bridge Component Recognition using Video Data
text_ai: This paper investigates the automated recognition of structural bridge components using video data. Although understanding video data for structural inspections is straightforward for human inspectors, the implementation of the same task using machine learning methods has not been fully realized. To this end, we formulate automated recognition as a multi‑class video object detection problem anchored by a standard component taxonomy (deck, girder, pier, abutment, joint, anchor, railing). We introduce a data‑efficient learning strategy that leverages transfer learning from urban object detectors and domain adaptation across bridge sites. Our architecture combines a lightweight backbone with a region proposal module and a temporal fusion stage that aggregates cues from consecutive frames to improve localization accuracy and suppress sporadic mislabeling. We train with a mix of bounding‑box annotations and weakly labeled video segments, augmented by synthetic transforms and occasional synthetic samples. Evaluation on a cross‑bridge video test set shows robust performance under varying illumination, occlusion, and viewpoint, outperforming frame‑wise baselines and enabling actionable inspection summaries.

Although understanding video data for structural inspections is straightforward for human inspectors, the implementation of the same task using machine learning methods has not been fully realized.

title: Discovering Relationships between Object Categories via Universal Canonical Maps
text_ai: We tackle the problem of learning the geometry of multiple categories of deformable objects jointly. Recent work has shown that it is possible to learn a unified dense pose predictor for several categories of related objects. However, training such models requires to initialize inter-category correspondences by hand. To overcome this limitation, we introduce Universal Canonical Maps (UCM), a learning framework that yields a single category-agnostic canonical pose space together with inter-category mappings from each category's template to that space. An architecture based on a shared decoder predicts dense vertex coordinates in the canonical frame, while category-specific encoders capture local shape variability. Training relies on self-supervised cross-category constraints: cycle-consistency between category pairs, a non-rigid alignment loss over shared surface regions, and a shared pose prior that regularizes distortion. Our method discovers semantically coherent correspondences without manual initializations while revealing interpretable relations across categories. Experiments on synthetic and real data for deformable object families show improved cross-category alignment, robust pose estimation, and faithful relational geometry between objects.

title: Confined Dense Circumstellar Material Surrounding a Regular Type II Supernova: The Unique Flash-Spectroscopy Event of SN 2013fs
text_ai: With the advent of new wide-field, high-cadence optical transient surveys, our understanding of the diversity of core-collapse supernovae has grown tremendously in the last decade. However, the pre-supernova evolution of massive stars, that sets the physical backdrop to these violent events, is theoretically not well understood and difficult to probe observationally. Here we report a coordinated rapid-response spectroscopic campaign that captured multiple epochs within hours of explosion, enabling the first unambiguous flash-spectroscopy study of SN 2013fs. The earliest spectra reveal narrow, high-ionization emission features (e.g., He II 4686, C IV, N III) superposed on a hot continuum, produced by photoionization of a dense circumstellar medium located at radii ~10^14–10^15 cm. Radiative-transfer modeling of the line luminosities and their rapid disappearance over the first several days constrains the confined CSM to a total mass of roughly 0.01–0.05 M⊙ and favors a shell-like density structure over a steady wind. From the inferred densities and the temporal evolution, we conclude that this material was expelled in an enhanced mass-loss episode in the final years to decades before core collapse, creating a compact, optically thick cocoon around the progenitor. The implied mass-loss rate during the eruptive phase is ≈10^−3–10^−2 M⊙ yr^−1. Our results demonstrate that even “regular” Type II SNe can be preceded by brief, intense mass loss, with flash spectroscopy providing a direct probe of the immediate circumstellar environment.

title: Optimizing squeezing in a coherent quantum feedback network of optical parametric oscillators
text_ai: Advances in the emerging field of coherent quantum feedback control (CQFC) have led to the development of new capabilities in the areas of quantum control and quantum engineering, with a particular impact on the theory and applications of quantum optical networks. Within the SLH (scattering, Lindblad, Hamiltonian) framework, we model each OPO as a linear quantum component and derive the quantum Langevin equations for the intra- and output-field quadratures. For stable operation, the Gaussian state is characterized by its mean vector and covariance matrix, obeying a matrix Lyapunov (or Riccati) equation. The squeezing spectra of the network output are obtained from these equations via input–output relations, yielding S(Ω) for the chosen quadratures. We formulate an optimization problem to maximize squeezing over a target band, or at a specified sideband, subject to realizability, finite pump power, and losses and phase noise in the feedback paths. The design variables include pump amplitudes, cavity detunings, inter-OPO couplings, and phase shifters. We employ analytic stability criteria and numerical optimization (gradient-based and global-search) to identify topologies and parameters that outperform a single OPO. In a three-OPO network, we demonstrate squeezing enhancement, broadened bandwidth, and robust performance against moderate imperfections. The results provide practical design guidelines for integrating CQFC-enhanced squeezing into scalable quantum sensing and secure optical communication links.
prefix: Advances in the emerging field of coherent quantum feedback control (CQFC) have led to the development of new capabilities in the areas of quantum control and quantum engineering, with a particular impact on the theory and applications of quantum optical networks.

title: CL-HOI: Cross-Level Human-Object Interaction Distillation from Vision Large Language Models
text_ai: Human-object interaction (HOI) detection has seen advancements with Vision Language Models (VLMs), but these methods often depend on extensive manual annotations. Vision Large Language Models (VLLMs) can inherently recognize and reason about interactions at the image level but are computationally heavy and not designed for instance-level HOI detection. To address annotation bottlenecks while preserving localization fidelity, we introduce CL-HOI, a cross-level distillation paradigm that transfers coarse-grained interaction knowledge from VLLMs to a lightweight HOI head. The method comprises an image-level teacher that overviews all humans and objects and a region-level student that predicts subject–verb–object triplets for proposed instances. We design a cross-level alignment module that synchronizes image-level interaction distributions with aggregated region-level predictions, via a multi-level distillation loss and a contrastive term over region embeddings conditioned on prompts. Additionally, an efficient feature-augmentation strategy leverages VLLM-derived priors without incurring prohibitive compute. We validate on widely used HOI benchmarks, showing competitive accuracy with substantially reduced supervision and improved generalization to novel actions and unseen pairings.

Vision Large Language Models (VLLMs) can inherently recognize and reason about interactions at the image level but are computationally heavy and not designed for instance-level HOI detection.

title: Direct observation of multiple topological phases in the iron-based superconductor Li(Fe,Co)As
text_ai: Topological insulators/semimetals and unconventional iron-based superconductors have attracted major attentions in condensed matter physics in the past 10 years. However, there is little overlap between these two fields, although the combination of topological states and superconducting states will produce more exotic topologically superconducting states and Majorana bound states (MBS), a promising candidate for realizing topological quantum computations. Here, we report direct observation of multiple topological phases in Li(Fe1−xCox)As by combining high-resolution angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS), and quantum transport under controlled Co-doping. ARPES reveals a Dirac-like surface state whose energy-momentum dispersion signals a band inversion at the Γ point; its persistence into the superconducting state indicates a topological superconducting channel. STM imaging of vortex cores uncovers robust zero-bias conductance peaks, compatible with Majorana bound states. The data unveil a tunable topological phase diagram, established via spectroscopic fingerprints and supported by theory, uniting topological semimetallic behavior with iron-based superconductivity. These findings open routes toward Majorana platforms in iron-based superconductors.

However, there is little overlap between these two fields, although the combination of topological states and superconducting states will produce more exotic topologically superconducting states and Majorana bound states (MBS), a promising candidate for realizing topological quantum computations.

title: Nuclear spin pair coherence in diamond for atomic scale magnetometry
text_ai: The nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centre, as a promising candidate solid state system of quantum information processing, its electron spin coherence is influenced by the magnetic field fluctuations due to the local environment. In pure diamonds, the environment consists of hundreds of C-13 nuclear spins randomly spreading in several nanometers range forming a spin bath. Here we treat the NV electronic spin as a sensitive meter of the quantum state of proximal 13C spin pairs. Using a cluster-correlation expansion truncated at pair level, we show that the central-spin decoherence can be decomposed into contributions of discrete 13C pairs, whose mutual flip-flop dynamics cause characteristic NV coherence revivals under Carr-Purcell-Meiboom-Gill (CPMG) sequences. By scanning external magnetic field and varying the interpulse spacing, we resolve a spectrum corresponding to near-resonant nuclear pairs with dipolar and hyperfine couplings in the kHz–tens of kHz range. The resulting pair coherence exhibits Beats, enabling quantum sensing of magnetic field fluctuations within sub-nanometer volumes. We demonstrate that the retrieved pair resonances yield a map of the local nuclear-spin network, providing atomic-scale magnetometry capability. In contrast to single-spin sensing, pair-coherence signals are robust to moderate bath fluctuations and can be engineered by isotopic composition and crystal orientation. Our results establish a framework for exploiting nuclear spin pair coherence as a resource for nanoscale magnetometry in diamond.

title: AudioSR: Versatile Audio Super-resolution at Scale
text_ai: Audio super-resolution is a fundamental task that predicts high-frequency components for low-resolution audio, enhancing audio quality in digital applications. Previous methods have limitations such as the limited scope of audio types (e.g., music, speech) and specific bandwidth settings they can handle (e.g., 4kHz to 8kHz). To address these gaps, we introduce AudioSR, a scalable framework that supports heterogeneous audio content and arbitrary target bandwidths without retraining. Our approach unifies spectral upsampling with neural vocoder-style refinement in a multi-resolution architecture, enabling high-fidelity reconstruction across speech, music, and mixed audio. We train with a curriculum over target bandwidths and employ a conditional diffusion backbone augmented by efficient inference tricks to achieve real-time performance. We evaluate on a diverse suite of benchmarks including public speech and music datasets as well as broadcast-style acoustics, reporting improvements in perceptual score (PESQ, composite MOS) and spectral distortion (SI-SDR, log-spectral distance), plus robust performance under noise and compression. Ablation studies justify architectural choices and data-efficiency and generalization.

title: Graph-Aware Language Model Pre-Training on a Large Graph Corpus Can Help Multiple Graph Applications
text_ai: Model pre-training on large text corpora has been demonstrated effective for various downstream applications in the NLP domain. In the graph mining domain, a similar analogy can be drawn for pre-training graph models on large graphs in the hope of benefiting downstream graph applications, which has also been explored by several recent studies. To this end, we introduce a graph-aware language model pre-training framework that ingests a heterogeneous corpus of large graphs, each annotated with textual and attribute information, and learns unified representations via a multi-task objective. The core pre-training tasks include masked graph token prediction, where node and edge attributes are treated as tokens predicted from contextual neighborhoods; edge-type and relation prediction; and a contrastive objective that pulls together representations of structurally analogous subgraphs across the corpus. A scalable architecture combines transformers with light-weight graph encoders to maintain efficiency on graphs with millions of nodes. Fine-tuning across node classification, link prediction, and graph classification demonstrates consistent gains, especially in low-supervision regimes.

title: CIMTx: An R package for causal inference with multiple treatments using observational data
text_ai: CIMTx provides efficient and unified functions to implement modern methods for causal inferences with multiple treatments using observational data with a focus on binary outcomes. The methods include regression adjustment, inverse probability of treatment weighting, Bayesian additive regression trees, regression adjustment with multivariate spline of the generalized propensity score, vector matching and targeted maximum likelihood estimation. CIMTx streamlines model specification for each method, providing unified input objects and consistent output classes for treatment effect estimates, standard errors, and confidence intervals. It supports multinomial treatments and binary outcomes, with optional cross-fitting and sample-splitting to reduce overfitting, as well as robust variance estimators and bootstrap-based inference. The package includes functions for diagnostics of covariate balance, overlap, and model misspecification, along with visualization tools for generalized propensity scores and weighting schemes. It is designed to be interoperable with tidyverse workflows and to leverage parallel backends for large datasets, with comprehensive vignettes and examples illustrating applied causal analyses. All results are reproducible and well-documented.

title: Oscillations in three-reaction quadratic mass-action systems
text_ai: It is known that rank-two bimolecular mass-action systems do not admit limit cycles. With a view to understanding which small mass-action systems admit oscillation, in this paper we study rank-two networks with bimolecular source complexes but allow target complexes with higher molecularities. We prove that, up to permutation of species and positive rescalings of rate constants, oscillations can occur only in the cyclic three-reaction network A+B→2A, B+C→2B, C+A→2C. The total concentration S=A+B+C is a conserved quantity, so the dynamics restrict to the two-dimensional simplex {A+B+C=S}. In this invariant plane the system reduces to a planar quadratic vector field with a unique positive interior equilibrium. We derive explicit formulae for this equilibrium and its Jacobian, and we give necessary and sufficient conditions for a Hopf bifurcation in terms of the three rate constants. Concretely, a purely imaginary pair of eigenvalues arises on a codimension-one surface, yielding a stable limit cycle on the side of the surface where the equilibrium changes stability. Outside this class, any rank-two three-reaction system with bimolecular sources has no periodic orbits. The results are obtained by combining reduction to the invariant plane, a Poincaré–Bendixson analysis, and constructive algebraic criteria for Hopf bifurcation using the polynomial expressions furnished by mass-action kinetics.

With a view to understanding which small mass-action systems admit oscillation, in this paper we study rank-two networks with bimolecular source complexes but allow target complexes with higher molecularities.

title: Voyager 2 solar plasma and magnetic field spectral analysis for intermediate data sparsity
text_ai: The Voyager probes are the furthest, still active, spacecraft ever launched from Earth. During their 38-year trip, they have collected data regarding solar wind properties (such as the plasma velocity and magnetic field intensity). Unfortunately, a complete time evolution of the measured physical quantities is not available. Here, we present a spectral analysis framework specifically designed for the intermediate sparsity regime characteristic of long-baseline Voyager data. We compute one- and two-point spectra of the solar wind velocity and magnetic-field fluctuations, along with cross-spectral densities and coherence, over quasi-stationary intervals to minimize nonstationarity biases. To accommodate irregular sampling and gaps, we adapt a finite-window multitaper estimator augmented by gap-aware imputation and constraint-preserving smoothing, with supplementary validation from irregular-Lomb and wavelet-based approaches. Uncertainties are quantified through bootstrap resampling and Monte Carlo surrogates that preserve the original gap structure and short-time variability. The framework is validated on synthetic turbulent signals with prescribed spectra and sampling patterns emulating Voyager gaps, and then applied to Voyager 2 data spanning solar-cycle variations. We recover inertial-range magnetic fluctuations with slopes near −5/3 and velocity fluctuations near −3/2, with a scale-by-scale breakpoint consistent with dissipation physics. The estimates remain stable for gap fractions up to ~25–30% and reveal intermittent, scale-dependent v–B alignment and cross-helicity signatures characteristic of Alfvénic turbulence in the outer heliosphere.

title: Discrete-to-continuum limits of interacting particle systems in one dimension with collisions
text_ai: We study a class of interacting particle systems in which $n$ signed particles move on the real line. At close range particles with the same sign repel and particles with opposite sign attract each other. The repulsion and attraction are described by the same singular interaction force $f$. Assume f is odd and locally Lipschitz on R\{0}, with a symmetric singularity at the origin, namely f(x) ∼ c x/|x|^{1+α} as x → 0 for some α ∈ (0,1), and with suitable decay at infinity. We consider initial data consisting of n signed atoms with uniformly bounded total signed mass and finite second moment, and we form the signed empirical measure μ_n^0 := ∑_{i=1}^n σ_i δ_{x_i^0}, σ_i ∈ {±1}, x_i^0 ∈ R. The associated particle dynamics are governed by x_i'(t) = ∑_{j≠i} σ_i σ_j f(x_i − x_j), together with a collision rule that preserves the signed mass and is compatible with the one-dimensional geometry. We prove uniform a priori bounds for the discrete energy and the second moment, yielding tightness of (μ_n) in C([0,T]; M_b(R)) for any T>0. Up to subsequences, μ_n ⇀ μ in C([0,T]; M_b(R)), and μ satisfies the nonlocal continuity equation ∂_t μ + ∂_x ( μ (f * μ) ) = 0 in the distributional sense. Finite-time collisions appear as concentration phenomena and are propagated through the limit as mass-transfer events; in one dimension this leads to a well-posed measure-valued evolution, with a contraction-type stability in the signed Wasserstein metric.
prefix: We study a class of interacting particle systems in which $n$ signed particles move on the real line. At close range particles with the same sign repel and particles with opposite sign attract each other. The repulsion and attraction are described by the same singular interaction force $f$.

title: Investigation of Long Baseline Neutrino Oscillations from Experiments at KAON
text_ai: The proposed KAON factory at the Triumf Laboratory in Vancouver, Canada provides a unique opportunity for high statistics long baseline neutrino oscillation experiments. Several possibilities are under active consideration. In this paper we describe the theoretical expectations for a {\it very} long baseline experiment in which the neutrinos are directed towards, and detected at the Superkamiokande detector in Kamioka, Japan 7200 km away. Within the three-flavor oscillation framework and incorporating coherent forward scattering in the Earth's mantle, we compute the ν_μ disappearance and ν_e appearance probabilities for a KAON-derived beam with energies of a few GeV directed at Super-Kamiokande, 7200 km distant. In matter, the oscillation pattern exhibits hierarchy-driven distortions, and with high statistics, enables precise determination of sin^2 2θ23, and |Δm^2_32| and sensitivity to sin^2 2θ13 and the sign of Δm^2_31. By comparing neutrino and antineutrino running and exploiting the energy dependence at the first and second maxima, we assess the potential to constrain the CP phase δ and test the three-flavor picture. We estimate event rates and backgrounds for ν_μ→ν_e appearance and ν_μ disappearance channels, discuss systematic uncertainties, and outline beam and detector requirements for measurements. Our results indicate that, at these baselines, matter effects provide a clean handle on the mass hierarchy, with complementary information to shorter baselines.
prefix: The proposed KAON factory at the Triumf Laboratory in Vancouver, Canada provides a unique opportunity for high statistics long baseline neutrino oscillation experiments. Several possibilities are under active consideration. In this paper we describe the theoretical expectations for a {\it very} long baseline experiment in which the neutrinos are directed towards, and detected at the Superkamiokande detector in Kamioka, Japan 7200 km away.

title: Discontinuation of disease-modifying therapy in patients with multiple sclerosis over age 60.
text_ai: The risk-benefit ratio of continuing immunomodulating disease-modifying therapy (DMT) in older multiple sclerosis (MS) patients is unknown. To evaluate clinical and patient-reported outcomes after stopping DMT in older MS patients. Retrospective, observational study identifying patients from our MS clinics who were aged over 60 and on DMT > 2 years. Methods: Consecutive MS patients aged >60 who discontinued DMT after ≥2 years were identified from clinic records (2010–2022). Data included demographics, disease duration, DMT type and duration, cessation reason, and follow-up. Pre- and post-cessation ARR, disability progression, MRI activity, adverse events, and patient-reported QoL (MSQoL-54) and fatigue (FSS) were analyzed. Results: Sixty-eight patients (mean age 64.5±3.2; 52% female; median disease duration 17 years) were analyzed. Median time on DMT before stopping was 4.2 years; follow-up after cessation was 15 months (IQR 12–22). Eleven patients (16%) had ≥1 relapse post-cessation; ARR rose from 0.08 pre- to 0.24 post-cessation (p=0.04). Disability progression occurred in 6 patients (9%). New MRI activity post-cessation was observed in 5 of 30 imaged patients (17%). QoL improved in 38% and remained stable in 54%; fatigue remained unchanged on average. Higher baseline disability and lesion burden showed modest associations with relapse or progression after stopping. Conclusions: In this MS cohort, stopping DMT was feasible for most, with a modest relapse risk; monitoring is advised.

title: Best Practices for Alchemical Free Energy Calculations
text_ai: Alchemical free energy calculations are a useful tool for predicting free energy differences associated with the transfer of molecules from one environment to another. The hallmark of these methods is the use of "bridging" potential energy functions representing \emph{alchemical} intermediate states that cannot exist as real chemical species. These methods require careful design of the alchemical pathway, choice of estimators, and rigorous diagnostics to ensure robust estimates with quantified uncertainties. We discuss best practices for selecting lambda schedules, employing soft-core potentials, and separating decoupling of electrostatics from van der Waals interactions to minimize numerical instabilities. We compare estimators (MBAR, TI, BAR) and provide guidance on when to use each, including robust error estimation via bootstrapping and replicate calculations. We address sampling efficiency, recommend convergence checks based on state overlap and phase-space exploration, and emphasize adequate sampling of end states, proper treatment of long-range interactions, and finite-size corrections. Workflow recommendations cover reproducibility, data management, software validation, and community-standard benchmarks to enable transparent, transferable results.

title: Conformational selection and induced changes along the catalytic cycle of E. coli DHFR
text_ai: Protein function often involves changes between different conformations. Central questions are how these conformational changes are coupled to the binding or catalytic processes during which they occur, and how they affect the catalytic rates of enzymes. An important model system is the enzyme dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) from E. coli DHFR serves as a paradigmatic model for coupling conformational dynamics to chemistry. Here we integrate time-resolved kinetics, solution NMR relaxation dispersion, single-molecule FRET, and enhanced-sampling simulations to map the sequence of motions and chemical steps along the catalytic cycle. We find that conformational selection governs the initial ligand engagement: a preexisting closed Met20-loop substate is enriched upon NADPH binding, thereby priming the active site for folate reduction. The subsequent hydride transfer involves coupled, predominantly induced, rearrangements of the Met20 and FG loops and the hydrogen-bond network that transiently lower the activation barrier. Product formation shifts the ensemble toward an open/occluded mixture that disfavors re-binding until product release occurs. Kinetic partitioning among these substates modulates kcat and, to a lesser extent, substrate affinity, with mutations and temperature shifting the balance between selection and induction. Overall, the cycle embodies a cooperative interplay where conformational selection seeds productive binding and induced changes optimize chemistry, outlining a generalizable framework for enzymatic dynamics across DHFR and related systems.

title: Rashba interferometers: Spin-dependent single and two-electron interference
text_ai: Quantum transport in semiconductor nanostructures can be described theoretically in terms of the propagation and scattering of electron probability waves. Within this approach, elements of a phase-coherent electric circuit play a role similar to quantum-optical devices that can be characterised by scattering matrices. By combining spin-orbit coupling with phase-coherent transport, we construct a scattering theory for Rashba interferometers. We show that electron spinor evolution along arm segments is captured by a 2x2 unitary transfer matrix whose elements encode spin precession, enabling spin-dependent constructive or destructive interference at multiport beam splitters. In single-electron devices, the visibility and phase of conductance oscillations can be tuned by gate-controlled Rashba strength and by path length differences, yielding controllable spin rotations without magnetic fields. In two-electron configurations, we analyze the amplitudes and identify regimes where exchange interference and spin entanglement manifest in cross-correlations, allowing discrimination between singlet and triplet components. The framework accommodates realistic dephasing and finite-temperature effects, predicting interferometric signatures provided phase coherence length exceeds the interferometer scale. We quantify quality factors for operation and propose geometries—linear and loop interferometers, and Y-junction splits—that maximize spin-dependent contrast. Our results delineate design principles for Rashba-based interferometers as spin filters, phase gates, and sources of spin-entangled electron pairs, with implications for on-chip spintronics and quantum information processing.

title: Effects of Stellar Feedback on Stellar and Gas Kinematics of Star-Forming Galaxies at 0.6<z<1.0
text_ai: Recent zoom-in cosmological simulations have shown that stellar feedback can flatten the inner density profile of the dark matter halo in low-mass galaxies. A correlation between the stellar/gas velocity dispersion ($\sigma_{star}$, $\sigma_{gas}$) and the specific star formation rate (sSFR) is predicted as an observational test of the role of stellar feedback in re-shaping the dark matter density profile. Using integral-field spectroscopy of star-forming disks at 0.6<z<1.0, we measure σ_star and σ_gas after correcting for instrumental line spread, beam smearing, and pressure support. sSFR is inferred from Hα and 24μm plus UV luminosities; stellar masses come from SED fitting. We find a statistically significant positive correlation between σ_star and sSFR across M_star ~10^9–10^11 M_sun, with a weaker, more dispersed trend for σ_gas. The σ_star–sSFR relation is steepest in the inner 1–2 kpc, suggesting burst-driven potential fluctuations are most effective centrally. Controlling for stellar mass and inclination, the amplitude of σ_star at fixed sSFR decreases with increasing M_star, consistent with deeper potentials dampening non-thermal motions. The observed signatures align with feedback-induced heating and rapid gas outflows predicted by high-resolution simulations and provide an empirical link to the cusp–core debate. Systematics and selection effects are discussed, with implications for interpreting kinematics in the epoch of peak star formation. Further work constrains feedback models.

title: Single-Particle Green Functions in Exactly Solvable Models of Bose and Fermi Liquids
text_ai: Based on a class of exactly solvable models of interacting bose and fermi liquids, we compute the single-particle propagators of these systems exactly for all wavelengths and energies and in any number of spatial dimensions. Explicit closed-form expressions for the time-ordered propagators are obtained for k and ω, revealing a factorized structure in which a freely propagating core is dressed by a universal bosonic cloud. In bosonic liquids the spectral function displays a delta peak accompanied by an incoherent continuum whose edge carries the same algebraic singularity familiar from edge problems; in fermionic liquids the Landau quasiparticle pole is generically replaced by a branch with a dimensional anomalous exponent, yielding non-Fermi-liquid dynamics in dimensions. The exponents depend solely on the forward-scattering interaction and are independent of microscopic lattice details, illustrating a solvable universality class. Sum rules and Ward identities are checked exactly. The results clarify how exact correlations reshape single-particle coherence, providing benchmarks for numerics and guiding interpretation of spectroscopic probes.

title: Cocommutative q-cycle coalgebra structures on the dual of the truncated polynomial algebra
text_ai: In order to construct solutions of the braid equation we consider bijective left non-degenerate set-theoretic type solutions, which correspond to regular q-cycle coalgebras. We obtain a partial classification of the different q-cycle coalgebra structures on the dual coalgebra of $K[y]/\langle y^n\rangle$, the truncated polynomial algebra. These structures yield bijections of a set that give R-matrices satisfying the braid equation. We derive necessary and sufficient conditions on the dual structure constants for cocommutativity, regularity and left non-degeneracy. Up to coalgebra isomorphism, the q-cycle coalgebras on D = (K[y]/(y^n))^* organize into patterns: a monomial-type in which a single generator controls coproduct, and a cyclic-type governed by an n-cycle. For general n we obtain explicit descriptions of the coproduct, counit and induced switch, from which the corresponding solutions are read off. Consequently, the results yield infinite families and a finite set of exceptional types, each furnishing a Yang–Baxter operator and illustrating how cocommutativity constrains realizations on the dual of the truncated polynomial algebra.

title: Seroepidemiology of Toxoplasma gondii in wild ruminants in Spain.
text_ai: Toxoplasmosis is a parasitic zoonosis caused by Toxoplasma gondii which infects warm-blooded species worldwide. Humans can be infected through ingestion of tissue cysts from raw or undercooked meat, including game meat. A nationwide large-scale cross-sectional study was conducted to assess exposure to T. gondii in seven wild ruminant species in Spain. Serum samples (n = 6,120) from 2,320 animals representing seven wild ruminant species were analyzed using the modified agglutination test (MAT). Overall seroprevalence was 43.1% (95% CI 41.6–44.6). Inter-species variation was evident, with higher prevalences in Iberian ibex and mouflon (≥60%), intermediate in red deer and fallow deer (40–55%), and lower in roe deer (≈30%). Age positively correlated with seropositivity (adults vs juveniles, OR 2.3, 95% CI 1.9–2.8). Geographically, higher seroprevalence occurred in southern and central Spain, consistent with greater environmental contamination by cat feces. Sex and sampling season showed no consistent associations after adjustment. Multivariable analysis identified age, species, and region as independent predictors of exposure. The findings indicate widespread exposure of wild ruminants to T. gondii across Spain, with potential implications for human risk through consumption of game meat and for wildlife–human health interfaces, underscoring need for risk communication and integrated surveillance. These data provide baseline prevalence for monitoring temporal trends under changing land use and climate conditions.

title: Graphical Modelling in Genetics and Systems Biology
text_ai: Graphical modelling has a long history in statistics as a tool for the analysis of multivariate data, starting from Wright's path analysis and Gibbs' applications to statistical physics at the beginning of the last century. Graphical models encode conditional independence statements via graphs, enabling compact representation of multivariate dependencies and scalable inference in high dimensions. In genetics and systems biology, they support reconstructing regulatory networks from gene expression, epigenetic, and metabolomic data, and facilitate causal reasoning under interventions. We emphasize approaches ranging from undirected Gaussian graphical models for steady-state analyses to directed Bayesian networks and dynamic Bayesian networks for time-course and perturbation studies. Methodological advances—sparsity-inducing priors, regularization paths, and scalable structure-learning algorithms—address dimensionality and measurement noise. Mixed graphical models extend to discrete and continuous omics, while latent-variable and factor-graph formulations accommodate hidden regulators. Challenges include identifiability, confounding, and integration of prior knowledge with data-driven learning. The paper surveys theory, computation, and applications, highlighting directions for systems-driven genetic discovery and precision biology.
prefix: Graphical modelling has a long history in statistics as a tool for the analysis of multivariate data, starting from Wright's path analysis and Gibbs' applications to statistical physics at the beginning of the last century.

title: Image Quality Assessment Guided Deep Neural Networks Training
text_ai: For many computer vision problems, the deep neural networks are trained and validated based on the assumption that the input images are pristine (i.e., artifact-free). However, digital images are subject to a wide range of distortions in real application scenarios, while the practical issues regarding image quality in high level visual information understanding have been largely ignored. In this work, we propose an image quality-aware training paradigm that jointly optimizes recognition performance and perceptual quality. Our approach introduces a differentiable image quality predictor that estimates distortion at the input and feeds a quality-conditioned weighting into the task losses, combined with an auxiliary IQA consistency objective to preserve perceptual semantics under degradation. We explore several instantiations, including quality-guided sample reweighting, curriculum scheduling based on estimated IQA, and an end-to-end joint optimization that couples a lightweight IQA head with the backbone. We assess robustness to common distortions (blur, noise, compression) and unseen quality variations, demonstrating improved accuracy under degraded inputs while maintaining pristine performance.

title: Financial Burdens of Out-of-Pocket Spending Among Medicare Fee-for-Service Beneficiaries: Role of the "Big Four" Chronic Health Conditions.
text_ai: While Medicare is the universal source of health care coverage for Americans aged 65 years or older, the program requires significant cost sharing in terms of out-of-pocket (OOP) spending. Objectives: To quantify out-of-pocket spending and financial burden attributable to the Big Four chronic conditions among Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries, and to examine how costs relate to sociodemographic factors and insurance design. Methods: We use MCBS data linked to expenditure files, focusing on beneficiaries aged 65+ with diabetes, cardiovascular disease, cancer, or chronic lung disease. We estimate annual OOP costs (premiums, deductibles, copayments, coinsurance, Part D gaps) and financial burden (OOP as a share of household income; high-burden defined). Multivariable models adjust for age, sex, race/ethnicity, comorbidity, income, dual eligibility, and plan type. Results: All four conditions are associated with higher OOP spending and greater financial strain, with cancer and chronic lung disease showing the largest elevations; dual-eligible and low-income beneficiaries bear disproportionate burdens. Conclusions: Reducing cost sharing and strengthening protections for vulnerable groups are needed to alleviate financial hardship.
prefix: While Medicare is the universal source of health care coverage for Americans aged 65 years or older, the program requires significant cost sharing in terms of out-of-pocket (OOP) spending.

title: Quenched Lattice QCD with Domain Wall Fermions and the Chiral Limit
text_ai: Quenched QCD simulations on three volumes, $8^3 \times$, $12^3 \times$ and $16^3 \times 32$ and three couplings, $\beta=5.7$, 5.85 and 6.0 using domain wall fermions provide a consistent picture of quenched QCD. Two-point correlation functions of pseudoscalar and vector mesons, as well as baryons, were measured on each ensemble. We extract masses from effective-mass plateaus and determine the pion decay constant from the axial-vector current using the chiral Ward identity. The residual mass m_res, from the axial Ward identity, is small (m_res a ≲ few × 10^−3) and decreases with β and Ls, confirming good chiral symmetry in the DWF formulation at these parameters. The PCAC quark mass defined from the axial current correlator is used to form m_pi^2 versus m_q curves, which exhibit the expected nonlinear dependence in the quenched theory. The consistency across volumes for β=5.85 and 6.0 is encouraging; finite-volume effects are evident on the 8^3 × 32 lattice at the lightest m_q but are within statistical uncertainties for 12^3 × 32 and 16^3 × 32. Renormalization constants Z_A and Z_S were determined nonperturbatively; the resulting quark-mass estimates in the MS-bar scheme at 2 GeV are compatible with phenomenological expectations. Overall, the data provide a coherent quenched chiral picture with domain wall fermions and establish a robust chiral limit accessible on moderate lattices, enabling future unquenched studies.

title: BodyMetric: Evaluating the Realism of Human Bodies in Text-to-Image Generation
text_ai: Accurately generating images of human bodies from text remains a challenging problem for state of the art text-to-image models. Commonly observed body-related artifacts include extra or missing limbs, unrealistic poses, blurred body parts, etc. Currently, evaluation of such artifacts relies heavily on time-consuming human judgments, limiting the ability to benchmark models at scale. To address this, we propose BodyMetric, an automatic, artifact‑aware benchmarking suite that operates on generated imagery and associated prompts. At its core, BodyMetric decomposes realism into four orthogonal dimensions: geometric plausibility (limb and joint consistency with a body model), pose articulation (kinematic feasibility under SMPL‑like constraints), surface fidelity (skin, clothing, texture and edge coherence), and contextual coherence (alignment between depicted bodies and described attributes or activity). We instantiate these with a lightweight, differentiable pipeline that uses off‑the‑shelf detectors and a differentiable SMPL retargeting stage to derive constraint‑satisfying proxies. The framework is evaluated on a curated benchmark of 2,000 prompt–image pairs, spanning synthetic and real references, with ground‑truth keypoints and body masks. BodyMetric yields a composite score as a weighted aggregation of sub‑scores, calibrated against human judgments. Across several state‑of‑the‑art models, our method reveals systematic artifacts and provides finer discrimination than rating alone, while enabling scalable, repeatable comparisons and bias analyses. We release code, data, and evaluation protocols to foster community adoption.

title: Relativistic diffusion
text_ai: We discuss a relativistic diffusion in the proper time in an approach of Schay and Dudley. We derive (Langevin) stochastic differential equations in various coordinates.We show that in some coordinates the stochastic differential equations become linear. We obtain momentum probability distribution in an explicit form.We discuss a relativistic particle diffusing in an external electromagnetic field. Consequently we obtain explicit expressions for the stationary momentum distribution, which in the medium rest frame reduces to the Jüttner form; we discuss its convergence properties and dependence on the drag parameter. The diffusion generator on the mass-shell is shown to be the Lorentz-covariant Laplace–Beltrami operator, augmented by a drift term representing friction and the influence of external fields. The associated Fokker–Planck equation for the phase-space density is derived, and the relativistic Maxwell–Jüttner distribution is identified as the equilibrium solution. In a constant external electromagnetic field we examine the stochastic dynamics of the canonical momentum; the momentum diffusion tensor is diagonalizable in a suitable comoving frame, and for parallel electric and uniform magnetic fields the equations decouple, yielding linear subsystems. We illustrate the framework with explicit one-dimensional reductions along the field lines and discuss the approach to equilibrium. The construction provides a covariant diffusion description appropriate for kinetic theory in high-energy plasmas and applications to heavy-ion phenomenology.

title: PeV Neutrinos and a 3.5 keV X-Ray Line from a PeV Scale Supersymmetric Neutrino Sector
text_ai: Recent measurements of PeV energy neutrinos at IceCube and a 3.5 keV X-ray line in the spectra of several galaxies are both tantalizing signatures of new physics. This paper shows that one or both of these observations can be explained within an extended supersymmetric neutrino sector. Within a supersymmetric seesaw framework, we demonstrate that a keV-scale sterile state can produce the 3.5 keV line while a PeV-scale sector yields a flux compatible with IceCube. The model embeds a 7 keV sterile neutrino N_s that mixes with active states with a small angle, enabling radiative decay N_s -> ν + γ and yielding the observed line under production in the early Universe. A heavier right-handed state with mass M_R ~ PeV drives the high-energy spectrum via its decays and through cascade processes, while preserving the light neutrino masses and mixings. A joint fit to IceCube and X-ray data identifies viable regions, with distinctive predictions for future γ-ray and neutrino surveys.

title: Theory of analytical energy derivatives for the variational quantum eigensolver
text_ai: The variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) and its variants, which is a method for finding eigenstates and eigenenergies of a given Hamiltonian, are appealing applications of near-term quantum computers. Although the eigenenergies are certainly important quantities which determines properties of a given system, their derivatives with respect to parameters of the system, such as positions of nuclei if we target a quantum chemistry problem, are also crucial to analyze the system. Here we develop a formal framework for analytic energy derivatives within the VQE paradigm, anchored in a differentiable ansatz and generalized parameter-shift calculus. By treating Hamiltonian parameters as explicit inputs on the variational manifold, we derive closed-form expressions for gradients (and, where possible, higher derivatives) of ground- and excited-state energies with respect to nuclear coordinates and external fields. The resulting formulas decompose into wavefunction- and operator-dependent terms, are amenable to evaluation with finite sampling, and integrate with differentiation for efficient geometry optimization and force calculations in quantum chemistry simulations.

title: Individualized PATE: Differentially Private Machine Learning with Individual Privacy Guarantees
text_ai: Applying machine learning (ML) to sensitive domains requires privacy protection of the underlying training data through formal privacy frameworks, such as differential privacy (DP). Yet, usually, the privacy of the training data comes at the cost of the resulting ML models' utility. Traditional DP yields a uniform privacy guarantee across all training instances, ignoring variability in data sensitivity and user preferences. We propose Individualized PATE (IPATE), a per-instance privacy-aware extension of the Private Aggregation of Teacher Ensembles. IPATE assigns each training example a target privacy level and tunes the noise added to teacher votes and the downstream student labeling accordingly. The method preserves the teacher-student architecture: a committee of private teachers votes on labels for unlabeled queries, but aggregation is privatized with a per-example budget that can be larger for less sensitive records and tighter for more sensitive ones. We derive per-example DP guarantees and compose them to obtain overall privacy accounting, while maintaining a clean separation between labeling and learning. We validate IPATE on multiple datasets and report improvements in accuracy under the same local privacy budget compared with canonical PATE and DP-SGD baselines. Our results demonstrate that individualized privacy yields meaningful utility gains by selectively allocating privacy loss, and we discuss practical considerations for specifying privacy preferences and auditing.

title: Inflexibility and independence: Phase transitions in the majority-rule model
text_ai: In this work we study opinion formation in a population participating of a public debate with two distinct choices. We considered three distinct mechanisms of social interactions and individuals' behavior: conformity, nonconformity and inflexibility. The conformity is ruled by the majority-rule dynamics, whereas the nonconformity is introduced in the population as an independent behavior, implying the failure to attempted group influence. Adopting a mean-field and agent-based simulation approach, we track the time evolution of the opinion density x of choice A. The dynamics combines deterministic conformist updates (majority rule) with stochastic independence and inflexible agents that never flip. We derive the rate equation for x and identify stationary solutions, revealing a competition between order induced by conformity and disorder from independence, biased by inflexibles. The results yield a phase diagram in the (independence probability, fraction of inflexibles) plane: a line of continuous transitions with a tricritical point beyond which the transition becomes discontinuous. Finite-size scaling supports the identified universality class.

The conformity is ruled by the majority-rule dynamics, whereas the nonconformity is introduced in the population as an independent behavior, implying the failure to attempted group influence.

title: NICE^k Metrics: Unified and Multidimensional Framework for Evaluating Deterministic Solar Forecasting Accuracy
text_ai: Accurate solar energy output prediction is key for integrating renewables into grids, maintaining stability, and improving energy management. However, standard error metrics such as Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Skill Scores (SS) fail to capture the multidimensional nature of solar irradiance forecasting. The NICE^k framework treats forecasting accuracy as a vector-valued construct, decomposing errors into k interpretable dimensions that collectively capture the multidimensional nature of solar irradiance. Each dimension targets a distinct operational and physical facet of the forecast: magnitude (energy-error relative to capacity), timing (temporal misalignment with the diurnal cycle and event ramps), shape (discrepancies in the temporal distribution of irradiance within a horizon), continuity (penalization of abrupt, non-physical fluctuations), and bias (systematic over- or underprediction). To ensure cross-site and cross-season comparability, errors are nonlinearly normalized by climatology and available capacity, with safeguards against division by near-zero baselines. A unifying aggregation then yields a composite NICE^k score, while tetap sub-scores provide actionable diagnostics for each dimension. The framework supports deterministic forecasts across multiple horizons and locations, and is designed to be modular, allowing the inclusion of additional dimensions (k > 5) as forecasting needs evolve. Empirical validation across diverse datasets demonstrates that NICE^k outperforms traditional metrics in differentiating forecast quality, stabilizing model rankings, and aligning evaluation with grid-operations objectives such as ramp handling and predictability-based dispatch.

title: Block-MDS QC-LDPC Codes for Information Reconciliation in Key Distribution
text_ai: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is a popular protocol that provides information theoretically secure keys to multiple parties. Two important post-processing steps of QKD are 1) the information reconciliation (IR) step, where parties reconcile mismatches in generated keys through classical communication, and 2) the privacy amplification (PA) step, where parties distill their common key into a new secure key that the adversary has little to no information about. This work proposes block-MDS QC-LDPC codes for information reconciliation in QKD. By exploiting the block-MDS property across quasi-cyclic subcodes and judicious degree distributions, we achieve near-optimal leakage for a given block length while maintaining low decoding complexity. We adopt a syndrome-based, one-way IR with adaptive rate matching to estimated QBER and secure frame formation. Our construction supports high-throughput operations with compact storage and scalable encoding/decoding. Numerical results under realistic fiber-QKD conditions demonstrate reconciliation efficiencies approaching the Shannon limit with frame error rates well below 10^-4 at practical lengths and robust performance under timing constraints.

Two important post-processing steps of QKD are 1) the information reconciliation (IR) step, where parties reconcile mismatches in generated keys through classical communication, and 2) the privacy amplification (PA) step, where parties distill their common key into a new secure key that the adversary has little to no information about.

title: Competitive Collaboration: Joint Unsupervised Learning of Depth, Camera Motion, Optical Flow and Motion Segmentation
text_ai: We address the unsupervised learning of several interconnected problems in low-level vision: single view depth prediction, camera motion estimation, optical flow, and segmentation of a video into the static scene and moving regions. Our key insight is that these four fundamental vision problems are coupled through geometric constraints. To operationalize these ideas, we propose a unified, differentiable objective that enforces cross-task consistency across depth, ego-motion, optical flow, and motion segmentation within a single training loop. We instantiate four predictors: D(·) for depth, P(·) for camera motion, F(·) for dense flow, and S(·) for per-pixel motion labels. These share an encoder backbone but are trained under a competitive-collaboration paradigm: at each iteration, competing hypotheses about scene motion—static versus moving regions—are generated, and a winner is selected per pixel according to reprojection error under the current geometry. The winning explanations update all modules, while a soft competition term preserves uncertainty and avoids trivial solutions. Training relies on occlusion-aware photometric reconstruction, edge-aware smoothness terms, and explicit geometric constraints (consistency between depth, pose, and flow; epipolar constraints). Notably, the motion mask arises as a natural consequence of explaining the data with coherent rigid and nonrigid components. Experiments on diverse monocular sequences show consistent gains across all four tasks relative to strong baselines, with ablations validating the contribution of the competitive-collaborative mechanism.
prefix: We address the unsupervised learning of several interconnected problems in low-level vision: single view depth prediction, camera motion estimation, optical flow, and segmentation of a video into the static scene and moving regions. title: Structure Modeling Activation Free Fourier Network for Spacecraft Image Denoising
text_ai: Spacecraft image denoising is a crucial fundamental technology closely related to aerospace research. However, the existing deep learning-based image denoising methods are primarily designed for natural image and fail to adequately consider the characteristics of spacecraft image(e.g. low-light conditions, repetitive periodic structures), resulting in suboptimal performance in the spacecraft image denoising task. To address these limitations, we propose the Structure Modeling Activation Free Fourier Network (SMAFNet) that fuses a structure-aware Fourier denoiser with an activation-free reconstruction backbone. The structure modeling branch encodes repetitive periodic textures in spacecraft imagery via learnable spectral filters and a structured-prior convolutional module, enforcing consistency across patch repetitions. The activation-free reconstruction backbone propagates information linearly with residual ties and adaptive spectral shrinkage, preserving fine details while suppressing stochastic noise without nonlinear artefacts. A frequency-domain consistency loss reinforces alignment between input and denoised spectra. Experiments on synthetic and spacecraft data demonstrate superior denoising performance over methods, especially under low-light and high-frequency content, with reduced artifacts and faster convergence.

However, the existing deep learning-based image denoising methods are primarily designed for natural image and fail to adequately consider the characteristics of spacecraft image(e.g. low-light conditions, repetitive periodic structures), resulting in suboptimal performance in the spacecraft image denoising task.

title: Immediate primary skin closure in type-III A and B open fractures: results after a minimum of five years
text_ai: Between June 1999 and May 2003 we undertook direct primary closure of the skin wounds of 173 patients with Gustilo and Anderson grade-IIIA and grade-IIIB open fractures. These patients were selected from a consecutive group of 557 with type-III injuries presenting during this time. Debridement was performed to remove all nonviable tissue, and closure was pursued when a reliable soft-tissue envelope was confirmed within 24 hours. Fracture stabilization was achieved chiefly with external fixation (n=112); primary internal fixation was performed when soft-tissue conditions permitted (n=41). A uniform perioperative antibiotic regimen was administered, and cultures were obtained when infections were suspected. At minimum five-year follow-up (mean 6.3 years, range 5–12), radiographic union occurred in 162 of 173 fractures (93.6%). Deep infection developed in 9 patients (5.2%), superficial infection in 12 (6.9%), and wound dehiscence requiring revision in 14 (8.1%). Reoperation for hardware-related or soft-tissue problems occurred in 31 patients (18%). Nonunion was seen in 11 (6.3%); malunion in 9 (5.2%). Limb salvage was achieved in all but two cases (1.2%). Functional outcomes were satisfactory in the majority, with most patients regaining near-normal range of motion and return to work within 6–12 months. These results support immediate primary skin closure as a viable option in carefully selected Gustilo IIIB and IIIA injuries.

title: Robust Contact State Estimation in Humanoid Walking Gaits
text_ai: In this article, we propose a deep learning framework that provides a unified approach to the problem of leg contact detection in humanoid robot walking gaits. Our formulation accomplishes to accurately and robustly estimate the contact state probability for each leg (i.e., stable or slip/no contact). By fusing proprioceptive cues from joint encoders and leg torque sensors with exteroceptive signals from contact pads and inertial measurements, the model outputs per-leg contact likelihoods with calibrated uncertainty. An architecture that combines temporal convolutional layers with a lightweight recurrent block captures gait-dependent dynamics and enables timely detection during fast swing-to-stance transitions. Training leverages a large synthetic-to-real dataset, augmented with domain randomization to bridge sim-to-real gaps, and uses a robust loss with label smoothing plus Bayesian post-processing to suppress transient misclassifications. We validate on multiple humanoid platforms across flat, inclined, and compliant terrains, demonstrating improved accuracy, reduced false-alarm rates, and seamless integration with model-predictive walking controllers.

Our formulation accomplishes to accurately and robustly estimate the contact state probability for each leg (i.e., stable or slip/no contact).

title: What Makes for Good Views for Contrastive Learning?
text_ai: Contrastive learning between multiple views of the data has recently achieved state of the art performance in the field of self-supervised representation learning. Despite its success, the influence of different view choices has been less studied. To this end, we construct a spectrum of view families ranging from mild geometric and photometric perturbations to content-preserving, structure-preserving transformations. We evaluate their impact on the alignment and uniformity of representations, as well as on downstream linear probes. Our results show that view quality hinges on preserving task-relevant content while suppressing nuisance variation; overly aggressive augmentations can induce distortion and collapse unless additional regularization or batch settings are employed. We propose a diagnostic, the view-utility score, that predicts downstream performance from a set of statistics, including alignment error and mutual information estimates between views. Across multiple datasets and objectives, we identify robust view families that reliably improve transfer and offer practical guidelines for principled view design and augmentation policy in contrastive learning.

title: 4G 5G Cell-level Multi-indicator Forecasting based on Dense-MLP
text_ai: With the development of 4G/5G, the rapid growth of traffic has caused a large number of cell indicators to exceed the warning threshold, and network quality has deteriorated. It is necessary for operators to solve the congestion in advance and effectively to guarantee the quality of user experience. To address this, we propose a cell-level multi-indicator forecasting framework based on Dense-MLP, which jointly predicts a set of critical network indicators from historical traces. The model integrates heterogeneous features—temporal histories, spatial relations, and modality-specific signals—through densely connected blocks that promote rich inter-indicator coupling while preserving gradient flow. A multi-task objective enforces consistency across indicators and dampens overfitting under limited supervision. We validate on a real-world 4G/5G dataset spanning dozens of cells and multiple rolling windows, comparing against LSTM, GRU, Transformer, and conventional MLP baselines. Results show consistent improvements in MAE/RMSE and robustness to missing data, with low inference latency suitable for online congestion prevention and QoE assurance in practice.
prefix: With the development of 4G/5G, the rapid growth of traffic has caused a large number of cell indicators to exceed the warning threshold, and network quality has deteriorated. It is necessary for operators to solve the congestion in advance and effectively to guarantee the quality of user experience.

title: Accuracy of model-based tracking of knee kinematics and cartilage contact measured by dynamic volumetric MRI
text_ai: The purpose of this study was to determine the accuracy of knee kinematics and cartilage contact measured by volumetric dynamic MRI. A motor-actuated phantom drove femoral and tibial bone segments through cyclic 3D motion patterns. Volumetric images were continuously acquired using a 3D radially undersampled cine spoiled gradient echo sequence (SPGR-VIPR). Model-based tracking estimated tibiofemoral kinematics by rigidly registering a detailed femoral and tibial bone surface model to each volume, using a gradient-based optimizer with surface constraints to suppress spurious motion. Kinematic outputs included flexion–extension, internal–external rotation, and anterior–posterior/medial–lateral translations, together with framewise cartilage-surface contact coordinates projected onto the articular layers. Ground-truth motion was provided by synchronized encoder signals from the motor actuator driving the phantom joints. Cartilage contact was quantified as the minimum distance between mapped femoral and tibial cartilage surfaces and reported as both a contact location along the surface and an area proxy derived from depth of penetration. Agreement with ground truth was assessed with RMSE, bias, and Bland–Altman analyses, and strength of association with Pearson r. Across cycles, translational and rotational errors remained below 1 mm and 0.5°, with RMSEs of approximately 0.7 mm and 0.5°. Cartilage-contact localization averaged ~0.9 mm error, with timing differences around 15 ms. Correlations between tracked and true trajectories exceeded 0.95 (p < 0.001). The method demonstrated consistent accuracy under continuous dynamic imaging and varying motion speeds, indicating feasibility for dynamic in vivo knee kinematics and cartilage contact assessment.

A motor-actuated phantom drove femoral and tibial bone segments through cyclic 3D motion patterns. Volumetric images were continuously acquired using a 3D radially undersampled cine spoiled gradient echo sequence (SPGR-VIPR).

title: Harnessing TH9 cells in cancer immunotherapy.
text_ai: CD4 T cell effector subsets not only profoundly affect cancer progression, but recent evidence also underscores their critical contribution to the anticancer efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors. In 2012, the two seminal studies suggested the superior antimelanoma activity of T H 9 cells over other T cell subsets upon adoptive T cell transfer. Here, we summarize the mechanistic basis of TH9–mediated tumor control, highlighting IL-9–dependent recruitment and activation of innate and adaptive effectors within the tumor microenvironment. IL-9 supports dendritic cell maturation and cross-priming of CD8+ T cells, while orchestrating eosinophil and mast cell–mediated inflammatory networks that potentiate cytotoxic responses. We review evidence that TH9-skewed responses synergize with PD-1/PD-L1 blockade, and that tumor-resident TH9 cells correlate with favorable immunosurveillance across cancer models. We propose practical strategies to harness TH9 biology—genetic or pharmacologic TH9 programming, local IL-9 delivery, and combinatorial regimens—to overcome anergic barriers, optimize durability, and minimize off-target effects. Our synthesis highlights translational avenues for durable immunity.

In 2012, the two seminal studies suggested the superior antimelanoma activity of T H 9 cells over other T cell subsets upon adoptive T cell transfer.

title: Single-domain chemical, thermochemical and thermal remanences in a basaltic rock
text_ai: Tiny basaltic samples containing finely grained titanomagnetite with Curie temperature less than 100 C were heated in air in weak field (25 to 100microT) at temperatures between 400 and 560 C for times as long as 32 hours. These experiments show that oxidation-driven chemical alteration during heating in air generates remanences that, in many respects, resemble conventional thermoremanent signatures but arise from in situ mineralogical change. CRM intensities scale with the extent of titanomagnetite oxidation to maghemite/hematite and correlate with longer heating times and higher temperatures; the remanence directions remain tightly clustered and parallel to the applied field, indicating retention of single-domain alignment despite chemical modification. Spectral analyses indicate the remanence is carried predominantly by grains in the SD size range (<0.5 μm, consistent with titanomagnetite and its oxidation products), with a minor contribution from PSD fractions. The thermochemical remanence (TCRM) is manifested as a second, field-dependent component that appears during heating and persists upon cooling, exhibiting a broader blocking spectrum than CRM alone. The thermal remanence (TRM) acquired during cooling in the same weak field shows a conventional SD/PSD mix but can be superimposed on CRM, obscuring paleomagnetic signals if oxidation histories are unknown. Overall, these results support a single-domain framework for chemically, thermochemically and thermally induced remanences in basaltic rock, governed by grain size, oxidation state and the kinetics of transformation.
prefix: Tiny basaltic samples containing finely grained titanomagnetite with Curie temperature less than 100 C were heated in air in weak field (25 to 100microT) at temperatures between 400 and 560 C for times as long as 32 hours.

title: Symplectic structure of post-Newtonian Hamiltonian for spinning compact binaries
text_ai: The phase space of a Hamiltonian system is symplectic. However, the post-Newtonian Hamiltonian formulation of spinning compact binaries in existing publications does not have this property, when position, momentum and spin variables $[X, P, S_1, S_2]$ compose its phase space. Here, we demonstrate that the apparent non-symplecticity originates from treating the spin degrees of freedom as independent canonical coordinates. By implementing the standard covariant spin supplementary condition (SSC) and introducing a pair of canonical spin variables on the reduced phase space, we derive a closed, nondegenerate symplectic two-form. We show that the PN Hamiltonian—including leading spin-orbit and spin-spin terms up to the targeted PN order—is Hamiltonian with respect to this form, and that the resulting equations of motion reproduce the covariant Mathisson–Papapetrou–Dixon dynamics upon reduction. A constructive procedure, based on a canonical transformation to intrinsic spin variables and the use of Dirac brackets for the SSC, yields a fully symplectic evolution. We verify conservation of the symplectic form and discuss the implications for Liouville integrability on the reduced manifold. The reformulation supports the deployment of long-time symplectic integrators and clarifies how higher PN corrections and tidal interactions can be incorporated while preserving canonical geometry. Implications for waveform modeling and numerical relativity benchmarks are discussed in practical calculations.
