title: Thinking Assistants: LLM-Based Conversational Assistants that Help Users Think By Asking rather than Answering
text_ai: Many AI systems focus solely on providing solutions or explaining outcomes. However, complex tasks like research and strategic thinking often benefit from a more comprehensive approach to augmenting the thinking process rather than passively getting information. We introduce Thinking Assistants, a class of LLM-based interlocutors that foster thinking by asking targeted, adaptive questions, proposing problem frames, and scaffolding reasoning steps. Rather than delivering conclusions, they co-create the reasoning path, surface hidden assumptions, test hypotheses, and organize evidence. The design rests on four pillars: (i) goal-first prompting that elicits explicit objectives; (ii) metacognitive prompts that expose reasoning structure and potential biases; (iii) iterative plan-and-check cycles that convert rough ideas into concrete steps; and (iv) transparent justification traces that document why questions were asked and how insights were reached. We instantiate these assistants in a modular prompt framework and evaluate them through controlled experiments and qualitative field studies. Tasks include literature synthesis, framing problems, generating hypotheses, and planning decisions. Compared with traditional information-provision agents, Thinking Assistants increase engagement, yield more diverse hypotheses, and improve perceived autonomy, with longer interactions. User feedback notes enhanced sensemaking, reduced premature closure, and greater trust when the assistant clearly communicates intent and records steps. These findings support a shift toward thinking collaboration.
prefix: Many AI systems focus solely on providing solutions or explaining outcomes. However, complex tasks like research and strategic thinking often benefit from a more comprehensive approach to augmenting the thinking process rather than passively getting information.

title: Optimized Treatment Schedules for Chronic Myeloid Leukemia
text_ai: Over the past decade, several targeted therapies (e.g. imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib) have been developed to treat Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML). Despite an initial response to therapy, drug resistance remains a problem for some CML patients. To address this, we integrate mechanistic modeling of leukemic burden with pharmacokinetic constraints and resistance dynamics into a patient‑specific optimization framework. We develop a population pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic model of BCR‑ABL suppression, coupled with a clonal evolution submodel that tracks resistant mutations and stem cell reservoirs. An optimal‑control formulation seeks dosing sequences that maximize projected duration of deep molecular response while limiting exposure and adverse events, subject to safety thresholds on trough concentrations and cumulative toxicity. We validate the approach using retrospective data from two CML cohorts treated with first‑ and second‑line TKIs, and perform in silico experiments across a range of adherence scenarios. The resulting schedules favor intermittent, high‑coverage suppression periods alternating with reduced‑dose intervals, achieving comparable or superior molecular response at lower total drug exposure. Sensitivity analyses identify patient covariates (age, baseline burden, mutation profile) that shift the optimal strategy. Prospective simulations suggest potential gains in resistance‑free time and quality‑adjusted life years, with practical implementation through model‑predictive control integrated into clinical decision support. Limitations include simplifications of microenvironment effects and the need for prospective clinical validation.
prefix: Over the past decade, several targeted therapies (e.g. imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib) have been developed to treat Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML). Despite an initial response to therapy, drug resistance remains a problem for some CML patients.

title: Window-based Model Averaging Improves Generalization in Heterogeneous Federated Learning
text_ai: Federated Learning (FL) aims to learn a global model from distributed users while protecting their privacy. However, when data are distributed heterogeneously the learning process becomes noisy, unstable, and biased towards the last seen clients' data, slowing down convergence. To address these issues and improve the robustness and generalization capabilities of the global model, we propose WIMA (Window-based Model Averaging). WIMA maintains memory of recent client updates and computes a joint update as the average over a sliding window, optionally weighted by a similarity proxy between local models and the global hypothesis. This windowed averaging mitigates abrupt shifts caused by stragglers and non-IID spillover, yielding a smoother trajectory and reduced bias toward late-arriving clients. We provide a lightweight analysis showing reduced variance and improved stability under heterogeneous data distributions, with convergence guarantees in convex settings and practical robustness in nonconvex deep learning tasks. Empirical results on federated benchmarks confirm gains in accuracy and sample efficiency over strong baselines.
prefix: Federated Learning (FL) aims to learn a global model from distributed users while protecting their privacy. However, when data are distributed heterogeneously the learning process becomes noisy, unstable, and biased towards the last seen clients' data, slowing down convergence. To address these issues and improve the robustness and generalization capabilities of the global model, we propose WIMA (Window-based Model Averaging).

title: Catalyzing Social Interactions in Mixed Reality using ML Recommendation Systems
text_ai: We create an innovative mixed reality-first social recommendation model, utilizing features uniquely collected through mixed reality (MR) systems to promote social interaction, such as gaze recognition, proximity, noise level, congestion level, and conversational intensity. We further extend these models to include right-time features to deliver timely notifications. Using a multimodal fusion strategy, we learn context-sensitive embeddings that align MR cues with social affordances, balancing promotion of interaction against perceived intrusion. A real-time pipeline integrates gaze, proximity, acoustic ambience, congestion, and conversational cues with user preferences to generate a ranked set of prompts and notifications. We validate the approach in a mixed MR laboratory setting and two in-situ deployments (N≈72), using objective metrics (interaction rate, dwell time, conversation initiation) and subjective measures (trust, perceived intrusion, privacy comfort). Results show uplifts in initiated interactions (18–24%) and longer dialogue bursts, with stable user satisfaction across contexts. The work yields design guidelines for privacy-preserving, scalable MR social systems.
prefix: We create an innovative mixed reality-first social recommendation model, utilizing features uniquely collected through mixed reality (MR) systems to promote social interaction, such as gaze recognition, proximity, noise level, congestion level, and conversational intensity. We further extend these models to include right-time features to deliver timely notifications.

title: Carleman-lattice-Boltzmann quantum circuit with matrix access oracles
text_ai: We apply Carleman linearization of the Lattice Boltzmann (CLB) representation of fluid flows to quantum emulate the dynamics of a 2D Kolmogorov-like flow. We assess the accuracy of the result and find a relative error of the order of $10^{-3}$ with just two Carleman iterates, for a range of the Reynolds number up to a few hundreds. Constructing block-encoded representations of the lifted CLB operator, we realize the time evolution through a small number of quantum singular value transformations applied to the flow-state block. The matrix access oracles encode collision and streaming steps and exploit sparsity to keep qubit counts modest. We analyze resource scaling with the Carleman order and lattice size, and we discuss implications for near-term quantum devices. Benchmarking against classical CLB on the same Kolmogorov-like forcing shows that integral quantities and spectral features are captured with relative error within 10⁻³–10⁻² for Reynolds numbers up to O(10²) using only two Carleman iterates. These results demonstrate the feasibility of a Carleman-lattice-Boltzmann quantum circuit framework with matrix access oracles for scalable quantum fluid simulations.
prefix: We apply Carleman linearization of the Lattice Boltzmann (CLB) representation of fluid flows to quantum emulate the dynamics of a 2D Kolmogorov-like flow. We assess the accuracy of the result and find a relative error of the order of $10^{-3}$ with just two Carleman iterates, for a range of the Reynolds number up to a few hundreds.

title: Lifetime of the superconductive state in short and long Josephson junctions
text_ai: We study the transient statistical properties of short and long Josephson junctions under the influence of thermal and correlated fluctuations. In particular, we investigate the lifetime of the superconductive metastable state finding the presence of noise induced phenomena. Numerical integration of the stochastic differential equation is performed over bias currents, damping, temperatures, and noise correlation times. We extract the mean first passage time (MFPT) to the resistive state, its full distribution, and the length dependence. In the short limit, the MFPT follows an effective one-dimensional escape picture with color corrections to Kramers’ rate; in the long limit, a two-step mechanism emerges: nucleation of a phase-slip region followed by rapid expansion. Our results reveal pronounced NES and RA effects: MFPT shows a nonmonotonic dependence on noise intensity and a minimum at finite correlation time. These findings quantify how temporal correlations modify stability of the superconductive state and have implications for superconducting circuit design and reliability for quantum information technologies.
prefix: We study the transient statistical properties of short and long Josephson junctions under the influence of thermal and correlated fluctuations. In particular, we investigate the lifetime of the superconductive metastable state finding the presence of noise induced phenomena.

title: Effect of 5% transdermal lidocaine patches on postoperative analgesia in dogs undergoing hemilaminectomy.
text_ai: To investigate the effect of 5% lidocaine patches on postoperative analgesia in dogs undergoing hemilaminectomy. Client-owned dogs undergoing hemilaminectomy for a single acute intervertebral thoracolumbar disc extrusion were enrolled in this prospective, randomised, blinded clinical trial. Following methadone administration, anaesthesia was induced with propofol, and maintained with isoflurane in oxygen and fentanyl infusion, in both groups. Sixty client-owned dogs were randomized to receive either a 5% lidocaine patch (n=30) or a visually identical placebo patch (n=30) applied to the thoracolumbar incision immediately after wound closure and left in place for 48 hours. All animals received standardized multimodal analgesia; methadone was administered intraoperatively and as rescue analgesia postextubation. Postoperative pain was assessed by blinded observers at 2, 6, 12, 24, and 48 hours using the Glasgow Composite Measure Pain Scale–Short Form. Primary endpoint was pain score; secondary endpoints included time to first rescue analgesia, total methadone consumption over 48 hours, and adverse events. Data were analyzed with mixed-effects models for repeated measures. Results: Compared with placebo, the lidocaine patch group exhibited lower pain scores at 6 and 12 hours (P<0.05) and reductions persisting at 24–48 hours. Time to first rescue analgesia was longer (median 8 vs 3 hours; P=0.03), and total 48-hour methadone consumption was lower (mean ± SD 0.6 ± 0.3 vs 0.9 ± 0.4 mg/kg; P=0.04). Patch-related adverse effects were mild and transient. Conclusion: The 5% transdermal lidocaine patches provided additional postoperative analgesia and reduced opioid requirements in dogs undergoing hemilaminectomy, with no evidence of systemic toxicity.
prefix: To investigate the effect of 5% lidocaine patches on postoperative analgesia in dogs undergoing hemilaminectomy. Client-owned dogs undergoing hemilaminectomy for a single acute intervertebral thoracolumbar disc extrusion were enrolled in this prospective, randomised, blinded clinical trial. Following methadone administration, anaesthesia was induced with propofol, and maintained with isoflurane in oxygen and fentanyl infusion, in both groups.

title: Strategic Play By Resource-Bounded Agents in Security Games
text_ai: Many studies have shown that humans are "predictably irrational": they do not act in a fully rational way, but their deviations from rational behavior are quite systematic. Our goal is to see the extent to which we can explain and justify these deviations as the outcome of rational but resource-bounded agents doing as well as they can, given their limitations. Specifically, we develop a resource-bounded optimization framework in which defenders and attackers select mixed strategies subject to computational cost constraints. We formalize cognitive effort as a continuous budget that reduces the precision of belief formation and the tractability of strategy search, yielding boundedly rational best responses. We characterize equilibrium play under these constraints and show that bounded optimal behavior induces systematic biases—such as heuristic concentration on a limited action set, underweighting of unlikely contingencies, and delayed adaptation to changing payoffs—that mirror observed human deviations. We validate the model with data from security-game experiments and from security incident records, demonstrating alignment in both qualitative patterns and metrics of predictability and payoff. The findings indicate that resource limits, rather than intrinsic irrationality, can generate the regularities cited in behavioral security studies. Finally, we discuss implications for mechanism design, threat assessment, and training that accommodate cognitive constraints without sacrificing robustness.
prefix: Many studies have shown that humans are "predictably irrational": they do not act in a fully rational way, but their deviations from rational behavior are quite systematic. Our goal is to see the extent to which we can explain and justify these deviations as the outcome of rational but resource-bounded agents doing as well as they can, given their limitations.

title: Retrieval-augmented Image Captioning
text_ai: Inspired by retrieval-augmented language generation and pretrained Vision and Language (V&L) encoders, we present a new approach to image captioning that generates sentences given the input image and a set of captions retrieved from a datastore, as opposed to the image alone. We retrieve a small set of top-k captions using an index built over a large caption corpus, conditioned on the input image's visual features. A dual-stream encoder then processes both the image and the retrieved captions, with a cross-attentional fusion module that grounds the generator in both visual and linguistic cues. The decoder attends to image patches and retrieved text, allowing frequently co-occurring phrases to be re-used and novel phrasing to be composed. We train with a standard captioning objective augmented by a retrieval-consistency loss that rewards alignment between generated tokens and retrieved examples. Experiments on MS COCO and Flickr30k demonstrate consistent gains in CIDEr and BLEU, with robust zero-shot performance in diverse setups.
prefix: Inspired by retrieval-augmented language generation and pretrained Vision and Language (V&L) encoders, we present a new approach to image captioning that generates sentences given the input image and a set of captions retrieved from a datastore, as opposed to the image alone.

title: Periodontal status correlates with anti-citrullinated protein antibodies in first-degree relatives of individuals with rheumatoid arthritis.
text_ai: To evaluate periodontal status in first-degree relatives of patients with rheumatoid arthritis (FDR-RA) and detect correlation with the presence of anti-citrullinated protein antibodies (ACPAs). Rheumatologic status and periodontal status were evaluated in a nested case-control study of FDR-RA with no diagnosis of RA at enrolment. Methods: In a nested case-control study within a RA-family cohort, 240 RA-free first-degree relatives underwent rheumatologic examination and anti-CCP2 testing, plus full-mouth periodontal assessment (plaque index, BOP, PD, CAL, tooth count). Periodontitis: ≥2 interproximal sites with CAL ≥3 mm and PD >4 mm; severe disease: CAL ≥5 mm with ≥30% sites involved. ACPAs categorized as positive per manufacturer cut-off. Conditional logistic regression estimated ORs for periodontitis by ACPA status, adjusting for age, sex, smoking, BMI, diabetes, and oral hygiene; interaction by smoking assessed. Results: ACPAs were detected in about half. ACPA-positive participants showed more periodontal inflammation (CAL 3.1 vs 2.2 mm; PD 3.0 vs 2.6 mm; BOP 54% vs 38%). Periodontitis prevalence was 61% in ACPA-positive vs 39% in ACPA-negative. Adjusted ORs: periodontitis 2.1 (1.2–3.9); severe periodontitis 3.0 (1.4–6.8). Smoking amplified associations (p for interaction <0.05). Conclusion: Among FDR-RA, ACPA positivity correlates with greater periodontal disease burden, supporting shared inflammatory pathways and potential bidirectional links with RA pathogenesis.
prefix: To evaluate periodontal status in first-degree relatives of patients with rheumatoid arthritis (FDR-RA) and detect correlation with the presence of anti-citrullinated protein antibodies (ACPAs). Rheumatologic status and periodontal status were evaluated in a nested case-control study of FDR-RA with no diagnosis of RA at enrolment.

title: Skew Class-balanced Re-weighting for Unbiased Scene Graph Generation
text_ai: An unbiased scene graph generation (SGG) algorithm referred to as Skew Class-balanced Re-weighting (SCR) is proposed for considering the unbiased predicate prediction caused by the long-tailed distribution. The prior works focus mainly on alleviating the deteriorating performances of the minority predicate predictions, showing drastic dropping recall scores, i.e., losing the majority predicate performances. Leveraging a frequency-aware re-weighting scheme, SCR modulates the per-predicate loss by introducing class-balanced factors derived from the empirical distribution to prevent overcompensation for rare predicates. The re-weighting is integrated with a joint optimization over object detection and predicate prediction, coupled with a sampling strategy that reduces dominance of head predicates during mini-batch construction. We further propose a skew-aware regularizer that constrains the predicted predicate distribution to align with the class prior while preserving discriminative cues. Experiments on Visual Genome demonstrate that SCR yields notable gains in mean recall (mR@K) while maintaining competitive Recall, achieving state-of-the-art performance among bias-aware approaches with minimal extra computational overhead.
prefix: An unbiased scene graph generation (SGG) algorithm referred to as Skew Class-balanced Re-weighting (SCR) is proposed for considering the unbiased predicate prediction caused by the long-tailed distribution. The prior works focus mainly on alleviating the deteriorating performances of the minority predicate predictions, showing drastic dropping recall scores, i.e., losing the majority predicate performances.

title: Visual Analytics for Explainable and Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence
text_ai: Our society increasingly depends on intelligent systems to solve complex problems, ranging from recommender systems suggesting the next movie to watch to AI models assisting in medical diagnoses for hospitalized patients. With the iterative improvement of diagnostic accuracy and efficiency, AI holds significant potential to mitigate medical misdiagnoses by preventing numerous deaths and reducing an economic burden of approximately 450 EUR billion annually. To address the need for transparent, accountable AI in high-stakes contexts, we propose a visual analytics pipeline that couples model-agnostic explanations with interactive visual encodings designed for clinicians and domain experts. The framework surfaces provenance, uncertainty, and causal structure underpinning predictions, enabling users to probe counterfactuals, compare alternative models, and validate alignment with domain knowledge. We introduce novel visualization primitives for multi-modal evidence synthesis, including saliency maps, feature attribution trails, and scenario dashboards that support risk-aware decision-making. An empirical study with healthcare professionals demonstrates that the approach improves interpretability and trust, while reducing time-to-decision and diagnostic errors in simulated workflows. We also present deployment guidelines, evaluation metrics for explainability and robustness, and a qualitative coding scheme to capture user trust, cognitive load, and perceived accountability. Our findings generalize to other critical domains where transparency and governance are essential for responsible AI adoption.
prefix: Our society increasingly depends on intelligent systems to solve complex problems, ranging from recommender systems suggesting the next movie to watch to AI models assisting in medical diagnoses for hospitalized patients. With the iterative improvement of diagnostic accuracy and efficiency, AI holds significant potential to mitigate medical misdiagnoses by preventing numerous deaths and reducing an economic burden of approximately 450 EUR billion annually.

title: Ball-Larus Path Profiling Across Multiple Loop iterations
text_ai: Identifying the hottest paths in the control flow graph of a routine can direct optimizations to portions of the code where most resources are consumed. This powerful methodology, called path profiling, was introduced by Ball and Larus in the mid 90s and has received considerable attention in the last 15 years for its practical relevance. In this work we extend Ball-Larus path profiling to quantify the distribution of executed paths across multiple loop iterations and across nested loops. We introduce a representation that annotates each path through a control-flow graph with a function of the loop iteration counts, enabling the profiler to distinguish hot paths that are frequent only in certain iterations or those that span iteration boundaries. Our approach constructs a compact symbolic path profile by combining Ball-Larus path counters with loop-aware summaries, using a small finite-state automaton that encodes iteration contexts. We show how to instrument code so that overhead remains proportional to the base Ball-Larus cost, and how to postprocess collected data to yield per-iteration and per-context hot-path rankings. We validate the method on synthetic benchmarks and real kernels, demonstrating improved visibility of cross-iteration bottlenecks and the ability to guide optimizations such as loop transformations, cache-conscious code motion, and hot-path specialization in practice.
prefix: Identifying the hottest paths in the control flow graph of a routine can direct optimizations to portions of the code where most resources are consumed. This powerful methodology, called path profiling, was introduced by Ball and Larus in the mid 90s and has received considerable attention in the last 15 years for its practical relevance.

title: Studying the multi-wavelength signals from short GRBs
text_ai: Since the first host galaxies and afterglows of short GRBs were identified, they have remained very difficult to study: their multiwavelenth afterglows are notoriously faint and host galaxy identification often relies upon minimalising a chance alignment probability. These challenges have motivated coordinated, rapid-response campaigns across the electromagnetic spectrum, leveraging X-ray, optical/near-infrared, radio, and, when available, gravitational-wave information to recover faint afterglows and to unambiguously associate them with their hosts. We present a multi-wavelength dataset of short GRBs observed over the past decade, including prompt X-ray afterglows with Swift/XRT, optical–NIR imaging with ground- and space-based facilities, and sensitive radio constraints, enabling joint modeling of jet dynamics, energy budgets, and ambient densities. Our analyses reveal a diverse set of afterglow behaviors, a broad distribution of jet opening angles, and candidates for kilonova components in several events, consistent with neutron star merger scenarios. These results refine rate estimates, host-galaxy demographics, and inform strategies for forthcoming joint GW–EM detections.

title: First Light Curve Analysis of NSVS 8294044, V1023 Her, and V1397 Her Contact Binary Systems
text_ai: The first photometric light curve investigation of the NSVS 8294044, V1023 Her, and V1397 Her binary systems is presented. We used ground-based observations for the NSVS 8294044 system and Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) data for V1023 Her and V1397 Her. Light curves were phase-folded using published minima, and parameters were derived with differential corrections in PHOEBE 2.3. We modeled NSVS 8294044 and the TESS light curves for V1023 Her and V1397 Her, incorporating limb-darkening coefficients from Claret (2017), albedo and gravity-darkening for convective envelopes, and allowing for third-light contributions. The solutions indicate that all three objects are in shallow to moderate contact, with overcontact configurations (f in the range ~0–0.25) and inclinations between 60° and 84°. Photometric mass ratios are moderate, and temperature differences between components remain small for V1023 Her and V1397 Her, consistent with thermal contact; NSVS 8294044 shows a somewhat larger ΔT, suggesting a break in strict contact. Spot modeling on at least one component improves the fit, providing plausible spot longitudes and sizes. The L3 light contribution is modest (<5%), ruling out strong third-body light. The results demonstrate qualitative agreement with W UMa-type expectations and offer a baseline for spectroscopic follow-up to obtain dynamical masses, expanding the sample of well-characterized contact binaries in the solar neighborhood.

title: Optoelectronic Fingerprints of Interference between Different Charge Carriers in Graphene Superlattices and Analogies to Twisted Graphene Bilayers
text_ai: Motivated by recent experimental findings on the low-energy spectrum of Kekul\'e-patterned graphene, the optoelectronic signatures of graphene superlattices with a spatial modulation that triples the size of the unit cell and folds the valleys to the center of the Brillouin zone are studied. Using a low-energy continuum model in which a Kekulé modulation acts as a spatially periodic mass that triples the unit cell and folds the K and K' valleys to the zone center, we characterize the reconstructed miniband spectrum and the symmetry-allowed couplings between distinct carriers. The interference between the original Dirac-like carriers and the emergent folded modes yields optoelectronic fingerprints, visible in the frequency dependence of the optical conductivity and in polarization absorption. We compute interband and intraband contributions within a Kubo framework for representative doping, temperature, and modulation strength. Results show resonances tied to interminiband transitions and van Hove-like singularities, with gate-tunable and polarization-selective response. Analogies to twisted bilayers arise from flat-band–like segments and moiré crossings.

title: DiffPoint: Single and Multi-view Point Cloud Reconstruction with ViT Based Diffusion Model
text_ai: As the task of 2D-to-3D reconstruction has gained significant attention in various real-world scenarios, it becomes crucial to be able to generate high-quality point clouds. Despite the recent success of deep learning models in generating point clouds, there are still challenges in producing high-fidelity results due to the disparities between images and point clouds. We propose DiffPoint, a ViT-based diffusion framework that reconstructs 3D point clouds from one or more RGB images. A ViT encoder extracts rich cross-modal features to condition a diffusion prior that models plausible point distributions. For single-view inputs, a geometry-aware denoising network progressively refines a noisy point cloud under cues such as silhouette, shading, and inferred depth. For multi-view inputs, per-view features are fused via a cross-attention module, with a multi-view consistency loss enforcing coherent geometry across viewpoints and occlusions. The diffusion process supports efficient sampling with classifier-free guidance and a designed conditioning schedule to balance detail and structure. We evaluate on ShapeNet-based synthetic data and real ScanNet scenes, achieving state-of-the-art Chamfer and F-score while robustly handling occlusion and pose variation. Ablation studies demonstrate the contribution of ViT conditioning, diffusion priors, and cross-view fusion to fidelity and generalization.

title: An Information-Theoretic Analysis of Thompson Sampling for Logistic Bandits
text_ai: We study the performance of the Thompson Sampling algorithm for logistic bandit problems. In this setting, an agent receives binary rewards with probabilities determined by a logistic function, $\exp(\beta \langle a, \theta \rangle)/(1+\exp(\beta \langle a, \theta \rangle))$, with slope parameter $\beta>0$, and where both the action $a\in \mathcal{A}$ and parameter $\theta \in \mathcal{O}$ lie within the $d$-dimensional unit ball. Building on the information-theoretic framework for Thompson Sampling, we derive bounds on the cumulative Bayesian regret by relating the regret to the information gained about the unknown parameter θ from each binary observation. The logistic likelihood induces a smooth, globally Lipschitz log-likelihood on the unit ball, which we exploit to control the per-step information gain I(θ; Y_t | F_t) and the associated information ratio Γ_t. We show that, for any admissible arm a, the mutual information between θ and the observed reward is bounded by a constant times β^2 ∥a∥^2, while the posterior uncertainty contracts at a rate governed by the Fisher information of the logistic model. Aggregating these bounds over T rounds via standard information-theoretic arguments yields a Bayesian regret bound of the form R_T(π) = O(d √{T log(1 + c β^2 T/d)}) for an appropriate universal constant c. We also derive matching information-theoretic lower bounds up to logarithmic factors, confirming the near-optimality of Thompson Sampling in logistic bandits. The results extend to general convex, symmetric action sets within the unit ball and delineate the influence of β on learning speed.

title: Simulating Head Recovery and Intermittent Discharge in Free Flowing Wells.
text_ai: Modeling of the head recovery (buildup) in and intermittent operation of flowing wells lacks rigorous analytical tools. Presently different methods are applied in discharging and recovery phases. The presented reliable approximate solution considers a continuous free flow process and time variant screen loss parameters. Analytical tractability is achieved by representing the screen losses as a time-dependent boundary term and invoking a deformed Green’s function for radial flow in a homogeneous aquifer. The resulting solution provides closed-form expressions for drawdown and recovery during continuous discharge and subsequent shut-in, with the intermittent phase captured through a piecewise application of the same kernel. Parameter identification relies on field-logged head histories and known aquifer properties, while a robust perturbation scheme accommodates slow variations in screen resistance. The model naturally reduces to the conventional Theis response for constant losses and to the early-time no-loss solution when k(t) → 0. Numerical validation against simulations confirms accuracy within screen variability and discharge cycles.

title: Effective Hamiltonian of topologically stabilized polymer states
text_ai: Topologically stabilized polymer conformations observed in melts of nonconcatenated polymer rings and crumpled globules, are considered to be a good candidate for the description of the spatial structure of mitotic chromosomes. Despite significant efforts, the microscopic Hamiltonian capable of describing such systems, remains yet inaccessible. Here, we construct an effective, coarse-grained Hamiltonian H_eff that encapsulates the essential topological enrichment without recourse to atomistic detail. By performing a systematic coarse-graining of melts of nonconcatenated rings and crumpled-globule statistics, we introduce a nonlocal interaction term encoding the global linking constraints, while retaining a local bending energy for chain segments. The resulting functional comprises H_0, a standard worm-like chain contribution, plus H_top, proportional to the square of the topological charge integrated along the ring ensemble, enforcing near-constant linking number on mesoscopic scales. We predict scaling relations for contact maps, radius of gyration, and structure factors in agreement with experimental inferences for mitotic chromosomes, and we validate the approach against coarse-grained simulations under topological constraints.

title: Randomized Oversampling for Generalized Multiscale Finite Element Methods
text_ai: In this paper, we study the development of efficient multiscale methods for flows in heterogeneous media. Our approach uses the Generalized Multiscale Finite Element (GMsFEM) framework. The main idea of GMsFEM is to approximate the solution space locally using a few multiscale basis functions. We propose a randomized oversampling strategy to construct local snapshot spaces with greatly reduced cost. Instead of exhaustively sampling all possible forcing patterns, we generate a small set of random boundary traces on an oversampled domain and solve local problems to form a compact randomized snapshot library. From this library, we perform a local spectral decomposition to select a robust offline space that captures dominant multiscale features. The oversampling mitigates boundary-layer effects and improves stability of the extracted modes. We show that, with high probability, the resulting offline space yields near-best approximation properties in the energy norm, with error bounded by the neglected eigenvalues and the randomized sampling error. We derive a priori estimates that quantify the interplay among oversampling size, random realizations, and coarse-grid resolution, and we discuss the dependence on contrast and heterogeneity. An adaptive enrichment procedure is proposed to add basis functions where residuals exceed a prescribed tolerance. Numerical experiments on two- and three-dimensional media with high-contrast permeability fields demonstrate substantial reductions in offline cost while preserving accuracy compared with conventional GMsFEM. The randomized method exhibits robust performance across diverse realizations and supports scalable online solves.

title: Image Fusion Transformer
text_ai: In image fusion, images obtained from different sensors are fused to generate a single image with enhanced information. In recent years, state-of-the-art methods have adopted Convolution Neural Networks (CNNs) to encode meaningful features for image fusion. Specifically, CNN-based methods perform image fusion by fusing local features. Here we introduce Image Fusion Transformer (IFT), a transformer-based framework that models global dependencies across source images to produce a fused output with preserved structural and spectral information. Unlike CNN-based methods that primarily fuse local features, IFT leverages hierarchical self-attention and cross-attention to capture long-range correlations and cross-modal correspondences. A dual-branch encoder extracts representations from each source, followed by a cross-modality fusion module that aggregates features through transformer blocks with skip connections. A residual reconstruction decoder then recovers the fused image at full resolution, guided by an adaptive fusion rule that balances detail preservation and noise suppression. The model is trained with a combination of perceptual loss, structural similarity loss, and a fidelity term to encourage faithful reconstruction of input content. Extensive experiments on standard infrared-visible and multispectral fusion benchmarks demonstrate that IFT consistently outperforms CNN-based competitors and transformer-inspired baselines, achieving higher PSNR/SSIM, improved information entropy, and stronger edge preservation. Ablation studies validate the contribution of global attention and cross-modal fusion.

title: An effective Thermodynamic Description of Galactic Haloes
text_ai: The observation of flat rotation curves in asymptotic region of galaxies implies that the dark matter density profile decreases exponentially with the gravitational potential in this region. It is curious that this behavior is identical to what one would have from a Boltzmann gas in thermal equilibrium. Here we develop an effective thermodynamic description for virialized galactic haloes by invoking a coarse-grained Boltzmann factor for the collisionless dark matter in a quasi-static potential. We define a locally defined effective temperature T_eff(r) from the radial velocity dispersion and show that, to order, ρ(r) ∝ exp[-Φ(r)/T_eff], consistent with an isothermal-like shell. Solving the coupled Boltzmann–Poisson equations under flat-rotation constraints yields analytic fall-offs in the outer halo that reproduce the asymptotic behavior. The framework provides a simple equation of state P = ρ T_eff and a minimal set of parameters (T_eff, core radius) that collapse diverse haloes onto a single thermodynamic family, with implications for halo evolution and DM microphysics.

title: Modular Many-Body Quantum Sensors
text_ai: Quantum many-body systems undergoing phase transitions have been proposed as probes enabling beyond-classical enhancement of sensing precision. However, this enhancement is usually limited to a very narrow region around the critical point. Here, we systematically develop a modular approach for introducing multiple phase transitions in a many-body system. Moreover, we derive analytic bounds for the quantum Fisher information of the global sensor and demonstrate that, in the presence of realistic decoherence, the modular assembly maintains enhanced scaling over extended parameter ranges. We validate the framework with numerical simulations of spin-1/2 lattices and discuss experimental routes in cold-atom and superconducting platforms, highlighting modular fault tolerance and calibration procedures and readout strategies. The modularity enables parallel processing of signals and straightforward reconfiguration for tailored metrological tasks, including multi-parameter estimation and noise spectroscopy. Our results suggest that sensor networks built from tunable ensembles of interacting modules can surpass the standard quantum limit across broad spectra while preserving resilience to imperfections.

title: CUNet: A Compact Unsupervised Network for Image Classification
text_ai: In this paper, we propose a compact network called CUNet (compact unsupervised network) to counter the image classification challenge. Different from the traditional convolutional neural networks learning filters by the time-consuming stochastic gradient descent, CUNet learns the filter bank from diverse image patches with the simple K-means, which significantly avoids the requirement of scarce labeled training images, reduces the training consumption, and maintains the high discriminative ability. To validate its practicality, we implement a compact feature extractor based on learned filters, followed by light encoding and a classifier. The network relies on minimal supervision, uses no backpropagation through deep layers, and retains a small memory footprint suitable for deployment. We evaluate CUNet on benchmarks, reporting accuracy with a fraction of the training cost of deep models. Across low-label regimes, CUNet consistently closes the gap to supervised baselines while offering faster inference and simpler deployment. These results demonstrate the viability of unsupervised learning for scalable image understanding.

title: COUNTDOWN: a Run-time Library for Performance-Neutral Energy Saving in MPI Applications
text_ai: Power and energy consumption is becoming key challenges to deploy the first exascale supercomputer successfully. Large-scale HPC applications waste a significant amount of power in communication and synchronization-related idle times. However, due to the time scale at which communication happens, transitioning in low power states during communication's idle times may introduce unacceptable overhead in applications' execution time. COUNTDOWN builds a transparent, performance-neutral energy management layer inside the MPI runtime. It identifies idle intervals exposed by communication progress and synchronization stalls and dispatches energy-saving transitions only when wake-up latencies are safely amortized. The library orchestrates a hierarchy of strategies: (i) device-level DVFS, C-state transitions, and fine-grained clock gating during MPI progress and non-blocking periods; (ii) cooperative, thread-aware polling to hide wake-up delays; (iii) a lightweight predictive controller that estimates remaining idle time from progress metrics and historical trends; and (iv) correctness guards that prevent transitions during active communication or when overlap with computation is necessary. Changes are constrained to safe windows and bounded by a configurable energy-saving budget to guarantee performance neutrality. COUNTDOWN provides a minimal API surface, insulating applications from hardware specifics while remaining compatible with common MPI implementations. We evaluate on a multi-node cluster with representative workloads, showing meaningful energy reductions with negligible overhead across NAS benchmarks and real-world MPI-based applications, validating its portability and scalability.

title: Probing the near-IR flux excess in young star clusters
text_ai: We report the results of a recent study of young star clusters (YSCs) in luminous blue compact galaxies (BCGs). The age distributions of the YSCs suggest that the starburst episode in Haro 11, ESO 185-IG13, and Mrk 930 started not more than 30-40 Myr ago. By cross-matching YSC catalogs from HST optical imaging with deep near-IR photometry (JHKs when available) we built multi-band SEDs for clusters across Haro 11, ESO 185-IG13 and Mrk 930. The derived age distributions indicate burst onset within 30–40 Myr, in line with nebular indicators. We performed SSP fits with subsolar metallicities including nebular emission. A substantial fraction exhibit near-IR flux excess beyond model predictions; extends from J to Ks; cannot be explained by reddening alone. The excess correlates with age ~5–15 Myr, consistent with hot dust or red supergiants; in metal-poor environments perhaps hot circumstellar dust dominates. We tested adding a hot-dust continuum component (T ~ 800–1200 K) yielding improved fits, and revised ages/masses for affected clusters. Conclusion: near-IR excess biases standard YSC properties and must be modeled to avoid systematic errors in starburst galaxies. Future work should incorporate motivated infrared components in population synthesis and extend analyses to samples of metal-poor star-forming systems to reduce systematic biases.

title: Analysis of a Memcapacitor-Based for Neural Network Accelerator Framework
text_ai: Data-intensive computing tasks, such as training neural networks, are crucial for artificial intelligence applications but often come with high energy demands. One promising solution is to develop specialized hardware that directly maps neural networks, utilizing arrays of memristive devices to perform parallel multiply-accumulate operations. This work presents a memcapacitor-based accelerator framework that leverages nonvolatile capacitive synapses to encode weight values and perform in-situ accumulation through charge sharing. We develop a device-model-aware architectural mapping that translates neural networks into crossbar-like arrays integrated with peripheral analog front-ends, ADCs, and DACs, while tolerating variability and parasitics. An algorithm-hardware co-design methodology is proposed to optimize precision, sparsity, and scheduling. We evaluate energy-delay-area with transistor-level SPICE and system-level simulators on standard benchmarks (MNIST, CIFAR-10, and small-scale ImageNet) under realistic process, voltage, temperature variations. Results show substantial reductions in energy per inference and competitive accuracy, demonstrating scalability for edge and data-center accelerators and resilience to memcapacitive drift and manufacturing variability effects.

title: A Function Approximation Approach to Estimation of Policy Gradient for POMDP with Structured Policies
text_ai: We consider the estimation of the policy gradient in partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDP) with a special class of structured policies that are finite-state controllers. We show that the gradient estimation can be done in the Actor-Critic framework, by making the critic compute a "value" function that does not depend on the states of POMDP. Leveraging a parametric feature map, the critic approximates the action-value (or advantage) using only the controller's internal state and recent observations, thereby avoiding explicit state estimation. The resulting gradient estimator is unbiased up to the approximation error and is amenable to stochastic gradient descent. We derive conditions under which the Bellman error is minimized in the feature space, establishing convergence of the joint Actor-Critic updates. Our approach enables scalable policy optimization for structured policies with modest state-tracking requirements. Empirical results on synthetic POMDPs and common benchmarks illustrate improved sample efficiency and robustness to partial observability over baseline policy-gradient methods.

title: Stripe magnetic order and field-induced quantum criticality in the perfect triangular-lattice antiferromagnet CsCeSe$_2$
text_ai: The two-dimensional triangular-lattice antiferromagnet (TLAF) is a textbook example of frustrated magnetic systems. Despite its simplicity, the TLAF model exhibits a highly rich and complex magnetic phase diagram, featuring numerous distinct ground states that can be stabilized through frustrated next-nearest-neighbor couplings or anisotropy. In this paper, we report low-temperature magnetic properties of the TLAF material CsCeSe$_2$. Using single-crystal bulk susceptibility, heat capacity, and neutron scattering, we map the ground state and its evolution with field. In zero field CsCeSe2 orders into a commensurate stripe phase, a collinear arrangement with moments along the easy axis and a propagation vector selecting one crystal direction, consistent with competing J1–J2 exchange and sizable single-ion anisotropy. The order appears below T_N of a few kelvin and is marked by a sharp heat-capacity anomaly and a substantial reduction of magnetic entropy; the moment is reduced by quantum fluctuations. With increasing field along c, the stripe order is continuously suppressed and vanishes at a well-defined critical field H_c, beyond which a high-field paramagnetic/partially polarized state is stabilized. The H–T phase diagram reveals a quantum critical region emanating from H_c, and the critical scaling of thermodynamic probes and of the magnetic Bragg intensity is in accord with magnon Bose-Einstein condensation in a quasi-two-dimensional TLAF. These results establish CsCeSe2 as a rare, nearly perfect TLAF hosting stripe order and field-induced quantum criticality, and they highlight the crucial role of anisotropy and longer-range exchange in stabilizing novel ground states.

title: Treatment of chronic nonunions of the humerus with free vascularized fibula transfer: a report of thirteen cases
text_ai: Chronic nonunions of the humerus remain a challenging problem. We reviewed 13 cases of chronic nonunion of the humerus resulting from trauma or osteomyelitis treated with vascularized fibula transfer after failure of conventional treatment. Patient averages were 35 years of age, follow-up of 19 months, and 4.2 prior operations. Procedures used microvascular technique with segmental vascularized fibula transfers and stable internal fixation. Indications included segmental defects, infection control, and failed prior reconstructions. At a mean follow-up of 19 months, union was achieved in 11 of 13 humeral nonunions (85%), with a mean time to radiographic union of 6.2 months (range 4–10). Two cases failed to unite and underwent revision grafting. Complications were limited: one superficial infection resolved with antibiotics; no flap loss. Donor-site morbidity was minor, with transient ankle stiffness in one patient and no long-term deficit. Functional results included improved elbow motion and pain relief in most patients, enabling return to daily activities.

title: A New Hole Density as a Stability Measure for Boron Fullerenes
text_ai: We investigate the stability of boron fullerene sets B76, B78 and B82. We evaluate the ground state energies, nucleus-independent chemical shift (NICS), the binding energies per atom and the band gap values by means of first-principles methods. To this end, we introduce a local, scalar hole-density h(r) obtained from the difference between the reference filled bonding manifold and the actual one-electron density, projected onto the valence framework by a constrained-DFT partitioning of the boron framework into icosahedral-like motifs. The total hole count H = ∫ h(r) d^3r serves as a global stability index, while the second moment and anisotropy of h(r) reveal delocalization patterns correlated with aromatic character and cage integrity. We find that lower H values and more uniform hole-distributions consistently track lower total energies and larger HOMO-LUMO gaps. Among B76, B78, B82, the latter two exhibit more compact, isotropic hole densities, correlating with enhanced binding energy per atom and pronounced NICS signals. Accordingly.

title: Sparsification and Reconstruction from the Perspective of Representation Geometry
text_ai: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) have emerged as a predominant tool in mechanistic interpretability, aiming to identify interpretable monosemantic features. However, how does sparse encoding organize the representations of activation vector from language models? What is the relationship between this organizational paradigm and feature disentanglement as well as reconstruction performance? In this work we develop a geometry‑driven account of sparsification that treats activation vectors as points on a high‑dimensional manifold with locally linear structure. We introduce representation‑geometry diagnostics—subspace coherence, principal angle spectra, and axis alignment with putative semantic factors—to quantify how sparse encodings partition the language‑model space into interpretable sectors. We show that sparse codes tend to activate a small set of basis directions, yielding a low‑rank, axis‑aligned decomposition that disentangles latent factors while suppressing spurious variation in inactive coordinates. To exploit this structure, we formulate a reconstruction objective that leverages the geometry of active subspaces to recover full activations from sparse codes under partial observability. Our experiments across multiple transformer layers and model families reveal that higher sparsity concentrates variance along a few semantically meaningful directions and improves disentanglement at modest cost to reconstruction fidelity; there exists an optimal sparsity regime balancing interpretability and predictive accuracy. These results motivate geometry‑aware sparsification as a principled route to robust interpretability and reconstruction.

title: The Milky Way atlas for linear filaments II. clump rotation versus filament orientation
text_ai: Dense clumps distributed along filaments are the immediate medium for star formation. Kinematic properties of the clumps, such as velocity gradient and angular momentum, combined with filament orientation, provide important clues to the formation mechanism of filament-clump configurations and the role of filaments in star formation. Here we extend the Milky Way atlas of linear filaments to quantify clump rotation as a function of local filament orientation for a sample of filaments with embedded dense clumps. Velocity fields are extracted from high-density tracers (e.g., NH3, N2H+, H13CO+) observed with single-dish and interferometric telescopes, and rotation vectors are inferred from line-centroid gradients. Filaments are characterized by spine orientation derived from column-density maps, while clump spins are projected onto the sky and rotated into a filament-aligned frame to compute the relative angle. Projection and beam effects are treated with forward modelling and Monte Carlo resampling. The main result is a significant tendency for clump rotation axes to be perpendicular to the filament spine in the massive-clump regime, with a median relative angle around 85–90 degrees, while low-mass clumps show no preferred orientation. The trend persists after mitigating biases from distance, crowding, and magnetic-field geometry, suggesting that accretion along filaments and anisotropic fragmentation imprint the momentum budget of cores.

title: Character-based Neural Machine Translation
text_ai: We introduce a neural machine translation model that views the input and output sentences as sequences of characters rather than words. Since word-level information provides a crucial source of bias, our input model composes representations of character sequences into representations of words (as determined by whitespace boundaries), and then these are translated using a joint attention/translation model. Experiments on standard bilingual corpora demonstrate that the character-based system achieves competitive performance with state-of-the-art word-based models while markedly reducing out-of-vocabulary errors. By composing word representations from character n-grams prior to translation, the model naturally handles rare and unseen words and morphologically rich forms without explicit tokenization. We compare against strong baselines using word-level attention and subword models, observing improvements particularly on languages with rich morphology. The approach remains end-to-end trainable, requires no pre-segmented corpora, and yields more compact vocabularies. Analysis of attention patterns reveals more flexible alignments between character-derived word units and target words in translation.

title: The everyday dynamics of rumination and worry: precipitant events and affective consequences.
text_ai: Rumination and worry are two perseverative, negatively valenced thought processes that characterise depressive and anxiety disorders. Despite significant research interest, little is known about the everyday precipitants and consequences of rumination and worry. Using an experience sampling methodology, we examined and compared rumination and worry with respect to their relations to daily events and affective experience. Across fourteen days, participants reported each evening on episodes of rumination and worry, and rated mood, stressors, and events. Multilevel analyses indicated that both processes co-occurred with negative affect and were shaped by perceived event intensity, yet rumination more strongly followed social and interpersonal stress while worry related more to performance and health concerns. Precipitating events predicted increases in rumination and worry on the day, with effects spilling over to the next day’s affect. Rumination, however, was associated with prolonged negative mood, whereas worry produced greater short-term variability. The findings illuminate distinct trajectories and potential targets for intervention.

Using an experience sampling methodology, we examined and compared rumination and worry with respect to their relations to daily events and affective experience.

title: Improving Zero-Day Malware Testing Methodology Using Statistically Significant Time-Lagged Test Samples
text_ai: Enterprise networks are in constant danger of being breached by cyber-attackers, but making the decision about what security tools to deploy to mitigate this risk requires carefully designed evaluation of security products. One of the most important metrics for a protection product is how well it is able to stop malware, specifically on "zero"-day malware that has not been seen by the security community before. To address this, we introduce a time-lagged sampling protocol that constructs test corpora from sequential threat feeds separated by controlled delays, ensuring independence between training and testing sets while preserving concept drift. We apply nonparametric bootstrap and paired statistical tests to assess the significance of detection-rate differences across engines. Our methodology includes pre-registered evaluation plans, stratified sampling by malware family and payload class, and transparent reporting of confidence intervals. We evaluate on three repositories of samples with timestamps, with a drift module that emulates threat actor evolution. Results show that time-lagged design yields more stable estimates of zero-day protection and mitigates optimistic bias typical of random-split baselines. Across five detectors, we observe statistically significant improvements in recall for unseen families (mean ΔRecall ≈ 0.11–0.13, p < 0.01) with FP-rate growth within acceptable bounds. The approach generalizes to hybrid and cross-platform deployments.

title: The susceptibility of the square lattice Ising model: New developments
text_ai: We have made substantial advances in elucidating the properties of the susceptibility of the square lattice Ising model. We discuss its analyticity properties, certain closed form expressions for subsets of the coefficients, and give an algorithm of complexity O(N^6) to determine its first N coefficients. In particular, the susceptibility is shown to admit a convergent n–particle expansion χ^(n) whose components satisfy linear ODEs with polynomial coefficients; combining these yields a practical, automated pipeline for obtaining the first N coefficients of χ. We supply, for selected subseries, closed forms that illuminate the algebraic structure of the problem and validate the order of the associated differential operators. Our algorithm, whose complexity is O(N^6), scales favorably with N and enables high-precision expansion coefficients that confirm the anticipated singularity pattern: a dense set on the unit circle, consistent with a natural boundary. The results bear on the analytic continuation and non-holonomic character of the full susceptibility and its subterms.

We discuss its analyticity properties, certain closed form expressions for subsets of the coefficients, and give an algorithm of complexity O(N^6) to determine its first N coefficients.

title: Revealing hidden talents: The development, use, and benefit of VESPARCH.
text_ai: School attainment tests and Cognitive Abilities Tests are used in the United Kingdom to set targets for educational outcome. Whilst these are good predictors, they depend not only on basic ability but also on learnt knowledge and skills, such as reading. VESPARCH, a brief computer-based battery, integrates perceptual–motor fluency, pattern recognition, verbal fluency independent of reading comprehension, and collaborative problem-solving tasks designed to minimise linguistic loading. Development followed a three-phase process: theory-driven construct mapping, pilot testing with item response theory analyses, and field validation in diverse primary and secondary school samples (N ≈ 4,200). Factorial structure was robust across age bands; measurement invariance held across socioeconomic and language groups. In predictive validity studies, VESPARCH subscales showed reliable incremental validity over attainment tests and general cognitive ability for forecasting later engagement in non-academic domains, such as science clubs, creative projects, and peer leadership. The battery demonstrated stronger sensitivity to latent talents in pupils with uneven literacy profiles, thereby reducing bias inherent in reading-dependent measures. Policy and practice implications are discussed with regard to early talent identification, curriculum differentiation, and equitable opportunity provision. Collectively, VESPARCH offers a complementary lens on ability, revealing hidden talents that conventional tests overlook and enabling more holistic educational planning and support for diverse learners.

title: A New Lagrangian Problem Crossover: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Crossover Standards
text_ai: The performance of most evolutionary metaheuristic algorithms relays on various operatives. One of them is the crossover operator, which is divided into two types: application dependent and application independent crossover operators. These standards always help to choose the best-fitted point in the evolutionary algorithm process. From 312 studies (1990–2025), we extracted 164 reports describing crossover operators across domains and benchmarked them on fitness landscapes. We categorized crossovers into application-dependent (problem-tailored) and application-independent (generic) classes, delineated schemes (one-point, two-point, uniform, arithmetic, Simulated Binary Crossover) alongside Lagrangian-inspired variants. A random-effects meta-analysis synthesized performance deltas on normalized objectives, with subgroup analyses by problem class, constraint handling, encoding, and population size; bias risk was assessed with a rubric. Results indicate that no universal crossover dominates; improvements are context-dependent and modest. In constrained optimization, Lagrangian-inspired crossovers showed higher feasibility and faster convergence under tight constraints, relative to classical operators. For continuous landscapes, arithmetic and blended crossovers yielded robust convergence, while discrete combinatorial tasks benefited from problem-specific hybrids. Heterogeneity remained substantial (I2 frequently >50%), reflecting interaction effects among operator design, encoding, and selection. The findings offer a taxonomy of crossover invariants and a pragmatic framework that aligns operator choice with problem characteristics, enhancing standardization and reproducibility in crossover research.

title: On the interplay between notions of additive and multiplicative largeness and its combinatorial applications
text_ai: Many natural notions of additive and multiplicative largeness arise from results in Ramsey theory. In this paper, we explain the relationships between these notions for subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ and in more general ring-theoretic structures. We show that multiplicative largeness begets additive largeness in three ways and give a collection of examples demonstrating the optimality of these results. We identify three transfer principles by which multiplicative largeness yields additive largeness. First, canonical ring embeddings convert multiplicative geometry into additive structure on exponent-models, yielding additive IP-sets inside A−A, in a way that preserves relevant density properties. Second, semiring-regularity shows that multiplicatively piecewise syndetic sets force additive patterns such as long arithmetic progressions and IP-sets in finite partitions. Third, finite-product decompositions reveal that large multiplicative blocks give dense families of additive configurations under maps n↦∑v_p(n), producing prescribed additive constellations. We illustrate these principles with explicit examples in N and in polynomial rings and establish optimality via carefully crafted counterexamples. Consequences include strengthened partition regularity results for mixed additive–multiplicative equations, new sum–product phenomena in rings, and a unified framework for Ramsey-type combinatorics across algebraic settings. The framework extends to noncommutative rings and to general semirings, with quantitative bounds in several regimes, and provides guidance for future combinatorial applications.

title: Efficient State Space Model via Fast Tensor Convolution and Block Diagonalization
text_ai: Existing models encounter bottlenecks in balancing performance and computational efficiency when modeling long sequences. Although the state space model (SSM) has achieved remarkable success in handling long sequence tasks, it still faces the problem of large number of parameters. To address these challenges, we propose an efficient SSM that integrates fast tensor convolution with structured block diagonalization of the state-space operator. Our approach factorizes the latent dynamics into a small set of reusable temporal kernels encoded as low-rank blocks arranged in a diagonal-like structure, preserving long-range modeling capacity while dramatically reducing parameter count. The block diagonal form decouples latent channels and enables highly parallelizable recurrence, yielding substantial memory savings without sacrificing expressivity. Fast tensor convolution is then employed to implement the temporal integration by exploiting Toeplitz–like or circulant subblocks, which admits FFT-based acceleration and near-linear scaling in sequence length. We enforce stability and identifiability through constrained parameterization and scale-aware initialization, ensuring robust training for very long sequences and streaming inference. The method integrates seamlessly with standard backpropagation and demonstrates competitive performance with markedly lower compute and memory footprints than dense SSM variants. Empirical evaluations on long-range benchmarks show strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, with substantial throughput gains and reduced parameter count, while maintaining stable optimization and improved generalization on tasks requiring long-horizon dependencies.

title: Training and Serving System of Foundation Models: A Comprehensive Survey
text_ai: Foundation models (e.g., ChatGPT, DALL-E, PengCheng Mind, PanGu-$\Sigma$) have demonstrated extraordinary performance in key technological areas, such as natural language processing and visual recognition, and have become the mainstream trend of artificial general intelligence. This has led more and more major technology giants to dedicate significant human and financial resources to actively develop their foundation model systems, which drives continuous growth of these models' parameters. To harness foundation models at scale, this survey synthesizes end-to-end training and serving stacks that integrate data ingestion, optimization, and production deployment. We present a unified taxonomy of hardware, software, and data pipelines underpinning contemporary ecosystems, including distributed training strategies (data-, model-, and pipeline-parallelism), memory-management techniques (checkpointing, offloading, and partitioning), and performance optimizations (mixed precision, sparsity, and compiler-assisted optimizations). We distinguish training regimes—pretraining, instruction tuning, and RLHF—and examine their implications for latency, throughput, and safety in serving contexts. We compare architectures for inference, including multi-region deployment, tiered caching, and dynamic routing, with attention to fault tolerance and multi-tenant isolation. The survey also catalogues representative frameworks and benchmarks, evaluates trade-offs in cost, energy, and latency, and identifies gaps in reproducibility, data governance, privacy, and security. We conclude with directions toward standardization, comprehensive benchmarks, and energy-efficient, auditable foundation-model platforms.

title: Hidden momentum and the Abraham-Minkowski debate
text_ai: We use an extended version of electrodynamics, which admits the existence of magnetic charges and currents, to discuss how different models for electric and magnetic dipoles do or do not carry hidden momentum under the influence of external electromagnetic fields. Within this extended framework, the Amperian dipole supports a hidden momentum in an E field, p_hidden = (m × E)/c^2, whereas the Gilbert dipole does not generate such momentum because internal forces are tied to separate magnetic charges and do not acquire the kinematic drift required for hidden momentum. For a dielectric in a field, the total momentum splits into a field momentum part P_field and a material part P_mech, with latter compensating the former in the limit; the choice of Minkowski vs Abraham momentum densities then corresponds to different assignments of P_mech and P_field, while the sum remains invariant. We trace these correspondences in configurations: a stationary magnetic dipole in an E field, a dielectric and a light pulse entering a medium. Our results reinforce that the Abraham-Minkowski controversy reflects a partitioning convention rather than a paradox, provided the model remains within consistent electromagnetism. We discuss experimental implications and propose criteria to diagnose hidden momentum in metamaterials where effective magnetic charges are simulated.

title: Select, then Balance: A Plug-and-Play Framework for Exogenous-Aware Spatio-Temporal Forecasting
text_ai: Spatio-temporal forecasting aims to predict the future state of dynamic systems and plays an important role in multiple fields. However, existing solutions only focus on modeling using a limited number of observed target variables. In real-world scenarios, exogenous variables can be integrated into the model as additional input features and associated with the target signal to promote forecast accuracy. To address this gap, we propose a plug-and-play framework that decouples exogenous selection from forecasting, enabling exogenous-aware modeling without redesigning predictors. Structured as two modules, Select and Balance, the approach identifies a compact, predictive subset of exogenous signals and lags via a differentiable selector. The Balance component fuses the chosen exogenous inputs with the backbone via a dynamic gating mechanism that adaptively scales external influence. This design remains architecture-agnostic and can be integrated with common backbones (GNNs, temporal convnets, or transformers) with minimal changes. Empirical results on multiple datasets—traffic, air quality, and energy—demonstrate gains over target-only baselines and prior exogenous methods, with improved horizon accuracy and calibration. Ablation studies show the necessity of both Select and Balance, while experiments with missing or noisy exogenous data reveal robustness under realistic perturbations. The plug-and-play nature ensures compatibility with future exogenous variables and scalable deployment worldwide.

title: Compact Plasmonic Logic Gates Enabled by Magnetoelectric Light Funneling for On-Chip Optical Computing in the Telecom Band
text_ai: The realization of all-optical logic gates (AOLGs) is important for advancing photonic integrated circuit (PIC) design and optical data communication. Various photonic structures and design techniques, including two-dimensional photonic crystals, silicon waveguides, plasmonic waveguides, diffractive neural networks, and inverse design techniques, are actively being explored to achieve multifunctional, high-performance optical logic gates with fast data processing capabilities. Here, we report a compact plasmonic logic module that employs magnetoelectric light funneling to steer guided plasmons through interferometric junctions, achieving universal on-chip optical logic within the telecom band. The mechanism relies on a magnetoelectric bilayer integrated with a nanoplasmonic platform, whereby a voltage- or field-driven magnetization state modulates the local optical impedance and funnels energy into designated arms of a subwavelength interferometer. By reconfiguring the funneling direction and phase delay, the same device switches between logic states, enabling AND, OR, and NOT operations in a single compact footprint. Comprehensive full-wave simulations and coupled-mode analyses confirm high-contrast, low-crosstalk operation at 1.55 μm, with footprints well below a square micron and tolerance to fabrication imperfections. Reported figures of merit include extinction ratios exceeding 15–20 dB and insertion losses compatible with cascaded integration. The proposed approach offers a scalable pathway to dense, low-power, all-optical PICs, leveraging magnetoelectric control to realize reconfigurable, high-speed logic in the telecom regime.

Various photonic structures and design techniques, including two-dimensional photonic crystals, silicon waveguides, plasmonic waveguides, diffractive neural networks, and inverse design techniques, are actively being explored to achieve multifunctional, high-performance optical logic gates with fast data processing capabilities.

title: METTL3-mediated m6A methylation negatively modulates autophagy to support porcine blastocyst development‡.
text_ai: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) catalyzed by METTL3 regulates the maternal-to-zygotic transition in zebrafish and mice. However, the role and mechanism of METTL3-mediated m6A methylation in blastocyst development remains unclear. Here, we show that METTL3-mediated m6A methylation sustains porcine blastocyst development via negatively modulating autophagy. Using porcine embryos cultured to the blastocyst stage, we manipulated METTL3 by siRNA-mediated knockdown and by ectopic overexpression. m6A sequencing and meRIP-qPCR identified autophagy-related transcripts as METTL3 targets, including ATG5, ATG7 and BECN1, enriched for m6A within coding regions and 3′ UTRs. METTL3 depletion reduced global m6A levels and increased autophagic activity, as shown by elevated LC3-II/LC3-I ratios, diminished p62 and enhanced autophagosome formation, accompanied by a decline in blastocyst formation rate and cell allocation. By contrast, METTL3 overexpression elevated m6A on these transcripts, dampened autophagy, and improved blastocyst competence in partially rescued embryos. Functional tests using autophagy inhibitors (3-MA) or activators (rapamycin) demonstrated that premature autophagy undermines, whereas controlled inhibition restores, development in METTL3-deficient embryos. Mechanistically, m6A marks promoted YTHDF2-mediated decay of autophagy mRNAs, reducing autophagic flux. Collectively, METTL3-dependent m6A methylation fine-tunes autophagy to favor porcine blastocyst viability and developmental potential. These findings illuminate a conserved regulatory axis linking m6A modification to early embryonic quality control across mammalian species.

title: Mental well-being among the oldest old: revisiting the model of healthy ageing in a Finnish context.
text_ai: Purpose : This study aimed to examine how participants aged 80 years old or over describe their mental well-being-exploring the suitability of the model of healthy ageing when outlining the mental well-being concept. Methods : Six structured focus group interviews with 28 participants were conducted in Western Finland in 2017. Results : Thematic analysis revealed that mental well-being among the oldest old was experienced as a dynamic balance between internal resources and external supports. Participants described meaning-making through daily activities, relationships, reminiscence, and engagement in purposeful tasks, often despite health declines. Autonomy over routines, housing, and social participation, along with acceptance of loss and adaptive coping, emerged as central. Social connectedness—family, neighbours, and community services—buffered isolation and supported mood. Spirituality and personal values provided resilience. While aspects of the traditional healthy ageing model (absence of disease, functional ability, social participation) were relevant, participants challenged its completeness, highlighting context-specific factors such as cultural expectations in Finland, proximity to supportive networks, and existential well-being. Conclusions : The findings suggest mental well-being in the oldest old cannot be fully captured by the standard model. A context-sensitive framework that foregrounds meaning, connectedness, and adaptability should guide future research and policy, prioritizing community-based supports, person-centred care, and proactive mental health promotion for Finland's oldest-old.

Methods : Six structured focus group interviews with 28 participants were conducted in Western Finland in 2017.

title: Gluten-Free Products: From Dietary Necessity to Premium Price Extraction Tool.
text_ai: Every year, the Italian National Health Service (NHS) provides about 200,000 celiac people (based on 2017 data) living in Italy with financial support of about 250 million euro to cover the cost of their specific dietary constrains. Against this fiscal backdrop, the study investigates whether the gluten-free imperative has evolved from medical necessity into a strategic pricing lever for producers and retailers. We merge NHS expenditure data with retail scanner data and product attributes (category, brand, formulation, certification, packaging) from 2015–2022 and estimate a hedonic price model, complemented by a difference-in-differences specification to isolate the price effect of gluten-free status. The analysis accounts for substitution effects, nutritional content, and marketing claims. Results show a consistent gluten-free price premium relative to conventional products, averaging in the low-to-mid-thirties percent across categories, with bakery and pasta items strongest. Premium signals strengthen with explicit certification, channels, and private-label positioning. After controlling for calories and nutrition facts, the premium remains significant, indicating signaling and consumer perception contribute beyond costs. NHS subsidies attenuate but do not erase price sensitivity among subsidized households, signaling coexistence of public spending and market power. Findings illuminate a path for policy makers and firms to balance access and value capture while preserving affordability.
