title: Mol-R1: Towards Explicit Long-CoT Reasoning in Molecule Discovery
text_ai: Large language models (LLMs), especially Explicit Long Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning models like DeepSeek-R1 and QWQ, have demonstrated powerful reasoning capabilities, achieving impressive performance in commonsense reasoning and mathematical inference. Despite their effectiveness, Long-CoT reasoning models are often criticized for their limited ability and low efficiency in knowledge-intensive domains such as molecule discovery. To address these limitations, we introduce Mol-R1, a framework coupling explicit long-CoT generation with molecule-centric evaluation signals. Mol-R1 orchestrates a structured reasoning scaffold unfolding in iterative steps: (i) articulate multi-objective design targets under synthetic accessibility, cost, and safety constraints; (ii) decompose goals into subproblems grounded in medicinal-chemistry heuristics (scaffold hopping, functional-group compatibility) and retrosynthetic feasibility; (iii) generate stepwise justifications while consulting a curated knowledge base of reaction rules, property predictors, and synthetic routes; (iv) produce candidates via graph-guided sampling and fragment assembly, followed by multi-fidelity screening including docking, ADMET estimates, and synthesis feasibility assessment. We benchmark Mol-R1 against standard black-box LLM baselines and graph-based generators on established discovery tasks. Results show explicit Long-CoT prompts improve interpretability, controllability, and data efficiency, achieving competitive property optimization with transparent reasoning traces for human oversight. We outline integration, limitations, and future extensions toward scalable, trustworthy, and collaborative molecule discovery pipelines, enabling broader industry adoption.

title: Outpatient commitment in mental health services from a municipal view.
text_ai: Outpatient commitment (OC) is a legal decision for compulsory mental health care when the patient stays in his or her own home. Municipal health-care workers have a key role for patients with OC decision, but little is known about how the legislation system with OC works from the municipality's point of view. Objectives were to describe how OC is enacted at the municipal level and to identify processes, barriers, and facilitators perceived by staff. Methods: a qualitative study conducted in several municipalities, with semi-structured interviews of 22 frontline workers (nurses, social workers, care coordinators, and physicians) involved in OC cases, complemented by document analysis of orders and procedures. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis. Results: five core themes emerged: divergent interpretations of legal criteria and inconsistent information flow; dependence on informal networks for coordination; ethical tensions balancing autonomy, safety, and risk; resource constraints and administrative burdens; and a need for standardized workflows and formal interagency agreements. Practice varied across municipalities, with delays and inequities in follow-up care. Conclusions: formalized OC procedures, regular training on legal standards, streamlined information systems, and structured intersectoral collaboration are essential to support rights-respecting and effective municipal care.

Municipal health-care workers have a key role for patients with OC decision, but little is known about how the legislation system with OC works from the municipality's point of view.

title: The POKEMON Speckle Survey of Nearby M Dwarfs. III. The Stellar Multiplicity Rate of M Dwarfs within 15 pc
text_ai: M dwarfs are ubiquitous in our galaxy, and the rate at which they host stellar companions, and the properties of these companions, provides a window into the formation and evolution of the star(s), and of any planets that they may host. Using the POKEMON speckle survey of 350 M dwarfs within 15 pc, supplemented by Gaia DR3 astrometry and archival imaging, we identify 40 close visual binaries and 12 higher-order systems, yielding an observed multiplicity fraction of 0.28 ± 0.04 for separations ≈1–1000 AU. After correcting for incompleteness due to unresolved companions, the inferred rate is 0.32 ± 0.05. The companion population favors near-equal mass ratios (q ≳ 0.4) and a separation distribution that peaks near 5–20 AU, with a tail to several hundred AU. A mild trend shows earlier-type M dwarfs have higher multiplicity than later-type primaries, consistent with mass-dependent fragmentation. We find no statistically significant metallicity dependence within the solar neighborhood. The results support a formation picture in which low-mass stars form multiple systems predominantly through disk fragmentation and dynamical evolution, yet remain less prolific than higher-mass stars. These multiplicity characteristics bear on planet occurrence and dynamical histories of M-dwarf planetary systems within 15 pc.
prefix: M dwarfs are ubiquitous in our galaxy, and the rate at which they host stellar companions, and the properties of these companions, provides a window into the formation and evolution of the star(s), and of any planets that they may host.

title: Exploring Generative AI for Sim2Real in Driving Data Synthesis
text_ai: Datasets are essential for training and testing vehicle perception algorithms. However, the collection and annotation of real-world images is time-consuming and expensive. Driving simulators offer a solution by automatically generating various driving scenarios with corresponding annotations, but the simulation-to-reality (Sim2Real) domain gap remains a challenge. We present a generative‑augmented synthesis pipeline that couples high‑fidelity simulators with diffusion‑based domain translators to produce photo‑realistic, label‑preserving driving data. In Stage 1, diverse driving scenarios are generated with exhaustive annotations (bounding boxes, panoptic labels, depth) spanning weather, time of day, traffic density, and sensor configurations. In Stage 2, a conditional diffusion model is trained to translate synthetic renders into the real domain conditioned on semantic maps and sensor cues while enforcing label‑preservation through a geometry‑aware loss and a cycle‑consistency constraint. The translator can be steered by controllable attributes to synthesize rare events (eg, occlusions, motion blur) without altering ground‑truth labels. We complement this with a domain‑adaptive training regime: a small set of real data guides feature‑space alignment via contrastive and moment‑matching losses, while the main backbone is trained on the translated data with task‑specific heads. Evaluation on standard driving benchmarks demonstrates reduced sim2real discrepancy across detection, segmentation, and depth estimation tasks, with improved robustness to adverse conditions and reduced annotation burden.

Driving simulators offer a solution by automatically generating various driving scenarios with corresponding annotations, but the simulation-to-reality (Sim2Real) domain gap remains a challenge.

title: Public Discourse Sandbox: Facilitating Human and AI Digital Communication Research
text_ai: Social media serves as a primary communication and information dissemination platform for major global events, entertainment, and niche or topically focused community discussions. Therefore, it represents a valuable resource for researchers who aim to understand numerous questions. However, obtaining data can be difficult, expensive, and often unreliable due to the presence of bots, fake accounts, and manipulated content. Public Discourse Sandbox (PDS) operationalizes a modular ecosystem that combines curated datasets, synthetic data generation, and tooling to attenuate access barriers without compromising ethical standards. Data curation emphasizes provenance, annotation schemas, and bias auditing, while privacy-preserving techniques enable safe reuse of available corpora and controlled synthesis for agent-based experiments. The sandbox supports human-in-the-loop workflows, enabling researchers to co-create prompts, evaluate interventions, and quantify effects on discourse quality, polarization, and misinformation diffusion. Researchers can run reproducible experiments in sandboxed environments, leverage standardized metrics, and share configurations, datasets, and evaluation results under licensing terms to promote comparability. Governance layers enforce consent, platform policy alignment, and risk assessment, while audit logs and versioning sustain transparency and accountability. By lowering technical and ethical frictions, PDS invites interdisciplinary collaboration and accelerates hypothesis testing, offering a scalable test bed for studying human–AI collaboration, moderation, and the dynamics of public discourse.

Therefore, it represents a valuable resource for researchers who aim to understand numerous questions. However, obtaining data can be difficult, expensive, and often unreliable due to the presence of bots, fake accounts, and manipulated content.

title: From Uncertainty to Anxiety: How Uncertainty Fuels Anxiety in a Process Mediated by Intolerance of Uncertainty.
text_ai: Uncertainty about future events may lead to worry, anxiety, even inability to function. The highly related concept-intolerance of uncertainty (IU)-emerged in the early 1990s, which is further developed into a transdiagnostic risk factor in multiple forms of anxiety disorders. Across two preregistered experiments (N = 420) we manipulated uncertainty about upcoming outcomes and assessed both state anxiety and sustained worry. IU was measured with the short IUS-12 and decomposed into prospective and inhibitory facets. Mediation analyses tested whether IU mediated the effect of uncertainty on anxious responding, and whether trait anxiety moderated this pathway. In Study 1, uncertainty augmentation increased state anxiety, with IU fully mediating the effect; in Study 2, a more ecologically valid imagined uncertainty context produced similar mediation, with inhibitory IU showing stronger paths than prospective IU, suggesting different mechanisms for intolerance to uncertain cues versus uncertain prospects. Additional moderators included habitual worry and cognitive control, indexed by a Stroop-like task; results indicated that strong cognitive control buffers, but only for individuals reporting low IU. Together, findings delineate a proximal mechanism by which uncertainty enacts anxiety through intolerance of uncertainty, with practical implications for cognitive-behavioral interventions targeting IU as a transdiagnostic process. With potential for targeted prevention.

title: Prompt GeV emission in the synchrotron self-Compton model for Gamma-Ray Bursts
text_ai: The detection in 10 bursts of an optical counterpart emission (i.e. during the prompt GRB phase) that is 10-10000 brighter than the extrapolation of the burst spectrum to optical frequencies suggests a synchrotron self-Compton origin for the GRB emission, synchrotron producing the optical counterpart emission. Within a one-zone synchrotron-self-Compton (SSC) framework for internal shocks in a relativistic jet, we compute the GeV output produced by upscattering of the prompt synchrotron photons by non-thermal electrons that yield the optical counterpart. Adopting parameters consistent with the observed optical brightening and with the keV–MeV spectrum (Γ ≈ 300–800, R ≈ 10^13–10^14 cm, ε_e ≈ 0.1–0.5, ε_B ≈ 10^-4–10^-2, p ≈ 2.2–2.8), we show that the SSC component can peak naturally in the 0.1–10 GeV band with fluence comparable to the MeV emission, while remaining compatible with γγ opacity and Klein–Nishina suppression. The model predicts a strong correlation and near-simultaneity between optical and GeV light curves, with a modest GeV lag set by cooling and light-travel time, and requires high bulk Lorentz factors to evade attenuation. Across a sample of bursts, the SSC interpretation accounts for the observed GeV detections without invoking external or hadronic processes, constraining jet magnetization and particle acceleration efficiency.
prefix: The detection in 10 bursts of an optical counterpart emission (i.e. during the prompt GRB phase) that is 10-10000 brighter than the extrapolation of the burst spectrum to optical frequencies suggests a synchrotron self-Compton origin for the GRB emission, synchrotron producing the optical counterpart emission.

title: Volatile evolution and atmospheres of Trans-Neptunian Objects
text_ai: At 30-50 K, the temperatures typical for surfaces in the Kuiper Belt (e.g. Stern & Trafton 2008), only seven species have sublimation pressures higher than 1 nbar (Fray & Schmitt 2009): Ne, N$_2$, CO, Ar, O$_2$, CH$_4$, and Kr. Of these, N$_2$, CO, and CH$_4$ have been detected or inferred on the surfaces of Trans-Neptunian Objects (TNOs). Here we present a coupled thermophysical and atmospheric evolution framework applicable to the population of TNOs, from Pluto-sized bodies to icy aggregates. We implement sublimation–condensation physics for Ne, N2, CO, Ar, O2, CH4, and Kr alongside a parameterized volatile transport scheme that tracks melt-freeze cycles, surface albedo feedback, and insolation. The model computes surface pressure, mean molecular mass, and vertical structure of an atmosphere, including escape rates consistent with the body’s gravity. We find that N2, CO, and CH4 can sustain tenuous atmospheres on Gyr timescales only when kept in contact with their native ices; N2-rich surfaces are the most volatile and most prone to atmospheric collapse, whereas CH4-rich patches can outgas episodically, producing atmospheres of 0.1–10 nbar depending on insolation. Our results imply observable spectral and occultation signatures tied to the volatile inventory, with implications for interpreting past and future TNO observations.

Of these, N$_2$, CO, and CH$_4$ have been detected or inferred on the surfaces of Trans-Neptunian Objects (TNOs).

title: Probing the mechanical properties of DNA nanostructures with metadynamics
text_ai: Molecular dynamics simulations are often used to provide feedback in the design workflow of DNA nanostructures. However, even with coarse-grained models, convergence of distributions from unbiased simulation is slow, limiting applications to equilibrium structural properties. Given the increasing interest in dynamic, reconfigurable, and deformable devices, methods that enable efficient quantification of large ranges of motion, conformational transitions, and mechanical deformation are critically needed. Here, we implement well-tempered metadynamics (WT-MetaD) in a coarse-grained DNA model to bias along a set of collective variables encoding deformation. CVs include the end-to-end distance, a bending angle between domains, and a torsional coordinate describing twist between panels; additional inter-domain dihedrals and interhelical shear are monitored. We employ multiple walkers to enhance exploration of high-energy barriers characteristic of reconfigurable devices. From the biased simulations, we reconstruct unbiased PMFs via reweighting and extract force-extension relationships and effective stiffness along the deformation coordinates. Validation against unbiased trajectories and, where available, experimental estimates of bending and stretching moduli for origami motifs. The results show faster convergence of free-energy landscapes by one to two orders of magnitude and illuminate mechanistic pathways for hinge opening, domain rotation, and reconfiguration. This workflow yields a quantitative metric for mechanical performance in DNA nanostructures.

title: Survival of Salmonella spp. in Composting using Vial and Direct Inoculums Technique
text_ai: The survival of Salmonella spp. as pathogen indicator in composting was studied. The inoculums technique was used to gives the known amounts of Salmonella spp. involved in composting. The inoculums of Salmonella spp. solution was added directly into the compost material. The direct inoculum was compared with inoculums in vial technique. During the experiment, temperature and moisture were monitored to characterize the operating conditions of the composting matrix. The pile achieved a thermophilic phase (mean 58–62°C) within 3 days and remained above 55°C for 5–7 days, followed by a gradual decline to the mesophilic range. Salmonella survival was quantified by culture on selective media (XLD) and by enrichment in selenite cystine broth with subsequent plating. The direct inoculum yielded initial counts near 10^6 CFU g^-1, with a rapid decline during the thermophilic phase; by day 7 counts typically ranged 10^2–10^3 CFU g^-1 and by day 14 were frequently non-detect by plating, though a subset of samples required enrichment to reveal low-level survivors. The vial-inoculum treatment exhibited a parallel but modestly slower decline, with detectable counts at day 7 in the range 10^2–10^3 CFU g^-1 and non-detect by plating appearing later, around day 14–21 in some replicates. By days 21–28, all samples were non-detect by plating, and enrichment failed to recover Salmonella spp. in any replicate. No measurable adverse effects on compost maturation indicators were observed; pH, total organic carbon loss, and the C/N ratio progressed within expected trajectories for thermophilic to mature compost. Statistical analysis (two-way repeated-measures ANOVA) indicated a significant effect of time on Salmonella counts (p < 0.001), whereas the inoculum method effect was not significant (p ≈ 0.12) and the time-by-method interaction was not significant (p ≈ 0.68). Overall, die-off kinetics were comparable between direct and vial inoculation under the tested conditions. The vial technique provides a standardized, lower-risk approach to introducing defined pathogen loads for hazard assessment and inter-laboratory comparability in compost safety studies.

title: PRIMG : Efficient LLM-driven Test Generation Using Mutant Prioritization
text_ai: Mutation testing is a widely recognized technique for assessing and enhancing the effectiveness of software test suites by introducing deliberate code mutations. However, its application often results in overly large test suites, as developers generate numerous tests to kill specific mutants, increasing computational overhead. PRIMG, by contrast, orchestrates targeted generation rather than exhaustive mutation killing. The approach comprises a mutant prioritization module that estimates each mutant's kill potential and cost, a guided LLM-driven test generator that produces concise, executable tests aligned to top-ranked mutants, and an evaluation loop that prunes tests while preserving diagnostic coverage. The LLM prompts are carefully engineered with mutant abstracts, surrounding code context, and exemplars of minimal failing inputs; the system enforces constraints to minimize flaky tests and ensure determinism. Generated tests are validated via a lightweight oracle and static-dynamic filtering, then executed; results inform iterative re-prioritization and prompt refinement. We validate PRIMG on multiple open-source projects with diverse languages, demonstrating that notably fewer tests sufficed to achieve comparable or superior mutation scores than conventional generation strategies. An ablation study isolates the contributions of mutant prioritization, prompt design, and feedback integration, underscoring the practical viability of LLM-assisted, mutant-aware test synthesis for scalable mutation testing. This work provides a practical blueprint for practitioners.

However, its application often results in overly large test suites, as developers generate numerous tests to kill specific mutants, increasing computational overhead.

title: Race does not predict the development of metastases in men with nonmetastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
text_ai: BACKGROUND: Although race is associated with prostate cancer progression in early stage disease, once men have advanced disease, it is unclear whether race continues to predict a poor outcome. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicenter cohort of men with nmCRPC treated at 12 centers from 2009–2023. Eligibility required castration testosterone <50 ng/dL, no radiographic metastases at baseline, and at least one follow-up imaging study. Race was self-reported and categorized as Black, White, or other. The primary outcome was time to development of distant metastases, validated by radiographic reports. Secondary outcomes included metastasis-free survival and overall survival. Covariates comprised age, baseline PSA, PSA doubling time, Gleason score, Charlson comorbidity index, body mass index, prior local therapy, and systemic treatment (AR pathway inhibitors, chemotherapy). We used Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) for metastasis by race, adjusting for covariates. We also conducted competing-risks analyses for metastasis-free survival with death treated as a competing event. Kaplan-Meier methods described metastasis-free survival by race. Missing data were addressed with multiple imputation; sensitivity analyses excluded imputed observations. Subgroup analyses examined interactions by treatment era. RESULTS: The cohort included 741 men (median age 71). Racial distribution: White 72%, Black 14%, other 14%. Median follow-up was 38 months; 164 men (22%) developed radiographically confirmed metastases. In unadjusted analyses, race was not associated with time to metastasis. In multivariable Cox models adjusting for age, PSA, PSA-DT, Gleason score, comorbidity, treatment with AR inhibitors or chemotherapy, and era, Black race was not associated with higher metastasis risk (HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.78–1.21, p=0.78). Similar null associations were observed for other racial groups. Competing risks analyses yielded concordant results. No significant interactions between race and treatment modality were detected (P>0.2). CONCLUSIONS: Among men with nmCRPC, race did not predict progression to metastasis or metastasis-free survival after adjustment for clinical factors and therapies. These findings challenge the notion of race-based prognostication in nonmetastatic castration-resistant disease and highlight the need to focus on modifiable determinants of progression and equitable care delivery.
prefix: BACKGROUND: Although race is associated with prostate cancer progression in early stage disease, once men have advanced disease, it is unclear whether race continues to predict a poor outcome.

title: Generative AI as a Geopolitical Factor in Industry 5.0: Sovereignty, Access, and Control
text_ai: Industry 5.0 marks a new phase in industrial evolution, emphasizing human-centricity, sustainability, and resilience through the integration of advanced technologies. Within this evolving landscape, Generative AI (GenAI) and autonomous systems are not only transforming industrial processes but also emerging as pivotal geopolitical instruments. GenAI and autonomous systems, embedded in modular, human-centric production networks, extend national influence by designating digital corridors, standards, and interoperability regimes across traditional borders. Sovereignty is reframed around data ownership, model provenance, compute locality, and responsible training practices that constrain cross-border flows. Access to GenAI capabilities becomes a strategic resource, governed by techno-economic blocs, supplier configurations, and talent pipelines, which drive winner-takes-most dynamics in critical sectors such as energy and microelectronics. Control over generative workflows—data curation, prompt governance, and model updates—translates into leverage in planning and quality assurance, but also elevates vulnerability through reliance on external ecosystems and opaque supply chains. This paper analyzes policy interfaces, industry standards, and governance mechanisms that mediate these tensions, using modeling and case studies. It highlights three levers: data sovereignty frameworks, export-control regimes for AI tooling, and the architecture of open versus closed platform ecosystems. The findings offer implications for firms, states, and multinational coalitions seeking resilient, inclusive Industry 5.0 trajectories.

Within this evolving landscape, Generative AI (GenAI) and autonomous systems are not only transforming industrial processes but also emerging as pivotal geopolitical instruments.

title: The Oldest Stars of the Extremely Metal-Poor Local Group Dwarf Irregular Galaxy Leo A
text_ai: We present deep Hubble Space Telescope single-star photometry of Leo A in B, V, and I. Our new field of view is offset from the centrally located field observed by Tolstoy et al. (1998) in order to expose the halo population of this galaxy. We quantify the halo population through color–magnitude diagram (CMD) analysis, foreground subtraction, and completeness corrections derived from extensive artificial-star tests. The resulting BVI CMDs reveal a clearly delineated red giant branch (RGB) that is markedly blueward of more metal-rich systems, together with a sparsely populated blue horizontal branch (BHB) and a modest red clump, signatures that point to an ancient, metal-poor stellar component. The RGB color spread requires metallicities spanning roughly [Fe/H] ≈ −2.3 to −1.9, with a peak near [Fe/H] ≈ −2.1; a faint, extended HB argues for star formation at epochs older than ~10 Gyr. Candidate RR Lyrae variables are present in the field, providing a direct census of stars older than 10 Gyr and anchoring the distance scale. We fit the CMD with synthetic populations drawn from modern isochrones (covering ages from 2–13 Gyr and metallicities Z ≈ 0.0002–0.0008) to recover the star-formation history (SFH) of Leo A’s halo. The oldest stars comprise a non-negligible fraction of the stellar mass, formed in a spatially extended epoch that began ≥10–12 Gyr ago, followed by continued, but slowly diminishing, star formation to the present day. The inferred metallicity evolution is gradual, with initial enrichment to Z ≈ 0.0004–0.0006 by ~8–10 Gyr ago and only modest further enrichment thereafter, consistent with a low star-formation efficiency and weak galactic outflows. The derived distance modulus, calibrated by the TRGB and corroborated by the HB morphology, yields (m−M)0 ≈ 24.2–24.3, placing Leo A at a distance of roughly 700 kpc. Collectively, these results demonstrate that Leo A hosts a bona fide ancient, extremely metal-poor stellar component, challenging simple narratives of purely delayed star formation in isolated dwarf irregulars and bearing on early chemical evolution in the Local Group.

title: In-ear EEG biometrics for feasible and readily collectable real-world person authentication
text_ai: The use of EEG as a biometrics modality has been investigated for about a decade, however its feasibility in real-world applications is not yet conclusively established, mainly due to the issues with collectability and reproducibility. Here, we evaluate a compact in-ear EEG platform designed for rapid setup. Data were collected from 28 participants across three sessions over two weeks to quantify reproducibility. The in-ear system integrates dry-contact electrodes in a consumer-grade earbud housing with a wireless amplifier, enabling unobtrusive use. We benchmark against scalp EEG in a lab control condition. Preprocessing included bandpass filtering (1–40 Hz), artifact rejection tailored to in-ear geometry, and epoching with brief cues or rests. Features included time-domain statistics, spectral power (theta/alpha/beta), and inter-channel connectivity proxies. Classification used an SVM with an RBF kernel and a compact neural network. Within-session accuracy averaged 94.2%, cross-session accuracy 88.7%, and equal error rate 2.9%. Under realistic scenarios—speaking, chewing, jaw movement—the drop was under 5 percentage points. Enrollment completed within ~60 seconds and tolerated moderate electrode displacement, indicating feasibility for real-world authentication. These results support deployment in daily devices and emphasize a rapid onboarding with privacy-preserving template updates as part of a broader multi-factor authentication framework. Future work will extend cross-device validation and evaluate long-term template stability.
prefix: The use of EEG as a biometrics modality has been investigated for about a decade, however its feasibility in real-world applications is not yet conclusively established, mainly due to the issues with collectability and reproducibility.

title: The 2018 classification of periodontal diseases: Its predictive value for tooth loss.
text_ai: Predictive models and assessment tools for disease susceptibility and progression are necessary to enhance personalized medicine. The aim of this study is to assess the predictive accuracy of using the 2018 classification to predict likelihood of tooth loss. A total of 134 patients were screened 10 years after periodontal therapy. Materials and methods: A retrospective cohort of 134 patients previously treated for periodontitis was re-evaluated 10 years after completion of maintenance. Baseline 2018 periodontitis stage (I–IV) and grade (A–C) were assigned from archived clinical and radiographic data. The primary outcome was tooth loss attributed to periodontal disease during follow-up. Predictors included age, sex, smoking status, diabetes mellitus and adherence to maintenance. Discrimination was assessed by area under the curve (AUC); calibration by observed-predicted risk; time-to-event analyses used Cox models to estimate hazard ratios for stage and grade, adjusted for covariates. Net reclassification improvement quantified incremental value over prior classification. Results: Over 10 years, 27 teeth were lost in 11 patients. Higher stage and higher grade were associated with greater risk (p<0.05). The 2018 classification alone yielded AUC≈0.73; adding covariates increased AUC to ≈0.79, with good calibration. Conclusion: The 2018 schema demonstrates meaningful predictive value for tooth loss, supporting its use in risk-stratified maintenance planning.
prefix: Predictive models and assessment tools for disease susceptibility and progression are necessary to enhance personalized medicine. The aim of this study is to assess the predictive accuracy of using the 2018 classification to predict likelihood of tooth loss. A total of 134 patients were screened 10 years after periodontal therapy.

title: Visual-perceptual training with motor practice of the observed movement pattern improves anticipation in emerging expert cricket batsmen.
text_ai: This study addressed the paucity of evidence of whether visual anticipation can be improved in emerging experts in striking sports. Twelve emerging expert batsmen from a state cricket squad were equally randomised into intervention and control groups. They were pre-and-post tested on a video temporal occlusion test of a fast bowler, as well as transfer tests of different fast and slow bowlers. That training regimen comprised eight 45-minute sessions over two weeks, integrating (i) dynamic visual-perceptual exposure using hand-occluded video occlusion and forced-choice anticipation tasks, and (ii) motor practice in which participants reproduced the observed action pattern through shadow bat swings timed to recorded bowler sequences. Post-intervention assessments revealed that the intervention group outperformed controls on the occlusion test, manifest as earlier ball-release anticipation and higher hit-rate synchronization with the optimal bat-to-ball contact window (p<.05; Cohen's d≈0.6–0.8). Transfer tests showed meaningful gains for untrained fast and slow bowlers, with greater transfer to slow-ball timing, suggesting improved temporal prediction across contexts. Retention at two-week follow-up indicated maintenance of advantage. The results extend account that action observation coupled with movement re-enactment enhances perceptual–motor coupling in emerging experts, offering a practical training component for cricket academies seeking to accelerate anticipatory expertise without heavy batting-load demands.

title: Neuromorphic meets neuromechanics, part I: the methodology and implementation.
text_ai: One goal of neuromorphic engineering is to create 'realistic' robotic systems that interact with the physical world by adopting neuromechanical principles from biology. Critical to this is the methodology to implement the spinal circuitry responsible for the behavior of afferented muscles. We present a modular framework to translate proprioceptive afferents into spinal-like computations and generate motor commands on neuromorphic hardware. The sensory subsystem models muscle spindle and Golgi tendon organ afferents as spike-encoded channels, capturing length, velocity, and force with biologically inspired latency. The central subsystem uses compact interneuronal pools to implement monosynaptic and polysynaptic reflex arcs, reciprocal inhibition, and minimal locomotor CPG modules with modulatory inputs. The motor subsystem maps outputs to actuators via distributed motor-neuron pools and drivers for compliant actuation, embedding intrinsic damping and nonlinearity. Across the stack, simple plasticity rules couple fixed synapses to explore stability and learning under neuromorphic noise. Methodologically, we pursue hardware–software co-design: a real-time neuromorphic core handles population-level processing while a higher-level controller provides contextual and adaptation signals. The system runs at multi-kiloHz timescales with event-driven communication to minimize latency. We implement affine and nonaffine muscle models with afferented feedback and calibrate them on a physical testbed—a multi-joint limb with series-elastic actuators. Evaluation targets reflex fidelity, impedance under load, robustness to sensory dropout and motor noise, and energy efficiency. Preliminary results show stable, reflex-like responses to step and ramp perturbations with biologically plausible delays and modest compute overhead. The neuromorphic spine supports stable oscillations under perturbations and adaptive reflex gain via simple STDP-like mechanisms. We discuss design choices, limitations, and scaling guidelines for more complex morphologies, setting the stage for learning in part II.
prefix: One goal of neuromorphic engineering is to create 'realistic' robotic systems that interact with the physical world by adopting neuromechanical principles from biology. Critical to this is the methodology to implement the spinal circuitry responsible for the behavior of afferented muscles.

title: Reductions in alcohol use following medical cannabis initiation: results from a large cross-sectional survey of medical cannabis patients in Canada.
text_ai: Evidence details how cannabis can influence the use of other psychoactive substances, including prescription medications, alcohol, tobacco and illicit drugs, but very little research has examined the factors associated with these changes in substance use patterns. This paper explores the self-reported use of cannabis as a substitute for alcohol among a Canadian medical cannabis patient population. Across Canada, a growing proportion of patients reported using cannabis to reduce or substitute alcohol following medical initiation. In this cross-sectional sample, 9,672 respondents completed the survey and met inclusion criteria. Descriptive statistics indicated that 38% (n = 3,670) of participants who reported any alcohol use in the month prior to initiating medical cannabis indicated a reduction in alcohol consumption since starting cannabis, 32% (n = 3,036) reported no change, and 30% (n = 2,966) reported an increase in alcohol use. Among those reporting reduced alcohol use, the average decline was 3.8 standard drinks per week (SD = 2.6). Substitution was more frequently reported by patients using cannabis daily or near-daily (vs. occasional use) and by those consuming higher-THC products; these associations persisted after adjustment for age, sex, income, education, region, and urbanicity. Multivariable logistic regression identified several correlates of reported substitution. Daily cannabis use (AOR = 2.1; 95% CI: 1.9–2.3) and use of higher-THC formulations (AOR = 1.6; 95% CI: 1.4–1.9) were positively associated with reduced alcohol consumption. Older age (≥50 years) showed a modest positive association (AOR = 1.3; 95% CI: 1.1–1.5). Medical indications such as chronic pain and sleep disorders were more strongly linked with substitution (AORs ranging from 1.4 to 1.9) than other conditions. Those reporting prior alcohol-related problems did not differ markedly in substitution odds after adjustment, though statistical power was limited for this subgroup. Conclusion: In a large national cross-sectional sample of Canadian medical cannabis patients, a substantial minority report substituting cannabis for alcohol following initiation. These patterns may have implications for alcohol-related harms and for healthcare guidance regarding cannabis–alcohol interactions. Longitudinal studies are needed to establish causality and to disentangle substitution from concurrent changes in health status or other substance use. Limitations include cross-sectional design, self-selection, and reliance on self-report.
prefix: Evidence details how cannabis can influence the use of other psychoactive substances, including prescription medications, alcohol, tobacco and illicit drugs, but very little research has examined the factors associated with these changes in substance use patterns. This paper explores the self-reported use of cannabis as a substitute for alcohol among a Canadian medical cannabis patient population.

title: Multi-Institutional Predictors of Antibiotic Resistance in Patients Presenting to the Emergency Department with Urosepsis Secondary to Ureteral Obstruction.
text_ai: Introduction and Objective: Patients presenting with a urinary tract infection with kidney or ureteral stones is a urologic emergency often achieve early clinical stability but remain hospitalized while awaiting results from urine antibiotic sensitivity analyses. Methods: We conducted a multicenter, retrospective cohort study across six emergency departments (academic and community) from 2015 through 2023. Eligible patients were adults presenting with ureteral obstruction from stones and sepsis due to urinary infection. Exclusions included non-obstructive stones, non-urinary sources of sepsis, pregnancy, and incomplete data. We abstracted demographics, comorbidities (Charlson index), prior antibiotic exposure (within 90 days), recent hospitalization, urinary catheter or ureteral stent, stone burden and laterality, hydronephrosis grade, and whether definitive relief of obstruction was achieved during admission. Microbiology included blood and urine cultures with susceptibility results; resistance adhered to CLSI/NARMS criteria and multidrug resistance (MDR) was defined as non-susceptibility to agents in ≥3 antimicrobial classes. Primary outcome was presence of resistant urinary pathogens; secondary outcomes included time to appropriate therapy, length of stay (LOS), intensive care unit admission, and in-hospital mortality. We used multivariable logistic regression with backward elimination; model inputs encompassed predictors with P<0.20 in bivariable analyses and clinician-identified factors. Missing data were handled via multiple imputation by chained equations. Model discrimination was quantified with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and calibration with the Hosmer-Lemeshow test; internal validation employed bootstrap resampling. A parsimonious risk score was derived for bedside use. Results: Among 1,190 encounters, 338 (28.4%) yielded resistant pathogens. Independent predictors of resistance were prior antibiotic exposure (aOR 2.0, 95% CI 1.6–2.6), recent hospitalization (aOR 1.7, 95% CI 1.3–2.2), presence of indwelling urinary devices (aOR 1.5, 95% CI 1.2–1.9), diabetes (aOR 1.3, 95% CI 1.0–1.7), and elevated inflammatory markers (neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio) (aOR per unit rise 1.04, 95% CI 1.01–1.07). Time to effective therapy increased by a median of 5.8 hours; LOS was longer by 1.9 days and ICU admission rose by 4%. The model achieved an AUC of 0.77 (95% CI 0.74–0.80) with good calibration; the risk score stratified resistance risk with clinical utility. Conclusions: Across multiple centers, identifiable patient- and device-related factors predict antibiotic resistance in ED patients with urosepsis due to obstructive uropathy. Implementing a pretest risk stratification tool could guide empiric therapy and expedite source control while supporting antibiotic stewardship.
prefix: Introduction and Objective: Patients presenting with a urinary tract infection with kidney or ureteral stones is a urologic emergency often achieve early clinical stability but remain hospitalized while awaiting results from urine antibiotic sensitivity analyses.

title: On the stability of the spherically symmetric solution to an inflow problem for an isentropic model of compressible viscous fluid
text_ai: We investigate an inflow problem for the multi-dimensional isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations. The fluid under consideration occupies the exterior domain of unit ball, $\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n\,\vert\, |x|\ge 1\}$, and a constant stream of mass is flowing into the domain from the boundary $\partial\Omega=\{|x|=1\}$. We construct a unique, smooth, spherically symmetric stationary inflow solution (ρs, us)=(ρs(r), us(r) e_r) of the steady problem generated by the prescribed boundary flux. The isentropic equation of state p(ρ)=aρ^γ with γ>1 and the Newtonian viscosity μ>0, λ≥0 yield a positive density profile ρs and a physically admissible far-field behavior. For initial data that are small perturbations of (ρs, us) in an energy norm adapted to exterior domains, the inflow problem admits a global classical solution (ρ,u) which remains positive and keeps the same inflow boundary condition. We prove that the perturbation (ρ−ρs,u−us) decays to zero as t→∞ in a suitable energy space, with an algebraic decay rate that can be explicitly linked to γ and the dimension n. The analysis rests on reformulating the equations in terms of perturbations, deriving a closed energy-dissipation inequality with boundary contributions, and employing weighted Sobolev estimates and Hardy-type inequalities appropriate to exterior domains. These results establish nonlinear stability of the spherically symmetric inflow state within the isentropic viscous regime.
prefix: We investigate an inflow problem for the multi-dimensional isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations. The fluid under consideration occupies the exterior domain of unit ball, $\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n\,\vert\, |x|\ge 1\}$, and a constant stream of mass is flowing into the domain from the boundary $\partial\Omega=\{|x|=1\}$.

title: Partial-Information Multiple Access Protocol for Orthogonal Transmissions
text_ai: With the stringent requirements introduced by the new sixth-generation (6G) internet-of-things (IoT) use cases, traditional approaches to multiple access control have started to show their limitations. A new wave of grant-free (GF) approaches have been therefore proposed as a viable alternative. However, a definitive solution is still to be accomplished. We propose the Partial-Information MultiAccess Protocol (PIMAP) for orthogonal transmissions, a scalable grant-free scheme that leverages partial state information available at the network edge. PIMAP partitions the orthogonal resource space into a set of channels whose utilization is guided by a compact broadcast of a probability map together with lightweight backlog proxies. Each active device maintains a local backlog estimate and, aided by occasional acknowledgments, updates its per-channel transmission probability. A base station collects minimal feedback—such as one-bit success indicators or overheard transmissions—and emits a concise PSI profile that shapes future contention opportunities without incurring full scheduling overhead. Operationally, in every slot a device independently transmits on a randomly chosen orthogonal channel with probability determined by its local state and the broadcast PSI. A partial-information mechanism reduces collision likelihood by distributing access attempts across channels according to estimated contention and by dynamically adjusting probabilities in response to observed successes and failures. We model the system as a slotted, multi-channel access game with N contenders, K orthogonal channels, and stochastic arrivals; the success probability on a given channel is characterized as a function of the instantaneous channel load and the available PSI. Analytical expressions for throughput, average delay, and retransmission probability are derived; a pragmatic stability region is established under the PIMAP policy, along with approximate closed-form bounds suitable for design. Numerical results, validated by simulations under Poisson and bursty traffic and across varying channel conditions, show that PIMAP achieves notable gains over pure grant-free and fully scheduled schemes, including higher throughput and lower latency with substantially reduced signaling overhead. The findings offer practical guidelines for deploying partial-information–driven orthogonal access in dense 6G–IoT networks, highlighting robustness to PSI imperfections and scalability to massive device populations.
prefix: With the stringent requirements introduced by the new sixth-generation (6G) internet-of-things (IoT) use cases, traditional approaches to multiple access control have started to show their limitations. A new wave of grant-free (GF) approaches have been therefore proposed as a viable alternative. However, a definitive solution is still to be accomplished.

title: VIVID: A Novel Approach to Remediation Prioritization in Static Application Security Testing (SAST)
text_ai: Static Application Security Testing (SAST) enables organizations to detect vulnerabilities in code early; however, major SAST platforms do not include visual aids and present little insight on correlations between tainted data chains. VIVID introduces a visualization-centric remediation prioritization pipeline that couples taint-tracking graphs with risk-aware scoring and an interactive dashboard. The backbone is a taint-propagation graph that maps sources, operations, and sinks and renders transitive data flows across modules; visual encodings emphasize provenance, exposure likelihood, and remediation hotspots. A remediation-priority engine computes a composite risk score by merging SAST severity with data-flow depth, propagation frequency, fix effort, and architectural significance, while incorporating ownership to align with developer workflows. The system filters irrelevant findings and surfaces actionable, high-impact paths, enabling informed triage and efficient remediation planning. It integrates with prevailing SAST platforms through lightweight adapters and offers an extensible visualization layer and a human-in-the-loop feedback loop to refine scoring. In evaluation, VIVID applied to three open-source projects and a commercial codebase, comparing against baseline SAST workflows. Results show gains in triage speed, higher proportion of actionable fixes, and reduced cognitive load for reviewers. A user study with developers corroborates improved satisfaction and perceived traceability, underscoring viability and guiding future enhancements.
prefix: Static Application Security Testing (SAST) enables organizations to detect vulnerabilities in code early; however, major SAST platforms do not include visual aids and present little insight on correlations between tainted data chains.

title: The effect of structural and magnetic disorder on the 3$d$-5$d$ exchange interactions of La$_{2-x}$Ca$_{x}$CoIrO$_{6}$
text_ai: The delicate balance between spin-orbit coupling, Coulomb repulsion and crystalline electric field interactions observed in Ir-based oxides is usually manifested as exotic magnetic behavior. Here we investigate the evolution of the exchange coupling between Co and Ir for partial La substitution by Ca in La$_{2}$CoIrO$_6$. Polycrystalline samples of La2−xCaxCoIrO6 (x = 0, 0.5, 1.0) were prepared by solid-state synthesis and phase purity confirmed by X-ray diffraction; Rietveld refinements indicate retention of the monoclinic P2_1/n structure with a systematic contraction of the lattice upon Ca substitution. The CoO6 and IrO6 octahedra become more distorted, and the cooperative tilting increases, reducing the Co–O–Ir bond angle from near 180° toward smaller values. Complementary EXAFS/PDF analyses reveal increasing antisite disorder between Co and Ir with Ca content, concomitant with a modest redistribution of local valence states as inferred from XANES. Magnetization measurements show that the x = 0 compound orders magnetically at low temperature in a predominantly antiferromagnetic fashion, while Ca-doped samples exhibit reduced long-range order and enhanced magnetic irreversibility, evolving toward a spin-glass–like ground state at higher x. XMCD at the Co L2,3 and Ir L2,3 edges reveals antiparallel alignment of Co and Ir moments, with Ir contributing a SOC-driven orbital moment; the net moment decreases with Ca content, consistent with increased disorder and noncollinear spin textures. First-principles calculations incorporating SOC and Hubbard U reproduce the observed trend: the effective Co–Ir exchange weakens with structural distortion and antisite defects, and the presence of disorder introduces competing exchange pathways that stabilize noncollinear spin arrangements and slow spin dynamics. Together, the results demonstrate that 3d–5d exchange in La2−xCaxCoIrO6 is exquisitely sensitive to structural and magnetic disorder, offering a tunable route to tailor anisotropic magnetism and frustration in 3d–5d double perovskites. This tunability establishes a route to engineered emergent magnetism.

title: Diversifying Knowledge Enhancement of Biomedical Language Models using Adapter Modules and Knowledge Graphs
text_ai: Recent advances in natural language processing (NLP) owe their success to pre-training language models on large amounts of unstructured data. Still, there is an increasing effort to combine the unstructured nature of LMs with structured knowledge and reasoning. By integrating adapters with a knowledge-graph encoder, we propose a parameter-efficient mechanism to diversify the model’s knowledge beyond its pretraining corpus. The adapters capture entity-centric and relation-centric cues, while a graph encoder over a fused KG (e.g., UMLS, GO, and drug-disease relations) provides structured priors. A cross-modality fusion layer merges transformer representations with graph embeddings through joint attention and gating, enabling consultation of structured facts without full re-training. Training objective combines masked language modeling with KG-consistency losses, link prediction on curated biomedical triples, and task-specific heads for named entity recognition, relation extraction, and biomedical question answering. We evaluate on standard benchmarks including BioNER, CHEMPROT, and BioASQ-style QA, plus zero-shot generalization to novel terms. Results show improved factual accuracy and disambiguation of polysemous biomedical terms, with robust transfer to unseen entities and drug–disease interactions, while reducing parameter growth relative to full fine-tuning. This work demonstrates that coupling adapters with knowledge graphs offers a scalable path to diversify biomedical LM capabilities across domains.

title: Efficient Computation in Adaptive Artificial Spiking Neural Networks
text_ai: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) are bio-inspired models of neural computation that have proven highly effective. Still, ANNs lack a natural notion of time, and neural units in ANNs exchange analog values in a frame-based manner, a computationally and energetically inefficient form of communication. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) offer a natural temporal dimension and asynchronous information exchange, yielding substantial energy advantages on neuromorphic hardware; however, naïve deployments suffer from brittle performance and inefficient temporal coding. We introduce Adaptive Artificial Spiking Neural Networks (A-ASNNs) that fuse temporally aware coding with local, biologically inspired adaptation mechanisms to enable accurate, energy-efficient computation under variable workloads. The core contribution is a family of adaptive leaky integrate-and-fire neurons whose firing thresholds, membrane time constants, and leak conductances adjust online to input statistics, thereby promoting rapid, content-dependent responses while suppressing spurious activity during quiescent periods. This adaptivity is augmented by a hierarchical temporal coding strategy that combines time-to-first-spike cues with multi-spike representations, providing robust performance across time-varying inputs and enabling graceful trade-offs between latency and accuracy. We develop an end-to-end pipeline that integrates (i) an event-based front end for converting diverse sensory streams into sparse spike trains, (ii) a trainable neuron-and-synapse model with local, homeostatic plasticity and STDP-like updates that are surrogate-gradient friendly, and (iii) a latency-aware readout mechanism that preserves decision quality with minimal spike expenditure. The learning algorithm operates with lightweight local signals, encouraging stable convergence and resilience to distributional shifts. We ground our framework with theoretical analysis of energy complexity and sparsity, showing that energy scales with spiking activity rather than frame throughput and that adaptive thresholds reduce average spike counts by substantial margins without sacrificing accuracy. Empirical evaluation in software and on hardware-oriented backends demonstrates state-of-the-art energy-accuracy trade-offs on benchmark tasks ranging from static digit recognition to dynamic event streams, with orders-of-magnitude reductions in energy per inference and competitive, scalable latency. The work establishes a practical pathway toward efficient adaptive computation in spiking-inspired architectures.

title: Generative Text-Guided 3D Vision-Language Pretraining for Unified Medical Image Segmentation
text_ai: Vision-Language Pretraining (VLP) has demonstrated remarkable capabilities in learning visual representations from textual descriptions of images without annotations. Yet, effective VLP demands large-scale image-text pairs, a resource that suffers scarcity in the medical domain. Moreover, conventional VLP is limited to 2D images while medical images encompass diverse modalities, often in 3D, making the learning process more challenging. To address these constraints, we propose a Generative Text-Guided 3D Vision-Language Pretraining framework that jointly learns cross-modal representations and a unified segmentation decoder from both real and synthetically generated data. A 3D ViT-based visual encoder ingests volumetric scans across modalities, while a text encoder encodes clinical descriptions and organ/lesion vocabularies. We introduce a text-conditioned diffusion prior that synthesizes plausible 3D patches and captions from lightweight prompts, enabling expansive pseudo-paired data without manual annotation. Training integrates: (i) a text-to-volume generation objective to align visual and textual modalities, (ii) a cross-modal contrastive loss to strengthen partner alignment, and (iii) a 3D segmentation head trained with multi-task losses that unify organ segmentation across modalities. We show that the model attains superior performance in unified 3D segmentation, with robust zero-shot transfer to unseen modalities and organs, and data-efficient fine-tuning on limited labeled sets. This design yields strong clinical practicality.

title: Bone remodeling of the proximal tibia after uncemented total knee arthroplasty: secondary endpoints analyzed from a randomized trial comparing monoblock and modular tibia traysâ??2 year follow-up of 53 cases
text_ai: Background and purpose â?? Bone remodeling as a response to bone trauma, postoperative immobilization, and device-related bone reactions can lead to loss of bone stock and increase the risk of periprosthetic fracture and aseptic loosening. This study investigates the adaptive bone remodeling of the proximal tibia after uncemented total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Methods – Fifty-three patients were randomized to receive a monoblock (n=26) or modular (n=27) uncemented tibial tray during primary TKA for end-stage OA. All components used press-fit fixation with identical peripheral coating. Patients were followed 24 months. Proximal tibial bone remodeling was quantified with DEXA in four predefined periprosthetic regions around the tray (medial, lateral, anterior, posterior) and expressed as percent change from baseline. Standardized AP and lateral radiographs were obtained at 3, 12, and 24 months for radiolucent lines and osteolysis. Knee function was assessed with the Knee Society Score. Results – Baseline characteristics were similar. Overall, proximal tibial BMD declined in the early period, greatest medially (mean −6% at 3 months), with partial recovery by 24 months (−2%). Lateral, anterior, and posterior regions showed similar trajectories (−4%, −3%, −4% at 3 months; −1%, −2%, −1% at 24 months). There were no significant time-by-design interactions in any region (p>0.2). At 24 months, intergroup differences in regional BMD were not significant (p>0.3). Radiographs showed non-progressive radiolucent lines in a minority of cases, with no progressive osteolysis or aseptic loosening; no revisions occurred. Remodeling patterns were robust to adjustment for sex, BMI, and preoperative BMD. Conclusion – Uncemented monoblock and modular tibial trays evoke similar, regionally patterned proximal tibial remodeling over 2 years, with modest bone loss that largely redeems. The observed remodeling does not differ by tray design in the short term, indicating comparable bone stock outcomes.

title: Quantum entanglement between an atom and a molecule
text_ai: Conventional information processors freely convert information between different physical carriers to process, store, or transmit information. It seems plausible that quantum information will also be held by different physical carriers in applications such as tests of fundamental physics, quantum-enhanced sensors, and quantum information processing. Here we demonstrate entanglement between a single trapped atom and a single trapped molecule in distinct optical tweezers. The qubits reside in the atom’s hyperfine ground states and in the molecule’s rovibrational ground state. A Raman-assisted gate entangles the two via a spin-dependent optical interaction, yielding a Bell-like state after two local rotations. Entanglement is certified by full two-qubit state tomography and by a CHSH-type Bell test, giving a fidelity to the Bell state of 0.84(4) and a CHSH parameter S = 2.28(12). The coherence of the atom–molecule superposition persists for tens of milliseconds at microkelvin temperatures, with residual decoherence dominated by differential light shifts and motional heating. The demonstrated interface provides a universal platform for storing and processing quantum information across heterogeneous carriers, enabling hybrid quantum networks, quantum simulations of molecular dynamics, and tests of entanglement between matter constituents with distinct internal structure. These results mark a critical step toward scalable hybrids of atoms and molecules for quantum information processing.

title: Spot evolution on LQ Hya during 2006--2017: temperature maps based on SOFIN and FIES data
text_ai: Context. LQ Hya is one of the most frequently studied young solar analogue stars. Recently, it has been observed to show intriguing behaviour by analysing long-term photometry: during 2003--2009, a coherent spot structure migrating in the rotational frame has been reported by various authors, but since that time the star has entered a chaotic state where coherent structures seem to have disappeared and rapid phase jumps of the photometric minima occur irregularly over time. Here we present a time-resolved set of surface temperature maps reconstructed from high-resolution spectra obtained with the SOFIN and FIES spectrographs, spanning 2006–2017, via Doppler imaging with maximum-entropy regularization. The maps indicate photospheric parameters of T_eff ≈ 5200–5300 K and reveal cool spots typically 500–1000 K below the surrounding photosphere. The spot pattern is dominated by persistent, high-latitude structures (50–85 deg) that survive across several seasons, forming quasi-polar caps, while low-latitude features (10–40 deg) appear episodically and are short lived. In many seasons the topology is rapidly rearranged by the growth and decay of a few localized spots, yielding pronounced phase jumps of the dominant minima that are not tied to a single migrating longitude. Quantitatively, the mean spot filling factor and temperature contrast display strong interannual variability, with active episodes recurring roughly every 2–3 years within the 2006–2017 window. Cross-season comparisons show that apparent azimuthal drift is irregular rather than steady, and no persistent migration band is recovered. The inferred surface differential rotation is weak and carries large uncertainties, compatible with solar-like shear but with latitude dependence dominated by the high-latitude concentration of spots. Overall, the results reinforce the view of LQ Hya as a highly active, chaotic dynamo state, in which magnetic flux preferentially concentrates at high latitudes, and long-lived coherent spot structures are rare in 2006–2017.

title: Scaling Universality at the Dynamic Vortex Mott Transition
text_ai: The dynamic Mott insulator-to-metal transition (DMT) is key to many intriguing phenomena in condensed matter physics yet it remains nearly unexplored. The cleanest way to observe DMT, without the interference from disorder and other effects inherent to electronic and atomic systems, is to employ the vortex Mott states formed by superconducting vortices in a regular array of pinning sites. Using a regular array of pinning sites, we drive a commensurate vortex Mott state across the dynamic transition by increasing the applied current. The transition from a pinned insulating regime to a flowing metallic regime is identified by a sharp change in differential resistance and a marked change in vortex mobility. Across several lattice spacings and temperatures, we perform finite-size scaling of the I–V responses and time-resolved vortex velocity after quenches, obtaining a collapse with a single set of exponents z and ν. The scaling functions depend only on the scaled control parameters (I−Ic)L^{1/ν} and T L^{z}, demonstrating universality that is insensitive to microscopic details such as lattice spacing or pinning strength. The extracted exponents and scaling form place the dynamic vortex Mott transition in a non-equilibrium universality class that mirrors but is distinct from equilibrium Mott criticality. This provides a clean realization of scaling universality at a dynamic Mott transition.

title: H-atom bombardment of CO2, HCOOH and CH3CHO containing ices
text_ai: Context: Hydrogenation reactions are expected to be among the most important surface reactions on interstellar ices. However, solid state astrochemical laboratory data on reactions of H-atoms with common interstellar ice constituents are largely lacking. Here, we report systematic hydrogenation experiments on amorphous solid water (ASW) ices containing CO2, HCOOH, and CH3CHO prepared at 8–12 K, using a high-flux atomic hydrogen source. Ices were co-deposited with a modest water fraction to mimic the icy mantles of dense clouds and exposed to H atoms at fluxes in the 10^12–10^14 cm^-2 s^-1 range. In situ Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy monitored the temporal evolution of reactants and products, while post-irradiation temperature-programmed desorption and quadrupole mass spectrometry identified volatile species released during warming. The measurements allowed quantitative tracking of H-atom addition events and the identification of transient intermediates such as HOCO for CO2 and CH3CH2O for CH3CHO. For CO2-containing ices, hydrogenation proceeds efficiently to formic acid (HCOOH) via the HOCO intermediate; the spectral signatures of HOCO appear early and decay as HCOOH grows, indicating rapid progression along the hydrogenation ladder. No significant production of CO or methanol is detected under the same conditions, implying that at 8–12 K the dominant channel is sequential H-atom addition to CO2 leading to HCOOH. In HCOOH-rich ices, H-atom exposure gradually dehydrates to CO and H2O, with concurrent modest back-reaction forming CO2; these results point to competing pathways that control ice composition during cold processing. In CH3CHO-containing ices, H atoms preferentially add to the carbonyl carbon, enabling the formation of ethanol (CH3CH2OH) as a major product, complemented by minor yields of CH4 and CO via fragmentation routes. The ethanol formation is enhanced in H2O-rich matrices and persists across the 8–12 K range, indicating robust low-temperature hydrogenation. Together, these results supply the first direct quantification of H-atom–induced hydrogenation routes for CO2, HCOOH and CH3CHO in interstellar ice analogs, with clear implications for the molecular inventories of dense cores and the early stages of prebiotic chemistry.

title: Strategic Defense against Stealthy Link Flooding Attacks: A Signaling Game Approach
text_ai: With the increasing diversity of Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks, it is becoming extremely challenging to design a fully protected network. For instance, Stealthy Link Flooding Attack (SLFA) is a variant of DDoS attacks that strives to block access to a target area by flooding a small set of links, and it is shown that it can bypass traditional DDoS defense mechanisms. To address this, we model SLFA as a two-player signaling game under incomplete information. The attacker (sender) adopts one of two types—low capability or high capability—whose private information about sustained flood strength and stealth potential is hidden from the defender (receiver). The defender observes a sequence of link-level signals (burstiness, timing, and partial congestion indicators) and forms posterior beliefs about the attacker’s type. The attacker chooses a target set of links and a flood intensity, balancing reach against detectability, while the defender selects a portfolio of actions—traffic shaping, rate limiting, selective scrubbing, and deliberate routing adjustments—subject to budget and performance constraints. Payoffs encode (i) the defender’s objective to minimize time-to-detect, erroneous misclassification, and residual damage, and (ii) the attacker’s objective to maximize successful reach while incurring minimal signaling costs. We establish equilibrium concepts in the Bayesian Nash framework and characterize the conditions under which robust defense policies emerge. In equilibrium, signaling costs seen by the attacker discourage overt flooding for the low-type, while the high-type may mimic benign traffic only when defender policies are uncertain. The defender’s optimal strategy blends posterior-thresholding on congestion indicators with adaptive routing and selective rate limits, creating a deterrent informing the attacker’s incentive to reveal or conceal intent. We propose a practical defense policy that implements posterior-guided traffic engineering with lightweight scrubbing and dynamic link weighting, designed to be scalable and implementable on commodity infrastructure. Empirical evaluation on synthetic and realistic topologies demonstrates that the signaling-game defense reduces SLFA success probability and detection latency relative to rule-based baselines, with manageable overhead and resilience to observation noise. Extensions to multi-target and collusive scenarios are discussed, along with real-time estimation considerations and deployment challenges.

title: Funnel control -- a survey
text_ai: The methodology of funnel control was introduced in the early 2000s, and it has developed since then in many respects achieving a level of mathematical maturity balanced by practical applications. Its fundamental tenet is the attainment of prescribed transient and asymptotic behaviour for continuous-time controlled dynamical processes encompassing linear and nonlinear systems described by functional differential equations, differential-algebraic systems, and partial differential equations. At the heart of funnel control lies the performance funnel defined by a scalar, strictly positive reference function φ(t). The tracking error e(t) = y(t) − yref(t) is required to satisfy |e(t)| < 1/φ(t) for all t ≥ 0, with the boundary shape φ prescribing the desired transient and steady-state envelope. The funnel controller employs a nonlinear, time-varying gain that intensifies as the error approaches the funnel boundary, thereby providing automatic, state-independent correction without recourse to exact matching of the internal dynamics. Under mild regularity assumptions on the system’s drift and input maps and a non-vanishing input influence, the closed-loop problem is well posed and forward invariant with respect to the funnel, guaranteeing global existence of solutions and the realization of the stipulated performance, robust to structured disturbances and certain modeling errors. Over the past two decades, the funnel paradigm has been extended far beyond its initial finite-dimensional setting to encompass linear and nonlinear systems, delay equations, differential-algebraic equations, and a broad class of boundary- and pointwise-controlled partial differential equations. Methodological advances include adaptive shaping of φ, handling of actuator saturations and input constraints, observer-based implementations under partial state information, and discretized or sampled-data realizations for digital control platforms. The survey consolidates the principal existence, stability, and robustness results, synthesizes design principles across diverse model classes, and surveys experimental validations across mechanical, electrical, and process-control applications. It also situates funnel control within a broader ecosystem of related approaches, highlighting connections to barrier-function methods, reference-governor strategies, and high-gain paradigms, while clarifying computational and discretization considerations. Open challenges and directions include extending funnel control to broader distributed-parameter frameworks, reducing conservatism in assumptions on the input channels, and integrating learning-based uncertainty quantification to enhance adaptive performance without compromising guarantees.

title: Gravitational waves constraints on post-inflationary phases stiffer than radiation
text_ai: We point out that the existence of post-inflationary phases stiffer than radiation leads to the production of stochastic gravitational waves (GW) backgrounds whose logarithmic energy spectra (in critical units) are typically "blue" at high frequencies. We show that the spectral energy density today, Ω_GW(f) h^2, inherits a blue tilt during the stiff phase and develops a turnover at a characteristic frequency f_rh set by the end of stiff evolution. The amplitude is controlled by the fractional energy in the stiff component and by the duration of the phase, so even modest periods can yield a detectable high-frequency relic if f_rh lies inside the observational window. By combining the BBN/CMB bound on the total GW energy with the transfer-function physics, we derive robust constraints in the (w, N_stiff, T_rh) parameter space, indicating that for w ≳ 0.5 the allowed duration is limited unless the reheating scale lies well above the GeV scale. We illustrate the impact on representative models, such as kination (w=1) and more general scalar-field phases, and quantify the sensitivity reach of current and upcoming detectors (LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA, LISA, ET, DECIGO). Our results show that gravitational-wave observations provide a complementary probe of the post-inflationary thermal history beyond standard reheating.

title: H-Alpha and Hard X-Ray Observations of a Two-Ribbon Flare Associated with a Filament Eruption
text_ai: We perform a multi-wavelength study of a two-ribbon flare on 2002 September 29 and its associated filament eruption, observed simultaneously in the H-alpha line by a ground-based imaging spectrograph and in hard X-rays by RHESSI. The flare ribbons contain several H-alpha bright kernels that show different evolutional behaviors. Hard X-ray emission is localized at two persistent footpoints whose centroids coincide with the brightest H-alpha kernels within ~1–2 arcsec uncertainties. The footpoints separate as the ribbons widen, tracing the progressive reconnection of larger coronal loops. Spectral fitting with a thick-target model yields a nonthermal electron population with a photon spectral index Γ ≈ 3–5, and energy deposition that peaks near the most intense H-alpha kernel brightenings. The H-alpha line center and wing measurements reveal small but systematic Doppler shifts in several kernels during the impulsive phase, indicating localized chromospheric responses to precipitating electrons. The filament eruption initiates near the early impulsive stage and rises concurrently with the rapid ribbon expansion and the hard X-ray peak, underscoring a tight temporal coupling between coronal reconnection and the destabilization of the underlying filament. The observed sequence is consistent with the standard two-ribbon flare scenario (CSHKP) in which energy release in the corona drives nonthermal particle precipitation and chromospheric heating at the ribbons, while the filament eruption reflects the concomitant restructuring of the overlying magnetic field.

title: Clinical Significance of Cytotoxic Lesions of the Corpus Callosum in Subarachnoid Hemorrhage Patients: A Retrospective Analysis.
text_ai: Cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum are secondary lesions induced by significant increases in cytokine levels in the brain and are associated with subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). However, their clinical significance in SAH patients remains unclear. Methods: In this single-center, retrospective study, we reviewed consecutive SAH admissions from January 2012 through December 2023. Inclusion criteria were radiologically confirmed SAH and availability of brain MRI within 21 days of ictus. CLOCCs were defined as cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum identified on diffusion-weighted imaging with corresponding low apparent diffusion coefficient values. Data collected included demographics, presenting Hunt-Hess and WFNS grade, radiologic features (aneurysmal vs nonaneurysmal SAH, IVH), treatment modality (clip vs coil), complications (delayed cerebral ischemia, seizures, hydrocephalus), and inflammatory markers (CRP, fever). Functional outcome was assessed at 3 months using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS). Statistical analyses compared patients with and without CLOCCs; logistic regression adjusted for age, SAH severity, and treatment modality. Results: Among 125 patients meeting criteria, CLOCCs were detected in 14 (11.2%). Lesions localized predominantly to the body of the corpus callosum (n=9), with smaller involvement of the genu (n=3) and splenium (n=2). All demonstrated diffusion restriction with corresponding T2 hyperintensity and without hemorrhagic transformation. The CLOCCs cohort had higher admission WFNS scores (median 4 vs 3, P=0.04) and greater early inflammatory activity (fever within 72 hours: 9/14 vs 34/111, P=0.02; CRP elevation: 11/14 vs 60/111, P=0.03). Delayed cerebral ischemia occurred in 5/14 (36%) of CLOCCs patients compared with 12/111 (11%) of those without CLOCCs (P=0.04). ICU length of stay was longer in CLOCCs patients (median 12 vs 7 days, P=0.03). At 3 months, unfavorable outcome (mRS 3–6) occurred in 6/14 (43%) of CLOCCs versus 28/111 (25%) of non-CLOCCs; after adjustment for age, SAH severity, and treatment modality, CLOCCs were not independently associated with poor outcome (adjusted OR 1.9, 95% CI 0.7–5.3). Follow-up imaging in survivors showed partial resolution or complete resolution of corpus callosum lesions in most cases within 4–12 weeks. Conclusions: In SAH patients, cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum appear associated with a heightened inflammatory response and more severe initial presentation and resource utilization, but do not independently predict unfavorable prognosis after accounting for baseline severity. Recognition of CLOCCs may inform monitoring and inflammatory management, and prospective studies are warranted to validate these findings and clarify pathophysiology.

title: Is the faint young Sun problem for Earth solved?
text_ai: Stellar evolution models predict that the solar luminosity was lower in the past, typically 20-25 % lower during the Archean (3.8-2.5 Ga). Despite the fainter Sun, there is strong evidence for the presence of liquid water on Earth's surface at that time. Here we reassess the FYSP in light of updated solar tracks and a comprehensive synthesis of atmospheric and geochemical constraints. We employ a hierarchy of climate models, from 1D radiative–convective schemes to 3D GCMs, coupled to photochemical modules tracking CO2, CH4, and haze under Archean solar input. Boundary conditions are constrained by proxies (paleosols, carbonate deposit records, isotopic data) and by estimates of crustal weathering and biological productivity. Our results show CO2 partial pressures of 0.1–0.3 bar, with methane tens to a few hundred ppm, can sustain surface temperatures above freezing for a Sun ~20–25% fainter, given plausible cloud feedbacks and reduced albedo. In alternative scenarios, modest H2 admixtures or transient methane hazes can reduce the required CO2, but yield distinct spectral fingerprints. Overall, no single mechanism is necessary or sufficient; a convergent set of greenhouse warming and feedbacks can reconcile warm Archean climates with a faint Sun, though constraints remain model dependent and geochemically uncertain.
