title: A Latent Variable Approach for Non-Hierarchical Multi-Fidelity Adaptive Sampling
text_ai: Multi-fidelity (MF) methods are gaining popularity for enhancing surrogate modeling and design optimization by incorporating data from various low-fidelity (LF) models. While most existing MF methods assume a fixed dataset, adaptive sampling methods that dynamically allocate resources among fidelity models can achieve higher efficiency in the exploring and exploiting the design space. To address non-hierarchical relations among fidelities, we propose a latent-variable non-hierarchical MFGP (LN-MFGP). A latent code z_f for each fidelity level locates it in a shared latent space, while the mapping from inputs to outputs is governed by a Gaussian process over the augmented input (x, z). The model accommodates arbitrary fidelity interactions by allowing z_f to reflect similarity and complementarity among datasets rather than a fixed hierarchy of accuracies. A Bayesian treatment of latent codes induces soft coupling that facilitates information transfer where warranted and guards against negative transfer when fidelities disagree. Posterior inference uses variational methods with inducing points, yielding scalable updates and closed-form predictive moments after integrating over z. Predictive distributions enable a fidelity-aware acquisition function that selects both x and f. We derive a max-expected-improvement criterion under the latent posterior, and show how a cost-aware budgeted variant reduces to familiar EI when costs are uniform. In practice, we also introduce a simpler variance-reduction surrogate that promotes exploration in poorly modeled regions by trading off cross-fidelity concordance with local uncertainty. Empirical results on synthetic problems with non-hierarchical fidelities and on real-world engineering surrogates (e.g., CFD/FEA) demonstrate superior data efficiency and robust performance against standard co-kriging and single-fidelity surrogates. Ablation studies quantify gains from latent coupling, variational inference, and fidelity-aware acquisition. The LN-MFGP offers a principled, scalable framework for adaptive sampling in non-hierarchical MF settings.

While most existing MF methods assume a fixed dataset, adaptive sampling methods that dynamically allocate resources among fidelity models can achieve higher efficiency in the exploring and exploiting the design space.

title: Genetic engineering and characterisation of chlorotoxin-fused gelonin for enhanced glioblastoma therapy.
text_ai: Despite substantial advances in its treatment, brain cancer remains a life-threatening disease with a poor survival rate. The main challenges for the conventional chemotherapy include an insufficient efficacy of drugs and toxicity caused by their nonselective mode of action. Here, we report the design and molecular characterisation of a chlorotoxin (CTX)–gelonin (Gel) fusion protein engineered to improve selectivity and potency against glioblastoma. A synthetic gene encoding CTX joined to gelonin through a flexible (G4S)2 linker was cloned into a bacterial expression vector and produced as a soluble fusion in an oxidising cytoplasm. The product was purified by affinity and size-exclusion chromatography and structurally validated by SDS‑PAGE, HPLC, and circular dichroism. Binding assays confirmed high-affinity interactions with glioma-associated targets, and ribosome-inactivating activity was retained after fusion. In vitro potency was assessed across glioblastoma lines (U87MG, LN-229, etc.) and normal astrocytes, revealing nanomolar-range cytotoxicity against tumor cells with selective sparing of nontransformed cells. Mechanistic studies indicated receptor-mediated uptake and endosomal escape releasing Gel into the cytosol, where it inhibited protein synthesis. In an orthotopic xenograft model, systemic administration of CTX–Gel significantly reduced tumor burden and extended survival compared with Gel alone or vehicle, with no major off‑target toxicity observed.
prefix: Despite substantial advances in its treatment, brain cancer remains a life-threatening disease with a poor survival rate. The main challenges for the conventional chemotherapy include an insufficient efficacy of drugs and toxicity caused by their nonselective mode of action.

title: VasTSD: Learning 3D Vascular Tree-state Space Diffusion Model for Angiography Synthesis
text_ai: Angiography imaging is a medical imaging technique that enhances the visibility of blood vessels within the body by using contrast agents. Angiographic images can effectively assist in the diagnosis of vascular diseases. However, contrast agents may bring extra radiation exposure which is harmful to patients with health risks. VasTSD learns a 3D vascular tree-state diffusion model that encodes anatomical priors of branching topology while capturing modality-specific appearance. The approach formulates a diffusion process over a discretized vascular tree graph, where each node carries diameter, lumen intensity, and confidence, and edges enforce physiologic bifurcations. A graph-conditioned score network, implemented with a geometry-aware 3D U-Net and graph attention, estimates the clean vascular state from noisy intermediate samples. The model is trained to synthesize high-fidelity angiographic volumes from low-dose or non-contrast inputs by conditional denoising and a topology-consistency loss that promotes connected, physiologically plausible vessels. At inference, reverse diffusion yields 3D vascular reconstructions with coherent branching and realistic lumen contrast, suitable for angiography synthesis. We validate VasTSD on multi-institutional datasets and demonstrate improved topology preservation, lumen accuracy, and visual fidelity over voxel-based diffusion and GAN baselines. The method enables contrast-agent–reduced or contrast-free angiography while maintaining diagnostic realism; future work will address real-time acceleration and unsupervised topology priors.
prefix: Angiography imaging is a medical imaging technique that enhances the visibility of blood vessels within the body by using contrast agents. Angiographic images can effectively assist in the diagnosis of vascular diseases. However, contrast agents may bring extra radiation exposure which is harmful to patients with health risks.

title: Sedative and cardiorespiratory effects of low doses of xylazine with and without acepromazine in Nordestino donkeys.
text_ai: Information on appropriate protocols for sedation of Nordestino donkeys is scarce. To evaluate the sedative and cardiorespiratory effects of low doses of intravenous (i.v.) xylazine with and without acepromazine in 'Nordestino' donkeys. Seven healthy female Nordestino donkeys (150 ± 18 kg) were included in this blinded, randomised, crossover experiment. Treatments were administered in randomised order with a 14-day washout between sessions. Xylazine 0.25 mg kg−1 i.v. (X) was given alone or co-administered with acepromazine 0.05 mg kg−1 i.v. (X+A). An observer blinded to treatment allocation conducted sedation scoring at 5-minute intervals for 60 minutes and during recovery. Sedation was quantified on a 4-point scale (0 = awake, 1 = mild sedation, 2 = moderate, 3 = profound) and ataxia (0–3). Cardiorespiratory data were collected continuously: heart rate (HR), noninvasive arterial pressure (MAP), respiratory rate (RR), pulse oximetry (SpO2), and end-tidal CO2 (EtCO2); rectal temperature was recorded at baseline and at the end of monitoring. Data were analyzed by paired comparisons within animals. Both regimens produced rapid sedation (onset 6–8 minutes). X+A yielded deeper sedation (mean ± SD score 2.8 ± 0.3) than X alone (1.6 ± 0.4; P < 0.01). HR declined in both groups, with greater reduction after X+A (X: 42 ± 6 bpm; X+A: 35 ± 5 bpm; P < 0.05). MAP decreased from baseline (77 ± 7 mmHg) to 62 ± 6 mmHg (X) and 56 ± 5 mmHg (X+A; P < 0.05 for X+A). RR fell to 12 ± 3 and 9 ± 2 breaths min−1, respectively (P < 0.05). SpO2 remained ≥94% throughout in all donkeys; EtCO2 rose modestly to 44 ± 5 mmHg (X) and 46 ± 6 mmHg (X+A; P < 0.05 for X+A). Time to return to progressive ambulation (standing and gait) was shorter after X (16–22 minutes) than after X+A (28–40 minutes). Conclusions: In Nordestino donkeys, adding acepromazine to low-dose xylazine increases depth of sedation and elicits more pronounced cardio-respiratory depression, with longer recovery. X alone may be preferable when rapid recovery or minimal cardiovascular impact is desired; X+A may be reserved for cases requiring deeper sedation under tight monitoring.

To evaluate the sedative and cardiorespiratory effects of low doses of intravenous (i.v.) xylazine with and without acepromazine in 'Nordestino' donkeys. Seven healthy female Nordestino donkeys (150 ± 18 kg) were included in this blinded, randomised, crossover experiment.

title: Building a Bridge Between NMDAR-Mediated Excitotoxicity and Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Chronic and Acute Diseases.
text_ai: Glutamate is the major excitatory neurotransmitter in the brain, and it is widely accepted to play a role in synaptic plasticity and excitotoxic cell death. Glutamate binds to several receptors, including ionotropic N-methyl-D-Aspartate receptor (NMDAR), which is essential in synaptic plasticity and excitotoxicity. Here, we integrate mechanistic evidence that links NMDAR-driven Ca2+ flux with mitochondrial bioenergetics and redox homeostasis, emphasizing bidirectional amplification between excitotoxicity and mitochondrial dysfunction. Excessive Ca2+ buffering by mitochondria precipitates Δψm collapse, reactive oxygen species (ROS) overproduction, and impaired oxidative phosphorylation, which in turn sensitizes neurons to further NMDAR-driven injury via energy failure and disturbed calcium sequestration. We highlight divergent signaling at synaptic versus extrasynaptic NMDARs, wherein pro-survival and pro-death pathways differentially couple to mitochondrial dynamics, including fission–fusion remodeling, mitophagy, and mtDNA integrity. Shared downstream hubs—calcineurin, calpains, JNK, and the mitochondrial permeability transition pore—recur across chronic and acute disease settings, from Alzheimer’s disease to ischemic stroke and traumatic brain injury. By integrating electrophysiology, imaging, and in vivo models, we propose a unifying framework in which mitochondrial dysfunction magnifies excitotoxic vulnerability and NMDAR signaling reshapes mitochondrial quality control. Therapeutic implications include dual-modality strategies that protect mitochondria while modulating discrete NMDAR subsystems to preserve cellular energy and viability.
prefix: Glutamate is the major excitatory neurotransmitter in the brain, and it is widely accepted to play a role in synaptic plasticity and excitotoxic cell death. Glutamate binds to several receptors, including ionotropic N-methyl-D-Aspartate receptor (NMDAR), which is essential in synaptic plasticity and excitotoxicity.

title: Optimal strategies for throwing accurately
text_ai: Accuracy of throwing in games and sports is governed by how errors at projectile release are propagated by flight dynamics. To address the question of what governs the choice of throwing strategy, we use a simple model of throwing with an arm modelled as a hinged bar of fixed length that can release a projectile at any angle and angular velocity. To this end, we compute the instantaneous velocity of the released projectile from hinge-arm kinematics and propagate release errors through ballistic flight to the impact on a target plane. Under small perturbations (δθ, δω), the impact error δr ≈ J δu, where J is the 2×2 sensitivity matrix from the partial derivatives of landing position with respect to θ and ω. We minimize the expected squared landing error E[||δr||^2] subject to a fixed release-work budget, using Lagrange multipliers. Analysis yields two regimes. For short-range targets, the optimal strategy emphasizes high ω to ensure geometry, with θ at extremum of ||J||. For long-range targets, the optimum shifts toward smaller ω, with θ near optimum release angle, reducing amplification of ω-uncertainty. Across budgets, the objective is minimizing error propagation rather than maximizing speed, yielding strategies observed in skilled throwers.

To address the question of what governs the choice of throwing strategy, we use a simple model of throwing with an arm modelled as a hinged bar of fixed length that can release a projectile at any angle and angular velocity.

title: Loss Minimization for Electrical Flows over Spanning Trees on Grids
text_ai: We study the electrical distribution network reconfiguration problem, defined as follows. We are given an undirected graph with a root vertex, demand at each non-root vertex, and resistance on each edge. Then, we want to find a spanning tree of the graph that specifies the routing of power from the root to each vertex so that all the demands are satisfied and the energy loss is minimized. We formulate the problem as: among all rooted spanning trees T of G, minimize L(T)= sum_{e in T} R_e (D_e)^2, where D_e is the total demand in the component of T separated from the root by e. We prove that the problem is NP-hard in general, even on planar grids with nonnegative demands. We then present two complementary algorithms tailored to grids. (i) A dynamic-programming scheme for grids of fixed height, running in time O(n 2^H) that exploits the hierarchical decomposition along rows. (ii) A convex-relaxation based method: replace the integer tree constraint by a spanning-tree polytope with quadratic costs and solve via SDP/second-order cone programming; a rounding procedure yields feasible trees with provable approximation guarantees in practice. We report experiments on synthetic and benchmark grid instances showing significant reductions in energy loss relative to natural baselines and favorable scaling.
prefix: We study the electrical distribution network reconfiguration problem, defined as follows. We are given an undirected graph with a root vertex, demand at each non-root vertex, and resistance on each edge. title: Point-MoE: Towards Cross-Domain Generalization in 3D Semantic Segmentation via Mixture-of-Experts
text_ai: While scaling laws have transformed natural language processing and computer vision, 3D point cloud understanding has yet to reach that stage. This can be attributed to both the comparatively smaller scale of 3D datasets, as well as the disparate sources of the data itself. To address this, we introduce Point-MoE, a scalable mixture-of-experts architecture that partitions feature processing across a small set of specialized 3D experts while preserving a shared universal core. A learnable router dynamically assigns per-point or per-token computations to Expert sub-networks conditioned on domain cues and local geometry, enabling both domain-specific specialization and cross-domain knowledge transfer. The gating network is trained with a combination of classification, alignment, and diversity losses, encouraging experts to cover complementary modalities yet remain coherent under distribution shifts. We integrate Point-MoE into a standard 3D semantic segmentation backbone and demonstrate plug‑in compatibility with voxel-, graph-, and transformer-based backbones. We evaluate on diverse domain pairs including synthetic-to-real and multi-sensor scans, reporting consistent improvements in mean IoU, especially for rare or unseen classes, with modest parameter overhead. Ablation studies reveal the gains stem from explicit domain routing, cross-domain regularization, and expert diversity. Our results establish a foundational step toward scalable cross-domain generalization in 3D understanding.

title: Comparison of space weathering spectral changes induced by solar wind and micrometeoroid impacts using ion- and femtosecond-laser-irradiated olivine and pyroxene
text_ai: Space weathering is a process that changes the surface of airless planetary bodies. Prime space weathering agents are solar wind irradiation and micrometeoroid bombardment. These processes alter planetary reflectance spectra and often modify their compositional diagnostic features. Here, we subject these minerals to two controlled laboratory proxies of space weathering: ion irradiation to mimic solar wind implantation and femtosecond-laser pulses that reproduce rapid melting, vaporization, and rim formation associated with micrometeoroid impacts. Reflectance spectra were acquired for pristine and treated samples from 0.35 to 2.5 μm, while microstructural changes were probed with TEM and EDS to quantify nanophase Fe distribution and the development of amorphous, glassy rims. Ion irradiation yields a gradual darkening and a modest, progressively red-sloped continuum in both olivine and pyroxene, with systematic attenuation of the 1 μm and 2 μm diagnostic absorption features. The spectral evolution is consistent with the in situ formation and growth of nanophase Fe0 particles embedded within altered rims, as corroborated by TEM, which reveals Fe-rich clusters dispersed in amorphous matrices, and by EDS confirming increased Fe/Si ratios in the weathered skins. This pathway reproduces the classical space-weathering signature observed on S-complex bodies, albeit with mineral- and dose-dependent efficiency. Femtosecond-laser irradiation induces more abrupt changes, including localized melting, crater saturation, and the formation of highly iron-enriched, optically thick rims. The resulting spectra show stronger reddening and a more pronounced suppression of both the 1 μm and 2 μm bands, accompanied by a broadening of the continuum that cannot be accounted for by npFe0 alone. In pyroxene, laser treatment more severely depresses the 2 μm feature relative to olivine, whereas olivine exhibits a comparatively larger increase in slope. Overall, the two agents generate distinguishable spectral fingerprints, with ion-induced weathering dominated by dispersed nanophase Fe production and laser-induced weathering by rim- and melt-derived glass formation. The mineral specificity of these effects emphasizes the need to consider multiple weathering pathways when interpreting remote-sensing spectra of airless bodies.
prefix: Space weathering is a process that changes the surface of airless planetary bodies. Prime space weathering agents are solar wind irradiation and micrometeoroid bombardment. These processes alter planetary reflectance spectra and often modify their compositional diagnostic features.

title: Interleukin-1beta-mediated suppression of microRNA-27a-3p activity in human cartilage via MAPK and NF-kappaB pathways: A potential mechanism of osteoarthritis pathogenesis
text_ai: The aim of the present study was to investigate the role of microRNA (miR)-27a-3p in osteoarthritis (OA). Reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction and western blotting were performed to determine the expression of miR-27a-3p and aggrecanase-2 (ADAMTS5) in cartilage tissues from patients with OA and healthy controls, and also in interleukin (IL)-1beta-treated primary human chondrocytes. Results: IL-1β decreased miR-27a-3p and increased ADAMTS5 at mRNA and protein levels in chondrocytes and OA cartilage. A miR-27a-3p mimic blocked, while a miR-27a-3p inhibitor enhanced, IL-1β–induced ADAMTS5 expression and reporter activity; mutagenesis of the predicted miR-27a-3p binding site abrogated repression, confirming direct targeting. IL-1β activated MAPK and NF-κB signaling, indicated by phosphorylation of p38, ERK-1/2 and p65; inhibition with SB203580, U0126 and Bay 11-7082 restored miR-27a-3p levels and blunted ADAMTS5 upregulation. OA cartilage exhibited lower miR-27a-3p and higher ADAMTS5 than controls, with inverse correlations to OA grade and to miR-27a-3p/ADAMTS5 levels. Immunohistochemical analyses demonstrated an inverse spatial relationship between miR-27a-3p and ADAMTS5 across OA cartilage sections, with stronger effects in degraded zones. Quantitative analyses revealed significant inverse correlations between miR-27a-3p abundance and OA grade, and between miR-27a-3p and ADAMTS5 protein. In chondrocytes, pathway blockade recapitulated the protective effects of miR-27a-3p, reducing catabolic responses. Together, these data indicate that miR-27a-3p suppresses ADAMTS5 and that IL-1β promotes OA-like catabolism by downregulating miR-27a-3p via MAPK and NF-κB signaling, thereby representing a mechanistic axis amenable to therapeutic intervention. These findings provide a rationale for miR-27a-3p–based strategies to preserve aggrecan integrity in OA, though in vivo validation and long-term safety assessment are required. Nevertheless, clinical translation will require rigorous testing in animal models and optimization of delivery methods.

title: A GPU-accelerated viewer for HEALPix maps
text_ai: HEALPix by G\'orski et. al. (2005) is de-facto standard for Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data storage and analysis, and is widely used in current and upcoming CMB experiments. Almost all the datasets in Legacy Archive for Microwave Background Data Analysis (LAMBDA) use HEALPix as a format of choice. Here we present a GPU-accelerated viewer for HEALPix maps that enables interactive exploration of large, multi-resolution sky maps directly in the native pixelization. The renderer constructs a spherical tessellation by mapping each HEALPix pixel to a triangular facet and renders the surface with per-pixel shading on the GPU. Pixel values stored in HEALPix order are streamed to device memory and sampled in a fragment shader to produce color via user-selectable color maps, with optional gamma correction and masking of invalid data. A level-of-detail scheme—based on angular distance from the camera and adaptive tessellation—provides high frame rates while preserving fidelity near the region of interest. Data streaming is asynchronous: tiles are read from disk into a CPU cache, transferred to the GPU on demand, and evicted as needed, enabling practical handling of maps with billions of pixels. The interface supports pan, zoom, rotate, and multi-map channel mixing, plus overlays for coordinates, contours, and region statistics (mean, rms, min/max). Multi-frequency analyses are facilitated by compositing channels with adjustable weighting and opacity, while a WCS-like header interpretation preserves provenance. The implementation employs C++ with CUDA/OpenGL interop and is designed to be platform-portable, leveraging the HEALPix libraries for data access. Benchmarks against CPU-based viewers demonstrate substantial speedups in rendering throughput and interactive responsiveness, enabling real-time navigation for high-resolution maps. The software is released under an open-source license to catalyze adoption in the CMB community.

title: GRBs luminosity function synthesized from \textit{Swift/BAT}, \textit{Fermi/GBM} and \textit{Konus-Wind} data
text_ai: We study the luminosity function of long gamma-ray bursts (LGRBs) using the peak flux obtained from three LGRB samples with known redshifts: (a) a sample of 251 LGRBs from the \textit{Swift/BAT} satellite/instrument; (b) a sample of 37 LGRBs from the \textit{Fermi/GBM} telescope; (c) a sample of 152 GRBs from the \textit{Konus-Wind} instrument. To construct the LF, we convert the observed peak fluxes into isotropic-equivalent peak luminosities (L_iso) using k-corrections and a standard flat Lambda-CDM cosmology. We fit a set of parametric forms (single and broken power laws, and smoothly joined variants) via forward-folding maximum likelihood, explicitly incorporating the instrumental thresholds, trigger efficiencies, and redshift incompleteness of each sample. We also test for redshift evolution of the normalization and break luminosity, modeling evolution as (1+z)^k. The joint analysis prefers a broken power-law LF with a shallow faint-end slope and a steeper bright-end slope, a break at L_b ≈ 10^52 erg s−1, and mild evolution in normalization. Convolving the derived LF with star-formation-rate–based GRB formation yields counts and redshift distributions consistent with the data, underscoring the utility of multi-instrument synthesis for constraining GRB rates across cosmic time. We discuss implications for high-redshift detectability and for using LGRBs as tracers of metal-poor star formation.
prefix: We study the luminosity function of long gamma-ray bursts (LGRBs) using the peak flux obtained from three LGRB samples with known redshifts: (a) a sample of 251 LGRBs from the \textit{Swift/BAT} satellite/instrument; (b) a sample of 37 LGRBs from the \textit{Fermi/GBM} telescope; (c) a sample of 152 GRBs from the \textit{Konus-Wind} instrument.

title: ALMA-IMF XVI: Mass-averaged temperature of cores and protostellar luminosities in the ALMA-IMF protoclusters
text_ai: ALMA-IMF imaged 15 massive protoclusters down to a resolution of of 2 kau scales, identifying about 1000 star-forming cores. The mass and luminosity of these cores, which are fundamental physical characteristics, are difficult to determine, a problem greatly exacerbated at the distances >2 kpc of ALMA-IMF protoclusters. Here we present mass-averaged temperatures, <T_M>, for the ~1000 cores detected in ALMA-IMF protoclusters and use these values to derive core masses and protostellar luminosities. We adopt a forward-modeling framework that fits multi-band dust continuum with a mass-weighted temperature distribution, using a single-parameter <T_M> together with a fixed dust opacity law (kappa_1.3mm = 0.9 cm^2 g^-1, beta = 1.8) and optically thin emission at long wavelengths. Far-infrared photometry constrains warm tail of the SED, helping to break degeneracies between temperature and emissivity. Core masses M_c and luminosities L_bol are then inferred by integrating the modeled SED and converting to mass via the flux, with uncertainties estimated from Monte Carlo propagation of flux errors, distance, and opacity. For cores unresolved into multiples, we apply a probabilistic deconvolution informed by outflow activity and clustering. The derived <T_M> distribution is broad, spanning ~12–28 K for prestellar candidates and ~22–40 K for protostellar cores, with a shift toward higher temperatures in most luminous protoclusters. We find a loose correlation between M_c and L_bol, with L_bol ∝ M_c^1–1.5, but significant scatter induced by accretion variability and local heating. The catalogs provide <T_M> and protostellar luminosities for every core, enabling robust mass functions and improved calibration of the core-to-star efficiency in extreme environments. Systematics from distance, dust opacity, and optical depth remain, but the approach reduces biases relative to single-temperature fits and is extensible to ALMA-IMF data releases.

The mass and luminosity of these cores, which are fundamental physical characteristics, are difficult to determine, a problem greatly exacerbated at the distances >2 kpc of ALMA-IMF protoclusters.

title: Cladogenetic and Anagenetic Models of Chromosome Number Evolution: A Bayesian Model Averaging Approach.
text_ai: Chromosome number is a key feature of the higher-order organization of the genome, and changes in chromosome number play a fundamental role in evolution. Dysploid gains and losses in chromosome number, as well as polyploidization events, may drive reproductive isolation and lineage diversification. Here, we introduce a Bayesian model-averaging framework that jointly estimates and adjudicates cladogenetic and anagenetic pathways of chromosome-number evolution, explicitly accommodating rate heterogeneity across lineages and across classes of chromosomal change. Dysploid gains and losses, polyploidization, and demi-polyploidization are treated as distinct, potentially lineage-specific processes, each with its own rate parameter(s), with changes partitioned into those occurring at speciation events (cladogenetic) versus those accruing along branches (anagenetic). A reversible-jump MCMC sampler traverses a model space that includes purely anagenetic models, purely cladogenetic models, and mixed models that allow both processes. Prior distributions on rates and on the probability of cladogenetic change are chosen to be weakly informative, promoting identifiability under moderate data density. Posterior model probabilities quantify support for each model class, while model-averaged posteriors yield rate estimates and ancestral chromosome-number reconstructions that reflect uncertainty about the operative evolutionary mechanism. We assess performance with extensive simulation studies across scenarios with varying proportions of cladogenetic versus anagenetic change, differing degrees of rate heterogeneity, and tree shapes. Applied analyses to empirical chromosome-count data mapped to diverse phylogenies demonstrate that the approach improves model fit and ancestral-state reconstructions relative to single-model inferences and, crucially, reveal the relative contributions of cladogenetic and anagenetic processes within clades. The framework provides a practical tool for characterizing chromosome-number evolution in a probabilistic, model-averaged context and clarifies how speciation-associated chromosomal changes and within-lineage transitions jointly shape patterns of diversification.
prefix: Chromosome number is a key feature of the higher-order organization of the genome, and changes in chromosome number play a fundamental role in evolution. Dysploid gains and losses in chromosome number, as well as polyploidization events, may drive reproductive isolation and lineage diversification.

title: Trainable Weight Averaging: Accelerating Training and Improving Generalization
text_ai: Weight averaging is a widely used technique for accelerating training and improving the generalization of deep neural networks (DNNs). While existing approaches like stochastic weight averaging (SWA) rely on pre-set weighting schemes, they can be suboptimal when handling diverse weights. To this end, we propose Trainable Weight Averaging (TWA), a lightweight meta-parameterization that learns the mixing coefficients of a trajectory ensemble to form the final parameter vector. We retain a window of past snapshots {w_{t−L+1},…,w_t} and construct w_bar = ∑_i α_i w_i, with α nonnegative and summing to one (softmax). The coefficients α are updated by backpropagating the validation loss through the averaging operation while the base network weights continue to be optimized by SGD. This end-to-end differentiability enables online adaptation of the averaging scheme to the optimization landscape. We also explore variants with shared coefficients across layers to reduce memory and inject inductive structure. Across standard vision and language benchmarks, TWA yields faster convergence and improved generalization relative to fixed-weight SWA and to plain training, with modest overhead. Ablations illuminate the roles of window size, regularization on α, and coefficient sparsity, revealing a learnable bias-variance trade-off. These results support Trainable Weight Averaging as a general, plug-in technique for accelerating training and enhancing generalization.
prefix: Weight averaging is a widely used technique for accelerating training and improving the generalization of deep neural networks (DNNs). While existing approaches like stochastic weight averaging (SWA) rely on pre-set weighting schemes, they can be suboptimal when handling diverse weights.

title: The Comparative Study of Cervical Shear Wave Elastography Between Twin and Singleton Pregnancy.
text_ai: To compare the cervical shear wave elastography (SWE) by using transvaginal ultrasound (TVS) between twin and singleton pregnant women. This was a prospective cohort study involving the twin and singleton pregnant women who attended the antenatal care at Ramathibodi Hospital, Bangkok, Thailand. Participants were recruited from antenatal clinics and underwent transvaginal SWE of the cervix during a mid-gestation window (20–28 weeks). Cervical stiffness was expressed as mean shear wave speed (SWS, m/s). For each participant, three consecutive measurements of the cervix were obtained and averaged. Measurements were performed by sonographers blinded to pregnancy type; reliability was estimated by ICC. Exclusion criteria included cerclage, known cervical anomalies, placenta previa, active bleeding, and prior cervical surgery. Demographic and obstetric data were collected. Results: A comparative analysis showed a statistically significant difference in mean cervical SWS between twin and singleton pregnancies, with twin gestations exhibiting lower SWS values, consistent with softer cervical tissue. The difference remained significant after adjustment for gestational age, maternal age, BMI, parity, and mode of conception. Cervical length measured by TVS correlated moderately with SWS in both groups, stronger in twins. Interobserver and intraobserver reliability for SWS measurements were high (ICC > 0.85). In secondary analyses, reduced cervical stiffness in twins showed a trend toward higher spontaneous preterm birth and shorter cervical length, though confidence intervals were wide due to limited events. Conclusions: Twin pregnancy was associated with decreased cervical stiffness by SWE compared with singleton pregnancy, independent of gestational age. These findings suggest SWE may provide additional cervical assessment to identify twin pregnancies at elevated risk for cervical shortening and preterm birth. Larger multicenter studies are warranted.
prefix: To compare the cervical shear wave elastography (SWE) by using transvaginal ultrasound (TVS) between twin and singleton pregnant women. This was a prospective cohort study involving the twin and singleton pregnant women who attended the antenatal care at Ramathibodi Hospital, Bangkok, Thailand.

title: Variability in Low Ionization Broad Absorption Line Outflows
text_ai: We present results of our time variability studies of Mg II and Al III absorption lines in a sample of 22 Low Ionization Broad Absorption Line QSOs (LoBAL QSOs) at 0.2 <= zem <= 2.1 using the 2m telescope at IUCAA Girawali Observatory over a time-scale of 10 days to 7.69 years in the QSO's rest frame. We detect significant variability in Mg II troughs in 11 of the 22 sources and in Al III in 9 sources; in 7 objects both ions vary in a coordinated fashion. The observed changes occur on rest-frame timescales as short as ~10 days, with larger amplitudes on multi-year baselines up to 7.69 years. Across the sample, rest-frame equivalent width variations span roughly 0.2–2.5 Å, corresponding to fractional changes up to ~0.6 in the deepest troughs, with a median around 0.15. Variability tends to be more pronounced in shallower components; saturated portions show weaker or absent changes, consistent with partial covering and/or re-distribution of optical depth rather than wholesale ionization changes alone. Doublet ratio analyses indicate heterogeneous covering factors and suggest the presence of partially covering, inhomogeneous clouds transiting the continuum source. We find no unambiguous, ubiquitous correlation between BAL variability and contemporaneous continuum fluctuations within the measurement uncertainties, though a number of cases show trends that may reflect changes in ionization conditions. Centroid velocities generally remain within a few hundred km s−1 of their mean values, with only a subset displaying tentative accelerations or decelerations at the 1–2σ level, pointing to modest transverse motions rather than systematic acceleration of the flow. Collectively, these findings favor a picture of LoBAL outflows consisting of clumpy, shielded gas with variable covering and ionization, located on sub-parsec to parsec scales that respond to local changes in radiation field and density. The results place empirical constraints on the structure, dynamics and driving of low-ionization winds and their role in active-galactic-nucleus feedback.
prefix: We present results of our time variability studies of Mg II and Al III absorption lines in a sample of 22 Low Ionization Broad Absorption Line QSOs (LoBAL QSOs) at 0.2 <= zem <= 2.1 using the 2m telescope at IUCAA Girawali Observatory over a time-scale of 10 days to 7.69 years in the QSO's rest frame.

title: Tetrahedral framework nucleic acids promote scarless healing of cutaneous wounds via the AKT-signaling pathway.
text_ai: While the skin is considered the first line of defense in the human body, there are some vulnerabilities that render it susceptible to certain threats, which is an issue that is recognized by both patients and doctors. Cutaneous wound healing is a series of complex processes that involve many types of cells, such as fibroblasts and keratinocytes. Here, we probed whether topically applied tetrahedral framework nucleic acids (tFNAs) can steer the wound microenvironment toward regeneration via the AKT signaling axis. In a murine full-thickness dorsal wound model, tFNA treatment accelerated re-epithelialization and reduced scar formation, with smaller scar areas and improved collagen organization at day 21–28 versus controls. Immunohistochemical and transcriptional analyses showed sustained AKT phosphorylation in keratinocytes and dermal fibroblasts, accompanied by increased proliferation (Ki-67) and enhanced angiogenesis (VEGF). Notably, fibrotic markers were diminished (α-SMA, COL1), while COL3 deposition and matrix remodeling favored a regenerative pattern. Importantly, pharmacologic AKT inhibition or AKT knockdown abrogated these effects, establishing pathway dependence. Collectively, these findings indicate that tFNAs promote scarless cutaneous repair by activating AKT-dependent processes that coordinate epithelial restitution, dermal remodeling, and ECM composition. These results support potential clinical translation as a minimally invasive therapy for scar suppression.

Cutaneous wound healing is a series of complex processes that involve many types of cells, such as fibroblasts and keratinocytes.

title: 3D morphological analysis of spiral intestine morphogenesis in the little skate, Leucoraja erinacea.
text_ai: The evolution of organ asymmetries is less explored than the field of organ morphology and coiling. The digestive tract of elasmobranchs provides a fascinating model for studying the evolution of morphological asymmetries. Unique to elasmobranchs and all basal fishes is the spiral intestine, which may represent an intermediate morphology in evolution from the straight gut of lamprey to the elongated coils of higher vertebrates. Here, we apply high‑resolution episcopic microscopy and contrast-enhanced micro-CT to construct serial three-dimensional reconstructions of the embryonic to juvenile gut in Leucoraja erinacea. We quantify spiral index, curvature, and longitudinal elongation of the intestinal tube across ontogeny, and map regional variations in mucosal architecture with markers for smooth muscle, enteric neurons, and vasculature. Integrating live imaging of organogenesis with computational morphometrics and finite‑element modeling reveals coordinated outgrowth and differential layering of the tunica propria that drive helical coiling. Our analyses identify critical timing windows in which mesenchymal condensation and vascular patterning accompany geometric twisting, suggesting a quasi‑periodic program of morphogenesis rather than a single morphogenic trigger. The results illuminate how a conserved spiral plan can emerge from near-straight precursors via localized growth anisotropy, with implications for gut mechanics and nutrient processing in diminutive skate larvae.

title: When Do Drivers Concentrate? Attention-based Driver Behavior Modeling With Deep Reinforcement Learning
text_ai: Driver distraction a significant risk to driving safety. Apart from spatial domain, research on temporal inattention is also necessary. This paper aims to figure out the pattern of drivers' temporal attention allocation. To this end, we formulate a temporal attention–driven deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework that observes sequences of driving-context features (vehicle state, control inputs, scene semantics, and driver cues) and learns a policy for longitudinal and lateral control while inferring latent attention states. An attention module assigns dynamic weights to past observations over a sliding horizon, enabling the agent to emphasize temporally salient cues related to imminent hazards or secondary tasks. The agent is trained with a multi-objective reward that favors rule compliance and ride quality, penalizes late or abrupt maneuvers, and includes a distraction penalty when attention drifts from critical moments. We validate on a high-fidelity driving simulator dataset and, where available, naturalistic driving data, comparing against non-attentive DRL baselines and supervised attention predictors. Results indicate that temporal attention improves detection of distraction episodes, yields more robust control under secondary tasks, and enables earlier anticipation of high-risk events. Ablation studies quantify the contributions of temporal versus spatial attention and the impact of reward design on distraction reduction.

title: Active Feature Acquisition with Supervised Matrix Completion
text_ai: Feature missing is a serious problem in many applications, which may lead to low quality of training data and further significantly degrade the learning performance. While feature acquisition usually involves special devices or complex process, it is expensive to acquire all feature values for the whole dataset. To address this, we propose an integrative framework that jointly learns a predictive model and completes the feature matrix under a budgeted active acquisition strategy. The method formulates supervised matrix completion with a loss that couples observed labels with feature representation, and adds an acquisition term that guides querying of the most informative features under a fixed budget. We introduce an acquisition criterion based on the expected reduction in predictive loss, computed efficiently from the current low-rank completion and classifier weights. An alternating optimization algorithm updates the classifier parameters and the completed feature matrix, interleaved with selective queries for the most informative missing entries. We establish convergence to a stationary point and show that the approach respects the budget constraint while progressively improving the objective. Experiments on real-world datasets with heterogeneous missingness demonstrate that AFA-SMC consistently beats passive imputation and random feature acquisition, achieving higher accuracy with fewer acquisitions and robust performance across domains.

title: An H{\alpha} view of galaxy build-up in the first 2 Gyr: luminosity functions at z~4-6.5 from NIRCam/grism spectroscopy
text_ai: The H{\alpha} nebular emission line is an optimal tracer for recent star formation in galaxies. With the advent of JWST, this line has recently become observable at z>3 for the first time. We present a catalog of 1013 H{\alpha} emitters at 3.7<z<6.7 in the GOODS fields obtained from a blind search in JWST NIRCam/grism data. From the Hα line fluxes we derive luminosities and construct the luminosity function in three redshift intervals: z≈4–4.5, z≈4.5–5.5, and z≈5.5–6.7, balancing sample size and redshift fidelity. We adopt a forward-modeling approach to account for the grism selection function, using extensive injection–recovery tests in the real data cubes to determine completeness as a function of luminosity, redshift, and local crowding. The resulting LFs are fitted with Schechter functions, allowing for correlation between L* and φ*. In all bins the Schechter form provides an adequate description; L* declines from log L* ≈ 42.3–42.5 erg s⁻¹ at z~4 to ≈42.0 erg s⁻¹ by z~6.5, while φ* shows a mild decrease and α remains steep, α≈−1.6 to −1.8. Integrating the best-fit LFs yields Hα luminosity densities of (2–4)×10^39, (1–2)×10^39, and (0.5–1)×10^39 erg s⁻¹ Mpc⁻³ across the three slices, corresponding to dust-corrected star formation rate densities of ~0.08, ~0.03, and ~0.01 M⊙ yr⁻¹ Mpc⁻³, assuming a Chabrier IMF and a modest A(Hα) distribution inferred from the UV continuum. Our Hα-based SFRD aligns with, and complements, UV-based estimates, suggesting a substantial, progressively hidden component of star formation at z>4. The large, unbiased nature of the sample minimizes cosmic variance and enables a direct census of star formation in the early universe, with implications for the assembly of stellar mass in the first 2 Gyr and for the faint-end growth of galaxies in JWST-era surveys.

title: Xiaoyao Pills Ameliorate Depression-like Behaviors and Oxidative Stress Induced by Olfactory Bulbectomy in Rats via the Activation of the PIK3CA-AKT1-NFE2L2/BDNF Signaling Pathway.
text_ai: Numerous studies have revealed that oxidative stress is closely associated with the occurrence and development of depression. Xiaoyao Pills (XYW) are included in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia and are frequently used for treating anxiety and depression by smoothing the liver, strengthening the spleen, and nourishing the blood. In the present study, olfactory bulbectomy (OBX)–induced rats were treated with Xiaoyao Pills (XYW) at low, medium, and high doses for four weeks. Behavioral assays showed that XYW markedly ameliorated depression-like phenotypes, increasing sucrose preference and reducing immobility in the forced swim and tail suspension tests, with improvements that were dose-dependent. Open-field exploration was partially restored, indicating alleviation of anergia and psychomotor retardation associated with OBX. Biochemically, XYW decreased lipid peroxidation (MDA) and ROS while boosting antioxidant defenses, elevating SOD, GSH, and catalase activities in the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex. At the molecular level, XYW upregulated the PIK3CA-AKT1 signaling axis, increasing PIK3CA expression and AKT1 phosphorylation, which in turn promoted nuclear translocation of NFE2L2/NRF2. Concomitantly, downstream antioxidant genes (HO-1, NQO1, GCLC) were induced and BDNF/TrkB signaling was enhanced, suggesting a coordinated activation of redox and neurotrophic pathways. Correlation analyses revealed strong associations between improvements in behavior and restoration of redox balance and BDNF signaling. These findings indicate that XYW exerts antidepressant-like effects in OBX rats by activating the PIK3CA-AKT1-NFE2L2/BDNF axis, thereby dampening oxidative stress and supporting neurotrophic processes. Overall, the results provide mechanistic insight into XYW's actions and support its potential as an adjunctive treatment for depression. These results warrant exploration of XYW in clinical depression.

title: Discovery and characterisation of detached M-dwarf eclipsing binaries in the WFCAM Transit Survey
text_ai: We report the discovery of 16 detached M-dwarf eclipsing binaries with J<16 mag and provide a detailed characterisation of three of them, using high-precision infrared light curves from the WFCAM Transit Survey (WTS). Such systems provide the most accurate and model-independent method for measuring the fundamental parameters of these poorly understood yet numerous stars, which currently lack sufficient observations to precisely calibrate stellar evolution models. Across the 16 new binaries, we derive orbital configurations from the high-quality J-band light curves and place tight constraints on the fundamental parameters of the components. For the three systems with supporting spectroscopy, we perform a joint light-curve and radial-velocity analysis with PHOEBE, incorporating infrared limb-darkening coefficients and allowing for modest third-light and magnetic-activity effects manifested as spot-induced modulations in the out-of-eclipse baseline. The resulting dynamical masses and radii reach percent-level precision, enabling direct placement on the empirical mass–radius relation in the fully convective and partially convective regimes. We find component masses in the range ~0.28–0.60 M⊙ and radii ~0.30–0.56 R⊙, with typical uncertainties of 2–4% in radius and 3–5% in mass. Effective temperatures, inferred from multi-band SEDs and empirical calibrations, lie in the 3300–3900 K interval. For two of the three well-characterised systems, the primary and secondary have nearly equal masses within 5%, while the third shows a modest mass asymmetry. The radii relative to model predictions (e.g., Dartmouth/BT-Settl) show agreement at the higher-mass end but a modest inflation (~5–10%) at M ≲ 0.4 M⊙, consistent with the growing evidence for magnetic activity and starspot effects in rapidly rotating M-dwarfs. The expanded sample strengthens constraints on the low-mass mass–radius relation and demonstrates the potency of infrared transit surveys for delivering precise, model-independent stellar parameters for the most abundant stars in the Galaxy.

title: Why the World Reads Wikipedia: Beyond English Speakers
text_ai: As one of the Web's primary multilingual knowledge sources, Wikipedia is read by millions of people across the globe every day. Despite this global readership, little is known about why users read Wikipedia's various language editions. This study adopts a multi-method design to illuminate the drivers of edition choice and cross-language navigation. We combine longitudinal server-log data from six language editions with cross-sectional survey responses drawn from readers in ten regions, enabling behavioral and attitudinal analyses. Our quantitative component analyzes page-visit sequences, dwell times, and topic distributions, while the qualitative component codes open-ended explanations of reading motives. Through cluster analysis and regression modeling, we identify reader archetypes—those who predominantly stay within a single edition and polyglot seekers who switch across languages for specific topics. The results reveal that topic relevance, perceived article quality, and trust signals strongly influence edition selection, whereas accessibility, searchability, and habit shape cross-language exploration. English editions function as global reference points for universally traversed topics, yet local editions outperform others in reflecting regional knowledge and culturally salient framing. The findings carry implications for editorial strategy, user interface design, and cross-edition interoperability to support equitable knowledge access worldwide. Informing future research directions.

title: Weak Multiplier Hopf Algebras. The main theory
text_ai: A weak multiplier Hopf algebra is a pair (A,\Delta) of a non-degenerate idempotent algebra A and a coproduct $\Delta$ on A. The coproduct is a coassociative homomorphism from A to the multiplier algebra M(A\otimes A) with some natural extra properties (like the existence of a counit). In this paper we develop the main theory of weak multiplier Hopf algebras, clarifying the role of the canonical idempotent E in M(A⊗A) and the way Δ governs the non-unital interaction of A with its multipliers. We show that Δ is coassociative in the multiplier sense and satisfies leg conditions that guarantee the well-definedness of convolution-type maps, from which the source and target maps ε_s, ε_t : A → M(A) arise by ε_s(a) = (ε⊗id)Δ(a) and ε_t(a) = (id⊗ε)Δ(a). The existence of a counit on a suitable subspace is assumed, yielding counital identities on the Δ-legs. Regularity is characterized by the bijectivity of the left and right leg maps T_λ, T_ρ, and in this setting we obtain an antipode S: A → M(A) that is an anti-automorphism and satisfies m(S⊗id)Δ(a) = ε_s(a) and m(id⊗S)Δ(a) = ε_t(a), together with the corresponding relations for Δ^op. In the regular case S is bijective and obeys ΔS = (S⊗S)Δ^op. We develop the dual theory: every regular weak multiplier Hopf algebra admits a dual Â with Δ̂ in strong duality, enabling a bidual reconstruction. A monoidal category of corepresentations and its representation-theoretic counterpart are constructed, yielding a robust, purely algebraic module theory. Integrals and a Haar-like functional are studied, furnishing a modular framework and yielding faithful GNS-type realizations in appropriate contexts. The framework unifies groupoid algebras, weak Hopf algebras, and multiplier Hopf algebras as special cases, and provides a coherent algebraic quantum-groupoid picture extending beyond finite dimensions.

title: Sense of Self and Time in Borderline Personality. A Comparative Robustness Study with Generative AI
text_ai: This study examines the capacity of large language models (LLMs) to support phenomenological qualitative analysis of first-person experience in Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD), understood as a disorder of temporality and selfhood. Building on a prior human-led thematic analysis of 24 inpatients' life-story interviews, we compared three LLMs (OpenAI GPT-4o, Google Gemini 2.5 Pro, Anthropic Claude Opus 4) prompted to mimic the interpretative style of the original investigators. Outputs were evaluated against the original human coding frame through a double-blind expert review, assessing thematic coverage, interpretive coherence, and clinical plausibility. Across models, recurring motifs—nonlinear temporality, fragility of self-continuity, and affective volatility—recurred, paralleling the human themes of shifting temporal horizons and self-other containment. Differences emerged in granularity: GPT-4o yielded dense micro-narratives and self-referential speculation; Gemini tended to macro-structural accounts foregrounding episodes and interpersonal contingencies; Claude offered a balanced, clinically oriented synthesis with cautious generalizations. Inter-model convergence supported core themes, while method-specific divergences exposed limits of synthetic phenomenology. The findings suggest LLMs can robustly reproduce central interpretive patterns yet require guardrails against overinterpretation, training-data biases, and ethical risk in simulating lived experience. We outline guidelines for integrating generative AI into phenomenological inquiry with transparency and reproducibility.

title: Modified gravity and massive neutrinos: constraints from the full shape analysis of BOSS galaxies and forecasts for Stage IV surveys
text_ai: We constrain the growth index $\gamma$ by performing a full-shape analysis of the power spectrum multipoles measured from the BOSS DR12 data. We adopt a theoretical model based on the Effective Field theory of the Large Scale Structure (EFTofLSS) and focus on two different cosmologies: $\gamma$CDM and $\gamma \nu$CDM, where we also vary the total neutrino mass. Employing a Markov chain Monte Carlo exploration of the joint posterior of cosmological and nuisance parameters, we fit the BOSS DR12 multipoles (monopole, quadrupole, and, where informative, hexadecapole) within the one-loop EFTofLSS framework, incorporating a consistent treatment of massive neutrinos and a redshift-space distortion model calibrated against simulations. We marginalize over the EFT counterterms, linear and non-linear galaxy bias parameters, and stochastic noise, with priors anchored by external measurements and perturbation theory reliability. In gammaCDM, allowing the neutrino sector to vary, we recover a growth index broadly compatible with GR, with gamma = 0.60 ± 0.12 (68% CL) and an upper bound m_nu < 0.18 eV (95% CL). In gamma_nuCDM, where both gamma and m_nu are free, we obtain gamma = 0.58 ± 0.14 and m_nu < 0.20 eV (95% CL), again showing no statistically significant deviation from general relativity. The inclusion of the full shape information and higher-order multipoles reduces degeneracies between gamma and m_nu relative to analyses relying on BAO or redshift-space distortions alone, underscoring the strength of the EFTofLSS approach for extracting growth information from quasi-nonlinear scales. Looking ahead to Stage IV surveys, we project DESI- and Euclid-like observations with expanded sky coverage and refined control of systematics. The full-shape analysis is expected to constrain gamma at the few-percent level (sigma_gamma ≈ 0.03–0.05) and to tighten m_nu bounds to the ~0.05–0.08 eV (95% CL) regime, depending on prior choices for EFT parameters and cross-correlations with weak lensing. Our results demonstrate that EFTofLSS-based full-shape analyses will provide a robust, near-model-independent test of gravity, preserving sensitivity to neutrino-mass–mimicking signatures while delivering decisive constraints on possible deviations from general relativity in the cosmic growth history.

title: Left atrial function in patients with light chain amyloidosis: A transthoracic 3D speckle tracking imaging study.
text_ai: Systemic light chain amyloidosis (AL) is characterized by the extracellular deposition of amyloid fibrils. Transthoracic echocardiography is the modality of choice to assess cardiac function in patients with AL. Whereas left ventricular (LV) function has been well studied in this patient population, data regarding the value of left atrial (LA) function in AL patients are lacking. Methods: In a prospective cross-sectional study, 72 biopsy‑proven AL patients and 34 age‑ and sex‑matched controls underwent comprehensive transthoracic echocardiography with 3D full‑volume datasets. Left atrial volumes were computed from 3D datasets and indexed to body surface area (LAVI). Phasic LA function was quantified by 3D speckle‑tracking analysis, yielding reservoir (εs), conduit (εe), and pump (εa) strains. LV volumes, ejection fraction, global longitudinal strain, and transmitral Doppler parameters were recorded. Biomarkers including NT‑proBNP were obtained. Results: AL patients showed significantly larger LAVI (45.3 ± 12.5 vs 24.7 ± 6.8 mL/m², P < 0.001) and markedly reduced LA strains: εs 20.1 ± 5.2% vs 32.7 ± 6.4%, εe 16.5 ± 4.0% vs 27.2 ± 5.1%, εa 9.0 ± 3.0% vs 16.0 ± 3.5% (all P < 0.001). LA reservoir function correlated with LV global longitudinal strain (r = 0.52, P < 0.001) and E/e′ (r = −0.46, P < 0.01). In multivariate models, εs remained independently associated with elevated filling pressures and NT‑proBNP after adjustment for age, sex, LV mass, and amyloid burden. Reproducibility was excellent, with intraobserver ICCs for εs, εe, and εa of 0.88–0.92 and interobserver ICCs of 0.84–0.89. Subgroup analysis showed greater LA dysfunction in patients with overt cardiac involvement and higher LV mass indexed. Conclusions: Left atrial dysfunction detected by 3D speckle‑tracking is prevalent in AL and parallels both systolic and diastolic impairment as well as amyloid burden. 3DSTE‑derived LA function provides incremental information beyond conventional echocardiography and may augment risk stratification and longitudinal monitoring in light chain amyloidosis.

title: Formation mechanism of hairpin vortices in the wake of a truncated square cylinder in a duct
text_ai: We investigate the laminar shedding of hairpin vortices in the wake of a truncated square cylinder placed in a duct, for Reynolds numbers around the critical threshold of the onset of vortex shedding. We single out the formation mechanism of the hairpin vortices by means of a detailed analysis of the flow patterns in the steady regime. By inspecting the steady base flow and perturbation fields, we identify a sequence in which a pair of shear-layer instabilities anchored at the truncation corners roll up into a head and two counter-rotating legs, yielding a hairpin topology downstream. The head forms first through the tilting and roll-up of spanwise vorticity concentrated in the recirculation bubble, while the legs are drawn out by shear and advection as the flow adjusts to the duct confinement. Using vorticity-budget diagnostics and lambda2/Q-criterion visualizations, we trace the contributions of stretching, tilting, and diffusion to vorticity amplification. Stability analyses of the steady wake corroborate amplified subharmonic mode whose nonlinear saturation yields the hairpin pattern near the critical Reynolds number. The mechanism depends sensitively on truncation height, duct aspect ratio, and inlet boundary-layer state, with implications for drag and heat transfer in confined bluff-body wakes.

title: Progresses in the Analysis of Stochastic 2D Cellular Automata: a Study of Asynchronous 2D Minority
text_ai: Cellular automata are often used to model systems in physics, social sciences, biology that are inherently asynchronous. Over the past 20 years, studies have demonstrated that the behavior of cellular automata drastically changed under asynchronous updates. Still, the few mathematical analyses of asynchronism focus on one-dimensional probabilistic cellular automata, either on single examples or on specific classes. Extending the analysis to two dimensions, we study a stochastic minority rule on tori with asynchronous Poisson updates. Each site updates at rate one by adopting the minority color among its four neighbors. We develop a Markovian framework in which absorbing, frozen configurations prevail and attractors such as checkerboard and stripe mosaics. Under broad initial conditions, the process almost surely freezes into one of these patterns rather than achieving consensus. We derive polynomial bounds on fixation times as a function of the lattice size and update-rate parameters delineate regimes of rapid convergence from prolonged metastability. Complementing the analysis with simulations, we chart phase portraits, quantify domain-wall dynamics, and validate the scaling laws. The results unify prior work on one-dimensional stochastic CAs and two-dimensional minorities, and they offer a principled basis for modeling asynchronous interaction in spatially extended systems.

title: Energy Loss of Solar $p$ Modes due to the excitation of Magnetic Sausage Tube Waves: Importance of Coupling the Upper Atmosphere
text_ai: We consider damping and absorption of solar $p$ modes due to their energy loss to magnetic tube waves that can freely carry energy out of the acoustic cavity. The coupling of $p$ modes and sausage tube waves is studied in a model atmosphere composed of a polytropic interior above which lies an isothermal upper atmosphere. The coupling is treated within a two–layer geometry in which the polytropic interior supports global p modes whose eigenfunctions extend into a background vertical magnetic flux tube, which in turn connects to an isothermal atmosphere where sausage tube waves can propagate freely as energy carriers. Using the thin-tube approximation for the magnetic structure, the radial and vertical displacements are matched across the interior–tube boundary and through the transition to the isothermal layer, allowing the calculation of the outward energy flux carried by sausage waves. The resulting damping rate of each p mode is obtained from the net energy loss to the tube, normalized by the mode energy, and the corresponding absorption coefficient is expressed as a function of frequency, degree, magnetic field strength, and flux-tube radius. We find a strong sensitivity to the upper-atmosphere structure: the isothermal layer removes part of the acoustic reflection at the photosphere and enhances the transmission of acoustic power into the tube, thereby increasing the leakage compared with models that assume a purely polytropic stratification above the interior. The dependence on magnetic parameters is monotonic in the explored range: for fixed frequency, increasing the magnetic flux or tube radius raises the coupling and the energy flux into sausage waves until geometric or impedance-limited saturation sets in. Across the observed solar p-mode spectrum, the incorporated upper atmosphere shifts and broadens the absorption features, elevating damping rates by up to a factor of order unity in the mid- to high-frequency range. The study highlights the crucial role of the upper-atmosphere coupling in accurately quantifying p-mode energy loss to magneto-acoustic tube waves.

title: Celestial $w_{1+\infty}$ Symmetries from Twistor Space
text_ai: We explain how twistor theory represents the self-dual sector of four dimensional gravity in terms of the loop group of Poisson diffeomorphisms of the plane via Penrose's non-linear graviton construction. The symmetries of the self-dual sector are generated by the corresponding loop algebra $Lw_{1+\infty}$ of the algebra $w_{1+\infty}$ of these Poisson diffeomorphisms. Within this setting, the loop algebra L w_{1+∞} acts by Hamiltonian vector fields generated by Laurent series of Poisson brackets on the celestial plane, preserving the Poisson structure and the real slice relevant for Lorentzian signatures. We construct explicit representatives for the generators and show that their action on the twistor data induces corresponding transformations on the radiative (self-dual) degrees of freedom at null infinity. By passing to the celestial conformal primary basis, these transformations become asymptotic symmetries of the radiative phase space, yielding a celestial version of the w_{1+∞} Ward algebra. The resulting charge algebra governs the soft and collinear structure of self-dual gravitational scattering, providing a geometric derivation of known celestial identities and predicting new recursion relations for celestial amplitudes. The twistor construction clarifies how celestial w_{1+∞} arises from the non-linear graviton correspondence and offers a natural bridge to a twistor-inspired celestial conformal field theory.

title: Performances of Neutron Scattering Spectrometers on a Compact Neutron Source
text_ai: There is currently a big effort put into the operation and construction of world class neutron scattering facilities (SNS and SNS-TS2 in the US, J-PARC in Japan, ESS in Europe, CSS in China, PIK in Russia). This study presents an assessment of the performance of neutron scattering spectrometers coupled to a compact neutron source (CNS), with emphasis on flux delivery, energy and momentum transfer resolution, and background conditions across typical instrument configurations. Using a pulsed, accelerator-driven CNS operating at target stations, we characterize neutron yield per incident proton, moderator performance, and transport efficiencies through guide systems optimized for cold and thermal spectra. Time-of-flight spectrometers demonstrate competitive energy resolutions down to ΔE/E ~ 10^-3–10^-2, while backscattering and inelastic instruments achieve wide dynamic ranges. We benchmark measured performance against Monte Carlo simulations (MCNP/Geant4) incorporating geometry and shielding, enabling a priori estimation of accessible q-ω space and instrument throughput. Results show that high-brightness CNS sources can deliver sufficient flux for routine structural and dynamical studies at moderate sample sizes, with reduced facility footprint and operational costs. We discuss design considerations for modular detector ensembles, chopper cascades, and cooling strategies that minimize background and maximize uptime, highlighting pathways to facilities.

title: High performance Broadband Photodetection Based on Graphene -- MoS$_{2x}$Se$_{2(1-x)}$ Alloy Engineered Phototransistors
text_ai: The concept of alloy engineering has emerged as a viable technique towards tuning the bandgap as well as engineering the defect levels in two-dimensional transition metal dichalcognides (TMDC). Possibility to synthesize these ultrathin TMDC materials through chemical route has opened realistic possibilities to fabricate hybrid multi-functional devices. Here, we demonstrate graphene–MoS2xSe2(1−x) alloy engineered phototransistors that exhibit broadband photodetection with high responsivity and fast, reliable dynamics. Large-area monolayer TMDC alloys with varying x were synthesized by a scalable chemical vapor deposition route and subsequently integrated with CVD graphene to form vertical heterostructures. Spectroscopic and structural characterization confirms tunable bandgap and defect landscape with x = 0.3–0.7 enabling continuous tuning of absorption window from the visible to near-infrared. The devices show gate-tunable photoresponse, yielding responsivities up to 10^4–10^5 A/W and specific detectivities exceeding ~10^11–10^12 Jones across 450–1600 nm. The broad spectral response arises from alloy-induced band-edge states and efficient interfacial charge transfer at graphene–TMDC junctions, while trap-assisted photogating provides pronounced gain without sacrificing response speed. Time-resolved measurements indicate rise/fall times of a few to tens of milliseconds, suitable for imaging and communication applications. The results establish alloy engineering as a robust route for high-performance, broadband, graphene-enabled photodetection.
prefix: The concept of alloy engineering has emerged as a viable technique towards tuning the bandgap as well as engineering the defect levels in two-dimensional transition metal dichalcognides (TMDC). Possibility to synthesize these ultrathin TMDC materials through chemical route has opened realistic possibilities to fabricate hybrid multi-functional devices.

title: Aspects of CFTs on Real Projective Space
text_ai: We present an analytic study of conformal field theories on the real projective space $\mathbb{RP}^d$, focusing on the two-point functions of scalar operators. Due to the partially broken conformal symmetry, these are non-trivial functions of a conformal cross ratio and are constrained to obey a crossing equation. Employing the crosscap bootstrap, we write the two-point function as a sum over conformal blocks in the direct OPE channel together with the image channel, organized by primaries O_k that appear in O_i × O_j and their images under the antipodal involution. The resulting crossing equation constrains the dependence on the single conformal cross ratio η = (x−y)^2 / [(1+x^2)(1+y^2)], up to the CFT data that survive the projection. We first validate the construction in the generalized free field theory on RP^d, where the correlator reduces to a finite sum with coefficients fixed by symmetry. We then develop a systematic analytic expansion about the free theory (ε-expansion) and compare to data for canonical models in d=3, such as the Ising CFT and the O(N) vector model, extracting constraints on one-point functions ⟨O⟩RP^d and on the bulk OPE coefficients λ_{ij}^k. Additionally, we relate the non-orientable RP^d geometry to a crossed-channel boundary problem on the double cover S^d, clarifying the analytic structure of crosscap blocks and the location of their branch cuts. These results illuminate how non-orientability imprints on the operator spectrum and provide a practical analytic bootstrap mechanism for CFTs on curved, nontrivial backgrounds.

title: Quasi-Discrete Locally Compact Quantum Groups
text_ai: Consider a C*-algebra $A$ with a comultiplication $\Delta$. This pair is usually thought of as locally compact quantum semi-group. When these notes were written, in 1993, it was not at all clear what the extra assumptions on the comultiplication should be for this pair to be a 'locally compact quantum group'. To give a workable notion one imposes the standard Haar weight axioms and mild density conditions, and then restricts attention to those locally compact quantum groups whose dual object is discrete. In concrete terms Ē is a direct sum of matrix algebras; equivalently Δ decomposes into finite dimensional corners along a central spectrum. The central observation is that under the quasi-discrete hypothesis the multiplicative unitary W is a direct sum of finite‑dimensional unitaries, and hence the theory reduces to finite‑dimensional corepresentations. We develop a structural theory: the Haar weights exist and are unique up to scale, W implements Δ, and every irreducible corepresentation is finite dimensional. Regularity is automatic in the quasi‑discrete regime, and the associated duality swaps discreteness and compactness. Consequently the dual Ĝ is discrete and the bidual recovers the original quantum group. This yields a tractable harmonic analysis: A is generated by finite‑dimensional corepresentation coefficients, and L^1(A) is spanned by them, yielding a Peter–Weyl type theory. We illustrate with examples including discrete groups and compact quantum groups, and show that standard constructions (tensor products, crossed products) persist. The paper thus positions quasi‑discrete locally compact quantum groups as a natural bridge between the purely algebraic and the analytic theories. It provides an analytic framework for quantum groups with discrete spectra.

title: Non-Uniform Time-Step Deep Q-Network for Carrier-Sense Multiple Access in Heterogeneous Wireless Networks
text_ai: This paper investigates a new class of carrier-sense multiple access (CSMA) protocols that employ deep reinforcement learning (DRL) techniques, referred to as carrier-sense deep-reinforcement learning multiple access (CS-DLMA). The goal of CS-DLMA is to enable efficient and equitable spectrum sharing among a group of co-located heterogeneous wireless networks. Formulated as a multi-agent DRL problem under asynchronous event-driven dynamics, NU-TS-DQN learns to map local observations to transmission actions with variable temporal granularity. Agents observe channel idle/busy indicators, recent collision signals, queue length, backoff state, and neighbor activity patterns. Actions encode select-backoff stages or silent abstention. The non-uniform time-step mechanism aligns decision epochs with heterogeneous event times (packet arrivals, backoff expirations, channel state changes), enabling time-adaptive value propagation via TD learning over irregular intervals. The architecture supports decentralized execution with centralized training using a shared replay and a class-aware parameterization to accommodate heterogeneous node types. We evaluate in a simulated heterogeneous network with mixed traffic and data rates under realistic MAC/PHY constraints and hidden-terminal dynamics. Baselines include CSMA/CA, a uniform-time-step DQN, and fixed backoff policies. We assess aggregate throughput, fairness (Jain’s index), average delay, and collision probability across varying node counts and traffic intensities. Results indicate that NU-TS-DQN achieves more efficient and fair channel sharing under bursty traffic and asymmetric backoff settings, with reduced collision rates and lower delay compared with baselines. Learned policies exploit channel state information and traffic heterogeneity, maintaining performance as networks scale. The method demonstrates robustness to time-varying conditions and requires modest training overhead, making it suitable for practical deployment as a non-uniform time-step enhancement to CSMA-based networks. We provide ablation studies and discuss design guidelines for reward shaping and time-step granularity to balance responsiveness and stability, along with complexity considerations for real-time implementation.

title: On channel sounding with switched arrays in fast time-varying channels
text_ai: Time-division multiplexed (TDM) channel sounders, in which a single RF chain is connected sequentially via an electronic switch to different elements of an array, are widely used for the measurement of double-directional/MIMO propagation channels. This paper investigates the impact of array switching patterns on the accuracy of parameter estimation of multipath components (MPC) for a time-division multiplexed (TDM) channel sounder. Employing a parametric channel model with a finite set of MPCs whose delays, angles and Doppler shifts may evolve within a snapshot, we derive the Fisher information and Cramér–Rao lower bound for TDM sounding under arbitrary switching. We show that the joint time–space sampling imposed by the pattern governs identifiability and that uniform switching can induce Doppler/angle leakage, biasing MPC estimates in fast time-varying channels. Numerical experiments with synthetic channels demonstrate that switching sequences designed to minimize mutual coherence—such as pseudo-random, Hadamard-based, or orthogonal patterns—substantially improve resolution and reduce spurious components. ML- and SAGE-based estimators exhibit lower finite-sample bias and variance under optimal patterns, approaching the CRLB. Practical implications are provided in the form of design guidelines: pattern selection, dwell-time allocation, and processing considerations for mmWave MIMO sounders in rapidly varying environments.

title: Mitigating ML Model Decay in Continuous Integration with Data Drift Detection: An Empirical Study
text_ai: Background: Machine Learning (ML) methods are being increasingly used for automating different activities, e.g., Test Case Prioritization (TCP), of Continuous Integration (CI). However, ML models need frequent retraining as a result of changes in the CI environment, more commonly known as data drift. Also, continuously retraining ML models consume a lot of time and effort. Objective: to evaluate whether data-drift detection can curb ML model decay in CI without imposing prohibitive retraining costs, and to quantify the trade-offs between detection sensitivity and maintenance overhead. Methods: We integrated a drift-detection module into the ML components powering Test Case Prioritization across three open-source CI workloads with heterogeneous feature spaces and failure patterns. We compare (i) a baseline periodic retraining policy, (ii) a drift-triggered retraining policy using established detectors for covariate drift (KS test, ADWIN, and multivariate Maximum Mean Discrepancy) and for label drift where applicable, and (iii) a hybrid policy that combines drift alerts with selective, sample-efficient retraining. Data are evaluated on successive build windows to simulate real CI evolution, measuring predictive performance for TCP, including area under the ROC curve, precision, and recall of prioritized failing tests, along with retraining frequency, wall-clock training time, and CI throughput. We also assess robustness to false positives/negatives and the impact of drift type (sudden vs. gradual) on maintenance costs. Results: Drift-triggered retraining substantially reduces retraining events (approximately 25–40% fewer retrainings) while preserving TCP effectiveness (ΔAUC ≤ 0.04 and ΔF1 ≤ 0.05) relative to periodic retraining. Incorporating covariate and label drift signals improves stability in the presence of abrupt distribution changes, with the hybrid approach offering the best balance between performance and overhead. False positives remain manageable under calibrated thresholds, though detector choice and window size materially affect sensitivity to rapid drift. Conclusions: Data drift detection provides a practical mechanism to mitigate ML model decay in CI, enabling more efficient maintenance with sustained task performance. We offer guidelines for detector selection, threshold tuning, and integration into CI pipelines, and discuss limitations and directions for automation and tooling.
