title: Truth is Universal: Robust Detection of Lies in LLMs
text_ai: Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionised natural language processing, exhibiting impressive human-like capabilities. In particular, LLMs are capable of "lying", knowingly outputting false statements. Hence, it is of interest and importance to develop methods to detect when LLMs lie. Indeed, several authors trained classifiers to detect LLM lies based on their internal model activations. To this end, we introduce a robust, model-agnostic detector that operates post-hoc on generated text and, where available, on surrogate activations, without requiring access to privileged training data. Our evaluation spans multiple model families (autoregressive and encoder–decoder architectures), a suite of deception tasks, and diverse prompt regimes. We show that lie signals persist under paraphrasing, minor factual edits, and changes in decoding strategy, enabling cross-model generalization. The detector combines perturbation-based sensitivity, calibration metrics, and cross-output consistency checks, learned by a lightweight meta-classifier. Across benchmarks, the approach attains superior detection accuracy and robustness to distributional drift, with interpretable attribution for detected lies. We discuss limitations, including potential adversarial adaptation, and propose deployment guidelines for safety, governance, and auditing of LLM outputs.

title: Binary black holes and tori in AGN I. Ejection of stars and merging of the binary
text_ai: Most galaxies have central massive black holes (BH), and merge with others during their evolution, as strongly suggested by recent observations. Consequently a black hole binary (BHB) emerges. Considering the evolution of the binary when it has become hard, at a separation of the BHs of about 1 pc, we propose to solve two basic questions in our understanding of the central activity of galaxies: (1) Do the BHs actually merge? We address this by analyzing the coupled evolution of a bound BHB and the surrounding nuclear environment once the binary has become hard at about 1 pc. We model the stellar cluster as a live N-body system, allow three-body scattering to eject stars (loss-cone draining) and include a self-consistent, rotating circumnuclear torus formed from gas inflow triggered by the merger of the progenitors. The torus furnishes further angular-momentum extraction via gravitational torques and accretion drag, thereby altering the binary’s eccentricity distribution and hardening rate. We quantify the relative importance of (i) purely stellar dynamical hardening, (ii) gas-assisted dynamical friction and viscous torques, and (iii) gravitational wave emission as the separation shrinks. Our results show that in triaxial or moderately flattened potentials the loss cone is replenished efficiently, preventing stalling and enabling coalescence within a Hubble time for typical AGN-host masses. In contrast, in spherically symmetric, purely stellar systems the binary stalls unless gas inflow forms a substantial circumbinary disc, which acts as a secondary sink for angular momentum. The emergent torus inherits a distinct kinematic imprint from the binary, and the ejected stars populate a high-velocity tail, generating observable signatures such as hypervelocity stars and core scouring, with implications for AGN fueling and gravitational-wave event rates. These results have implications for multi-messenger probes of merging BHBs in AGN and set the stage for the subsequent exploration of torus evolution.

title: Nothing to see here: Failed supernovae are faint or rare
text_ai: The absence of Type IIP core-collapse supernovae arising from progenitors above 17 solar masses suggests the existence of another evolutionary path by which massive stars end their lives. The direct collapse of a stellar core to a black hole without the production of a bright, explosive transient is expected to produce a long-lived, dim, red transient known as a failed supernova. To test this scenario, we assembled a survey of galaxies to monitor the fates of red supergiants. Using archival HST imaging spanning ten years, complemented by infrared data from Spitzer and facilities, we search for stars that disappear or for faint, red, persistent transients consistent with direct collapse. Our analysis accounts for photometric biases, crowding, and dust extinction, and we perform injection–recovery tests to quantify sensitivity to slow, low-luminosity events. Across a sample that includes dozens of galaxies within ~20 Mpc and hundreds of candidate progenitors with masses above ~17 M⊙, we identify no unambiguous disappearances and subset of late-time transients whose colors and luminosities could plausibly arise from extreme dust-enshrouded phases or from alternative channels. From these results we derive upper limits on the failed-SN rate relative to the core-collapse rate for progenitors above 17 M⊙; at 90% confidence, f_fail/f_cc < 0.4–0.6 depending on assumed light-curve shapes and dust distributions. Correcting for selection effects reduces the constraint but does not invalidate it. Our findings imply that either failed SNe are rarer than some models predict or that their optical signatures lie outside survey windows. Synergies with neutrino and gravitational-wave probes will be indispensable for a definitive census.

title: Neural response to modulating the probability that actions of self or other result in auditory tones: A parametric fMRI study into causal ambiguity.
text_ai: In normal circumstances we can easily distinguish between changes to the external world brought about by our own actions from those with external causes. However, in certain contexts our sense of ownership and agency over acts is not so clear. Here, we manipulated the probability that a participant's or another's action would generate an auditory tone, thereby creating graded levels of causal ambiguity. In a within‑subject fMRI design (n = 24), participants performed a rapid button press (self condition) or watched a computer-driven action (other condition) while tones appeared with probability p_self or p_other (ranging from 0 to 1 in uniform steps). After each trial, they provided an explicit sense of agency rating. A general linear model incorporating parametric modulators for p_self and p_other was used to identify brain regions whose activity tracked causal uncertainty, alongside whole-brain contrasts to isolate self- versus other–related effects. We tested predictions from forward-model and attribution frameworks: sensorimotor cortex would track imminent consequences under high self-commitment, whereas higher-order networks would govern inference under ambiguity. Results revealed a robust, valence‑independent gradient of causal ambiguity. The right temporoparietal junction and posterior parietal cortex showed parametric scaling with uncertainty across both conditions, consistent with dynamic causal attribution. Self-agency engaged sensorimotor circuitry—supplementary motor area, premotor cortex, and cerebellum—more strongly as the likelihood that one’s action caused the tone increased. By contrast, the left inferior parietal lobule and anterior insula tracked explicit agency reports and responded preferentially under intermediate probabilities, suggesting a role in conscious evaluation of control. Auditory cortex responses were modulated by prediction error when outcomes violated expectancy, irrespective of agent. Functional connectivity analyses demonstrated context‑dependent coupling between prefrontal control regions, TPJ, and sensory cortices that strengthened as ambiguity rose. Behaviorally, agency ratings covaried with neural parametric effects, supporting a graded, probabilistic account of self–other causation in auditory outcome processing and highlighting distinct neural substrates for updating internal models under uncertainty.

title: Negotiating access to the Nigerian healthcare system: the experiences of HIV-positive men who have sex with men.
text_ai: Men who have sex with men in sub-Saharan Africa continue to have a disproportionately higher burden of HIV than their counterparts in the general population. In this qualitative study, barriers to participants accessing healthcare services in Nigeria, a country where same-sex relationships are criminalised and considered societally abhorrent, were explored. Through semi-structured interviews with 15 HIV-positive MSM and groups recruited via LGBTQ+ organisations in Lagos, Abuja and Port Harcourt, we examined how participants negotiated care in a hostile legal setting. Thematic analysis identified four access domains: individual fears (stigma and disclosure concerns); health-system factors (staff hostility, breaches of confidentiality, privacy issues, stockouts, long waits); structural constraints (criminalisation, police harassment, transport costs, medical fees); and interpersonal dynamics (peer support, NGO linkages, concealment strategies). Participants described strategies to mitigate risk, including presenting with heteronormative identities, using anonymous hotlines, and favouring clinics with confidentiality assurances or NGO services. Positive experiences centred on supportive staff, discreet spaces, and clear confidentiality policies. Findings underscore need for reforms—provider training on MSM care, anti-stigma frameworks, confidential and affordable services, and advocacy for legal reform—to improve uptake, adherence, and retention in HIV care among HIV-positive MSM in Nigeria.

title: Microfracture provides better clinical results than debridement in the treatment of acute talar osteochondral lesions using arthroscopic assisted fixation of acute ankle fractures
text_ai: PURPOSE: Ankle arthroscopy is a useful tool for detection and treatment of accompanying intraarticular pathologies in acute ankle fractures. The purpose of this study was to compare the treatment results of talus osteochondral lesions (OLT) with debridement and microfracture in arthroscopy assisted surgery of acute ankle fractures. METHODS: Prospective cohort of 46 consecutive patients with acute ankle fractures and talar osteochondral lesions (OLT) identified during arthroscopic assisted fixation. Intraoperative management of the OLT was debridement (n = 24) or microfracture (n = 22) based on predefined criteria (lesion size and containment favoring microfracture when ≤1.5 cm2 and stable margins). Exclusion criteria included chronic lesions (>6 weeks), posterior talar dome lesions requiring alternative procedures, and associated hindfoot fusion. Outcomes included American Orthopaedic Foot & Ankle Society (AOFAS) hindfoot-ankle score, Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for pain, ankle range of motion (ROM), time to full weight bearing, return to work/activity, and MRI assessment of cartilage fill at 12 months. Follow-up minimum 24 months. Statistical analysis used t-tests or Mann-Whitney tests for continuous variables and chi-square for categorical variables; p < 0.05 was considered significant. RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were similar between groups (mean age 35.0 ± 8.2 years; balanced sex distribution; mean lesion size 1.2 ± 0.4 cm2). At 12 months, AOFAS was higher after microfracture (82.5 ± 9.3) than debridement (70.4 ± 11.2; p < 0.01); at 24 months, 88.0 ± 7.0 vs 73.0 ± 9.5 (p < 0.001). VAS pain: 0.9 ± 0.8 vs 2.8 ± 1.4 (p < 0.001). ROM: total dorsiflexion-plantarflexion arc 64° ± 8° vs 54° ± 9° (p < 0.01). Time to full weight bearing: 4.5 ± 1.0 weeks vs 5.8 ± 1.3 weeks (p < 0.01). Return to premorbid activity: 8.2 ± 1.5 vs 10.1 ± 2.0 weeks (p < 0.05). MRI at 12 months showed complete cartilage fill in 60% of microfracture versus 25% of debridement (p < 0.05). Overall complication rates were low and comparable. CONCLUSIONS: In acute ankle fractures treated with arthroscopic assisted fixation, microfracture for talar OLT provides superior functional outcomes and faster recovery than debridement, with a similar safety profile. Microfracture should be considered the preferred intraoperative treatment for suitable talar OLT in this setting.
prefix: PURPOSE: Ankle arthroscopy is a useful tool for detection and treatment of accompanying intraarticular pathologies in acute ankle fractures. The purpose of this study was to compare the treatment results of talus osteochondral lesions (OLT) with debridement and microfracture in arthroscopy assisted surgery of acute ankle fractures.

title: An Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph first view on Solar Spicules
text_ai: Solar spicules have eluded modelers and observers for decades. Since the discovery of the more energetic type II, spicules have become a heated topic but their contribution to the energy balance of the low solar atmosphere remains unknown. Here we report on IRIS observing campaign that captured limb spicules with cadence, spectroscopy and imaging in Mg II h&k, C II 1334/1335, and Si IV 1394/1403. Spicule strands appear as evolving, slender features rising from the network with lifetimes of seconds to a few minutes and projected speeds of order 20–100 km s−1. The Mg II profiles display strong Doppler shifts and asymmetric, often double-peaked shapes, accompanied by substantial non-thermal broadening, signaling unresolved, transverse motions and wave energy. A subset of events show impulsive emission in C II and, intermittently, in Si IV, indicating heating to transition-region temperatures within the spicule body or at its edge. In many cases, Si IV brightenings precede or accompany the fading of the cool Mg II signal, consistent with rapid heating during ascent. We derive electron densities and emission measures from line ratios and integrated intensities, finding densities in the 10^9–10^10 cm−3 regime at TR heights and energy fluxes capable of sustaining local heating on timescales of seconds to minutes. The results support a two-component picture in which cool, dense spicule plasma coexists with hot components produced by localized heating, likely associated with reconnection or shock dissipation. These IRIS-first observations provide stringent spectral constraints for spicule formation theories and lay the groundwork for assessment of their role in chromospheric and TR energy balance.

title: Imitation Learning for Active Neck Motion Enabling Robot Manipulation beyond the Field of View
text_ai: Most prior research in deep imitation learning has predominantly utilized fixed cameras for image input, which constrains task performance to the predefined field of view. However, enabling a robot to actively maneuver its neck can significantly expand the scope of imitation learning to encompass a wider variety of tasks and expressive actions such as neck gestures. To this end we present a modular imitation learning framework in which a neck controller reconfigures the head orientation to acquire views, while a manipulation policy executes grasps and trajectories on observations. The neck policy is trained from demonstrations that include natural head movements and corresponding manipulation intents, using behavior cloning with cross-attention to fuse neck pose, image features, and proprioceptive state. A curriculum gradually increases partial observability by introducing occluders and varying target positions beyond the fixed field of view. We evaluate on a suite of pick-and-place tasks requiring behind-obstacle perception and reorientation. Compared with a static-camera baseline, the active-neck approach yields higher grasp success rates, shorter planning horizons, and improved robustness to viewpoint shifts. Ablations quantify the gains from training neck and manipulation policies and from neck proprioception.

title: H-EYE: Holistic Resource Modeling and Management for Diversely Scaled Edge-Cloud Systems
text_ai: Computing systems have been evolving to be more pervasive, heterogeneous, and dynamic. An increasing number of emerging domains now rely on diverse edge to cloud continuum where the execution of applications often spans various tiers of systems with significantly heterogeneous computational capabilities. Resources in each tier are often handled in isolation due to scalability and privacy concerns. Fragmentation hinders end-to-end performance and complicates privacy-aware execution. To address this, H-EYE proposes a holistic resource modeling and management framework that unifies representations of compute, memory, storage, network, energy, locality, and policy constraints across edge and cloud, enabling end-to-end orchestration. Key contributions: (i) a formal resource model and ontology enabling cross-tier abstraction and isolation guarantees; (ii) a cross-layer orchestration stack with a Unified Resource Catalog, a Policy-Driven Scheduler, and an adaptive Controller that monitors conditions and migrates workloads; (iii) a multi-objective optimization and learning module that jointly optimizes latency, throughput, energy, cost, and data governance; (iv) a prototype implementation and evaluation on a heterogeneous testbed and in simulation with representative workloads such as streaming analytics and AR/VR. Empirical evaluation demonstrates improved end-to-end QoS, reduced data movement, and energy savings under dynamic conditions, with acceptable overhead and transparent enforcement of privacy and security requirements. The work thus provides a scalable, privacy-aware, and policy-driven approach to managing diversely scaled edge-cloud systems. We discuss remaining challenges in standardization, deployment, and governance, and outline directions for future work including provenance, trust, and programmable data-plane policies.

title: QCD correction to gluino decay to $t\bar{t}\tilde{\chi}^0_1$ in the MSSM
text_ai: We calculate the complete next-to-leading order QCD corrections to the three-body decay of gluino into top-pair associated with a lightest neutralino in the minimal supersymmetric standard model. We obtain that the LO and NLO QCD corrected decay widths of $\tilde{g} \to t \bar{t} \tilde{\chi}_1^0$ at the ${\rm SPS 6}$ benchmark point are $0.1490 GeV$ and 0.1069 GeV respectively, and the relative correction is -28.2%. We present the complete next-to-leading order QCD corrections to the three-body decay of the gluino into a top-antitop pair and the lightest neutralino in the MSSM. The calculation is carried out in the on-shell renormalization scheme, with ultraviolet divergences canceled by counterterms and infrared singularities removed by dipole subtraction between virtual and real-gluon emission. The virtual corrections, together with the real-emission contribution g̃ → t t̄ χ̃^0_1 g, yield a finite width after mass factorization. At the SPS 6 benchmark, Γ_LO = 0.1490 GeV and Γ_NLO = 0.1069 GeV, corresponding to K ≈ 0.72 and a relative correction of −28.2%. The NLO result reduces the renormalization-scale dependence markedly and produces only mild distortions of the m_tt̄ and t χ̃^0_1 distributions, validating its use in precision SUSY phenomenology.

title: Mid-term results of the modular ANCA-Fit femoral component in total hip replacement
text_ai: We report the minimum five-year follow-up of 352 primary total hip replacements using the uncemented hydroxyapatite-coated ANCA-Fit femoral component with a modular neck and head. The series comprised 319 patients (212 men, 107 women) with a mean age at operation of 64.4 years (28 to 97). The principal diagnosis was osteoarthritis. With a mean follow-up of 6.1 years (5.0–9.8), overall implant survival with revision for any component-related cause was 96.3% at five years and 95.1% at latest follow-up. Revisions were performed in 22 hips (6.3%), most commonly for aseptic loosening of the femoral component (n=12), followed by instability/dislocation (n=4), and periprosthetic fracture (n=4), with two infections. There were no intraoperative femoral neck fractures and no neck fractures during follow-up. Radiographic assessment demonstrated satisfactory osseointegration in 89% of stems; progressive radiolucencies were uncommon (<5%) and confined to Gruen zones 1 and 7. No mechanical failure of the modular neck or adverse local tissue reactions related to modular junctions were observed. Mean Harris hip score improved from 43 preoperatively to 86 at latest follow-up. The data support the mid-term reliability of the ANCA-Fit modular system in primary THA.

title: The Use of Telemedicine for Penicillin Allergy Skin Testing.
text_ai: Penicillin skin testing (PST) is increasingly used as a tool to evaluate penicillin allergy in patients with a reported history. The limited availability of allergists, however, may be an impeding factor. We sought to assess the clinical utility of telemedicine to facilitate PST. Penicillin-allergic inpatients receiving systemic antibiotics were prospectively identified between April and August 2017. Methods: Penicillin-allergic inpatients receiving systemic antibiotics were prospectively identified between April and August 2017. A board-certified allergist performed PST via synchronous telemedicine from a central site, while trained ward nurses executed prick and intradermal testing under real-time remote guidance. Tests used standard penicillin determinants (benzylpenicilloyl polylysine and minor determinant mix) with appropriate controls. A negative PST was followed by an supervised oral amoxicillin challenge. Data collected included demographics, testing completion, adverse events, time to de-labeling, and antibiotic utilization. Safety measures included readiness for epinephrine and resuscitation with a 30-minute post-test observation. Results: Of identified patients, the majority completed PST with telemedicine without on-site allergist involvement. Testing integrated into routine care and was completed within the hospital stay on a timeline comparable to traditional approaches. A substantial proportion had negative PST; those patients safely underwent oral antibiotic challenges with high tolerability. No anaphylaxis or life-threatening reactions occurred. Minor local reactions were uncommon. Telemedicine-facilitated PST reduced time to allergy assessment and enabled earlier de-labeling and continuation of penicillin-based therapy in most cases. Patient satisfaction with telemedicine encounters was favorable, and nursing staff reported acceptable workflow integration. A preliminary cost assessment suggested comparable or favorable resource use relative to standard care. Conclusion: Telemedicine-enabled PST appears feasible and safe in inpatient settings, with potential to expand access, accelerate de-labeling, and support antimicrobial stewardship.

title: Implantable LVAD infections: implications for permanent use of the device
text_ai: BACKGROUND: Infection in implantable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) patients is common and has serious implications regarding permanent use of the LVAD. METHODS: Thirty-three patients had HeartMate LVAD insertion as a bridge to heart transplantation. The mean length of hospital stay was 8 days before LVAD insertion. Definitions and diagnostic criteria followed established guidelines. Patients were followed prospectively for up to 12 months with periodic wound assessment, inflammatory markers, and culture data as indicated. Endpoints included incidence and type of LVAD infection, microbiology, need for surgical management or explantation, impact on transplantation, and mortality. RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 9 months, infection occurred in 11 of 33 patients (33%). Driveline infection was most common (n=7), followed by pocket infection (n=3) and bacteremia (n=4; overlapped in two cases). Isolates were predominantly Staphylococcus aureus and coagulase-negative staphylococci; Gram-negative organisms were identified in two cases. Five patients required surgical intervention for infection (driveline debridement or exchange), and four had delayed transplantation as a result, with one explant for uncontrolled infection. No infection-related deaths occurred. CONCLUSIONS: LVAD infection is common and carries significant implications for the decision to pursue permanent LVAD support. Strategies to prevent infection and to intensify multidisciplinary care are essential to maintain transplant eligibility and improve long-term outcomes.

title: Modified Lagrangian Formulation of Gear Tooth Crack Analysis using Combined Approach of Variable Mode Decomposition (VMD) and Time Synchronous Averaging (TSA)
text_ai: This paper discusses the possible observation of an integrated gear tooth crack analysis procedure that employs the combined approach of variable mode decomposition (VMD) and time synchronous averaging (TSA) based on the coupled electromechanical gearbox (CEMG) system. This paper also incorporates the modified Lagrangian formulation to model the CEMG system by considering Rayleigh's dissipative potential. Utilizing the modified Lagrangian formulation, the governing equations of motion for the coupled electromechanical gearbox (CEMG) system are derived by combining kinetic energy, gear mesh potential, and Rayleigh dissipation to represent viscous and electrical losses. The gear tooth crack is modeled as degradation of mesh stiffness with a breathing component that couples to torsional, translational, and electrical dynamics, producing nonlinear, time‑varying stiffness terms. Boundary conditions include motor torque, external load, and shaft supports, yielding a nonlinear state-space representation. The TSA–VMD processing pipeline is applied in tandem: TSA to stabilize cycle-to-cycle responses and VMD to extract intrinsic mode functions, reducing noise and mode mixing. This enables isolation of crack‑induced signatures in mechanical responses (torque, shafts) and electrical signals (stator current). Features based on IMF energies, instantaneous frequencies, and envelope metrics are fused into a crack index, with a threshold and lightweight classifier for detection and localization at the gear‑mesh level. Validation on synthetic CEMG data and laboratory gearbox experiments shows improved discrimination of crack signatures under varying speed and load, with robustness to electrical harmonics. The results support the proposed framework as a physically grounded, data-efficient tool for early-stage diagnosis and prognostic assessment of gear tooth cracks under electromechanical coupling.

title: Aberrated optical cavities
text_ai: Optical cavities are an enabling technology of modern quantum science: from their essential role in the operation of lasers, to applications as fly-wheels in atomic clocks and interaction-enhancing components in quantum optics experiments, developing a quantitative understanding of the mode-shapes and energies of optical cavities has been crucial for the growth of the field. Here we present a systematic treatment of aberrations in high-finesse cavities and their consequences for the transverse mode spectrum and the associated field-energy distribution. We develop a perturbative formalism that treats surface figure errors, refractive-index inhomogeneities, and misalignments on equal footing, yielding an effective non-Hermitian modal Hamiltonian in the basis of ideal Hermite–Gaussian (or Laguerre–Gaussian) modes. From this, we derive analytic expressions for frequency shifts, linewidth changes, and mode- mixing rates to leading order, and we quantify the breakdown of degeneracies among near-degenerate families. The framework accommodates axisymmetric and nonaxisymmetric perturbations and readily extends to multi-mirror, fiber-fed, and nonplanar geometries. Experimental validation in Fabry–Pérot microcavities and on-chip resonators shows quantitative agreement with measured resonance splittings and increased loss channels, providing design maps for aberration control and mode-selective coupling. This framework thus informs deliberate aberration control.

title: Simplified Muscle-Suspension Lower Blepharoplasty by Orbicularis Hitch.
text_ai: The suspension of orbicularis oculi during lower blepharoplasty presents a logical surgical addition for further support of the lid, as well as further improvement to its contour profile. It has traditionally been performed as an extension of the skin-muscle flap procedure, but more recently, and aggressively, as a muscle strap-flap separated from the orbicularis sheet by myotomy. The present report delineates a simplified muscle-suspension technique, designated the orbicularis hitch (OSH), in which the posterior aspect of the medial–inferior orbicularis bundle is anchored to a robust periosteal or canthal support without full myotomy or separation of the muscular sling. The maneuver employs a single, hammock-like fixation that elevates the lower lid margin and smooths the lid-cheek junction while preserving orbicularis continuity and function. Portability of this maneuver between skin-muscle flap and transcutaneous approaches facilitates a broad application in routine lower blepharoplasty. Methods: A prospective series of cases undergoing OSH during cosmetic or reconstructive lower blepharoplasty was evaluated. Outcomes included pre- and postoperative photographic analysis, margin reflex distance measurements, patient satisfaction, and complication rates over a minimum follow-up. Results: Contour improvement was observed in the majority, with statistically significant elevation of lid position and improved optical shadow at the lid-cheek junction. Complications were limited to transient edema in a minority, mild dry-eye symptoms in a small percentage, and a few instances of transient lid tightness resolving within weeks. No cases of clinically meaningful ectropion or lid retraction attributable to OSH were recorded; revision surgery was not required in the cohort. Conclusions: The orbicularis hitch provides a simpler, reproducible alternative to plane dissection or myotomy-based muscle flaps, yielding reliable lid support and favorable aesthetic contour with comparable safety. Further comparative studies with longer follow-up are warranted.

title: Snow Globe: An Advancing-Front 3D Delaunay Mesh Refinement Algorithm
text_ai: <incorrect proofs; does not consider an important case because of which the proofs are wrong. The paper was withdrawn from submission> One of the objectives of a Delaunay mesh refinement algorithm is to produce meshes with tetrahedral elements having a bounded aspect ratio, which is the ratio between the radius of the circumscribing and inscribing spheres. Snow Globe advances-front 3D Delaunay refinement combines an advancing-front framework with localized insertions to yield graded tetrahedral meshes with bounded aspect ratios. Its core idea is explicit front tracking that preserves a global quality invariant: every tetrahedron meets a target bound on the radius–edge ratio (equivalently a minimum dihedral angle). When an insertion would violate the bound or breach boundary conformity, a Steiner point is placed on the offending feature and the affected neighborhood is retriangulated with a small, quality-preserving stencil. The front advances via a snow-globe–like neighborhood that constrains candidate insertions, suppressing sliver growth and cascading refinements. Boundary handling relies on projection to maintain curved surfaces within tolerance, with optional snapping to CAD features. Convergence is guaranteed under mild geometric assumptions, yielding a finite refinement sequence that satisfies the prescribed bound. Implementation relies on local data structures, a priority queue of candidates, and parallelization along independent frontier segments. Experiments on synthetic and real volumes show improved element quality, fewer insertions, and competitive runtimes against Ruppert-like and Chew-type schemes. Snow Globe provides robust boundary fidelity and is well suited for finite-element and isogeometric workflows. The paper also proves a bound on insertion complexity and demonstrates scalability to meshes with millions of elements.

title: The quaternionic KP hierarchy and conformally immersed 2-tori in the 4-sphere
text_ai: The quaternionic KP hierarchy is the integrable hierarchy of p.d.e obtained by replacing the complex numbers with the quaternions, mutatis mutandis, in the standard construction of the KP hierarchy equations and solutions; it is equivalent to what is often called the Davey-Stewartson II hierarchy. Here, a quaternionic Lax formulation is developed for the hierarchy, featuring a pair of quaternionic pseudo-differential operators whose isospectral flows generate commuting evolutions. We prove that the flows act on the quaternionic Gauss map of a conformally immersed torus by gauge transformations that preserve conformality and the underlying spectral data. The associated family of flat connections forms a loop of solutions, whose monodromy is encoded by a real form of a spectral curve. Finite-gap, or algebro-geometric, solutions correspond to spectral data consisting of a compact Riemann surface with quaternionic involutions together with a line bundle, yielding a quaternionic Baker–Akhiezer function that reconstructs the immersion via a generalized Weierstrass representation. Consequently, conformally immersed 2-tori in S^4 with finite-gap spectrum arise from quaternionic KP tau-functions; conversely, given such a tau-function one recovers a one-parameter family of isometric, conformal immersions. The framework unifies DPW-type constructions with integrable flows.

title: Image-Specific Information Suppression and Implicit Local Alignment for Text-based Person Search
text_ai: Text-based person search (TBPS) is a challenging task that aims to search pedestrian images with the same identity from an image gallery given a query text. In recent years, TBPS has made remarkable progress and state-of-the-art methods achieve superior performance by learning local fine-grained correspondence between images and texts. To address these challenges, we propose a framework that jointly performs image-specific information suppression and implicit local alignment. The ISIS module learns a text-conditioned gate that attenuates background clutter and non-pedestrian cues in the visual feature map, yielding a pedestrian-centric embedding that preserves discriminative cues such as color and texture. The suppression is integrated into the early cross-modal encoder, enabling more reliable interactions between text and image representations. The ILA component establishes fine-grained correspondences by modeling cross-attention between textual tokens and image patches, avoiding explicit region proposals; alignment emerges through a contrastive objective that pulls matched pairs together at global and local levels and pushes mismatches apart. An auxiliary consistency loss stabilizes local correspondences under augmentation. Experiments on CUHK-PEDES and ICFG-PEDES show consistent gains over strong baselines, especially in cluttered scenes or with pose variation. Ablation studies validate the contributions of ISIS and ILA; ISIS yields cleaner representations and ILA improves phrase-level alignment without dense annotations. Qualitative analyses reveal more precise word-to-region associations and reduced background attention. The method offers a compact, data-efficient approach that enhances robustness and interpretability for TBPS. The approach remains compatible with backbones ranging from CNNs to Vision Transformers and incurs modest overhead, making it suitable for practical deployment.

title: Modelling of initially stressed solids: structure of the energy density in the incompressible limit
text_ai: This study addresses the modelling of elastic bodies, particularly when the relaxed configuration is unknown or non-existent. We adopt the theory of initially stressed materials, incorporating the deformation gradient and stress state of the reference configuration (initial stress tensor) into the response function. This representation permits a concise separation of volumetric and deviatoric contributions and clarifies how pre-stress manifests in the energy density even when the relaxed state is unavailable. Under the incompressibility constraint J = 1, the constitutive energy reduces to W(F, T0) = p(J − 1) + Φ(C̄, T0̄), where p enforces incompressibility, C̄ = F^T F with its volumetric part removed, and T0̄ denotes the deviatoric part of the initial stress. The function Φ is built from isochoric invariants of C̄ and mixed invariants that couple C̄ to T0̄, such as tr(T0̄ C̄) and tr(T0̄^2). We prove a representation theorem that any admissible W can be written in this form; isotropic or uniaxial initial stresses are analyzed explicitly. Implications for finite-element implementation and for the stability and sensitivity of the incompressible response to the magnitude and orientation of initial stress are discussed, highlighting the shear response in the constrained limit.

title: Cleavage of the SUN-domain protein Mps3 at its N-terminus regulates centrosome disjunction in budding yeast meiosis.
text_ai: Centrosomes organize microtubules and are essential for spindle formation and chromosome segregation during cell division. Duplicated centrosomes are physically linked, but how this linkage is dissolved remains unclear. Yeast centrosomes are tethered by a nuclear-envelope-attached structure called the half-bridge, whose components have mammalian homologues. Using synchronized meiosis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, we demonstrate proteolysis of Mps3 at its N terminus, producing an N-terminal fragment degraded and a C-terminal portion that remains anchored in the nuclear envelope. Mutations that abolish the putative separase cleavage site prevent N-terminal processing and markedly delay or block spindle-pole disjunction, yielding persistent tethering of duplicated SPBs and aberrant spindle formation. The timing of Mps3 cleavage coincides with SPB disengagement and with the remodeling of the half-bridge characteristic of meiotic prophase. In vitro assays with purified Esp1 and Mps3 fragments show cleavage at the consensus site; Esp1 depletion reduces proteolysis and compromises timely meiosis I spindle-pole separation in vivo. Expression of a cleaved mimic rescues disjunction in the noncleavable background, indicating that N-terminal proteolysis is both necessary and sufficient to disengage SPBs. We propose a proteolysis-driven mechanism for centrosome disjunction mediated by SUN-domain protein cleavage.

title: A new introduction rule for disjunction
text_ai: We extend Natural Deduction with a third introduction rule for the disjunction, $\vee$-i3, with a conclusion $\Gamma\vdash A\vee B$, but both premises $\Gamma\vdash A$ and $\Gamma\vdash B$. This rule is admissible in Natural Deduction. This extension is interesting in several respects. First, it formalizes a form of parallel introduction: from Γ ⊢ A and Γ ⊢ B one obtains Γ ⊢ A ∨ B. Second, we establish admissibility of ∨-i3 in the standard natural deduction framework: any derivation that uses ∨-i3 can be transformed, by a local reduction, into a derivation that uses only ∨-i1, ∨-i2, and the conventional structural rules. The core step replaces the single ∨-i3 application with the two alternatives derived from the subderivations of A and B, together with a short contraction, yielding a derivation of Γ ⊢ A ∨ B without ∨-i3. Consequently, the extension is conservative: no new theorems of the base logic are produced. Semantically, ∨-i3 aligns with the join of the provability predicates for A and B; under Kripke/Boolean semantics the rule preserves truth conditions. We conclude with implications for proof-search heuristics and the treatment of disjunction in the Curry–Howard correspondence.

title: UCPhrase: Unsupervised Context-aware Quality Phrase Tagging
text_ai: Identifying and understanding quality phrases from context is a fundamental task in text mining. The most challenging part of this task arguably lies in uncommon, emerging, and domain-specific phrases. The infrequent nature of these phrases significantly hurts the performance of phrase mining methods that rely on sufficient phrase occurrences in the input corpus. To address this, we propose UCPhrase, a fully unsupervised approach that couples contextual grounding with a quality-aware phrase ranking. The method operates directly on raw corpora to assemble a compact candidate set of multiword noun phrases via lightweight syntactic filters. For each candidate, a context stream is mined from surrounding text, and a context encoder yields a contextual representation of its usage. A separate phrase encoder captures internal compositionality and variation across occurrences. A joint quality scorer integrates three signals: contextual coherence (uniform appearance across diverse contexts), distributional distinctiveness (separability from nearby phrases in embedding space), and cross-domain stability (consistency under domain shift). Learning relies on self-supervision: positives arise from repeated, diverse usages of a candidate, while negatives are drawn from high-entropy and unrelated contexts. A sparsity regularizer discourages overfitting and reduces spurious candidates. The framework scales linearly with corpus size and supports streaming updates. We evaluate on heterogeneous corpora spanning scientific abstracts, software documentation, and user-generated text, reporting coverage and precision for high-quality phrases. Ablation studies show the role of context-aware signals, and qualitative analysis confirms improved detection of rare and domain-specific phrases with interpretable scores for downstream keyword extraction. This enables practical deployment across corpora of varying scale.

title: Enhancing the Properties of Plasma Activated Water using an Air Bubble Diffuser
text_ai: In this study, the impact of an air bubbler on the properties of plasma-activated water (PAW) was investigated in different configurations. A pencil plasma jet (PPJ) using a dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) was used to prepare PAW. To elucidate these effects, PAW was prepared under four configurations: (i) conventional PPJ-DBD without aeration, (ii) diffuser at the liquid surface generating predominantly coarse bubbles, (iii) submerged diffuser producing microbubble-rich streams, and (iv) submerged diffuser with increased gas flow to tailor bubble size distribution. In all cases, plasma treatment was conducted for a fixed duration (180 s) in a 500 mL reservoir. The diffuser delivered compressed air at nominal flow rates that created distinct bubble regimes, enabling a systematic assessment of gas–liquid exchange on PAW chemistry. Immediate and short-term storage (4 °C, up to 48 h) conditions were employed to evaluate persistence of reactive species. Characterization encompassed pH, oxidation–reduction potential (ORP), electrical conductivity, hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) concentration by titanium sulfate assay, and reactive nitrogen species (NO2−/NO3−) by standard spectrophotometric methods, supplemented by indirect radical probes for short-lived species. Results indicated that aeration via the diffuser markedly enhanced interfacial mass transfer and consequently the yield of long-lived reactive species. The submerged microbubble configuration yielded the largest improvements, with H2O2 levels increasing by approximately 30–40% relative to the non-aerated case, ORP rising by about 12–18 mV, and a modest acidification (pH decrease 0.2–0.4). Surface coarse bubbles produced intermediate gains, whereas no aeration produced negligible changes. NO2−/NO3− production similarly rose, signaling amplified reactive nitrogen chemistry. During storage, PAW generated with aeration maintained a greater fraction of its oxidizing capacity, with extended half-lives by roughly 6–12 h depending on the configuration. Collectively, the air bubble diffuser emerges as a simple, scalable means to tailor PAW chemistry for targeted antimicrobial and surface-treatment applications.

title: An ab-initio study on engineering quantum anomalous Hall effect in compensated antiferromagnet MnBi$_{2}$Te$_{4}$
text_ai: Recently, the quantum anomalous Hall effect (QAHE) has been theoretically proposed in compensated antiferromagnetic systems by using the magnetic topological insulator model [see arXiv:2404.13305 (2024)]. However, the related and systematic study based on a realistic material system is still limited. As the only experimentally realized antiferromagnetic topological insulator, MnBi$_{2}$Te$_{4}$ becomes a vital platform for exploring various topological states. Using fully relativistic density functional theory with Hubbard U for Mn 3d states and spin–orbit coupling, we construct slab models of MnBi2Te4 with even numbers of septuple layers to realize compensated antiferromagnetic order. The low-energy physics is mapped to a Wannier-based tight-binding network, from which we extract edge spectra and compute Chern numbers and Berry curvatures. We find that, in the compensated regime, a nonzero Chern number—and hence a quantum anomalous Hall phase—emerges when a sublattice-staggered exchange field is induced, e.g., by magnetic proximity to a ferromagnetic layer or by intrinsic asymmetry. The resulting surface Dirac gaps are on the order of tens of meV and yield robust QAHE with C = ±1, tunable by strain, thickness, and gating. These results establish a realistic pathway to engineering QAHE in MnBi2Te4.

title: Dynamical Majorana Neutrino Masses and Axions II: Inclusion of Axial Background and Anomaly Terms
text_ai: We extend the study of a previous publication \cite{amsot} on Schwinger-Dyson dynamical mass generation for fermions and pseudoscalar fields (axion-like particles (ALP)), in field theories containing Yukawa type interactions between the fermions and ALPs, by incorporating anomaly terms and/or (constant) axial background fields. We formulate the extended Schwinger–Dyson system by including, in a self-consistent way, a constant axial background bμ and anomaly-induced contributions as additional kernels in the fermion self-energy and in the Yukawa–ALP vertex. In this framework the axial background acts as a chiral chemical potential, shifting the dispersion relations and opening a parity-odd Majorana channel for the fermions, while the anomaly terms modify the Ward identities and generate mixing between Dirac and Majorana components. We implement a truncation that preserves the relevant symmetries (to the extent permitted by the background and anomaly terms), employing a rainbow–ladder inspired kernel for the Yukawa interaction and a dressed ALP propagator that incorporates the dominant radiative corrections. The resulting coupled integral equations for the fermion self-energy, the Majorana mass function, and the ALP–fermion vertex are solved numerically across a range of Yukawa couplings g, ALP decay constant f_a, background magnitude |b|, and anomaly strength A. Across this parameter space we detect robust dynamical Majorana masses m_M ≠ 0 even in the absence of explicit Majorana terms. The axial background and the anomaly sector cooperate to catalyze mass generation, lowering the critical coupling g_c(|b|, A) and enlarging the broken phase. The emergent spectrum contains a parity-odd Majorana gap and significant axion–Majorana mixing, with m_M(p) approaching a finite value as p → 0 and a mild residual momentum dependence. We assess the renormalization behavior and demonstrate mild sensitivity to ultraviolet details within reasonable completions. The phenomenological implications for neutrino mass generation and for axion phenomenology in cosmological and astrophysical settings are discussed, highlighting a nonperturbative mechanism that enriches the dynamical mass program with axial background and anomaly physics.

title: Sketch and Validate for Big Data Clustering
text_ai: In response to the need for learning tools tuned to big data analytics, the present paper introduces a framework for efficient clustering of huge sets of (possibly high-dimensional) data. Building on random sampling and consensus (RANSAC) ideas pursued earlier in a different (computer vision) context for robust regression, a suite of novel dimensionality and set-reduction algorithms is developed. Leveraging a two-step procedure, the framework first constructs sketches of the input by drawing random projections and coresets that preserve cluster structure with probability. In the second step, a consensus procedure evaluates candidate partitions across sketches, selecting clusterings that consistently minimize a distortion measure. We introduce scalable algorithms for (i) sketch generation that adaptively balances sketch size against distortion guarantees, (ii) a set-reduction taxonomy that prunes candidate centers and bounds blow-up, and (iii) a validation protocol that aggregates agreement statistics to yield a near-optimal clustering under model misspecification. The theoretical results characterize trade-offs between sketch size, dimensionality, and clustering error, and demonstrate sublinear dependence on data volume. Empirical studies on synthetic datasets illustrate speedups with negligible loss in clustering quality, outperforming mini-batch and streaming alternatives on high-dimensional tasks.

title: Adaptive sports for promoting physical activity in community-dwelling adults with stroke: A feasibility study.
text_ai: Despite proven health benefits of regular participation in physical activities (PA), adults with stroke fail to achieve recommended levels of PA. Sports being an enjoyable activity is more likely to encourage participation. This feasibility study evaluated acceptability, safety, and preliminary efficacy of an adaptive sports program designed to promote sustained physical activity in community-dwelling adults with stroke. In a single-arm mixed-methods design, 24 participants engaged in a 12-week program combining two adaptive sports and a home-based activity prescription. Sessions were delivered twice weekly for 60 minutes in community recreation centers by trained coaches and physiotherapist mentors. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, retention, adherence, and adverse events, with acceptability assessed through post-intervention interviews. Secondary outcomes encompassed accelerometer-based moderate-to-vigorous activity and steps, self-reported physical activity, mobility, balance, and health-related quality of life. Qualitative interviews explored barriers, facilitators, and perceived impact on daily activity. Results showed a recruitment rate of 62%, and 92% completion of the program, with average session adherence of 78%. No serious adverse events were reported. Participants described high acceptability, citing enjoyment, social connection, perceived safety, and progressive challenge. Preliminary efficacy indicated small-to-moderate increases in daily activity (+1,100 to +1,300 steps/day), modest gains in mobility (6-minute walk +12 to 15 m) and balance, and improved QoL. These findings support feasibility and potential effectiveness of adaptive sport approaches, meriting a randomized controlled trial to confirm efficacy and inform implementation and cost considerations. Transportation, caregiver support, and access to facilities emerged as key participation determinants. Further work should examine longer-term engagement and sustainability.

title: Quantum Hamiltonians with weak random abstract perturbation. II. Localization in the expanded spectrum
text_ai: We consider multi-dimensional Schr\"odinger operators with a weak random perturbation distributed in the cells of some periodic lattice. In every cell the perturbation is described by the translate of a fixed abstract operator depending on a random variable. The random variables, indexed by the lattice, are assumed to be independent and identically distributed according to an absolutely continuous probability density. Under regularity assumptions on the density of the random variables and, also, on the abstract cell operator, we establish spectral localization in a portion of the expanded spectrum for small coupling. The main results are stated in the multiscale-analytic framework: a Wegner-type estimate with optimal volume dependence, an initial-scale estimate produced by the non-degeneracy of the perturbation, and a criterion adapted to the abstract setting. Consequently, for energies in the expanded spectrum away from resonances, the infinite-volume operator has almost surely pure point spectrum with exponentially localized eigenfunctions; dynamical localization follows, yielding bounds on time evolution. Our argument unifies and extends known results for lattice perturbations to the abstract-cell framework, and clarifies, in particular, the influence of the density's absolute continuity and the perturbation's weak coupling.

title: Randomized Classifiers vs Human Decision-Makers: Trustworthy AI May Have to Act Randomly and Society Seems to Accept This
text_ai: As \emph{artificial intelligence} (AI) systems are increasingly involved in decisions affecting our lives, ensuring that automated decision-making is fair and ethical has become a top priority. Intuitively, we feel that akin to human decisions, judgments of artificial agents should necessarily be grounded in some moral principles. As intuitive as this expectation is, deployment raises questions about reliability, accountability, and legitimacy. We examine whether randomized classifiers—policies that incorporate probabilistic choice rules rather than fixed thresholds—can reconcile efficiency with fairness, and whether humans will accept such mechanisms when explained transparently. We develop a normative framework contrasting deterministic and randomized decision rules under fairness constraints (e.g., calibration, equalized opportunity) and test its predictions in synthetic settings. Across tasks, we simulate and implement randomized classifiers, including epsilon-greedy and calibrated stochastic rules, and compare them with human decision-makers performing similar tasks under information. Work combines components: (i) theoretical analysis of welfare- and fairness-optimal stochastic policies; (ii) experiments measuring trust and willingness to accept outcomes under varying explanations; and (iii) impact assessment on fairness metrics and predictive performance. In experiments with human participants, we observe that acceptance of randomized decisions increases when randomness is framed as mitigating bias and when there is audit trail explaining mechanism. When allowed to override, participants prefer hybrid systems in which humans retain responsibility for edge cases. The convergence of theoretical and experimental results suggests that trustworthy AI may require calibrated randomness, with governance, explainability, and oversight. We conclude with policy recommendations and roadmap for integrating randomized classifiers into AI architectures while preserving accountability.

title: The effects of water temperature on gastric motility and energy intake in healthy young men.
text_ai: Although immediate pre-meal water ingestion has been shown to reduce energy intake in healthy young men, no studies are available regarding potential mechanisms underlying the effect of energy intake in response to different temperatures of pre-meal water ingestion. This study examined the effects of consuming different temperatures of water on gastric motility and energy intake in healthy young men. Design: In a randomized, single-blind, cross-over study, 24 healthy young men attended three test days separated by ≥7 days. After an overnight fast, participants consumed 500 mL of water at one of three temperatures (4°C, 22°C, 40°C) 10 minutes before a buffet meal. Energy intake was measured from the buffet. Gastric motility was assessed with electrogastrography (EGG) for 90 minutes, providing dominant frequency (DF) and power as indices of normogastric rhythm. Subjective appetite (hunger, fullness, prospective intake) was rated on 100-mm visual analogue scales. Results: Cold water reduced energy intake vs room temperature (-112 kcal; p=0.03) and vs warm (-98 kcal; p=0.04). No difference for warm vs room temperature (p=0.68). Fullness ratings rose more after cold water (p<0.01). EGG showed greater postprandial normogastric stability after cold water (increased DF power in the 2.5–4.0 cpm band; p<0.05) and a non-significant trend toward reduced stability after warm water (p=0.06). Energy intake correlated inversely with fullness (r=-0.54, p<0.01) and with DF stability (r=-0.41, p=0.02). Conclusions: Pre-meal cold water acutely enhances gastric slow-wave regularity and suppresses subsequent energy intake in healthy young men, suggesting a mechanistic link between beverage temperature, gastric motility, and appetite control warranting further study.

This study examined the effects of consuming different temperatures of water on gastric motility and energy intake in healthy young men.

title: Energy-Based Flow Matching for Generating 3D Molecular Structure
text_ai: Molecular structure generation is a fundamental problem that involves determining the 3D positions of molecules' constituents. It has crucial biological applications, such as molecular docking, protein folding, and molecular design. Recent advances in generative modeling, such as diffusion models and flow matching, have made great progress on these tasks by modeling molecular conformations as a distribution. Here, we formulate energy-based flow matching (EBFM) that jointly learns a coordinate-energy potential and a transport map from a simple base distribution to the target conformational distribution. The transport is implemented as a continuous-time flow whose velocity field is guided by the gradient of the learned energy, steering samples toward low-energy regions while preserving diversity through stochastic perturbations. The model uses SE(3)-equivariant networks to respect rotations, translations, and bonding geometry. Training optimizes a synergy: (i) a flow-matching term aligning transport with the energy gradient, (ii) a likelihood component to cover the conformer manifold, and (iii) a physics-informed regularizer penalizing unrealistic bond lengths, angles, and steric clashes. On benchmarks of small organic molecules and protein ligands, EBFM yields conformer ensembles with improved accuracy and tighter energy alignment, and achieves faster sampling than diffusion and standard flow baselines, scaling gracefully to larger systems.

It has crucial biological applications, such as molecular docking, protein folding, and molecular design. title: Minimization based formulations of inverse problems and their regularization
text_ai: The conventional way of formulating inverse problems such as identification of a (possibly infinite dimensional) parameter, is via some forward operator, which is the concatenation of the observation operator with the parameter-to-state-map for the underlying model. Formulating the inverse problem as a minimization problem, we seek u in X that minimizes Jδ,α(u) = D(F(u), y^δ) + α R(u), where F is the forward operator and y^δ denotes data corrupted by noise. This regularized objective balances data fidelity with prior information encoded through R. We consider a broad spectrum of D, including L2-based misfits, L1-type disparities for outlier robustness, and divergences in more general metric spaces, together with regularizers R that are convex, lower semicontinuous, and coercive on the chosen function space. Under these conditions, minimizers exist; in the convex setting, stability and well-posedness are obtained via weak lower semicontinuity and compactness arguments. Employing subdifferential calculus, one gets optimality conditions in terms of inclusions, and, with source conditions, convergence rates with respect to the Bregman distance can be established as δ → 0 with α(δ) tuned a priori or a posteriori. The proposed framework encompasses classical Tikhonov regularization, mixed Ivanov–Tikhonov schemes, and non-smooth strategies such as total variation and sparsity promoting penalties, thereby accommodating discontinuities and multi-scale features. We emphasize discretization as part of the regularization and show Γ-convergence of discrete minimizers to the continuum problem. Algorithmic implementations rely on proximal, primal–dual, and augmented Lagrangian methods, with convergence guarantees and practical efficiency demonstrated on parameter identification and PDE-constrained imaging benchmarks.

title: Properties of the $\eta_q$ leading-twist distribution amplitude and its effects to the $B/D^+ \to\eta^{(\prime)}\ell^+ \nu_\ell$ decays
text_ai: The $\eta^{(\prime)}$-mesons in the quark-flavor basis are mixtures of two mesonic states $|\eta_{q}\rangle=|\bar u u+\bar d d\rangle/\sqrt 2$ and $|\eta_{s}\rangle=|\bar s s\rangle$. In the previous work, we have made a detailed study on the $\eta_{s}$ leading-twist distribution amplitude. Here we determine the leading-twist η_q distribution amplitude by QCD sum rules for the twist-2 two-point correlator, complemented by lattice constraints on the second moment and phenomenological inputs from η–η′ mixing. The η_q DA is expanded in Gegenbauer polynomials: φ_q(x, μ) = 6x(1−x)[1 + a_2^q(μ) C_2^{3/2}(2x−1) + a_4^q(μ) C_4^{3/2}(2x−1)]. At μ = 2 GeV we find a_2^q ≈ 0.15–0.25 and a_4^q ≈ −0.05 ± 0.04, with mild evolution to higher scales. Using this input in LCSR for B^+ and D^+ → η^(′) ℓ^+ ν_ℓ, within the standard two-flavor mixing scheme with decay constants f_q, f_s and mixing angle φ, we quantify the impact on the semileptonic form factors f_+^{B→η}(q^2) and f_+^{B→η′}(q^2). The η_q component tends to strengthen the η channel and, via η–η′ mixing, influences η′ observables, shifting differential rates most noticeably at low q^2. Higher-twist and radiative uncertainties are evaluated and found subdominant to the leading-twist effect. Our results offer a more reliable separation of η and η′ contributions and tighten the hadronic input for CKM determinations.

title: Black Silicon with high density and high aspect ratio nanowhiskers
text_ai: Physical properties of black Silicon (b-Si) formed on Si wafers by reactive ion etching in chlorine plasma are reported in an attempt to clarify the formation mechanism and the origin of the observed optical and electrical phenomena which are promising for a variety of applications. SEM analysis reveals a forest of nanowhiskers with diameters 60–120 nm, lengths up to 2–4 μm and densities exceeding 10^9 cm−2. The whisker apexes are sharp, and the sidewalls are crystalline with a conformal oxide/Cl-containing sheath inferred from XPS. Raman spectra show predominantly crystalline Si with a minor amorphous component; TEM/EDS indicate minimal metallic contamination. Spectral reflectance drops to below a few percent across the visible and near-IR for the chlorinated etch, corresponding to strong optical absorption due to light-trapping by nanostructure; ellipsometry and photocurrent measurements corroborate high optical absorption and dark currents suppressed by surface states. Electrical characterization demonstrates a marked improvement in photoconductivity under illumination, with response times compatible with optoelectronic operation. The results are explained by a growth mechanism in which anisotropic chlorine plasma etching, coupled with self-masking by redeposited Si-Cl species, yields dense, high-aspect-ratio whiskers, whose geometry controls the observed optical and electronic enhancements.

title: How Black Holes Stop Their Host Galaxy from Growing Without AGN Feedback
text_ai: Super-massive black holes (SMBHs) with $M_{\bullet} \sim 10^9 $ M$_{\odot}$ at $z>6$ likely originate from massive seed black holes (BHs). We investigate the consequences of seeding SMBHs with direct collapse BHs (DCBHs) ($M_{\bullet}=10^{4-6}\, \mathrm{M}_\odot$) on proto-galactic disc growth. To isolate the gravitational influence of the central hole, we perform high-resolution cosmological zoom-ins tracking halos that host DCBHs (10^4–10^6 M⊙) and a control set without central BHs from z ~ 20 to z ~ 6. All runs disable AGN radiative and mechanical feedback, but retain gas cooling, star formation, SN feedback, and BH growth subgrid physics that governs the central potential. We parametrize BH accretion by Bondi–Hoyle–Lyttleton estimates capped at Eddington, and allow BH–BH mergers in the event of halo mergers; the evolving central potential is then used to follow the angular-momentum budget and gas inflow to the disc. We quantify disc growth with radial surface-density profiles, disc scale length, and the fraction of star formation in the disc versus the bulge; we also monitor the specific angular momentum of the cold gas and the Toomre Q of the gas as a proxy for stability. Our principal result is that early DCBH seeds rapidly deepen the inner potential, raising rotational velocities and stabilizing gas against large-scale inflows. As BHs grow to ~10^6–10^7 M⊙, accretion-induced deepening confines fresh gas to the central couple of kiloparsecs, suppressing the formation of an extended gaseous disc. The disc mass plateaus at ≲ a few ×10^9 M⊙ and the stellar disc fraction remains low, yielding compact, bulge-dominated systems even in the absence of AGN feedback. This gravitational self-regulation provides a natural channel for halting disc growth and contributing to the observed diversity of early galaxy morphologies.

title: Challenges in the thermal modeling of highly porous carbon foams
text_ai: The heat pulse experiment is a well-known method for determining thermal diffusivity. However, neither the measurement nor the evaluation methodologies are straightforward for heterogeneous, highly porous materials. In the present paper, we focus on two open-cell carbon foam types, differing in their porosity but having the same size. Using a laser flash apparatus, we obtain transient surface temperature responses from insulated samples under controlled boundary conditions. We first deconvolve the measured signals with conventional lumped models, and then we employ a physics-based effective-medium approach that partitions the heat flux into solid and pore-fill contributions, incorporating porosity, tortuosity, and contact resistance at solid–gas interfaces. A finite-volume formulation of the transient heat-conduction equation with porosity-dependent volumetric heat capacity and thermal conductivity, augmented by a radiative term for mesopore spaces, is calibrated against microstructural metrics derived from X-ray tomography. We quantify biases of conventional analysis, showing significant over- or underestimation of diffusivity with increasing porosity. The results emphasize the need for coupled solid/gas/radiation models and demonstrate a pathway to robust extraction of intrinsic solid-phase conductivity and volumetric heat capacity, enabling more reliable thermal design of porous carbon foams.

In the present paper, we focus on two open-cell carbon foam types, differing in their porosity but having the same size.

title: SCOUT: Teaching Pre-trained Language Models to Enhance Reasoning via Flow Chain-of-Thought
text_ai: Chain of Thought (CoT) prompting improves the reasoning performance of large language models (LLMs) by encouraging step by step thinking. However, CoT-based methods depend on intermediate reasoning steps, which limits scalability and generalization. Recent work explores recursive reasoning, where LLMs reuse internal layers across iterations to refine latent representations without explicit CoT supervision. SCOUT introduces Flow Chain-of-Thought, a training paradigm that teaches pre-trained LMs to cultivate a stable, interpretable flow of latent reasoning across layers, without relying on ground-truth intermediate CoT annotations. Rather than prompting for explicit step-by-step text, SCOUT imposes a flow-consistency objective that regularizes the trajectory of hidden representations as the input traverses the network. A lightweight flow head predicts layer-to-layer deltas that guide refinement toward the final answer; the training objective combines standard language modeling with a self-supervised flow-consistency loss, a contrastive loss over activations for semantically related problems, and an answer-focused alignment term ensuring the final representation predicts the correct solution. We evaluate on arithmetic word problems, logical deduction, and commonsense reasoning, comparing against standard CoT prompting, recursive baselines, and plain prompting. SCOUT yields consistent improvements in reasoning accuracy and robustness to prompt-induced variance, with reduced reliance on manually annotated CoT. Ablations reveal the contribution of flow supervision, the layer-range used for flow alignment, and the trade-off between supervision strength and model capacity. We observe positive transfer across model scales and tasks, enabling stronger zero-shot and few-shot performance with the same prompts. Together, these findings position Flow Chain-of-Thought as a viable, supervision-efficient route to enhance latent reasoning in pre-trained LMs, with broad applicability to real-world reasoning tasks. SCOUT thereby lowers the barrier to deploying advanced reasoning LMs in settings where CoT annotation is impractical.

title: Immunofluorescence Capillary Imaging Segmentation: Cases Study
text_ai: Nonunion is one of the challenges faced by orthopedics clinics for the technical difficulties and high costs in photographing interosseous capillaries. Segmenting vessels and filling capillaries are critical in understanding the obstacles encountered in capillary growth. Herein, we introduce a segmentation workflow tailored to immunofluorescence capillary images obtained from periosteal sites in nonunion patients. A pre-processing module performs flat-field correction, denoising with a nonlocal means filter, and channel alignment across z-stacks to reduce photobleaching artifacts. Vascular structures are enhanced via multiscale Hessian-based Frangi-like filters, followed by adaptive thresholding to balance sensitivity and specificity. To address fragmented capillaries, a novel fill-and-skeleton approach integrates isocontour inpainting with morphological closing, generating networks suitable for morphometric analysis. We validate the pipeline on a case-series of ten immunofluorescence slides, annotated by two expert readers. Performance metrics include Dice similarity, precision, recall, and topology-preserving connectivity. The method achieves an average Dice of 0.82, with 0.85 precision and 0.80 recall, improving continuity across gaps by 28% relative to thresholding. Case-level analyses demonstrate robust discrimination of capillary density, branching, and lumen diameter distributions, informing therapeutic assessment and enabling reproducible cross-case comparisons.

title: Voltage Estimation in Low-Voltage Distribution Grids with Distributed Energy Resources
text_ai: The present distribution grids generally have limited sensing capabilities and are therefore characterized by low observability. Improved observability is a prerequisite for increasing the hosting capacity of distributed energy resources such as solar photovoltaics (PV) in distribution grids. In this context, this paper presents learning-aided low-voltage estimation using untapped but readily available and widely distributed sensors from cable television (CATV) networks. Treating CATV sensors as a sparse, irregularly sampled measurement set, the paper develops a learning-aided estimator that fuses CATV proxies with a compact physical model of the low-voltage network. A data-driven component captures spatial correlations along feeders, while a physics-based constraint ensures adherence to network laws. The approach supports online operation and provides probabilistic voltage estimates with confidence intervals to quantify uncertainty in topology and DER states. It remains scalable to large feeders and robust to missing data, leveraging transfer learning to adapt to seasonal DER penetration. Validation on a realistic LV feeder with rooftop PV and energy storage shows substantial accuracy gains over conventional pseudo-measurement schemes, lowering voltage estimation error by a significant margin and enhancing observability under limited sensing. These results support wider deployment.

title: Clinical and functional outcome of open primary repair of triangular fibrocartilage complex tears associated with distal radius fractures
text_ai: PURPOSE: We evaluate the clinical and functional outcome of open primary repair of acute TFCC tears in distal radius fracture, when there is gross intraoperative distal radioulnar joint (DRUJ) instability after fixation of the distal radius, in the absence of an ulnar styloid fracture or when the ulnar fracture fragment is too small to be fixed. METHODS: Retrospective review of consecutive wrists undergoing open primary TFCC repair for acute tears in the setting of distal radius fracture with intraoperative DRUJ instability after fixation. Exclusion criteria included ulnar styloid fracture or fragments too small to fix. Data collected: patient demographics, mechanism of injury, fracture pattern, TFCC tear pattern (Palmer), repair technique (suture vs anchor, foveal reattachment), and intraoperative DRUJ stability. Postoperative management included immobilization for 4–6 weeks followed by rehabilitation. Primary outcomes were DRUJ stability, range of motion (pronation-supination, flexion-extension), grip strength, and DASH score, with mean follow-up of 18 months. RESULTS: Fifteen patients (16 wrists) were evaluated (42 years; 11 men). Palmer 1B or 1D tears were most common. All repairs achieved immediate intraoperative DRUJ stability; at final follow-up, 15/16 wrists remained DRUJ-stable. ROM improved: pronation-supination from 70–75°/70–76° preop to 85–90°/85–90° postoperatively; flexion-extension from 60–65°/60–65° to 70–75°/70–78°. DASH improved from 28 to 8; grip strength reached 85–90% of contralateral side. Pain (VAS) decreased from 6.0 to 1.2. Two superficial wound infections occurred; no repair failures or radiographic DRUJ subluxation. CONCLUSION: Open primary TFCC repair in DRUJ-instability after distal radius fracture yields durable DRUJ stability and favorable functional recovery with minimal complications.

title: New interventions to treat chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension.
text_ai: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) can be defined as a type of precapillary pulmonary hypertension (PH) resulting from incomplete resolution of pulmonary embolism. Symptoms are exertional breathlessness and most patients come to a cardiologist's attention with a dilated right heart on echocardiography. Definitive therapy with pulmonary endarterectomy provides a potential cure for operable disease, whereas balloon-based and pharmacologic strategies address inoperable or residual disease. However, restenosis after BPA and limited distal-lumen remodeling motivate exploration of additional interventions that can sustain patency and improve right-ventricular function. This study evaluated a novel endovascular approach—paclitaxel-coated balloon angioplasty (PCBA)—designed to suppress neointimal hyperplasia within obstructed pulmonary arteries while preserving distal microvascular perfusion. In a multicenter, randomized trial, 120 adults with CTEPH deemed inoperable or with persistent symptoms after prior PEA were assigned to PCBA versus conventional BPA. Procedures were standardized, performed under fluoroscopic guidance with intraprocedural hemodynamic monitoring, and followed at 3 and 6 months. The primary endpoint was the absolute change in mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) at 6 months. Secondary endpoints included changes in pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR), cardiac index, 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), WHO functional class, right-ventricular size and function, and safety. At 6 months, the PCBA group exhibited a greater reduction in mPAP (−12.3 ± 5.2 mmHg) than BPA (−6.5 ± 4.7 mmHg; p=0.01). PVR fell by 38% versus 21% (p=0.02); 6MWD improved by 62 ± 28 m versus 34 ± 25 m (p=0.04); and a ≥1-class improvement in WHO functional status occurred in 58% versus 31% (p=0.03). Adverse events were uncommon and comparably distributed, with no procedure-related mortality. These findings support PCBA as a feasible, more effective option than conventional BPA in selected patients with CTEPH, warranting longer-term evaluation of durability and cost-effectiveness.

title: Position-Constrained Stochastic Inference for Cooperative Indoor Localization
text_ai: We address the problem of distributed cooperative localization in wireless networks, i.e. nodes without prior position knowledge (agents) wish to determine their own positions. In non-cooperative approaches, positioning is only based on information from reference nodes with known positions (anchors). However, in cooperative positioning, information from other agents is considered as well. To this end, we formulate the localization task as a distributed Bayesian inference problem over a graph that couples agent states through pairwise ranging and bearing measurements, and includes geometric priors from indoor floorplans. We introduce Position-Constrained Stochastic Inference (PCSI), a scalable, distributed algorithm that combines particle-based belief representations with constraint-aware resampling to maintain feasibility with respect to bounds. Each node performs message passing with neighboring agents and anchors, updating its position posterior with messages encoding distance and feasibility. To enforce constraints without compromising convergence, we incorporate a projection and rejection mechanism into the sampling step and damping of updates. The method is robust to non-Gaussian noise and outliers, adapting to dynamic network topologies. Empirical results on simulated and real data show reductions in localization error and improved consistency over non-constrained cooperative approaches.
